description: Curated knowledge for the Snapmaker Orca print assistant. Entries are original summaries of the cited sources (the Snapmaker wiki and public printing references); see each entry's sources.

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan 3D printing safety rules
entries.summary: Treat the nozzles, glass plate and heated bed as hot whenever the Artisan is heating, printing or has just finished. Snapmaker wants the 3D Printing Module run inside the Enclosure, in a ventilated room or with an air purifier because some filaments give off fumes, and asks you to read each filament's safety data sheet.
facts: Do not touch the nozzle, glass build plate or heated bed while heating, printing or just after a job.
Unplug the machine before maintenance or modifications, and never connect or disconnect cables with power on.
Two people are needed to lift and assemble the machine and Enclosure; keep the space beside the base plate clear for the moving modules and platform.
Do not press on the linear module steel strips.
Run it indoors on a solid level bench, away from rain and damp, and never leave it powered on unattended.
Ventilate or use an air purifier, especially with ABS, which releases toxic fumes.
Switch off immediately on a burning smell, sparks, odd lights or noises, unexpected stops or visible internal damage.
Minors may only operate it with adult supervision.

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan 3D printing specifications
entries.summary: Snapmaker Artisan is a modular 3-in-1 machine (3D printing, laser, CNC). For printing it uses the Dual Extrusion Module: one toolhead with a left (L) and a right (R) nozzle, the right one raised by a small motor when idle. It prints on a zoned heated bed with a glass build plate or a magnetic PEI steel sheet, inside the Snapmaker Enclosure. Key numbers from the Artisan wiki follow.
facts: Toolhead: Dual Extrusion Module with two hot ends (Nozzle L and Nozzle R); nozzle centres are about 25 mm apart; the right hot end is lifted by a lifting motor and lead screw.
Levelling sensor: a photoelectric switch inside the Dual Extruder (no separate probe is connected on the Artisan version).
Bed levelling grids of 9 (3x3), 25 (5x5) or 81 (9x9) points; factory default is Auto Mode, 25 points, Heated Leveling at 65 C.
Zoned heated bed: with Bed Heating Area = Whole Bed the inner zone reaches up to 110 C and the outer zone up to 80 C; Inner Zone mode heats only the centre.
Print surfaces: glass build plate with a smooth glass side and a PEI-coated side, or an optional PEI spring steel sheet held by a soft magnetic sticker.
Motion: five belt-driven linear modules (2 x Y, 2 x Z, 1 x X) covered by steel strips; recommended print and travel speed up to 200 mm/s; default acceleration 2000 mm/s^2.
Each nozzle has its own filament runout sensor switch; Filament Runout Recovery pauses and resumes the job.
One tap of Load on the touchscreen feeds 90 mm of filament.
Operating environment: 0-40 C (32-104 F) and 30-70% relative humidity.
Bench for machine plus Enclosure: at least 1035 mm wide x 1690 mm long, rated above 65 kg.
Enclosure: hall-switch door detection, LED strips and an exhaust fan, wired through the Enclosure converter.
Integrated Controller with Android touchscreen, Wi-Fi, USB port and emergency stop button; firmware 2.8.0+ accepts uploads straight from Snapmaker Orca (device IP:8080).

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan 3D printing workflow and sending G-code to the machine
entries.summary: An Artisan print runs: check room, hardware and filament; pick the plate surface; calibrate (optional after setup); load filament; slice; transfer the file; print while watching the first layer; remove the part. Luban accepts STL or OBJ and needs the right machine selected. Third-party G-code used to be USB-only; firmware 2.8.0 lets Snapmaker Orca upload over Wi-Fi.
steps: Check the environment, hardware and filament, then choose the glass or PEI surface.
Calibrate if needed and load filament into each nozzle the job uses.
Luban: confirm the machine in Preferences > Machine Settings, import the STL/OBJ, pick a preset, click Generate G-Code, then Export.
Wi-Fi from Luban: Export > Load G-code to Workspace, then Send to Device in the preview; the job can then be started and watched from the computer.
USB: export the G-code to a flash drive, plug it into the Controller and tap Start > USB to pick the file.
Snapmaker Orca (firmware 2.8.0+): connect to the device IP with :8080 and upload directly.
Watch the first layer and stop early if it does not stick.

entries.title: Recovering the Artisan touchscreen after an Android system crash
entries.summary: If the touchscreen's Android system has crashed, Snapmaker's recovery is a factory data reset from Android Recovery using a USB keyboard, then switching off factory test modes in the debug menu, then flashing user firmware from a USB drive and rerunning the setup guide. All user data on the screen is erased.
steps: Plug a USB keyboard into the controller's USB port and power on into Android Recovery.
With the arrow keys and Enter choose Factory data reset and confirm the wipe; wait a few minutes for the restart.
At the Chinese 'system interface not responding' pop-up, pick the second option (wait).
Tap debug at the top and switch off mock mode and USB factory mode; each restarts the screen within about 2 seconds. Close any error pop-ups.
Flash the firmware linked on Snapmaker's recovery page from a USB drive using local update.
When the setup guide appears, power off, reconnect the other modules, power on and complete initialisation.

sources.title: Recovery process after Artisan Android system crashes

entries.title: Breakaway support for PLA settings on Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: Breakaway support for PLA is a support-only material: it bonds to PLA well enough to hold it, yet snaps off by hand. It prints differently from normal PLA, so do not use it for parts. Artisan values: 220-230 C nozzle, 68 C bed on the PEI surface, up to 80 mm/s, 1 mm retraction at 35 mm/s, fan on. It is brittle and absorbs moisture, so keep it dry.

settings.advice: 220-230 C for breakaway support on Artisan.
68 C on the PEI surface.
1 mm.
35 mm/s.
Up to 80 mm/s for breakaway supports.
Enable in the breakaway filament profile so Orca uses it only for supports.
Point to the extruder holding the breakaway filament.

entries.title: Cleaning the Artisan build plate: residue, grease, dust and glue
entries.summary: Skin oil, dust and leftover glue or filament all weaken first-layer adhesion on the Artisan glass plate. Scrape off filament after every print, wipe away glue each time you use it, and remove grease and dust at least every two weeks.
steps: Filament residue (after every print): scrape with the palette knife held below 30 degrees to the glass; if it resists, heat the bed to 50 C via Control > Heated Bed and scrape again wearing gloves.
Glue (every time it was applied): power off and wipe the plate with the kit cloth dampened with water.
Grease and dust (at least every two weeks): power off and wipe with a water-dampened cloth until no smears remain; use ethyl alcohol if water does not lift the grease.

sources.title: Remove the Filament Residues from the Build Plate

entries.title: Artisan XY Offset calibration or Check Model print fails
entries.summary: A failed XY calibration pattern or Check Model is usually caused by a nozzle set too high (no adhesion), a wrong right-nozzle Z offset (it scrapes, or its lines will not bond to the left nozzle's), two different filaments loaded, bent hot ends, or a scale that was not saved properly. Use standard PLA in both nozzles for calibration.
symptoms: First layer of the calibration print does not stick
Right nozzle drags through lines already laid by the left nozzle
Right nozzle's lines do not bond to the left nozzle's lines
Scale cannot be saved during XY Offset Calibration
Right nozzle output is shifted on the Check Model
causes: Nozzle too far from the 3D printing platform
Right nozzle Z offset incorrect
Different materials in the two nozzles, e.g. PLA and PETG
Hot ends not level with each other, bent or deformed
Scale not saved correctly during XY calibration
steps: Load standard PLA in both nozzles.
If the nozzle is clearly too high, lower the Z offset on the screen; if not, put solid glue on the platform.
For scraping or bonding problems, redo Z Offset Calibration; if that fails run Sensor Calibration (nozzle just touching the card) and then Z offset again.
If a scale will not save, check both nozzles sit at the same height and replace any bent or deformed hot end.
Repeat XY Offset Calibration several times, saving the best-overlapping scale each round, to converge on the right value.
Measure the distance between nozzle centres with calipers; it should be about 25 mm.
If the Check Model is offset, reprint the XY calibration and save the best-matching scale.

entries.title: Cleaning the Dual Extrusion Module dust screens
entries.summary: Dust builds up on the screens on both sides of the Dual Extrusion Module and restricts its cooling airflow. Clean them at least every two weeks.
steps: Power off and remove the Dual Extrusion Module.
Wet a cotton swab with water and work it inside each air inlet until the screen is free of dust and water.
Use a new swab for any further pass if dust remains.

sources.title: Clean the Dust Screen of the Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Cleaning the Artisan extruder gears
entries.summary: Pushing filament grinds off fine shavings; as they build up they flatten the gear teeth, which then slip instead of gripping, hurting extrusion. Brush the gears at least every two weeks.
steps: Unload the filament.
Power off, open the module's front cover and press the extruder buckle down to open the dual-gear extruder.
Brush the shavings out of the gear teeth with a stiff brush (not included).
Close the buckle and cover and reload the filament.

entries.title: Cleaning the Artisan nozzle tips
entries.summary: Plastic stuck to the outside of a nozzle hardens when it cools and can cause jams or dark smudges on the next print. Clean each nozzle hot, at least every two weeks.
steps: Tap Control > Filament and heat the nozzle to 200 C.
Scrub the residue off the tip with the wire brush from the toolbox, minding the hot metal.
Keep the brush off the black thermal insulating casing.
Repeat on the other nozzle.

entries.title: Artisan Cura profiles and the M109 C5 W0 tweak for faster nozzle switching
entries.summary: Snapmaker published Cura project profiles for Artisan named a400-pla+pla-v3.3mf (PLA in both nozzles) and a400-pla+pva-v3.3mf (PLA with PVA support). Its first-use notes say switching between the two hot ends becomes seamless if each M109 is replaced by M109 C5 W0, done in Cura with the post-processing plugin.

settings.advice: Snapmaker's Artisan tip is to replace M109 waits with M109 C5 W0 for seamless hot end switching; apply the same edit to Orca's tool change G-code if it waits with plain M109.

entries.title: Opening the Artisan Dual Extruder to replace top cover, mainboard or heating kit
entries.summary: The Dual Extruder, shared by Snapmaker 2.0 and Artisan, opens the same way for the top cover kit, the main control board and the hot ends heating kit (heating board plus 5P cable). Power off first and never plug or unplug while powered.
steps: Remove the four top cover screws with an H1.5 driver.
Take off the front door panel and the hot ends.
Remove the four back screws with an H2.0 driver and push the inner module out of its shell.

Top cover or mainboard: remove the four H2.0 screws joining them (one sits in the centre). A new top cover needs its connector wedges pressed in from above and the quick-connect fittings slid in beside them.

Mainboard: photograph all connectors, scrape off the white factory adhesive with tweezers and pull plugs gently so ports do not tear off. Artisan levels with a photoelectric switch, so the probe sensor port stays empty.

Heating kit: unplug the hot end 5P cable from the mainboard, remove the two H1.5 heating board screws, route the new cable through the gap in the extruder bracket and mount the board snug against the bracket, or the hot ends may not connect.
Reassemble in reverse order.

sources.title: Dual Extruder top cover kit replacement guide
Dual Extruder hot ends heating kit replacement guide

entries.title: Artisan says the Enclosure door is open when it is closed
entries.summary: A permanent 'enclosure door is opened' alert means the door magnets, the hall switch behind column 2, its cable or the Enclosure converter is at fault. For 3D printing you can temporarily switch door detection off in Settings > Enclosure; it cannot be disabled for laser work.
steps: Workaround: Settings > Enclosure, disable door detection while 3D printing.
Hold a metal object near the door handle to check the magnet; if there is no pull, contact Support.
Check the hall switch cord is plugged into the Enclosure converter and undamaged.
With power on and the door closed, measure the connector near the hall sensor: 5V to GND should read 5 V.
If it does, measure hall1 or hall2 to GND: 0 V with the door shut and 5 V when opened; wrong values mean the hall switch and short cable need replacing.
If 5 V is missing, test the hall sensor cable for continuity; if it is fine, the Enclosure converter needs replacing through Support.

sources.title: The machine screen shows that the door is open even if it has been closed

entries.title: Artisan Enclosure door has a gap or will not close fully
entries.summary: A door that touches only two of its three magnets, or leaves a gap, has usually warped slightly in shipping, during assembly or from heat. Straighten it gently or add Snapmaker's printable door latch. A fully closed door matters for warp-prone filaments such as ABS and ASA.
steps: Place a plastic object about 20 mm thick near the door handle.
Press gently on the top and bottom ends of the door to flex it straight.
If it warps again, print the enclosure door buckle STL, slip a short length of PTFE tube (or a piece of filament tube) over it, and mount it on the Enclosure as in Snapmaker's video.

sources.title: The enclosure door panel has visible gaps or deformations

entries.title: Artisan Enclosure LED strips or fan not working: connector and voltage checks
entries.summary: If the Enclosure LEDs stay dark while the screen shows them on, or the fan or LED cable will not plug in, check the wiring, the Enclosure controller's connectors and its 24 V LED output, then the short and long LED cables and the strip itself.
steps: Power off, unplug and firmly reconnect every Enclosure cable, then test again.
Measure the 2-pin LED port on the Enclosure PCB; it should supply 24 V, and no voltage means the port is faulty.
If 24 V is present, connect the short LED cable and measure its far end; no 24 V there means the short cable is faulty.
If all of that checks out, the long LED cable or the strip is likely bad; contact Support.
Loose or bent connectors: peel the sticker off the Enclosure controller, remove its two H2.0 screws, straighten bent pins and fix them with hot-melt glue, or ask Support for a replacement.

sources.title: Troubleshooting for Artisan LED light strip not lighting up

entries.title: Artisan errors 13-1 to 13-8, 13-10 and 220: nozzle heating faults
entries.summary: These codes come from the Dual Extrusion Module heaters: 13-1/13-2 abnormal heating (Nozzle L/R), 13-3/13-4 abnormal temperature control, 13-5/13-6 underheat, 13-7/13-8 overheat, and 13-10 or 220 abnormal hot end. Snapmaker refers these to its hot end heating-failure guide and Support; first make sure the hot end is seated correctly.
steps: Note the side: odd codes (13-1, 13-3, 13-5, 13-7) are Nozzle L, even codes (13-2, 13-4, 13-6, 13-8) are Nozzle R.
Power off, let the hot end cool, and check it is installed correctly (Snapmaker's fix for 220).
Reseat the hot end, power on and heat again.
If it recurs, contact Snapmaker Support; if they find the hot end heating board or 5P cable faulty, both come in the hot ends heating kit.

sources.title: Dual Extruder hot ends heating kit replacement guide

entries.title: Artisan error 13-12 / 13-17 / 13-18: extruder pushed up, printing paused
entries.summary: The Dual Extruder pauses the job when its levelling sensor sees a hot end being pushed up: 13-12 is an abnormal calibration sensor trigger, 13-17/13-18 mean the extruder is repeatedly lifted. Usual causes: high filament feed resistance (kinked tube, knotted or wrongly wound spool, sticky holder), a clogged nozzle, the nozzle hitting a warped part, or a levelling sensor that has slipped down.
causes: High feed resistance: kinked or crushed PTFE tube, knotted filament, spool mounted the wrong way, friction at the holder
Clogged nozzle, or filament stuck outside that cannot be drawn in
Warped part rising into the nozzle path and pushing the hot end up
Levelling sensor inside the module loose and sitting too low (too sensitive)
steps: Make sure the PTFE (Teflon) tube is not kinked or crushed and the filament has no knots.
Mount the spool so it unwinds clockwise on the filament holder.
If it happens on the first layers, fix warping: re-level, use a brim or raft, add a thin layer of solid glue, and enable travel that avoids printed parts and supports.

Raise the levelling sensor slightly: remove four back screws (H2.0), the hot ends and four top screws (H1.5), lift off cover and shell, then ease the sensor up with tweezers placed between PCB and sensor so the hot end must rise further to trigger it.
If it persists, add bearings to the filament holder to turn sliding friction into rolling friction.
Clear any nozzle clog and contact Support with your results if nothing helps.

settings.advice: Add a brim when the error appears in early layers because edges warp up.
A raft also holds warped edges down, at the cost of time, filament and harder removal.
Enable so travel moves detour around printed parts instead of crossing them.

sources.title: Error code: 13-12/13-18 The extruder is continuously pulled up and printing is paused

entries.title: Artisan error 13-15: right extruder (Extruder R) cannot lift or home
entries.summary: The right hot end of the Dual Extruder is raised by a lifting motor and lead screw. If it will not lift or home, often with stalling or buzzing and both blue board LEDs lit at power-on, check the motor screws and position, its wiring (not swapped with the levelling sensor lead) and the lead screw seating before blaming the motor.
causes: Loose lifting motor screws
Motor shifted so its lead screw binds
Loose, unplugged or misconnected lifting motor wires, often after fitting a replacement kit
Lead screw installed incorrectly
Failed lifting motor
steps: Tighten the lifting motor screws and confirm the motor sits in its correct position.
Check the lifting motor cable is seated and not swapped with the levelling sensor cable.
Make sure the lead screw nut sits centred in its groove with the smooth face outward.
Loosen the motor screws, lift the motor out of the groove, power on and home; if it does not turn properly the motor is faulty.
Update to firmware 2.8.1, which improved dual-nozzle lift detection to reduce false alarms.
Send photos or video to Snapmaker Support if it is still unresolved.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide: Dual Extrusion Module extruder R failed to home/cannot lift

entries.title: Artisan error 2050-10 after M593 F0 (input shaping, ringing tower)
entries.summary: 2050-10 appears after a G-code file runs M593 F0, which sets the vibration-suppression frequency to zero; the Artisan firmware does not guard against this and becomes unstable. It is often seen with input-shaping ringing tower prints or at the end of a job, after which X stops and homing fails. Reset the values over a serial link and avoid M593 F0.
steps: Connect a computer to Artisan over serial with Pronterface or LightBurn.
Send M593 P1 X Y F38 and then M500 to restore and save the vibration compensation settings.
Remove any M593 F0 line from calibration, ringing tower or custom G-code before printing again.

settings.advice: Make sure start, end and custom G-code never send M593 with F0 to Artisan; it triggers 2050-10.

entries.title: Artisan error 2050-5: failed to home, X-axis noise
entries.summary: 2050-5 means a linear module could not reach home, typically because something blocks it. A known Artisan cause is the X-axis bracket: using M5x16 screws instead of M5x12, or mounting the bracket the wrong way round, makes the X axis grind and fail to home.
steps: Make sure no linear module is obstructed.
Take the X axis off its bracket and jog it; if it now runs normally, the wrong screws were used: fit M5x12, not M5x16.
Remove the X-axis bracket, rotate it 180 degrees, refit it and test homing.
If homing still fails, run the limit switch test (Settings > Device Maintenance > Machine Information) and contact Support with photos or video.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide for Artisan X-axis noise and unable to home

entries.title: Artisan controller error codes 2050-3, 2050-7, 2050-8
entries.summary: 2050-3 means the Integrated Controller overheated: power off, let it cool for a while and restart. 2050-7 and 2050-8 report an abnormal power supply for the system and for motion respectively: power off and check the mains supply. Other 2050 codes have their own entries: 2050-1 toolhead not detected, 2050-5 failed to home, 2050-10 bad M593 F0 command.
steps: 2050-3: switch off, wait for the controller to cool, restart; keep its surroundings ventilated.
2050-7 / 2050-8: switch off and confirm the outlet and power cable deliver normal power before restarting.
Contact Snapmaker Support if the code keeps returning.

entries.title: Artisan heated bed errors 515-5, 515-6, 515-10: underheat, not detected, negative temperature
entries.summary: Heated Bed Underheat (515-5/515-6) or Heated Bed Not Detected (515-10), often with a negative bed reading, usually trace to the bed cable, the 7P heated bed extension cable, or the mainboard's bed port; a very cold room can also cause underheat. Work from the plugs inward, testing the NTC 3950 thermistor circuit with a multimeter.
causes: Faulty heated bed cable or cold or broken solder joints
Faulty 7P heated bed extension cable
Faulty heated bed port on the main control board
Very low ambient temperature or an abnormal temperature sensor (515-5/515-6)
steps: Power off and check the bed cable to extension cable joint is fully seated and aligned.
Check the extension cable connection at the main control board.
With power on, wiggle the bed cable; if the displayed temperature jumps, that cable has a bad connection.

Measure resistance between pins 1-2 and 1-3 of the bed cable connector on a kilohm range and compare with an NTC 3950 table for the room temperature (Snapmaker's reference values are at about 26 C); open or wrong readings mean the bed or its cable is faulty.
Remove the cover screws (H2.0) and inspect the bed cable solder joints; resolder cold or loose joints if you can.
Abnormal resistance with sound joints and no change when wiggled points to the heated bed itself.
If the bed cable reads correctly, test the 7P extension cable the same way; if both are fine, the main control board is the likely culprit.
A new bed cable is soldered on following the 7P pin layout, with the bed cold and unplugged (soldering iron, safety goggles); contact Support for parts.

sources.title: Artisan heated bed underheat and error code 515-10 or 515-6
Guide for replacing the heated bed cable on the Artisan

entries.title: Other Artisan heated bed error codes: 515-1 to 515-4, 515-7, 515-8, 515-9, 515-11
entries.summary: 515-1/515-2 (abnormal bed heating) and 515-3/515-4 (abnormal bed temperature control) are cleared by powering off, reseating the heated bed cable and restarting. 515-7/515-8 (bed overheat) and 515-11 (bed self-check failed) need Snapmaker Support. 515-9 means the 3D printing platform is fitted with a toolhead other than the 3D Printing Module.
steps: 515-1 to 515-4: power off, unplug and firmly replug the heated bed cable, restart.
515-7, 515-8 or 515-11: stop using the bed and contact Snapmaker Support.
515-9: power off, fit the Dual Extrusion Module or swap the work platform to match the installed toolhead, then restart.

entries.title: Artisan linear module error codes 516-1 to 516-6
entries.summary: 516 codes come from the linear modules: 516-1 a module disconnected, 516-2 no module detected, 516-3/516-4/516-5 the X, Y or Z modules not detected, and 516-6 the toolhead is already at its lowest point. For 516-1 to 516-5, power off, reconnect the named module cables to the Integrated Controller and restart.
steps: Power off before touching any cable.
Reconnect the module(s) named by the code, matching each cable label to the port label (2 x Y, 2 x Z, 1 x X); swapped linear module cables cause faults.
Restart; if an axis still fails, use the X/Y port-swap test to tell a bad module from a bad controller port.
516-6 is a travel limit notice, not a fault: stop jogging the toolhead downward.

sources.title: The X-Linear Module of Artisan can't move

entries.title: How Snapmaker Artisan touchscreen error codes are structured
entries.summary: An Artisan error code reads owner-error: the first number names the part that raised it and the second the fault. For 3D printing the relevant owners are 13 (3D Printing Module), 515 (heated bed), 516 (linear modules), 2050 (controller), 16 (Enclosure), 7 (air purifier) and the three-digit 2xx workflow codes. Contact Snapmaker Support if the listed fix fails or the error keeps returning.
facts: 13 = 3D Printing Module (Dual Extrusion Module).
515 = Heated Bed; 516 = Linear Module; 2050 = Controller.
16 = Enclosure; 7 = Air Purifier.
200 = Workflow, shown as three-digit codes such as 204 or 220.
14 and 2 = Laser Module; 1 = 50W CNC Module; 15 = 200W CNC Module; 6 = Rotary Module.

entries.title: Artisan errors 2050-1, 13-9, 13-16, 217: toolhead not detected or disconnected
entries.summary: These codes mean the controller has lost contact with the Dual Extrusion Module: 2050-1 toolhead not detected, 13-9 and 217 toolhead disconnected, 13-16 abnormal toolhead communication. In each case power off, firmly reconnect the toolhead cable at both the toolhead and the Integrated Controller, and restart.
steps: Power off; never plug or unplug with power on.
Reseat the toolhead cable at the toolhead and at the toolhead port of the Integrated Controller.
Power on; if the code returns, check the cable for damage and contact Snapmaker Support.
If a paused job will not resume after changing toolheads, see codes 213 and 214: recovery needs the same toolhead.

entries.title: Artisan workflow error codes 204, 213, 214, 218, 219, 227 plus 13-13, 16-1, 7-1
entries.summary: Workflow codes seen when printing: 204 G-code file unusable (corrupted characters or too long a file name), 213 job recovery failed (different toolhead or hardware fault), 214 toolhead differs from the one used before the pause, 218 operation unavailable while another problem is open, 219 abnormal extruder, 227 Enclosure door still open. Also 13-13 calibration failed, 16-1 Enclosure disconnected, 7-1 air purifier disconnected.
steps: 204: re-export the G-code with a short, plain file name and make sure the file is not corrupted.
213 / 214: resume only with the same toolhead that started the job; otherwise start the print again.
218: clear the other pending error first.
219: contact Support if it happens often.
227: close the Enclosure door; if it is already shut, check the door detection hardware.
13-13: quit the calibration and run it again.
16-1 / 7-1: power off, reconnect the Enclosure or air purifier cable and restart.

entries.title: Exporting Artisan system logs for Snapmaker Support
entries.summary: Support often asks for logs. Plug a USB drive into the Artisan, open Settings > About machine, scroll to System Logs, tap Export and choose the method; send the files whose names contain FW and SC. If an error or a stuck calibration keeps you out of Settings, power off, disconnect the toolhead and try again.

entries.title: Removing a filament blob or leak on the Artisan hot end
entries.summary: A ball of plastic around the heater block usually starts when the first layer fails and filament keeps building up on the nozzle, or when the nozzle or heatbreak works loose and plastic leaks out beside the heater block. Small blobs can be picked off hot, mild leaks need the nozzle tightened hot, and heavy leaks need a new hot end.
symptoms: Nozzle and heater block encased in plastic
Plastic seeping where heatbreak or nozzle meets the heater block
causes: First layer not sticking, so extruded filament collects around the nozzle
Nozzle/heatbreak joint loosened during installation or use
steps: Blob on the heater block only: heat the hot end, pull the plastic off with tweezers, wipe the block and fit a new silicone sleeve.

Blob spreading to nearby parts: trim it with diagonal pliers without nicking the hot end cable, remove the toolhead bottom cover and front door, loosen the lower hot end throat bolts and clear plastic from the bracket until the hot end comes out; check for worn parts.

Mild leak: heat to 230-240 C (PLA) or 270-280 C (ABS), switch off, quickly pull the hot end wearing heat-resistant gloves, tighten the nozzle with two adjustable wrenches (or wrench and vice), and clear the leaked plastic.
Heavy leak: remove and replace the whole hot end.
Request replacement parts from Support if anything is damaged.

entries.title: Artisan extruder buckle loose: extrusion stops mid-print
entries.summary: The Dual Extrusion Module's extruder buckle (idler clamp) can lose clamping force and spring open, so the gears slip on the filament after many retractions or extra resistance. The job runs to the end with nothing coming out, because the runout sensor still sees filament. Wedge the buckle with a printed block, then get silicone pads or the buckles kit from Snapmaker.
symptoms: Print starts normally, then stops extruding partway
Intermittent extrusion
Manual or touchscreen loading still extrudes
Lots of filament dust near the gear when the buckle is opened
Job finishes with no runout pause and an incomplete part
causes: Buckle clamping force weakening with use or due to tolerances
Filament slipping on the gears after repeated retractions or high extrusion resistance
steps: If both extruders slip and cannot print at all, push a 3 mm plastic block (or folded paper) into the buckle as a stopgap.
Print the wedge model from the wiki (buckle wedge.stl or blockv2.stl) in PLA or TPU.
Remove the stopgap and press the printed wedge into the buckle to restore clamping force.
For a lasting fix, ask Snapmaker for the self-adhesive silicone pads that sit inside the buckle, or replace the buckles kit (H1.5 and H2.0 drivers, following Snapmaker's video).

sources.title: The extruder buckle of the Dual Extrusion Module gets loose
3D printing half without filaments extrusion and filaments extrusion intermittent
Dual Extruder buckles kit replacement guide

entries.title: Artisan extrusion motor does not turn or makes noise
entries.summary: An extruder gear that will not turn or grinds points to a damaged or loose motor cable, a failed motor, a seized planetary gear or a faulty Dual Extrusion Module control board. Swapping the left and right motors shows whether the motor or the board is to blame.
steps: Open the module: four back screws (H2.0), detach the hot ends, four top screws (H1.5).
Inspect the faulty motor's cable and the control board pins for looseness or damage.
Remove the two motor screws and turn the planetary gear with a screwdriver to check it spins freely.
Swap the left and right extrusion motors, reconnect, heat a hot end and tap Load.
If the fault moves with the motor, the motor is bad; if it stays on the same side, the module's control board is faulty.
Share the results with Snapmaker Support for parts.

entries.title: Filament Runout Recovery on Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: When a nozzle's runout sensor detects the filament has run out, Artisan pauses and shows a dialog to load new filament and continue from the pause point, or to cancel. Auto Loading works here, so you only need to push the new filament in until it is drawn in. If the sensor misfires, detection can be switched off from the settings while printing.
steps: When the dialog appears, trim the new filament end and push it into the tube until the extruder pulls it in.
Choose to continue; printing resumes at the pause position.
If the sensor reports runout with filament present, see the filament runout sensor error entry.

entries.title: Artisan filament runout sensor false alarms or no detection
entries.summary: Two failure modes: runout is reported with filament still loaded, or the spool runs out and the machine carries on without pausing. Old Dual Extrusion Modules without the replacement kit have sensor switches that wear out; new or kit-upgraded modules usually have a wiring problem, a loose sensor board or a wrongly fitted copper block or trigger pad. Also confirm detection is enabled.
symptoms: Runout error while filament is still loaded
No pause or warning when the filament actually runs out
causes: Worn sensor switch on an old-version module without the replacement kit
Broken wire or damaged or loose terminal on the sensor switch
Loose fixing screws on the filament sensor circuit board
Replacement kit fitted without the copper block, wearing the switch
Trigger pad or copper block installed the wrong way so the lever never touches the filament
Filament detection switched off
steps: Stopgap for false alarms: turn filament detection off in the settings on the print screen and finish the job.
Old module without the kit: replace the runout sensor using the Dual Extrusion Module replacement kit (ask Support).
Otherwise power off and remove the toolhead: four back screws (H2.0), detach hot ends, four top screws (H1.5), then front cover and shell.
Check both sensor switches for broken wires, loose connectors or pushed-out pins and reconnect or repair them.
Tighten the sensor board screws if loose.
Remove the sensor board; check the switch for wear and the copper block and trigger pad for correct orientation, fixing or requesting parts as needed.
Reassemble, and re-enable detection if it had been turned off.

entries.title: Storing filament and spotting damp filament (Artisan)
entries.summary: Most filaments, PVA, TPU and PA (nylon) above all, absorb moisture from the air, which degrades prints and can clog the nozzle. Keep opened spools sealed with desiccant or in a filament dryer at -20 to 30 C and under 50% humidity, and dry damp spools using the filament maker's figures.
symptoms: Filament snaps easily when bent or pulled
Crackling or popping as it extrudes
Bubbles or spots on the filament or on the print surface
Heavy stringing or oozing even with retraction enabled
Weak parts and poor first-layer adhesion
causes: Spool left unsealed in humid air
Hygroscopic materials (PVA, TPU, PA) stored without desiccant
steps: Keep unused spools in a vacuum bag with desiccant or in a dry box.
Store at -20 to 30 C and below 50% relative humidity.
If any symptom above appears, dry the spool at the temperature and time the filament maker specifies.
Re-test with a dried or freshly opened spool to confirm moisture was the cause.

entries.title: Filament tangled or stuck at the Artisan extruder gears (PVA, TPU, breakaway)
entries.summary: No extrusion, and filament wrapped around the gears when the buckle is opened, most often happens with PVA, TPU or breakaway support. Moisture makes PVA and breakaway sticky and TPU is soft; clogs push back; wrong temperature, long or fast retractions and high speeds make them buckle; loose or worn extruder parts and poor cooling add to it.
symptoms: Nozzle stops extruding
Filament kinked or wrapped around the extruder gear when the buckle is opened
causes: Damp PVA or breakaway filament turning sticky; soft TPU compressing
Clogged hot end or nozzle
Nozzle temperature too high (over-softened) or too low (poor flow)
Retraction distance or speed too high
Print speed too fast for flexible or soluble filament
Loose extruder set screw, worn or dirty gears, wrong feed tube gap or loose buckle
Poor toolhead cooling overheating the filament path
steps: Check the spool for tangles or knots; dry PVA and breakaway filament in a dry box and keep them sealed.
For TPU, use 95A high-flow material (Snapmaker TPU95 HF).
Clear or replace a clogged hot end or nozzle.
Use Snapmaker's recommended temperature and retraction for the filament and slow down for PVA and TPU.
Check the extruder set screw, gear wear and residue, the feed tube gap and buckle tension.
Confirm the cooling fan runs, check whether the Dual Extruder has the newer front door with better cooling, or try printing with the front door open.

settings.advice: Reduce for PVA and TPU; long retractions stretch soft filament and make it tangle at the gear.
Lower if soft filament jams after retractions.
Lower in PVA and TPU profiles so the whole print slows and the gears do not buckle the filament.
Stay inside the filament's recommended range; both too hot and too cold encourage jams.

entries.title: Updating Snapmaker Artisan firmware (Wi-Fi or USB)
entries.summary: Artisan prompts for new firmware when it is online. Update over Wi-Fi from Settings > Firmware Update, or put the file from Snapmaker's support site on a USB drive and use Local Update. Snapmaker recommends running the latest touchscreen firmware before printing.
steps: Wi-Fi: join a network, tap Settings > Firmware Update, tap Download if a newer version is listed, then Update; 'Already Latest' means nothing to do.
USB: download the latest Artisan firmware via Support > Product Support > Snapmaker Artisan > Firmware on snapmaker.com and copy it to a flash drive.
Insert the drive in the Integrated Controller, tap Settings > Firmware Update > Local Update, select the file and tap Update.

entries.title: Artisan firmware V2.8.0: Snapmaker Orca direct connection and Repeat Job
entries.summary: V2.8.0 lets Snapmaker Orca send G-code to Artisan over Wi-Fi directly via the OctoPrint protocol, so Luban is no longer needed as a relay; the address becomes device IP:8080. It also adds a Repeat Job button when a job finishes. Known issues involve simultaneous uploads and uploads during calibration.
facts: Direct Machine Connection: Snapmaker Orca talks to the machine over the OctoPrint protocol; Luban no longer has to open the connection first.
Address format is now device IP:8080, for example 192.168.0.1:8080.
Repeat Job button on the touchscreen restarts a finished 3D print (or laser/CNC job) with one tap.
Known issue: starting an Orca upload during bed-level preheat or XY offset calibration on the dual-nozzle toolhead interrupts the calibration.
Known issue: uploading from Luban and Orca at the same time makes the job fail.
Known issue: an Orca upload can hang at 0%; restart the machine and send logs plus a description to Snapmaker.

entries.title: Artisan firmware V2.8.1: zoned bed heating and nozzle lift detection fixes
entries.summary: V2.8.1 changes zoned bed heating so the outer zones are brought to 80 C whenever the centre zone is above 80 C, which reduces PEI plate deformation in high-temperature prints. It also improves dual-nozzle lift status detection to cut false alarms; the remaining changes concern the laser flame sensor.
facts: Outer bed zones automatically heat to 80 C when the centre zone is set above 80 C.
Fewer false alarms from dual-nozzle lift status detection.
Laser-only changes: flame sensor sensitivity reminder and tuning.

entries.title: Heated Bed Leveling on Snapmaker Artisan (Auto, Manual, grid size)
entries.summary: Artisan probes a grid of points and then moves the toolhead up or down during printing so the nozzle-to-plate gap stays constant even on an imperfect bed. Defaults: Auto Mode, Heated Leveling at 65 C, 25 points. If the first layer still sticks badly after Auto levelling, enable Heated Leveling, pick a denser grid, or level manually.
steps: Wipe both nozzle tips clean.
Tap Calibration > Heated Bed Leveling, then the top-right corner to open Mode Selection.
Auto Mode: confirm and tap Start; bed and nozzles heat and probing runs on its own (keep hands off hot surfaces).
Manual Mode: confirm, tap Start and set each point by following the prompts.
Heated Leveling (Auto Mode only): enter a bed temperature above room temperature before confirming; enter one below it, such as 0, to turn it off.
Grid: choose 9 (3x3), 25 (5x5) or 81 (9x9) points from the drop-down for the selected mode; more points give more precise data and better first-layer contact.
Follow levelling with Z Offset Calibration, then XY Offset Calibration.

entries.title: Installing or swapping the Artisan Dual Extrusion Module (quick-swap bracket)
entries.summary: The Dual Extrusion Module slides into the quick-swap toolhead bracket and is locked by its cam handle. Shut the machine down first, or use Settings > Module Assistant > Replace Module to swap without turning the power off. A toolhead that is not fully seated and locked can wobble, causing layer shifts or layer lines.
steps: Power off (or start Module Assistant > Replace Module); never plug cables with power on.
Loosen the bracket handle, slide the toolhead fully in, and tighten the handle all the way.
Plug the toolhead cable into the toolhead.

Adjustable quick-swap plate: it should slide in smoothly, give slight friction as the cam handle tightens, and not shift sideways once locked; if not, adjust the plate height (M4x12 screws, H2.0 and H2.5 keys).
Use the 3D printing platform with this toolhead; a mismatch raises 515-9 and risks damage.

sources.title: Install the quick swap toolhead plate (adjustable version)

entries.title: Visible layer lines or ridges on Artisan prints
entries.summary: Pronounced lines or ridges on walls point to a toolhead that wobbles on the X module, loose Dual Extruder guide rails, uneven extrusion (poor or damp filament, a partial clog, extruder gear trouble) or an unstable nozzle temperature or cooling fan.
causes: Dual Extruder loose on the X linear module or quick-release not locked
Loose Dual Extruder guide rails
Poor-quality, inconsistent-diameter or damp filament
Partly clogged nozzle or hot end
Loose extruder set screw, worn or dirty gears, or wrong feed tube to gear gap
Fluctuating nozzle temperature
Print cooling fan not running
steps: Shake the Dual Extruder; make sure the quick-release locks it and the guide rails do not move (contact Support if they are loose).
Try another spool to rule out filament quality or moisture.
Clear the nozzle or swap in another hot end.
Check the extruder set screw, the gears for wear or residue, and the metal feed tube to gear gap.
Watch the nozzle temperature on screen during printing for swings.
Open the Dual Extruder front door and confirm the cooling fan spins and moves air.

entries.title: Layer shifting on Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: Layers stepping sideways come from speed or acceleration beyond what Artisan handles, or from mechanics: a wobbling Dual Extruder or loose guide rails (X shifts), an uneven support platform or loose heated bed (Y shifts), debris on steel strips, or slack or damaged timing belts. Keep speeds at or under 200 mm/s and acceleration at the 2000 mm/s^2 default.
symptoms: Upper layers offset from lower ones in X or Y
Step-like jog in the part's walls
causes: Print speed above about 200 mm/s
Acceleration raised above the 2000 mm/s^2 default
Dual Extruder loose on the X module, quick-release not locked, or loose guide rails
Uneven support platform or heated bed not held firmly
Debris on the steel strips or dry, rough sliders
Loose or damaged timing belts
steps: Lower print speeds to 200 mm/s or less.
Confirm acceleration is still 2000 mm/s^2: connect over serial with Pronterface or LightBurn and send M503 to read the firmware values.
X shifts: shake the Dual Extruder, check the quick-release locks it firmly and that its guide rails are tight.
Y shifts: look for a gap or rocking between support platform and printing platform (fit silicone bed shims) and check the heated bed is secure.
Clean debris off the steel strips; if a slider feels rough with power off, apply silicone lubricant (e.g. WD-40 Specialist or B'laster silicone) and push it back and forth a few times.
Check timing belt tension and look for worn or torn belts.
Send photos or video to Support if shifting continues.

settings.advice: Keep at or below Artisan's 2000 mm/s^2 default; lower it if shifts appear on fast moves.
Keep within Artisan's 200 mm/s limit; reduce if layers shift.
Infill is usually the fastest feature; keep at or below 200 mm/s on Artisan.
Do not exceed 200 mm/s on Artisan to avoid skipped steps.

sources.title: Installing the silicone bed shim for Artisan

entries.title: Artisan linear module cannot return home: limit switch test
entries.summary: If an axis will not travel to its home end (Z up, X left, Y front), suspect the limit switch wiring, the limit switch board, the module's adapter board or the controller mainboard. The touchscreen shows each switch's state, so you can see which module reads as triggered, and swapping sockets separates a module fault from a mainboard fault.
steps: Power off, slide every module to mid-travel by hand, power on and open Settings > Device Maintenance > Machine Information.
Every limit switch should read OFF; one showing ON marks the suspect module.

Socket swap (Z1 example): power off, plug the Z1 module into the Z2 socket and Z2 into Z1, power on. Per Snapmaker, Z1 OFF and Z2 ON means the mainboard is damaged; Z1 ON and Z2 OFF means keep checking the Z1 module.
Remove that module and its four top cover screws; check the switch wiring, the switch and adapter board pins, and any debris blocking the switch.
Test continuity of the switch wiring and the module cable with a multimeter in buzzer mode (a beep means intact).
Remove the steel strip screws (sharp edges) and the switch's fixing screw, short its two pins with tweezers and watch the reported state; if it changes, the limit switch board is faulty.
Report your steps and results to Support if unresolved.

entries.title: Artisan linear module hits its limit switch noisily: replacing the switch
entries.summary: A knock or noise when a slider reaches the end of its travel points to a faulty or damaged limit switch. Get a replacement from Snapmaker and swap it at the end of the module that has no cable.
steps: Power off and obtain the replacement limit switch from Snapmaker.
At the end without the cable, remove the two steel strip screws (H2.5) and the iron clamp piece, then the four end cap screws (H3.0) and the end cap, minding the sharp strip.
Unplug the switch cable, remove the switch's two screws (H2.5), fit the new switch and plug it in.
Refit the screws, steel strip and end cap.
Jog the module to the end from the screen; if the noise remains, contact Snapmaker again.

sources.title: Artisan's Linear Module hits the limit switch and generates noise when moving
Artisan linear module limit switch replacement guide

entries.title: Artisan linear module squeaks or grinds when moving
entries.summary: Noise from a moving linear module, powered or pushed by hand, is usually friction between the steel strip and the EVA foam strip inside the slider; otherwise a part inside the module has come loose. Clean and lubricate the strip, or leave the foam strip out, since it only keeps dust off and 3D printing makes little dust.
steps: Power off; have a cloth, tweezers, a screwdriver and silicone lubricant or dashboard wax (e.g. WD-40 or B'laster silicone) ready.
Prise the slider off with tweezers, remove the EVA foam strip and refit the slider; push it by hand to see whether the noise is gone (mind the sharp strip).
If it is quiet: clean the foam strip, put it back, apply a little silicone lubricant or wax to the steel strip and slide it 3-5 times.
If still noisy: remove the four bolts on both sides (H2.0), lift off the steel strip, push the slider and look for a worn belt or loose timing pulley.
Film what you find and open a Support ticket.

sources.title: The linear module produces an unusual sound when moving

entries.title: Replacing an Artisan XY linear module cable
entries.summary: The XY linear module cable plugs into a PCB under the end cap on the cable side of the module. Swapping it needs H2.5 and H3.0 drivers; power off first and watch the sharp steel strip.
steps: On the cable end, remove the two steel strip screws with the H2.5 driver.
Remove the four end cap screws with the H3.0 driver and lift the end cap.
Unplug the old cable from the PCB and plug in the new one.
Refit the end cap and steel strip.

sources.title: Artisan linear module-XY Cable replacement guide

entries.title: Loading and unloading filament on the Artisan Dual Extrusion Module
entries.summary: Artisan has touchscreen-assisted loading (recommended), Auto Loading (only in the first-use wizard and during runout recovery) and manual loading. Heat the nozzle to the filament's normal printing temperature for both loading and unloading.
steps: Tap Control > Filament, select the nozzle, enter the filament's printing temperature and tap Heat.
If filament is already inside, tap Unload to pull it out automatically, and store that spool sealed.
Hang the new spool, cut the bent tip off with the diagonal pliers, and push the filament into the tube until it meets resistance.
Tap Load; each tap feeds 90 mm, so repeat until plastic flows from the nozzle.
Brush leftover plastic off the nozzle with the wire brush.
Auto Loading: push the filament in until the extruder grabs it; the Controller beeps when it succeeds.
Manual fallback: heat the nozzle, open the toolhead front cover, press the extruder buckle down to open the dual-gear extruder, feed filament until it extrudes, then close buckle and cover.

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan 3D printing maintenance intervals
entries.summary: Snapmaker's routine for the Artisan 3D printer: scrape the plate after every print, remove glue after each use, and every two weeks clean the plate, both nozzles, the extruder gears, the module dust screens and the linear module steel strips. Lubricate the steel strips if the sliders feel rough.
facts: After every print: scrape filament residue off the build plate.
After each use of glue: wipe it off with a damp cloth.
Every 2 weeks: wipe grease and dust off the build plate.
Every 2 weeks: brush both nozzles clean while heated to 200 C.
Every 2 weeks: brush the extruder gears.
Every 2 weeks: clean the dust screens on both sides of the Dual Extrusion Module.
Every 2 weeks: clean the linear module steel strips; if a slider feels rough with power off, apply silicone lubricant to the strip and slide it back and forth.

sources.title: Remove the Filament Residues from the Build Plate
Remove the Grease and Dust from the Build Plate
Remove the Adhesive from the Build Plate
Clean the Dust Screen of the Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Artisan metal guide tube slipped: filament tangles at gear, hot end stuck
entries.summary: The metal guide tube below the extruder gear is slightly undersized and can slide out of place. That leaves a gap between gear and tube, so filament misses the hole, bunches around the gear and can also lock the hot end in. Filament jammed between the hot end and the tube likewise stops the hot end from coming out.
symptoms: Filament will not extrude
Filament bent and wrapped around the gear
Hot end cannot be pulled out
causes: Loose, displaced metal guide tube leaving a gap to the gear
Filament stuck between hot end and metal guide tube
steps: Open the front cover, press the buckle to open the gears and pick filament off the gear with flat tweezers.
Cut filament that is tight on the gear with pliers, or grip and pull it out of the guide tube.
If filament is trapped between hot end and tube, open the outer panel and snip it with diagonal pliers.
Hold the bottom of a displaced tube with flat tweezers and push it up to clear the hot end, then remove the hot end.
Coat the outside of the tube evenly with AB (two-part) glue, push it back to its original position and leave it 24 hours to set.

sources.title: The metal guide tube at the gear is loose and displaced
Remove the hot end clogged by the filament

entries.title: Artisan nozzle scrapes or presses into the bed during levelling calibration
entries.summary: If the nozzle digs into the glass platform while levelling, watch a homing cycle first. If Z does not rise to the top, the toolhead does not reach the far left, or the platform does not come to the front, a linear module or controller port is at fault. If homing completes normally, suspect the photoelectric switch inside the Dual Extruder.
symptoms: Nozzle scrapes the glass platform during calibration
Nozzle keeps pushing down into the bed while probing
causes: Z-axis limit switch already triggered so Z never homes (module or controller port fault)
Faulty photoelectric switch, damaged cable or loose terminal inside the Dual Extruder
steps: Tap home and check that Z rises fully, the toolhead goes to the far left on X, and the platform moves to the front on Y.
If any of those fail, follow the linear module homing and limit switch test.
If homing is normal, power off and remove the toolhead.
Open it: four back screws (H2.0), detach the hot ends, four top screws (H1.5), then remove front cover and shell.
Inspect the photoelectric switch cable and terminal; push a loose plug firmly home.
If the cable is damaged or nothing is found, photograph it and contact Snapmaker Support.

sources.title: Nozzle scraping bed during leveling calibration

entries.title: Artisan nozzle scrapes the bed during printing
entries.summary: Scrape marks during a print usually mean the nozzle runs too low (levelling or Z offset skipped or wrong, or Sensor Calibration used when not needed), the Dual Extruder bracket or guide rail is loose, the right nozzle failed to lift, or a Z limit switch triggers falsely so the X axis never reaches its top position.
symptoms: Nozzle drags on the heated bed while printing
Visible nozzle tracks on the build plate
causes: Levelling and Z offset not done or done wrongly
Sensor Calibration run when it was not needed
Loose Dual Extruder bracket or guide rail
Right nozzle not lifting
False Z-axis limit switch trigger, e.g. light reflected by the steel strip
steps: Redo Heated Bed Leveling and Z Offset Calibration, then test print.
If you ran Sensor Calibration, redo Z offset in Manual Mode; the sensor is factory-tuned and normally needs no recalibration.
Wiggle the Dual Extruder; if bracket or guide rail moves, tighten their screws, and contact Support with a video if it still moves.
Home the machine and watch the right nozzle lift; with it enabled both blue LEDs inside the Dual Extruder should be lit, and lifting the right nozzle by hand should toggle the right LED.
Check the Z limit switch states under Settings > Device Maintenance > Machine Information.
For false Z triggers, remove the two end-cap screws holding each Z steel strip and stick black tape on the strip above the photoelectric switch, on both Z modules.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide for nozzle scrapes on the bed during printing

entries.title: Artisan PEI steel sheet bulges when the bed is hot
entries.summary: With the centre zone above about 80 C the PEI steel sheet can bulge. Causes: a wrinkled or bumpy soft magnetic sticker or a misaligned sheet, use outside Snapmaker's PEI guidance, or a big gap between the inner zone (up to 110 C) and an unheated or 80 C-capped outer zone. Firmware 2.8.1 now heats the outer zone to 80 C whenever the centre exceeds 80 C.
causes: Soft magnetic sticker not flat (wrinkles or bumps) or sheet not aligned with its holders
Bed temperatures or usage outside Snapmaker's PEI sheet recommendations
Bed Heating Area set to Inner Zone, leaving the outer zone at room temperature while the centre runs hot
steps: Remove the PEI sheet and inspect the magnetic sticker; replace it if it is not smooth and flat.
Refit the sheet aligned with its holders.
Keep bed temperatures within Snapmaker's PEI sheet guidance and avoid Inner Zone heating for hot prints.
Update to firmware 2.8.1 (or Snapmaker's temporary firmware): both zones heat together below 80 C, and above 80 C the outer zone is held at 80 C.
Then redo Heated Bed Leveling, Z Offset Calibration and XY Offset Calibration in that order.

settings.advice: Keep PEI bed temperatures within Snapmaker's guidance; above 80 C in the centre zone the sheet can bulge.

sources.title: Artisan PEI steel sheet bulging when heated
Installing the PEI sheet for Artisan

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan pre-print checklist: environment, cables and assembly
entries.summary: Before the first print, or after re-assembly, check the room, the bench, every cable and the mechanical assembly. A cold room slows heating and makes parts warp; swapped linear module cables cause malfunctions or damage. Also make sure the plate and nozzle tips are clean, the filament is dry and firmware and slicer are up to date.
steps: Room: keep it at 0-40 C and 30-70% relative humidity; warm it or close the Enclosure when cold, cool it when hot, and avoid very dry air with static.
Bench: at least 1035 x 1690 mm, level, clean, dry, rated above 65 kg, in a spot where fumes can be ventilated.
Integrated Controller ports: 2 Y-axis, 2 Z-axis, 1 X-axis, 1 toolhead, 1 heated bed and 1 Enclosure cable, each matched by label to its port; power off before replugging.
Enclosure converter: Enclosure cable, hall switch cord, LED strip cord and exhaust fan cord.
Shake the X, Y and Z modules and tighten screws on anything that moves (the Y axes most often).
Push the support platform back and forth to confirm it clears the Z axes, then fully tighten its cam handle.
Check the 3D printing platform cannot be lifted off the support platform, matches the Dual Extrusion Module, and that the toolhead bracket cam handle is fully locked.
Clean the build plate and nozzle tips, use dry filament, and check Settings > Firmware Update for new firmware.

entries.title: PVA support filament settings for Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: PVA is a water-soluble support for PLA, TPU, PVB and nylon. It soaks up water fast: damp PVA turns soft and bendy like TPU, pops or bubbles while printing, clogs, strings and sticks poorly. Dry it before use and keep it in a dry box. Snapmaker's Artisan values: 215-225 C nozzle, 68 C bed, up to 60 mm/s, 0.8 mm retraction at 20 mm/s, fan on.

settings.advice: 215-225 C for dry Snapmaker PVA; 210-220 C for soft, third-party or slightly damp PVA.
68 C on Artisan (set the bed temperature key for the plate type you use).
0.8 mm for dry Snapmaker PVA; 0 mm for soft or damp PVA.
20 mm/s for PVA.
Keep PVA supports at or below 60 mm/s, or 40 mm/s for soft or third-party PVA.
Keep within the same 60/40 mm/s PVA limits.

facts: Snapmaker PVA on Artisan: nozzle 215-225 C, bed 68 C, speed up to 60 mm/s, retraction 0.8 mm at 20 mm/s, cooling fan on.
Third-party, soft or partly damp PVA: nozzle 210-220 C, bed 68 C, speed up to 40 mm/s, retraction 0 mm, cooling fan on.
Damp test: if the PVA bends like TPU or makes bubbling sounds while printing, dry it before continuing.
If the first layer will not stick, use PVA solid glue or an adhesive spray made for 3D printing.

sources.title: PVA/TPU/Breakaway Support for PLA Printing Guide

entries.title: Removing prints from the Artisan glass plate or PEI sheet
entries.summary: Parts release more easily as they cool and shrink, so let the plate reach room temperature first. On PEI, never pry a part off above 40 C or the coating can be damaged. The PEI steel sheet can be removed and flexed; stubborn parts can be levered with the palette knife at a shallow angle, or loosened by cooling the underside of the plate.
steps: Let bed and part cool to room temperature (under 40 C for PEI surfaces).
PEI sheet platform: lift the sheet off and flex it slightly to pop the part free.
Glass plate: take it off the bed, slide the palette knife under the part at under 30 degrees and lever gently, blade pointing away from you.
Still stuck: once fully cool, run cold water over the back of the plate only; never over the part and never on a warm plate, which may crack.
If water-soluble glue was used on glass, soak the contact area in warm water until the glue lets go.

entries.title: Fixing a rocking Artisan 3D printing platform with silicone bed shims
entries.summary: A visible gap between the support platform and the 3D printing platform, or corners that rock when you press the two together, means the platform is uneven and can cause Y-axis layer shifts. Snapmaker supplies two adhesive silicone bed shims to take up the gap.
steps: Turn the machine off and remove the 3D printing platform.
Peel the backing off both silicone shims.
Stick both to the underside of the 3D printing platform, at the two positions Snapmaker marks; they go on the printing platform, never the support platform.
Refit the platform and check that it no longer rocks.

sources.title: Installing the silicone bed shim for Artisan

entries.title: Stringing and oozing on Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: Fine strands between parts usually come from damp filament, a nozzle that is too hot, too little retraction, slow travel moves, or a worn or partly clogged nozzle. Dry or replace the filament first, then tune temperature, retraction and travel speed (Artisan travel up to 200 mm/s).
causes: Filament has absorbed moisture
Printing temperature too high
Retraction too short or too slow
Travel speed too low
Clogged or worn nozzle
steps: Dry the spool in a dry box or try a well-sealed fresh one.
Lower nozzle temperature in small steps while keeping layer bonding acceptable.
Increase retraction distance and speed.
Raise travel speed, staying at or below 200 mm/s on Artisan to avoid skipped steps.
Clean, unclog or replace a worn nozzle or hot end.

settings.advice: Lower in small steps until strings fade while layers still bond.
Increase gradually so more filament is pulled back before travel.
Increase so the filament retracts faster before travel moves.
Raise to cut ooze time, but keep at or below 200 mm/s on Artisan.

entries.title: Removing supports and dissolving PVA supports (Artisan)
entries.summary: Supports can be removed with the supplied diagonal pliers (outer supports), needle-nose pliers (deep supports) or a precision knife (tangled areas; wear gloves). With the dual extruder you can print supports in water-soluble PVA and dissolve them instead, which can take hours.
steps: Optionally snap off PVA sections that come away easily.
Soak the part in warm water until the PVA is gone; hotter water and fresh water speed it up.
Rinse thoroughly in clean water and let the part air dry.
Dispose of PVA-laden water as the PVA maker or local authority directs; it needs special treatment.

settings.advice: Set to the extruder loaded with PVA (or breakaway material) so supports print from the second nozzle.
Use PVA at least for the interface so contact surfaces dissolve cleanly.
Enable in the PVA filament profile so Orca treats it as a soluble support material.

entries.title: Artisan beeps at power-on or shows Chinese error pop-ups
entries.summary: Some Artisan touchscreen messages only appear in Chinese. Beeping just after power-on with a Chinese error, or an emergency stop pop-up with a red cross, means the emergency stop button is pressed. A 'Bluetooth repeatedly stops' pop-up means the screen's storage is nearly full, and an 'Allow USB debugging?' prompt comes from a device plugged into the USB port.
steps: Emergency stop: twist the button clockwise to release it, then tap continue; the machine reboots.
Bluetooth stops: delete local G-code files until about 300 MB is free (see Settings > About Machine).
USB debugging prompt: tap Cancel unless you deliberately connected a debugging device.

sources.title: The controller beeps after being powered on
How to solve Artisan touchscreen displaying chinese error messages issue

entries.title: TPU settings for the Artisan Dual Extrusion Module
entries.summary: The Artisan dual extruder handles TPU of 90A or harder (TPU90A, TPU95A, TPU95-HF). Print it on the smooth glass side: on PEI or coated surfaces TPU can bond so well that the part cannot be removed. If the filament winds around the gear, turn retraction off.

settings.advice: 210-230 C for TPU on Artisan.
50 C, printing on the smooth glass side rather than PEI.
0.5 mm; set to 0 if the TPU coils around the extruder gear.
20 mm/s for TPU.
Cap it so no feature exceeds Snapmaker's limit for the grade: 30 mm/s (90A), 60 mm/s (95A) or 80 mm/s (95-HF).

facts: All grades: nozzle 210-230 C, bed 50 C, smooth glass surface, retraction 0.5 mm at 20 mm/s, cooling fan on.
TPU90A: up to 30 mm/s.
TPU95A: up to 60 mm/s.
TPU95-HF (high flow): up to 80 mm/s.
Grades softer than 90A (e.g. 83A, 85A) are below the recommended hardness for the dual extruder.
If TPU winds around the extruder gear, disable retraction.

sources.title: PVA/TPU/Breakaway Support for PLA Printing Guide

entries.title: Warping on Snapmaker Artisan prints
entries.summary: Warping is the base of a part curling off the plate. On Artisan the usual causes are a bed temperature that is too low, part cooling starting too early (critical for ABS/ASA), a cold room, or weak first-layer adhesion from a dirty plate. Raise the bed temperature, keep the Enclosure shut with fans off for ABS/ASA, clean the plate, and add a brim, raft or glue.
symptoms: Corners or edges lift and curl up
Uneven or rocking base on the finished part
causes: Bed temperature too low for the filament
Part cooling fan running too early, especially with ABS and ASA
Low ambient temperature
Grease, dust or glue residue weakening first-layer adhesion
High-shrinkage filament
steps: Use the filament's recommended bed temperature; if warping continues, go 5-10 C above it.
For ABS and ASA keep the part cooling fan and the Enclosure fan off and print with the Enclosure door closed.
Raise the room temperature or use the Enclosure if the room is cold.
Wipe the plate with a cloth dampened with ethyl alcohol before printing.
Re-level the bed if the first layer looks uneven.
Add a brim or raft for parts that still curl later in the print.
Spread a thin even layer of water-soluble liquid glue or printing tape; wipe glue off afterwards with a damp cloth.

settings.advice: Raise 5-10 C above the filament's recommended bed temperature if corners still lift (use the temperature key for the plate type in use).
Keep at or slightly above the other-layer bed temperature to anchor the first layer.
Increase so the part fan stays off for the first layers.
For ABS and ASA keep part cooling off or very low; Snapmaker advises no cooling fan for these.
If the profile drives the Enclosure exhaust fan, keep it at 0 for ABS/ASA so the chamber stays warm.
Add an outer brim on parts with sharp corners or small footprints.
Widen if edges still curl later in the print.
Set above 0 for very warp-prone parts; costs time and filament and is harder to remove.

entries.title: Artisan cannot connect over Wi-Fi to Luban or Snapmaker Orca
entries.summary: Connection failures usually mean the machine is not really on Wi-Fi, another program already holds the connection, or the signal is weak. Confirm Wi-Fi on the touchscreen, restart the computer, and connect by IP address if discovery fails. With firmware 2.8.0+ Snapmaker Orca connects directly at IP:8080; do not send from Luban and Orca at the same time.
steps: Check the Wi-Fi status on the machine screen and restart the computer.
Retry the connection from Luban.
If it still fails, read the machine's IP address on its screen, type it into Luban and click Connect.
For Snapmaker Orca, use the device IP plus :8080 (e.g. 192.168.0.1:8080).
Close other apps connected to the machine; uploading from Luban and Orca simultaneously makes the job fail.

entries.title: Artisan X linear module will not move: port swap test
entries.summary: If the toolhead will not move in X during printing or when jogged, either the X linear module or the controller's X port is damaged. Swapping the X cable with one Y cable shows which.
steps: Power off and label the left Y module as Y1.
Unplug the X and Y1 cables at the Controller; plug Y1 into the X port and X into the Y1 port.
Power on, skip the error messages, and jog X on the control screen: if the heated bed now moves front-to-back the X port is fine, otherwise the port is faulty.
Jog Y: if the X module now moves left-right the module is fine, otherwise the X module is faulty.
Restore the cables and send the results to Support.

sources.title: The X-Linear Module of Artisan can't move

entries.title: XY Offset Calibration for the Artisan dual nozzles
entries.summary: XY offset is the horizontal distance between the left and right nozzles. The nozzles are not moved physically: the machine prints line patterns, you pick the pair that lines up best, and it then corrects toolhead moves on the fly so two colours or materials register. Run it on a clean glass plate after levelling and Z offset.
steps: Clean the glass build plate.
Tap Calibration > XY Offset Calibration > Start to print the calibration models.
Remove the print and tap Next to confirm the plate is clear.
On the X model pick the best-aligned pair of lines, tap Next, then Save.
Do the same on the Y model.
Optionally tap Start Checking to print the Check Model and verify the result.

entries.title: Z Offset Calibration and Sensor Calibration on Snapmaker Artisan
entries.summary: Z offset is the nozzle-to-plate gap; levelling keeps it even, Z Offset Calibration sets its value for both nozzles. In Auto Mode each nozzle touches the glass plate; Manual Mode lets you jog each one. Sensor Calibration re-tunes the smart sensor's travel if Auto results are wrong. It is set at the factory, so use it only when needed and redo Z offset afterwards.
steps: Clean both nozzle tips.
Tap Calibration > Z Offset Calibration, open Mode Selection (top-right), choose Auto Mode and tap Start.
If the first layer is consistently too high or too low, use Manual Mode and set each nozzle by following the prompts.
If Auto Mode keeps giving wrong values, run Sensor Calibration: the machine first auto-calibrates both nozzles, then asks you to fine-tune them by hand.
In Sensor Calibration lower the nozzle only until it lightly touches the calibration card, which should still pull out easily.
Always repeat Z Offset Calibration after Sensor Calibration.
Z offset can also be nudged on the screen during a print when the first layer is too high.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide for nozzle scrapes on the bed during printing

entries.title: Calibrating adaptive pressure advance (PA vs flow and acceleration)
entries.summary: Run PA pattern tests over a grid of print speeds (as a stand-in for flow) and accelerations, note the best PA, flow and acceleration of each, and enter the triplets into the adaptive PA model. A good starting grid for CoreXY printers is accelerations 1k, 2k, 4k and speeds 50, 100, 150, 200 mm/s (12 tests). Do not calibrate above the acceleration your input shaper recommends, or shaper smoothing will look like PA errors.
steps: Calibrate normal PA and flow ratio first
Choose accelerations up to the input shaper's recommended max (e.g. 1k, 2k, 4k)
Choose speeds such as 50, 100, 150, 200 mm/s; avoid over about 200-250 mm/s in the pattern
Use a small PA step (about 0.001) and an end value that shows gaps at the slowest test
Print all tests; read flow from the label or the Flow preview
Record PA, flow, acceleration for each test and paste one triplet per line
Save the filament profile and enable adaptive PA

settings.advice: Paste the measured PA,flow,acceleration triplets.
Enable after entering the model.

facts: Optimal PA usually falls as flow and acceleration rise; if not, check the extruder
If no difference is visible between values at low flow, use the values from higher flows
If results barely vary, adaptive PA brings little benefit

entries.title: Bed leveling and bed mesh concepts
entries.summary: A bed mesh probes the bed at a grid of points and adjusts Z during printing so the first layer has even squish despite a warped or tilted surface. It only approximates the bed shape and cannot fix mechanical problems or an inaccurate probe, and it depends on a correctly calibrated Z offset. Adaptive meshes probe only where objects are, which is faster but best when the full mesh varies by no more than about one layer height.
steps: Calibrate the probe Z offset (or Z endstop) first
Run a full mesh and check the range; large ranges point to mechanical issues worth fixing first
Use adaptive meshing via the start G-code for faster probing of the print area
Fine-tune the first layer with live Z adjustment

settings.advice: Smaller spacing for warped beds.
Add margin so brims and skirts are inside the meshed area.

entries.title: Cornering calibration (jerk / junction deviation / square corner velocity)
entries.summary: The cornering test raises the cornering value with height to find the maximum before corners lose sharpness. It adapts to firmware: Klipper square corner velocity, Marlin 2 junction deviation (or classic jerk), RepRap instantaneous speed change. Print with high acceleration and speed and a glossy opaque filament. Most printers do not need it, since firmware already limits cornering and higher values may not speed up real prints.
steps: Set acceleration and speed high enough to show ringing (e.g. 2000 mm/s2, 100 mm/s)
Run a wide-range cornering test first
Measure the height where corners start to soften and read the value there
Print a narrower second test up to that point (Ringing Tower model recommended)
Save the value in Printer settings > Motion ability > Jerk limitation, or in firmware
Restore normal acceleration and jerk afterwards

settings.advice: Store the calibrated JD for Marlin 2; 0 means classic jerk.
Keep within the calibrated maximum.

facts: If the whole tower looks the same, you probably hit the firmware limit
Klipper example: SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT SQUARE_CORNER_VELOCITY=5.0
Marlin example: M205 J0.012 then M500
RepRapFirmware M566 uses mm/min (multiply mm/s by 60)

entries.title: Tuning first layer squish (Z offset) with test patches
entries.summary: After rough leveling and Z offset, fine-tune squish by printing flat square patches spread over the bed and adjusting Z live. Good squish leaves no gaps between lines on top or bottom, few ridges or hairs on top, and lines still visible underneath. Too much squish gives ridges, lumps and faded bottom lines; too little shows gaps you can see through. If unsure, lean slightly toward more squish. A 0.25 mm first layer with wide lines is more forgiving.
symptoms: Gaps you can see through between first-layer lines (nozzle too high)
Ridges, hairs or lumps on top and invisible lines underneath (nozzle too low)
Lines not sticking or lifting
steps: Set first layer height to about 0.25 mm and first-layer line width to about 120%
Place several single-layer square patches around the bed
Print and adjust Z live (baby stepping) until lines merge without ridges
On textured plates, squish slightly more so plastic fills the texture
Save the final Z offset in the printer

settings.advice: 0.25 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle is forgiving.
About 120% helps lines merge and stick.
Slicer-side Z offset; prefer adjusting Z offset in the printer firmware.

sources.title: Ellis' Print Tuning Guide - First Layer Squish
Prusa Knowledge Base - PLA (textured sheet live-Z advice)

entries.title: Flow ratio calibration: 2-pass (Pass 1 and Pass 2) method
entries.summary: The legacy 2-pass test uses percentage modifiers. Pass 1 prints nine blocks; pick the smoothest top and compute new = old x (100 + modifier) / 100. Pass 2 prints ten finer blocks from -9 to 0 using the updated value; apply the same formula again. Save the filament profile after each pass so the second pass starts from the new value.
steps: Select printer, filament and process
Calibration > Flow rate > Pass 1; print the nine blocks
Pick the smoothest top: e.g. old 0.98 with +5 gives 0.98 x 1.05 = 1.029
Save the filament profile
Run Pass 2 and pick again: e.g. 1.029 with -6 gives 1.029 x 0.94 = 0.967
Save the filament profile and start a new project

settings.advice: Apply old x (100 + modifier) / 100 after each pass.

sources.title: Ellis' Print Tuning Guide - Extrusion Multiplier

entries.title: Flow ratio calibration: YOLO (Archimedean chords) method
entries.summary: The YOLO flow test prints blocks with flow modifiers around the filament's current flow ratio in a single pass. Pick the block with the smoothest top, no gaps between lines and minimal ridge where the inner spiral meets the outer arcs. New flow ratio = old flow ratio + modifier (e.g. 0.98 + 0.01 = 0.99). Select the correct filament first, because the test starts from its current value.
steps: Select printer and the exact filament profile to calibrate
Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended) for 0.01 steps, or perfectionist for 0.005 steps
Print the blocks and inspect top surfaces in good light; feel them by hand
Choose the smoothest block just before gaps appear
Add its modifier to the old flow ratio and save the filament profile

settings.advice: Set to old value plus the chosen block's modifier.

facts: Recommended range is -0.05 to +0.05; perfectionist -0.04 to +0.035
The inner spiral prints last so excess material shows up along the contact line
Bambu Lab printers: do not tick the printer's own flow calibration option for this test

entries.title: Input shaping concepts: ringing, shaper types and max acceleration
entries.summary: Ringing (ghosting, echoing) is a faint repeat of edges on walls caused by frame vibration after sharp direction changes. Input shaping shapes motion commands so they cancel the printer's resonance. Fix mechanical causes first (loose belts, wobbly frame, heavy toolhead). MZV is a good default; EI tolerates frequency changes better (bed slingers, deltas) but smooths more. Very high acceleration with shaping causes corner rounding, which caps useful acceleration.
causes: Loose or springy belts
Insufficiently rigid frame or loose parts
Heavy moving mass
Accelerations above what the shaper handles
facts: Klipper: ringing frequency = speed x number of oscillations / distance, e.g. 100 x 6 / 12.14 = 49.4 Hz
Klipper recommends keeping square corner velocity at 5 and raising acceleration instead
Disable pressure advance while measuring ringing
Bed-slinger resonance can drop as the printed part adds mass to the bed, favoring EI
Do not calibrate adaptive PA above the shaper's recommended max acceleration

entries.title: Input shaping frequency and damping test in OrcaSlicer
entries.summary: If the printer has no accelerometer auto-calibration, Orca's manual test prints a ringing tower with the shaper frequency varying by height. Measure the X and Y heights where ringing is lowest and read the frequency, then run the damping test at that frequency. Save type, frequencies and damping in firmware and in Motion ability. Use high acceleration and speed and a glossy opaque filament; restore normal settings after.
steps: Use glossy opaque filament with max volumetric speed of at least 10 mm3/s
Run the frequency test (default range 15-110 Hz) with the shaper type your firmware supports
Measure the X and Y heights with the least ringing and read the frequencies
