symptoms: Visible gap between the two platforms
Bed moves when its corners are pressed
Inconsistent leveling and first layers
steps: Press the printing platform toward the support platform at the left and right corners and look for play or gaps.
Stick a shim or two (each 0.5 to 0.8 mm) at the marked location on the support platform, or place the kit's two silicone bed shims under the 3D printing platform.
Redo bed leveling and Z Offset calibration.

sources.title: Replacement kit instructions (for the Dual Extrusion Module and Artisan)

entries.title: ASA recommended print settings (warm enclosure needed)
entries.summary: Snapmaker's ASA reference: nozzle 240-260 C, bed 75-95 C, fan off, and a warm surrounding of 50-70 C, so print it enclosed. Retraction is slightly longer than for most materials at 1-3 mm. Use the PEI-coated side and dry at 80 C for 8 hours.

settings.advice: Use 75-95 C within your bed's limit (80 C on A350-size Snapmaker 2.0).
Keep part cooling off or minimal.
Use 1-3 mm.

facts: Nozzle 240-260 C; bed 75-95 C; speed 30-50 mm/s.
Retraction 1-3 mm at 20-40 mm/s; part-cooling fan off.
Ambient during printing 50-70 C.
Standby 160 C; drying 80 C for 8 h; plate: PEI-coated side.

entries.title: Breakaway PLA (support material) recommended print settings
entries.summary: Breakaway PLA is a support material that snaps off PLA and TPU parts. Snapmaker suggests a hotter nozzle than normal PLA (220-230 C), slow printing at 20-40 mm/s, the fan on, and the PEI-coated plate side. Dry at 55 C for 6 hours.

settings.advice: Assign the Breakaway PLA extruder to the support interface so supports peel cleanly off PLA or TPU parts.
Keep around 20-40 mm/s when supports are printed in Breakaway PLA.
About 120 C while the Breakaway PLA nozzle is parked.

facts: Nozzle 220-230 C; bed 25-65 C; speed 20-40 mm/s.
Retraction 0-2 mm at 20-50 mm/s; part-cooling fan on.
Standby temperature 120 C; drying 55 C for 6 h.
Pairs with PLA and TPU. Plate: PEI-coated side.

entries.title: Cleaning residue off the build plate and using glue (Snapmaker 2.0 / Artisan)
entries.summary: Leftover filament leaves the plate uneven and spoils the next first layer. Scrape with the palette knife held under 30 degrees to the plate. If residue resists, warm the bed and try again: about 50 C via Control > Heated Bed per the adhesion guide, or 70 C per the Snapmaker 2.0 manual. Water-soluble liquid glue or printing tape helps materials that need it and washes off with water.
steps: Keep the palette knife at an angle of less than 30 degrees to the glass plate and scrape gently so the surface is not damaged.
For stubborn residue, heat the bed (Control > Heated Bed on the Touchscreen, about 50 C; the 2.0 manual suggests 70 C / 158 F) and scrape with the knife's sharp edge.
Wear gloves and never touch the heated bed with bare hands.
For materials that need it, spread a thin even layer of water-soluble liquid glue or 3D printing tape over the print area.
After printing, wipe off remaining glue with a cloth dampened with water.
facts: Snapmaker recommends liquid glue rather than a glue stick.

entries.title: Dual Extrusion Module 'Abnormal Hot End' warning, no heating or reading above 300 C
entries.summary: Applies to the dual module on Snapmaker 2.0 and Artisan: the 'Abnormal Hot End' message, a hot end that will not heat, or a nozzle reading over 300 C. Typical causes are a hot end not seated properly, grease leaking onto the gold-finger contacts, loose or damaged heater/PT100 wires, deformed contacts on the hot end board, or other wiring faults.
causes: Hot end not installed correctly
Grease from the hot end on the gold fingers
Heating tube wires loose or damaged
Gold fingers on the hot end board bent or damaged
Other wiring faults (5P cable)
steps: Reseat the hot end fully and shake it gently; it should not feel loose.
Clean any grease off the gold fingers with an alcohol swab.
Swap hot ends to see whether the fault follows the hot end or stays with the module.
Stays with the module: check the hot end board's gold fingers for deformation and that the boards sit tight against the extruder bracket.
Follows the hot end: measure the heater (about 14 Ω) and PT100 (about 110 Ω), and tug the wires gently to find loose ones.
Check both ends of the 5P cable to the mainboard for seating and bent pins; with a hot end fitted, pins 2-3 should read about 110 Ω.
If unresolved, contact support with results and photos.
facts: Dual hot end reference resistances: heater about 14 Ω, PT100 about 110 Ω at room temperature.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide for Dual Extrusion Module abnormal hot end and heating failure

entries.title: Installing silicone buckle wedges on a loose Dual Extrusion Module extruder buckle
entries.summary: Wedges restore grip when the extruder buckle has loosened, which shows up as filament feeding only while you press the buckle in. Fit them only to a loose buckle; adding them to a normal one can crack it. If wedges are already installed, keep the new ones as spares.
symptoms: Filament extrudes only while the extruder buckle is pressed inward
steps: Remove the Dual Extrusion Module from the machine.
Peel the adhesive backing off a wedge and insert it into one buckle.
Use tweezers to set it in the middle position, neither too far forward nor too far back.
Repeat on the other buckle.

sources.title: Installing the silicone buckle wedge for the Dual Extrusion Module
Filament is not extruded (Dual Extrusion Module)

entries.title: Filament bent or tangled in the Dual Extrusion Module extruder gears (TPU feeding)
entries.summary: Bent or tangled filament in the gears happens when feeding resistance rises, from a badly placed spool or a sharply bent filament tube, and flexible TPU is the most affected. A metal guide tube under the gear that has slipped down and left a gap also lets TPU curl up.
symptoms: Filament visibly bent or wound around the extruder gears
No extrusion when printing or loading
causes: High feeding resistance from spool placement or a tightly bent filament tube
Metal guide tube below the gear loose and dropped, leaving a gap
steps: If filament is loaded, unload and pull it out.
Open the front cover and press the extruder buckle to open the dual-gear extruder.
Remove stuck filament with pliers, a hex key, screwdriver or tweezers; clear small shavings with an air gun, small brush or cotton swabs.
Press the buckle back into place and reload.
Reduce resistance: position the spool properly and avoid sharp bends in the filament tube.
If the guide tube under the gear has dropped, follow the loose guide tube repair.

settings.advice: Snapmaker's TPU recommendation is 0 mm retraction; retracting flexible filament adds feeding trouble.
Keep TPU slow, about 20-40 mm/s for TPU95 and 30-60 mm/s for TPU90, per Snapmaker's filament library.

entries.title: Dual Extrusion Module gear set screw loose (motor sounds normal, nothing feeds)
entries.summary: If filament extrudes when pushed by hand but not during printing, and the motor sounds normal on Load while nothing feeds, the extruder gear set screw has worked loose from assembly tolerance, shipping vibration or wear. Rotate the gear until the screw faces you, align the gears and tighten it with an H1.5 key.
symptoms: No extrusion during printing but manual pushing works
Normal motor sound on Load with no filament movement
causes: Set screw loosened by assembly deviation, transport vibration or long use
steps: Open the front cover and press the extruder buckle to open the extruder.
If the set screw side of the gear faces inward, insert a piece of filament, close the buckle and slowly push or pull the filament to turn the gears; reopen and repeat until the screw is visible.
Align the two gears: with filament inserted and the buckle closed, move the filament back and forth a little, then reopen.
Snug the set screw down using an H1.5 screwdriver (the supplied grey hex key works) and close the buckle.
Reload and confirm smooth extrusion.

sources.title: The set screw of the extruder gets loose (Dual Extrusion Module)

entries.title: Dual extrusion: compatible filament pairs, supports and standby temperatures
entries.summary: Snapmaker's filament library lists which materials bond well together for dual extrusion and a standby temperature for the parked nozzle. Soluble PVA suits PLA, PETG, TPU and nylon parts; Breakaway PLA suits PLA and TPU; HIPS pairs with ABS and PETG. Lowering the idle nozzle to its standby value limits oozing and degradation while the other nozzle prints.

settings.advice: Choose the second extruder's support material from the compatible list for the model material.
Put PVA or Breakaway PLA on the interface for easy removal and cleaner undersides.
Set each filament's idle temperature to its standby value so the parked nozzle oozes less.
Enable if you want the inactive nozzle dropped to its idle temperature between tool changes.

facts: PLA pairs with PLA, Breakaway PLA, PVA. PETG with PVA, PETG. ABS with ABS. ASA with ASA. HIPS with ABS, PETG.
TPU grades pair with Breakaway PLA, other TPUs, PVA. Nylons (CoPA, PA6-CF, PA12-CF, PA6-GF) pair with each other and PVA.
Standby: PLA 150 C, Breakaway PLA 120 C, ABS 160 C, ASA 160 C, HIPS 150 C, PETG 140 C, PVA 100 C, TPU 120 C, nylons 180 C.

entries.title: Clearing a clogged heat break or heat sink on the Dual Extrusion Module (heat creep)
entries.summary: If filament softens too early inside the heat break or heat sink, from an over-high nozzle temperature or poor hot end cooling, it jams and may not even unload. Cut and pull the filament, disassemble the hot end, and clear or replace the affected parts. The vented front cover in the replacement kit improves cooling and reduces these clogs.
symptoms: No extrusion during printing or manual loading
Filament cannot be unloaded
causes: Nozzle temperature too high
Hot end heat dissipation not working properly
steps: Open the front cover and press the extruder buckle to open the gears.
Cut the filament with diagonal pliers near the feed opening under the gears and pull it out of the module.
Disassemble the hot end and pick loose pieces out of the heat break and heat sink.
Swollen filament stuck in the heat break: break it up with a metal rod thinner than 2 mm, warming the spot with a lighter if needed.
Filament stuck in the heat sink: replace the Teflon tube.
Reassemble and refit the hot end, then push a length of PLA through to clean the path.

settings.advice: Keep inside the filament's recommended range; too much heat lets filament soften up in the heat break.

sources.title: Replacement kit instructions (for the Dual Extrusion Module and Artisan)

entries.title: Disassembling the Dual Extrusion Module hot end (nozzle, heat break, heat sink)
entries.summary: Stripping the quick-swap hot end lets you clear stubborn clogs in the nozzle, heat break or heat sink. It is delicate work and careless steps can damage parts. Unload the filament and remove the hot end first. Tools: H1.5 screwdriver, 4-inch and 8-inch adjustable wrenches.
steps: Hot side: pull off the insulating silicone casing and unplug the wires.
Back off the heat block's two set screws (H1.5) and slide out the heating rod and thermistor.
Loosen the heat sink set screw and pull the heat break out of the heat sink.
Grip the heat block with the 8-inch wrench and warm the nozzle with a lighter to melt filament inside, so the nozzle is not damaged when unscrewed.
Still holding the block, unscrew the nozzle counterclockwise with the 4-inch wrench, then the heat break the same way.
Cold side: loosen the rear set screw on the heat sink and unscrew the upper throat tube counterclockwise with the 4-inch wrench while holding with the 8-inch wrench.

sources.title: How to disassemble the hot end of Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Dual Extrusion Module not extruding: step-by-step diagnosis
entries.summary: Filament not coming out of a Dual Extrusion Module nozzle can have several causes, sometimes at once: clogs in the extruder, hot end or nozzle, a loose extruder buckle, a loose gear set screw, a loose extruder motor cord or a stalled motor. Work through them from easiest to hardest.
causes: Extruder, hot end or nozzle clogged
Extruder buckle loose so the gears cannot grip
Gear set screw loose
Extruder motor cord loose or damaged
Extruder stepper motor stalling
steps: Heat the affected nozzle to the filament's normal temperature, tap Load and push the filament down by hand.
Still nothing means a clog: open the front cover, press the buckle to open the dual-gear extruder and look for bent or tangled filament at the gears. None there: check the nozzle and hot end.
Clogs can coexist, so check all three locations before moving on.
If it extrudes when pushed, tap Load while pressing the extruder buckle inward; extrusion now means the buckle is loose.
Still no feed: listen to the motor during Load. Silence suggests a loose or damaged motor cord; clicking means a stall (contact support); a normal sound means a loose set screw.

sources.title: Filament is not extruded (Dual Extrusion Module)

entries.title: Clearing a clogged nozzle on the Dual Extrusion Module
entries.summary: Filament that carbonizes after long exposure to high temperature can block the nozzle. First try pushing the blockage up from the tip at temperature; if that fails, remove the nozzle and soften the residue with a lighter before cleaning it out.
symptoms: No filament from the nozzle when printing or loading
Extruded strand thinner than normal
causes: Carbonized filament built up after prolonged excessive temperature
steps: Heat the nozzle slightly above the stuck filament's usual print temperature, around 220 C for PLA.
Push a wire thinner than the nozzle bore up through the tip to clear the material.
Clean the outside with a wire brush or tweezers, wearing heat-resistant gloves.
If that fails: remove the nozzle from the hot end (H1.5 screwdriver, 4-inch and 8-inch adjustable wrenches).
Warm the nozzle with a lighter to soften the filament, clean it inside and out with a wire brush or tweezers, then reassemble.
Reload filament; if the strand is still thin, clean again.

settings.advice: Stay within the filament's recommended range; long periods at excessive temperature carbonize filament in the nozzle.

entries.title: Dual Extrusion Module replacement kit: buckle wedges, vented front cover, runout sensor, bed shims
entries.summary: Snapmaker's replacement kit targets known Dual Extrusion Module weak points: silicone buckle wedges add clamping force to a loosening extruder buckle; an upgraded front cover with vent holes improves hot end cooling and reduces clogs; a revised runout sensor with metal trigger pads wears less. Silicone bed shims for the Artisan are included too. The module parts fit only the Dual Extrusion Module.
facts: Buckle wedges: only for buckles that have actually loosened.
Front cover swap: remove the module; tools are tweezers and an H1.5 screwdriver (video guide).
Runout sensor swap: remove the module; H2.0 and H1.5 screwdrivers and tweezers.
Silicone bed shims (Artisan only) go under the 3D printing platform to fill gaps with the support platform.

sources.title: Replacement kit instructions (for the Dual Extrusion Module and Artisan)
Replacing the front cover of the Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Replacing and testing the Dual Extrusion Module filament runout sensor
entries.summary: The kit sensor adds metal trigger pads held by copper blocks. The job needs the shell opened and the lift motor removed. Before closing up, check that the right extruder lifts during homing and the control board's red light comes on when filament is inserted on each side.
steps: With the module removed (H2.0, H1.5, tweezers): detach any quick-swap plate, remove four back screws (H2.0), the hot ends and four top screws (H1.5), then the front cover and shell.
Unplug both motor cords, remove the two motor screws (H2.0) and lift out the motor without moving its lead screw nut.
Remove the two sensor screws (H1.5), peel the adhesive off the connectors and unplug the old sensor.
Fit the trigger pads and secure them with the copper blocks, opening facing down.

Identify left and right sensors, place the plastic spacer, set the sensor on it and fit the screw loosely; a test filament must still slide freely. Repeat on the other side, then replug the sensor cord.
Refit the motor; if the lead screw nut sits outside the iron buckle, push the right extruder in first. On the 2.0 module, keep the proximity sensor cord from being pinched.
Replug the motor cords. Power off, plug in the module, power on: the right extruder must lift while homing.
Insert filament on each side; the red light on the control board should come on. If not, recheck pads and copper blocks.
Refit shell, front cover, top and back screws, and hot ends.

sources.title: Replacing the filament runout sensor of the Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Enclosure door detection on Snapmaker 2.0 and Artisan (stops jobs when the door opens)
entries.summary: The Artisan and 2.0 enclosures sense the door with a hall switch. With Door Detection on, opening the door halts the running job or ends calibration at once. If you need to open the door often during a job, turn Door Detection off on the Touchscreen before starting.
steps: Make sure the hall switch cord is plugged into the enclosure converter and the enclosure cable is in the correct machine port.
Turn Door Detection on or off on the Touchscreen before starting a task.

sources.title: Turning on/off Door Detection of the Artisan & 2.0 Enclosure

entries.title: HIPS recommended print settings
entries.summary: Snapmaker's HIPS reference: nozzle 230-250 C, bed 60-80 C, fan off, 40-80 mm/s. It pairs with ABS and PETG, prints on the PEI-coated side and needs only a short dry at 60 C for 3 hours.

settings.advice: Keep part cooling off or minimal.

facts: Nozzle 230-250 C; bed 60-80 C; speed 40-80 mm/s.
Retraction 0.5-3 mm at 30-70 mm/s; part-cooling fan off.
Standby 150 C; drying 60 C for 3 h.
Pairs with ABS and PETG. Plate: PEI-coated side.

entries.title: Filament blob wrapped around the nozzle or hot end: removal and prevention
entries.summary: A blob builds up when the first layer comes loose (poor calibration or too fast) and filament piles onto the nozzle; poor-quality or damp filament adds to it. Heat the nozzle 30 C above the temperature the blob formed at, cut it away with pliers, and brush off what is left.
symptoms: Lump of filament enclosing the nozzle and heat block
causes: First layer not sticking (calibration or speed)
Low-quality filament with impurities or uneven diameter
Damp filament from poor storage
steps: Make sure the hot end is installed correctly, or the machine will not heat it.
Heat the nozzle to 30 C above the temperature at which the blob formed.
Wearing heat-resistant gloves, cut away large chunks with diagonal pliers, keeping clear of the thermistor wire and heating rod.
Remove small remnants with a wire brush.
If it will not come off or the hot end is damaged, replace the hot end.
Prevent it: keep the plate clean, make the first layer stick and watch the start of each print, and use good, dry filament.

settings.advice: Slow the first layer; most blobs start when the first layer detaches early in the print.

sources.title: Many filaments are wrapped around the nozzle (Extruder/Nozzle blob)

entries.title: CoPA, PA6-CF, PA12-CF and PA6-GF nylon print settings
entries.summary: Snapmaker's nylon and fibre-filled nylons need high nozzle temperatures (250-270 C for CoPA, up to 300 C for the PA composites), a cool 25-50 C bed on the PEI-coated side, the part fan off and a warm room. They absorb moisture fast: dry at 100 C for 8 hours, and for CoPA, PA6-CF and PA6-GF feed from a dryer during printing. PVA works as soluble support.

settings.advice: Use 250-270 C for CoPA, 260-300 C for PA12-CF, 280-300 C for PA6-CF/PA6-GF; never above the module limit.
Keep the bed at 25-50 C.
Keep part cooling off or minimal.
Use the optional hardened 0.4 mm nozzle where available for fibre-filled grades and set the type accordingly.

facts: CoPA: 250-270 C, 30-60 mm/s, ambient 40-60 C.
PA6-CF: 280-300 C, 60 mm/s, ambient 25-50 C.
PA12-CF: 260-300 C, 30-60 mm/s, retraction speed 40 mm/s.
PA6-GF: 280-300 C, 60 mm/s, ambient 40-60 C.
All: bed 25-50 C, retraction 0-2 mm (40-60 mm/s), fan off, standby 180 C, drying 100 C for 8 h, PEI-coated side.
Pairs with PVA and the other PA grades. Snapmaker 2.0 needs the Dual Extrusion Module (300 C) for these; the single module's brass nozzle is unsuitable for nylon.

entries.title: PETG recommended print settings (Snapmaker filament library)
entries.summary: Snapmaker's PETG reference: nozzle 230-240 C, bed 70-80 C, 30-50 mm/s, short retraction, part-cooling fan off. It pairs with PVA for soluble supports, prints on the PEI-coated side, and should be dried at 65 C for 6 hours since it absorbs moisture.

settings.advice: Use 70-80 C.
Snapmaker's table lists the part fan off for PETG; keep cooling low.
About 140 C for the parked nozzle.

facts: Nozzle 230-240 C; bed 70-80 C; speed 30-50 mm/s.
Retraction 0-2 mm at 20-50 mm/s; part-cooling fan off.
Standby 140 C; drying 65 C for 6 h.
Pairs with PVA and PETG. Plate: PEI-coated side.

entries.title: PLA recommended print settings (Snapmaker filament library)
entries.summary: Snapmaker's reference values for PLA: nozzle 190-220 C, bed 50-65 C, part-cooling fan on and short retraction. Dry it at 55 C for 6 hours if it has absorbed moisture. It prints on the PEI-coated or glass side and pairs with Breakaway PLA or PVA for supports.

settings.advice: Use 190-220 C; go toward the top end for faster printing.
Use 50-65 C on the bed (or the field for your selected plate type).
Keep between 0 and 2 mm.
Run part cooling; PLA wants the fan on.
About 150 C for the parked nozzle in dual extrusion.

facts: Nozzle 190-220 C; bed 50-65 C; speed 10-200 mm/s.
Retraction 0-2 mm at 20-50 mm/s; part-cooling fan on.
Standby (idle) temperature 150 C.
Drying: 55 C for 6 h.
Compatible partners: PLA, Breakaway PLA, PVA. Plate: PEI-coated side or glass side.

entries.title: Poor first layer adhesion on Snapmaker 2.0 and Artisan: causes and fixes
entries.summary: Update firmware first (Artisan needs at least v2.2.4). Most adhesion failures trace back to calibration: preheat the bed for 15 minutes, then redo 25-point leveling and Z Offset. Other causes are a fast first layer, residue on the plate, the wrong plate side or no glue for the material, a crusty nozzle tip, damp filament, and a cold room that steals heat.
symptoms: First layer lifts or will not bond
Whole print fails in the first minutes
causes: Leveling or Z Offset calibration done badly
First layer too fast to solidify onto the plate
Filament residue making the plate uneven
Wrong build plate side for the filament, or missing glue/tape the material needs
Filament crusted around the nozzle tip
Damp filament
Low ambient temperature so nozzle or bed cannot hold set temperature
steps: Mid-print, lower the Z Offset a little to close the gap. Going too close blocks extrusion and can damage plate and nozzle.
Before the next print, preheat the bed at 65 C for 15 minutes, then redo Heated Bed Leveling (25-point recommended) and Z Offset Calibration.
From then on, preheat the bed about 15 minutes before each print at your usual bed temperature.
Still poor: redo Z Offset in Manual mode, or run Sensor Calibration (Dual Extrusion Module only) and redo it in Auto mode; or relevel manually, with more points or a hotter bed.
Slow the first layer and check the initial layer adhesion settings; if unsure, go back to the default profile values.
Remove residue from the plate and use the plate side the filament library recommends.
Where the material needs it, apply an even coat of water-soluble liquid glue or printing tape; wipe it off later with a damp cloth.
Heat the nozzle enough to soften crusted filament and clean the tip with a nozzle brush or tweezers.
Dry damp filament or switch to a dry spool.
In a cold room, raise nozzle and bed temperatures somewhat to make up for heat loss.

settings.advice: Reduce when the first layer is dragged or will not bond; the filament needs time to solidify on the plate.
Raise a few degrees in a cold room or for hard-to-stick materials, staying under the bed limit.
Raise slightly when the ambient temperature is low.
Prefer the Touchscreen Z Offset; use this slicer offset only for a small, consistent correction you want on every print.

entries.title: PVA water-soluble support: print settings, drying and storage
entries.summary: PVA dissolves in water, which makes it ideal for supports with PLA, PETG, TPU and nylon (PA) parts. It soaks up moisture very easily, so feed it from a filament dryer while printing and store it below 25% relative humidity. Snapmaker suggests a 215-225 C nozzle, slow 30-40 mm/s printing and minimal retraction.

settings.advice: Assign the PVA extruder to supports (or at least to the interface) so they wash away in water.
Use PVA for the interface to get clean surfaces where supports touch the model.
Keep at 0-1 mm for PVA.
Mark the PVA profile as soluble so the slicer treats it as dissolvable support.

facts: Nozzle 215-225 C; bed 25-60 C; speed 30-40 mm/s.
Retraction 0-1 mm at 10-30 mm/s; part-cooling fan on.
Standby 100 C; drying 80 C for 12 h; store at room temperature below 25% RH.
Pairs with PLA, PETG, TPU (TPU90/95/HF/Foam) and PA (CoPA, PA6-CF, PA12-CF, PA6-GF). Plate: PEI-coated side.

entries.title: Replacing the nozzle on Snapmaker 2.0 single and dual extruders and on the J1
entries.summary: Swap the nozzle when filament leaks between nozzle and heat block, a blob cannot be cleaned off, the nozzle is clogged, or you want a different nozzle type. Warm it above 100 C first so the metal expands and it loosens more easily, then hold the heat block steady and turn the nozzle counterclockwise.
steps: Heat the nozzle above 100 C, then remove the hot end and its silicone cover, taking care not to get burned.
Snapmaker 2.0 single nozzle: nozzle up, fit an H6 inner hex socket over it, hold the heat block with a wrench and turn the socket counterclockwise.
Dual extruder: hold the heat block with one adjustable wrench and the nozzle with a second set to its size; unscrew counterclockwise.
J1: clamp the heat block nozzle-up in a vise, break the nozzle loose with an adjustable wrench, then unscrew by hand.
Start the new nozzle by hand clockwise, aligned with the heat block hole, then snug it with the wrench or socket.

settings.advice: Update to match the new nozzle (0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8 mm options exist for the 2.0 dual module) and re-slice.

entries.title: Removing and refitting the Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module hot end
entries.summary: The Single Extrusion Module hot end is clamped by screws loosened with an H2.0 screwdriver; shut the machine down first if the module stays mounted. On refitting, push the nozzle in as far as it goes before tightening, leave clearance to the print cooling vent, and confirm the nozzle sits about 1 mm below the proximity sensor.
steps: Turn the machine off; the module can stay on the machine.
Loosen the hot end retaining screws with the H2.0 screwdriver and pull the hot end out.
Insert the new hot end fully, keep a gap on both sides to the print cooling vent, and tighten.
Check the nozzle tip is about 1 mm below the proximity sensor; adjust the sensor if not.
Relevel the bed and redo Z Offset.

sources.title: Detaching the hot end (Single Extrusion Module)
3D printing module Air Passage and Proximity Sensor replacement guide
What should I do if the 3D Printing Module pushes into the Print Sheet?

entries.title: SnapDryer filament dryer: setup, feeding direction, tube length and safety
entries.summary: The SnapDryer keeps filament dry while it feeds the printer (the SnapDryer Box version comes without the Dry Dock). Fill the desiccant box with the color-changing silica gel, face the filament exit toward the lid outlet, and cut the supplied 1500 mm tube to the length your setup needs. Keep the filament wound tight so a loose end cannot block the heating vent.
steps: Open the box, fill the desiccant box with the color-changing silica gel, remove the paper and seat the desiccant box inside.
Thread the filament through the top cover before placing the spool so its unwinding direction lines up with the outlet; otherwise feeding drags.
Feed from the top cover when the dryer sits level with the machine; feed from the side if the dryer is much higher, to keep tube bends gentle.
Use the spool roller to mount spools with damaged edges.
Size the tube by jogging the toolhead to its farthest point (inside the enclosure if fitted) and measuring to the dryer outlet; or keep the full 1500 mm if you may move it later.
facts: Use only the original power adapter; operate indoors on a stable level surface away from water; unplug when not in use.
Never put loose desiccant in the box bottom or objects in the heating vents; remove the desiccant box before refilling it.
Do not leave the dryer unattended in Continuous Mode, and do not touch the heating vent while it runs.

entries.title: Storing filament to prevent moisture problems
entries.summary: Most filaments, PLA and PETG especially, take up moisture from the air, and damp filament clogs nozzles and spoils prints. Between prints, keep spools in a vacuum bag with desiccant and write the opening date on it. Use an opened spool within about a month; sealed spools last about 24 months.
facts: Opened filament: use within about one month. Vacuum-sealed: about 24 months.
Store at about 25 C (77 F) and around 40% relative humidity.
Keep out of direct sunlight.
PVA and TPU need drier storage: below 25% relative humidity.

entries.title: Filaments supported by the Dual Extrusion Module, Artisan and J1
entries.summary: Snapmaker lists which materials each platform supports. The Artisan and the Dual Extrusion Module cover a broad range including soluble PVA, flexible TPUs and fibre-filled nylons; the J1 list is similar and adds PC, TPE and PP. The Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module is limited to PLA, ABS, PETG and TPU.

settings.advice: Pick the matching type so temperature and cooling presets fit; avoid materials outside your module's supported list.

facts: Artisan and Dual Extrusion Module - rigid: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, HIPS; supports: Breakaway PLA, PVA; flexible: TPU90, TPU95, High Flow TPU95, TPU-Foam; nylon: CoPA, PA6-CF, PA6-GF, PA12-CF.
J1 - rigid: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, HIPS, PC, PP; support: PVA; flexible: TPU, TPE; nylon: PA, PA-CF, PA-GF.
Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module: PLA, ABS, PETG, TPU.

entries.title: TPU90, TPU95, High Flow TPU95 and TPU-Foam recommended print settings
entries.summary: Snapmaker's flexible filaments all print with no retraction, the part fan on and on the glass side of the plate. Nozzle 210-230 C (200-220 C for High Flow TPU95), bed 25-60 C. Speed is the main difference: TPU95 20-40 mm/s, TPU90 and TPU-Foam 30-60, High Flow TPU95 40-100 mm/s. TPU absorbs moisture; dry at 65-70 C for 8 hours and store below 25% RH.

settings.advice: Set to 0 mm for all Snapmaker TPU grades.
Keep within the grade's range, e.g. 20-40 mm/s for TPU95; slower feeds more reliably.
Keep low for standard TPU; only the High Flow grade tolerates up to 100 mm/s printing.
About 120 C for a parked TPU nozzle.

facts: High Flow TPU95 (TPU95-HF): 200-220 C, bed 25-50 C, 40-100 mm/s, dry 70 C 8 h.
TPU-Foam: 210-230 C, bed 25-60 C, 30-60 (units mislabeled on the source page), dry 70 C 8 h.
All: retraction 0 mm, retraction speed 15 mm/s, fan on, standby 120 C (not given for TPU-Foam), glass side.
Pairs with Breakaway PLA, other TPUs and PVA.

entries.title: Loading filament into a J1 extruder (aided loading)
entries.summary: In aided loading the J1 extruder motor feeds the filament once it is inserted and gripped. Heat the extruder (default 200 °C, or the filament's own temperature), thread the filament through the guide tube, push it into the head while holding the toggle, then tap Load until plastic flows. Note the crossover: the left extruder's filament entry is on the right side of the machine, and vice versa.
steps: Tap Control > Extruder, set the target temperature and tap Heat; Load only unlocks close to the set temperature.
Remove the top panel and hang the spool on its holder.
Cut the filament end at about 45° with diagonal pliers.
Feed it into the filament entry until it pokes out of the far end of the guide tube.
Hold the toggle on the extruder pushed back, insert the filament until you feel resistance, then let go.
At temperature tap Load, wait for plastic to flow from the nozzle, then tap Stop Loading.
Seat the guide tube in the extruder and its tube clip, refit the top panel and brush excess plastic off the nozzle.

entries.title: J1 heated bed calibration fails (nozzle presses into bed, or bed drops without contact)
entries.summary: J1 calibration relies on the nozzle electrically touching the bed pads. If the bed keeps rising and the nozzle digs in, the hot end probe signal is open (often blue threadlocker on the hot end board screws blocking conduction) or the FFC cable is damaged. If calibration fails without the nozzle ever touching, a PT100 or a worn black fan wire is shorting to the casing: left hot end if the bed stays put, right hot end if the bed keeps dropping.
symptoms: Bed keeps rising after contact and the nozzle presses into and deforms it.
Calibration fails without the nozzle touching the bed.
Nozzle never touches and the bed moves down in steps before calibration fails.
causes: Hotend probe signal open circuit (e.g. threadlocker insulating the screws).
Bent or damaged FFC ribbon cable.
PT100 or hot end fan black wire shorting to the casing (left hot end when the bed is static, right hot end when the bed drops).
steps: Clean filament off the nozzles and calibrate without filament loaded.
Nozzle pressing into the bed: set a multimeter to continuity, put the black lead on pin 1 of the hot end PCB (probe signal) and the red lead on the heater block.
No continuity: loosen the two lower hot end board screws, clean the blue threadlocker off, retighten and measure again.
Continuity present: inspect the FFC ribbon cable for bends and check that it is seated straight and tight.
Fails without touching and the bed stays still: inspect the left hot end's black fan wire for worn insulation touching the casing.
Fails without touching and the bed drops: inspect the right hot end's black fan wire.
If the wire is intact, the PT100 may be damaged; contact support.

sources.title: How to resolve J1(s) heated bed calibration failures

entries.title: Fine-tuning J1 bed corners with the hand-twist knobs (0.05 mm per notch)
entries.summary: After auto-levelling, seating the glass plate on the bed can shift corner heights slightly. Print Snapmaker's four-corner first-layer test G-code, measure each corner square with calipers and turn the black hand-twist knob under that corner until all of them read 0.2 mm. Each knob has 10 notches, and one notch moves the corner 0.05 mm.
steps: Download and print the corner test model linked on the wiki page.
Measure each of the four corner squares with calipers and write the value on it.
For any corner that is not 0.2 mm thick, turn that corner's black knob under the heated bed; one notch equals 0.05 mm.
Reprint the test to confirm.

sources.title: First layer has poor adhesion or appears uneven at the corners.
Helpful tips for J1/J1s new users to avoid common pitfalls

entries.title: J1 error 'Abnormal Temp. Control-Bed': bed cannot reach temperature with the fan on
entries.summary: The J1 firmware raises 'Abnormal Temp. Control-Bed' when the heated bed fails to reach its target within a set time. A common trigger is the part cooling fan running fast while printing high-temperature materials like ABS and PETG, which draws heat away from the bed. Switch the fan off or turn it down for these materials, or unplug the fan cable while printing them.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows 'Abnormal Temp. Control-Bed'.
Bed heats slowly or stalls below target while the part fan is running.
causes: Part cooling fan at high speed during ABS or PETG prints.
Bed heating protection timing out before the target temperature is reached.
steps: In the slicer, turn the part cooling fan off or set it low for ABS and PETG.
Alternatively unplug the print cooling fan cable for those prints.
Retry; if it persists, contact Snapmaker support with photos or video.

settings.advice: Set to 0 or low for ABS and PETG on the J1; a strong fan can stop the bed reaching temperature.
Keep at 0 for ABS and PETG profiles.

facts: Values quoted on this page: ABS nozzle 245-265 °C, bed 80-100 °C; PETG nozzle 230-250 °C, bed 60-80 °C (the filament library lists ABS bed 90-100 °C and PETG 230-240 °C / 70-80 °C).

sources.title: The temperature control of the heated bed is abnormal (J1/J1s)

entries.title: Adjusting J1 X and Y belt tension with the printed tension gauge
entries.summary: Loose belts make J1 head motion inaccurate; overtight belts wear out sooner. Check every three months, after long-distance transport, when a belt is noisy, or with layer shifts (especially in dual-filament prints) or poor first-layer adhesion. On firmware V2.2.2 or later, print the X and Y belt tension gauges in PLA from the touchscreen's Local folder, clip them on and adjust until each gauge closes with no visible gap.
steps: Print the X and Y tension gauges from the Local folder (firmware V2.2.2+) in PLA.
Turn the motors off (Control > Motor), then power off and unplug.

X belt: push the left head fully left and the right head fully right, remove both side panels (H2.0), clip the gauge on the X belt and turn the hex screws at both ends of the X rail with the 5.5 mm wrench until the gauge closes.
Y belts: also push the X rail fully inward, clip the gauge on the left Y belt and turn the upper-left screw on the back by hand until it closes; repeat on the right belt with the upper-right screw.
Refit the side panels.

sources.title: Adjusting the tension of the belts

entries.title: J1 touchscreen stays black at power-on
entries.summary: A black J1 screen at power-on (including after a power cut mid-print) can be the AC cord, rocker switch, power supply, mainboard or screen. Quick clues: if the light bar lights, or the axes are locked and cannot be pushed by hand, the power supply works; if Luban can control the printer over a USB serial connection, the power supply and mainboard work and the screen or its cable is suspect.
causes: AC power cord loose or damaged.
Rocker switch with poor contact or damage.
Failed power supply.
Failed mainboard.
Failed touchscreen or loose screen FFC cable.
steps: Power off, unplug and firmly reseat the AC cord.
Switch on and watch the rocker switch's red light; if it stays dark, test the cord with a multimeter or a spare cord, flick the switch several times, and inspect its wiring under the bottom cover.
Measure the two large pins of the add-on port with a multimeter on DC: about 24 V means the power supply is fine.

Under the bottom cover, check the mainboard's red LED. If lit, try controlling the printer from Luban over USB serial; if not, measure for 24 V at the mainboard power connector, keeping clear of high-voltage areas.
If the power supply and mainboard work, reseat the touchscreen FFC cable at the mainboard.
Contact support if the screen is still black.

sources.title: The touchscreen is black when power on the machine

entries.title: PEI side or glass side: choosing the J1 build plate surface
entries.summary: The J1/J1s plate has a PEI-coated face and a bare glass face. PEI is the default: dependable adhesion with little upkeep and good heat transfer. Use the glass face for a very smooth, flat underside, for TPU, or once the PEI is worn; prepare it by cleaning with ethyl alcohol and applying glue (PVP stick, liquid glue or tape). Keep glue off the PEI face, and let PEI cool before removing prints.
facts: Glass side is recommended for TPU90, TPU95, TPU95-HF and TPU-Foam; most other J1 filaments use the PEI side.
ASA and HIPS stick better with liquid glue, which Snapmaker prefers over glue stick.
Glue on PEI makes parts harder to release and can damage the coating, especially if prints are pried off while hot.
Removing prints while the PEI glass plate is still hot damages the coating; wait for room temperature.
After changing or modifying the plate, update the glass thickness value on the touchscreen.

sources.title: Choosing the proper build plate side
Helpful tips for J1/J1s new users to avoid common pitfalls

entries.title: Checking J1 offset calibration with the verification print
entries.summary: After XY and Z offset calibration, Calibration Check > Start prints a built-in verification model with both heads. Inspect it as the touchscreen describes to judge whether the calibration worked; if it did not, clean the nozzles and repeat the relevant calibration.
steps: Tap Calibration Check > Start.
Follow the prompts while the verification model prints.
Assess the model against the on-screen guidance.
If it fails, clean both nozzles and redo Z and/or XY offset calibration.

entries.title: Cleaning the J1 base panel and Z lead screw area
entries.summary: Plastic scraps and small parts that pile up on the J1 base panel can stop the printer working properly, particularly near the Z lead screw where they can block the bed. Monthly, raise the bed with Control > Jog Mode (Z+) and wipe the base panel clean. Never store items there, or the bed will not home to the correct position.
steps: Tap Control > Jog Mode and press Z+ to lift the heated bed.
Wipe the base panel with the cloth, paying attention to the area around the Z lead screw.
Keep the base panel free of stored items.

entries.title: Cleaning J1 extruder drive and idler gears
entries.summary: Gripping filament grinds shavings off it that collect on the J1 extruder gears, reducing grip and extrusion (eventually to nothing) and possibly dropping into the nozzle. Clean monthly: press the idler latch on the front of the print head to open it, swab the idler gear and then the drive gear with a cotton swab until clean, and close the latch.
steps: Press down the idler latch on the front of the print head to open it.
Clean the idler gear with a cotton swab until no debris is visible.
Clean the drive gear the same way.
Close the idler latch.

entries.title: Cleaning the J1 PEI glass plate: residue, glue, grease and dust
entries.summary: Clean the plate at least monthly, or whenever residue, glue or weak first-layer adhesion appears. Scrape leftover plastic with the palette knife held at under 30° to protect the PEI, wipe glue off with a damp cloth, and wash off skin oil and dust with water (or alcohol), then dry the plate by heating it to 60 °C.
steps: Residue: scrape gently with the palette knife at less than 30° to the plate; warm the bed to 50 °C if it is stubborn (wear gloves).
Glue: power off and unplug, wipe with the cloth and clean water until no residue remains; warm to 50 °C if needed.
Grease and dust: once the plate is at room temperature, remove it, wash with clean water and the wiping cloth (alcohol if water is not enough), then rinse again.
Refit the plate and heat the bed to 60 °C via Control > Heated Bed to dry it.

sources.title: Choosing the proper build plate side

entries.title: Cleaning the J1 heated bed surface
entries.summary: Debris on the heated bed under the glass plate can make J1 calibration fail, so wipe the bed at least once a month. Power off and unplug, lift off the glass plate and set it somewhere safe, wipe the bed gently with the supplied cloth until nothing visible remains, then refit the plate.
steps: Power off and unplug the printer.
Remove the glass plate and put it in a safe place.
Wipe the heated bed gently with the wiping cloth until it is clean.
Reinstall the glass plate.

entries.title: Cleaning J1 nozzles with the wire brush
entries.summary: Clean each J1 nozzle at every calibration and before each print. Residue that hardens on the nozzle can spoil contact-based calibration, cause jams or leave dark marks on the next print. Heat the extruder to 200 °C under Control > Extruder and scrub the outside with the supplied wire brush.
steps: Power on and heat the extruder to 200 °C via Control > Extruder.
Brush residue off the nozzle surface, keeping the brush away from the nozzle tip so it does not wear.
Wear insulated gloves; the nozzle is hot.
If the nozzle did not bounce back quickly when touching a calibration point, clean it and calibrate again.

entries.title: J1 clogs caused by slicer settings: retraction, temperature and speed
entries.summary: Check slicer settings before hardware. Excessive retraction draws softened filament up into the hot end's PTFE section where it jams; a nozzle too cold for the chosen speed cannot melt filament fast enough; and special filaments like silk PLA clog at high speed. Luban 4.7.3+ and Snapmaker Cura Plugin 0.9.0+ include revised retraction values; in other slicers keep retraction at 2 mm or less.
symptoms: Nothing extrudes from the nozzle.
Extruder clicks during loading.
'Failed to Load Filament' appears.
causes: Retraction values too high.
Nozzle temperature too low for the print speed.
Speed too high for a special filament such as silk PLA.
steps: If filament is stuck in the head, heat it, tap Unload and pull it out; if it will not come out, go to the drive-gear checks instead.
Set the nozzle temperature inside the filament's recommended range.
If you print faster than the filament's recommended speed, halve the speed as a test; if extrusion improves, raise the nozzle temperature 10-15 °C for the fast profile.
Slow down silk and other special filaments and run them hotter.
Reload and test-print; if it still fails, follow the full J1 clog flowchart.

settings.advice: Keep at 2 mm or less (0-2 mm for most filaments, 0 mm for TPU); long retractions jam the 15 mm PTFE liner in the standard hot end.
Stay in the filament's recommended range; add 10-15 °C for high-speed profiles.
Halve as a test if extrusion fails at high speed; keep silk PLA at or below 100 mm/s.
Lower for silk and other special filaments.
Lower to cap flow automatically when the hot end cannot keep up at high speed.

sources.title: Inappropriate print settings cause a clog
The hot end or nozzle is clogged (J1)

entries.title: J1 filament not extruding or clogged: diagnosis order
entries.summary: When a J1 head will not extrude, clicks while loading or shows 'Failed to Load Filament', check causes in this order: slicer settings, a false filament-sensor trigger, a misaligned or loose drive gear, filament jammed in the extruder gears, then a hot end or nozzle clog. Each test narrows the fault before you take anything apart.
symptoms: No filament comes out of the nozzle.
Clicking from the extruder while loading.
'Failed to Load Filament' message on the screen.
causes: Unsuitable print settings.
False trigger of the filament sensor.
Drive gears misaligned or drive gear set screw loose.
Extruder clogged at the gears.
Hot end clogged.
Nozzle clogged.
steps: Rule out settings: retraction too long, nozzle too cold for the speed, or a special filament printed too fast.
Test with Control > Extruder > Heat > Load. If filament loads properly, the error was probably a false sensor trigger.
Motors off (Control > Motor), move the head off the wiper, open the idler latch, heat, and push filament through by hand. If it extrudes, the drive gear is misaligned or its set screw is loose.
If hand-pushing fails, look inside with the latch open: filament bent or tangled at the gears means an extruder clog.
Otherwise the blockage is in the hot end or nozzle; clear it or replace the hot end.
If none of this works, open a Snapmaker support ticket with full details.

sources.title: Troubleshooting flowchart for clogging/filament not extruding (J1)

entries.title: J1/J1s community upgrades and mods (top panel risers, cooling, filament storage)
entries.summary: Snapmaker lists popular community mods for J1/J1s but warns that DIY changes are at your own risk, unsupported, and forfeit warranty and after-sales support. Common mods: top panel risers (vent the chamber for PLA without removing the lid, less feed-tube friction), better part-cooling fans and ducts, spools moved inside or above the machine to keep filament dry and cut feed resistance, filters for ABS/ASA fumes, cameras and flexible magnetic PEI plates.
facts: Top panel risers: 4 printed parts (PETG suggested, printed in copy mode) and 8 magnets of 10×2 mm; unplug before fitting and don't load objects on the raised lid.
With any official hot end, keep silk PLA at or below 100 mm/s and the nozzle at 220 °C or higher to limit clogs and improve the silky finish.
Interference-fit hot ends do not allow the nozzle to be swapped alone; threaded hot ends do.
Filament internalisation mod uses 608z bearings and 3 m of 2×4 mm PTFE tube; when changing the PTFE tube, pry the E-clip off gently with tweezers so it is not lost or damaged.

sources.title: Snapmaker J1/J1s Upgrades and Mods Community Resources

entries.title: Dual-material, dual-colour and soluble-support printing on the J1
entries.summary: Each J1 head heats independently, so one part can combine materials with very different temperatures, or pair a model material with breakaway or soluble support printed only by the second head. Two nozzles ooze more than one, so Snapmaker advises a prime tower or ooze shield on every dual-colour or dual-material job. PVA dissolves in water and HIPS in limonene.
steps: For dual colour, export each colour region from CAD as its own model file, import both and align (merge) them in the slicer.
Use Normal print mode.
Set the filament loaded in each extruder, then assign an extruder to each model or part.
Choose a process profile per extruder, slice and check the layer preview.
Enable a prime tower (or ooze shield) before printing.
If merged parts do not line up, correct the geometry in the design software rather than in the slicer.

settings.advice: Turn on for dual-colour or dual-material prints so each nozzle purges after a tool change before printing visible surfaces.
Enable to drop the idle nozzle to a standby temperature between tool changes and limit oozing onto the part.
Use J1 standby values: PLA 150 °C, PETG 140 °C, ABS/ASA 160 °C, HIPS 150 °C, PVA 100 °C, TPU 120 °C, CoPA/PA-CF/PA-GF 180 °C.
Assign the support extruder's filament (PVA, HIPS or Breakaway PLA) so the second head builds the supports.
Use the soluble or breakaway filament at least for the interface layers for clean separation from the model.
Mark PVA as soluble so it is treated as support material.

facts: Pairings from the J1 filament library: PLA with Breakaway PLA or PVA; PETG with PVA or HIPS; ABS with HIPS; TPU with Breakaway PLA or PVA; CoPA and PA6-CF/PA12-CF/PA6-GF with PVA.
Soluble supports leave no support marks and allow hard-to-reach internal supports.

entries.title: Adjusting J1 enclosure light brightness
entries.summary: The light inside the J1 enclosure can be dimmed or brightened mid-print under Adjust > Lighting by dragging the round dial. The level is stored and reused for later jobs until you change it. Updating to firmware newer than V2.5.9 keeps it; rolling back below V2.5.9 resets it.
steps: Tap Adjust during a print.
Scroll down the left menu and tap Lighting.
Drag on the round dial to set brightness.

sources.title: Adjusting the lighting brightness of J1

entries.title: J1/J1s operating environment: temperature, humidity and workbench
entries.summary: Run the J1/J1s at 10-35 °C (50-95 °F) and 10-90% relative humidity without condensation. A hot room hurts PLA prints and can damage components; a cold room hurts ABS and PA and makes edges warp. Very damp air can harm components through moisture, and very dry air invites static that can make the printer misbehave.
facts: Workbench: rated above the printer's weight, stable, level, clean and dry.
Print ABS in a well-ventilated room; with an air purifier, put the bench near a vent.
Use a fan or air conditioning to cool a hot room, heating for a cold one, and a humidifier or dehumidifier to stay within range.
Filament makers' own ambient recommendations take precedence for specific materials.

entries.title: Exporting J1 system logs for support
entries.summary: System logs record what the printer was doing and help locate faults. Insert a USB flash drive, tap Settings > About, find System Logs, tap Export and choose USB Flash Drive (export to Snapmaker software is also offered), then wait for the Exported message. The files are named FW and SC; send them to Snapmaker support with a description of the problem.
steps: Insert a USB flash drive.
Tap Settings > About and locate System Logs.
Tap Export > USB Flash Drive and wait until the screen says Exported.
Attach the FW and SC files to your support ticket.

sources.title: Troubleshooting guide for J1 Wi-Fi connectivity problems

entries.title: J1 extruder clog: filament bent or tangled in the drive gears
entries.summary: An extruder clog means filament has buckled or wrapped around the J1's drive gears. Typical causes are PLA softening in a hot enclosure with the top panel on, and TPU softer than 90A (or any flexible filament fed too fast) bending inside the extruder. Open the idler latch to confirm, pull the filament out and clean the gears.
symptoms: No filament from the nozzle.
'Failed to Load Filament' message.
causes: PLA printed with the top panel on gets soft in the warm chamber and jams in the drive gears.
TPU below 90A, or flexible filament loaded too quickly, twists inside the extruder.
steps: Motors off (Control > Motor), move the head off the wiper, press the idler latch open and look for bent or twisted filament at the gears.
Remove the stuck filament with a hex key (H1.5 or H2.0), diagonal pliers or tweezers.
If it will not come free, loosen (not remove) the print head side cover screws to widen the gap, extract the filament, then retighten them.
Blow or brush particles out of the gears with an air gun, small brush or cotton swab.
Reload and test; if it still fails, treat it as a hot end or nozzle clog.
To prevent repeats, remove the top panel for PLA and use TPU of 90A or harder, loaded slowly.

entries.title: J1 extruder clicking: drive gears misaligned or set screw loose
entries.summary: If a J1 head clicks or will not extrude with Load, yet filament comes out when you push it through the opened extruder by hand, the drive gear has probably slid out of line with its partner or its set screw has loosened on the motor shaft. Realign the gear and tighten the set screw with the grey H1.5 hex key.
symptoms: No extrusion or clicking when loading with the Load button.
Filament pushed by hand through the open extruder extrudes normally.
causes: The two drive gears are not lined up with each other.
Set screw on the driving gear has worked loose.
steps: Turn the motors off (Control > Motor), slide the head off the nozzle wiper and press the idler latch to open the extruder.
Check that the filament lines up with the teeth of the driving gear; with no filament loaded, the gear's end face should be flush with the end of the motor shaft.
Make sure the set screw presses on the flat of the motor shaft.
If anything is off, slide the gear into place and tighten the set screw (H1.5).
Rotate the gear to confirm it turns together with the shaft, then close the latch.
Heat, insert filament and tap Load; extrusion should be steady with no clicking. Contact support if not.

sources.title: Extruder drive gears are not aligned/Extruder driving gear set screw is loose (J1)

entries.title: J1 extruder motor not turning (spins freely by hand when powered)
entries.summary: If a J1 extruder motor will not turn on Load and can be spun by hand while the printer is on (other motors stay locked), the motor is not being driven. Causes: a loose or damaged motor cable, a bent or damaged FFC ribbon cable, a loose FFC-to-adapter-board connection, a faulty motor or a faulty mainboard. Swapping left and right connections isolates the bad part.
symptoms: Extruder motor stops turning and rotates freely by hand with power on, while other motors are locked.
With the latch open, tapping Load does not turn the motor.
causes: Motor cable loose or damaged.
FFC cable bent or damaged.
FFC cable loose at the FFC adapter board.
Faulty motor.
Faulty mainboard.
steps: Inspect the FFC ribbon cable for kinks or damage and confirm it sits straight and fully in its connector.
Check the FFC connection at the adapter board; the connector is fragile, so handle it gently.
Check the extruder motor cable for looseness or damage.

Exchange the two FFC cables (left and right) at the adapter board: if the fault stays with the same print head, the head or motor is to blame; if it moves to the other side, suspect the adapter board or mainboard.
Swap the extruder motor leads on the mainboard (E0 = left, E1 = right) to test the mainboard port.
Send results with photos or video to Snapmaker support.

entries.title: J1 error 'Temperature control of the left/right extruder is abnormal': reseat the hot end
entries.summary: This J1 message usually means the hot end is not making good contact with the print head's PCB. Power off, loosen the two side screws on the extruder (pink H2.0 key, do not remove them), release and pull the hot end out, push it back in fully, lock it, and test by running bed levelling. Recalibrate afterwards so the two heads stay aligned.
symptoms: Screen error: temperature control of the left (or right) extruder is abnormal.
causes: Hot end not making good electrical contact with the print head PCB.
steps: Power off the printer.
Using the pink H2.0 hex key, back off the pair of screws on the extruder's side without taking them out.
Right extruder only: roll the knob on the print head to the right until the hot end kit is released.
Pull the hot end kit down and out, then push it straight back up into the head.
Roll the knob to the left until it stops (both heads).
Power on, start Heated Bed Leveling and watch whether the error returns.
Redo XY and Z offset calibration so the heads are realigned.
If the error persists, work through the enhanced checks (sock, screws, PT100 and heater, FFC cable).

sources.title: The temperature control of the extruder is abnormal

entries.title: J1 'Failed to Load Filament' keeps appearing although filament loads fine
entries.summary: The J1 filament sensor checks that filament is moving, so it pauses on clogs, runout and tangles. If 'Failed to Load Filament' keeps appearing but filament extrudes normally via Control > Extruder > Heat > Load, it is a false trigger: high feed resistance, a sensor wheel jammed by debris, or the sensor not pressing on the filament (missing washer, weak spring). Update to firmware 2.7.2 or later first.
symptoms: 'Failed to Load Filament' pops up again and again during prints.
Filament loads and extrudes normally from the Load button.
causes: Too much feed resistance in the filament path.
Sensor wheel not turning freely, e.g. plastic debris stuck near the sensor.
Sensor only partly touching the filament because the washer is missing or the spring is weak.
steps: Note which head (left, right or both) reported it, tap OK, heat that extruder (via Adjust or Control > Extruder) and tap Load. Plastic coming out confirms a false trigger; if none comes out, check the drive gears instead.
Cut feed resistance: look for flattened or damaged filament tubes and tangled or knotted spools; as a test, remove the top cover and tubes and feed the head directly.
Update firmware to 2.7.2 or later.

Clean the sensor: turn motors off, open the print head side cover, lift out the orange case that holds the sensor (wires stay connected) and check its wheel spins freely; open the case and clear debris if not.
Make sure the washer and spring are in place, close and refit the case, check the wiring, refit the side cover, turn motors back on and test.
If it is clean but still triggers, print and fit the spacer STL Snapmaker provides for the filament detection assembly.
Last resort: turn off runout detection for that head in Machine Settings to keep printing, and ask support for a replacement detection assembly.

sources.title: False trigger of the "Failed to Load Filament" error (J1)

entries.title: J1 'The system failed to obtain motherboard data' after a firmware update
entries.summary: If the J1 screen shows no files or a scrambled interface and, after a restart, reports 'The system failed to obtain motherboard data', a firmware upgrade usually went wrong. The fix is reflashing the mainboard firmware (2.2.11) over USB with Snapmaker's Chinese-language Windows serial tool; doing so without Snapmaker Support's approval leaves any resulting damage outside warranty.
steps: Download Snapmaker Serial Port Assistant V1.6.5 and the J1_MC_APP_V2.2.11 firmware linked on the wiki.
Connect the printer to the PC with a USB cable.

Pick the COM port and establish the serial connection (the corner should show COM1 115200 True), open the Snapmaker menu, choose SCAP, click Choose Upgrade File and open the 2.2.11 file, all within 6 seconds of connecting.
Do not switch windows; wait for the progress bar to reach 100%. If it does not move, retry faster.
Restart. If homing fails afterwards, roll back to firmware 2.3.5.
Once it works, update to the latest firmware from a USB drive.

entries.title: ABS, ASA and HIPS settings for the J1 (enclosed, fan off)
entries.summary: J1 values: ABS 245-265 °C, bed 90-100 °C, 30-50 mm/s, standby 160 °C, PEI side or glued glass. ASA 240-260 °C, bed 75-95 °C, retraction 1-3 mm, chamber 50-70 °C, PEI. HIPS 230-250 °C, bed 60-80 °C, 40-80 mm/s, retraction 0.5-3 mm at 30-70 mm/s, standby 150 °C. All three: part fan off; dry ABS/ASA at 80 °C for 8 h, HIPS at 60 °C for 3 h. Close the doors, fit the top panel and ventilate for ABS fumes.

settings.advice: ABS 90-100 °C (80-100 °C on the bed-error page), ASA 75-95 °C, HIPS 60-80 °C.
Off for ABS, ASA and HIPS; a running fan also risks the Abnormal Temp. Control-Bed error.
ABS 0-2 mm, ASA 1-3 mm, HIPS 0.5-3 mm.
Standby: ABS and ASA 160 °C, HIPS 150 °C.

facts: ASA and HIPS adhere better with liquid glue.
HIPS pairs with ABS or PETG as a support and dissolves in limonene.
ABS fumes and particles are harmful to breathe; print with ventilation or an air purifier.

entries.title: Nylon and fibre-filled nylon (CoPA, PA6-CF, PA12-CF, PA6-GF) on the J1
entries.summary: J1 values: CoPA 250-270 °C at 30-60 mm/s; PA6-CF and PA6-GF 280-300 °C at 60 mm/s; PA12-CF 260-300 °C at 30-60 mm/s. All: bed 25-50 °C, retraction 0-2 mm at about 40-60 mm/s, part fan off, standby 180 °C, PEI side, dry at 100 °C for 8 h. They absorb moisture fast, so print from a dryer. Suggested chamber: CoPA and PA6-GF 40-60 °C, PA6-CF 25-50 °C. They pair with each other and with PVA.

settings.advice: CoPA 250-270 °C, PA12-CF 260-300 °C, PA6-CF/PA6-GF 280-300 °C (near the J1's 300 °C limit).
25-50 °C on the PEI side.
Off for all nylon grades.
180 °C standby.

entries.title: PETG settings for the J1
entries.summary: J1 filament library values for PETG: nozzle 230-240 °C, bed 70-80 °C, 30-50 mm/s, retraction 0-2 mm at 20-50 mm/s, part fan off, standby 140 °C, dry at 65 °C for 6 h, PEI-coated side. It pairs with PVA (or HIPS) for supports. The bed-error page quotes slightly different ranges (nozzle 230-250 °C, bed 60-80 °C) and warns that a strong fan while printing PETG can keep the bed from reaching temperature.

settings.advice: 230-240 °C per the J1 filament library.
70-80 °C (60-80 °C quoted on the bed-error page).
Keep off or low; a fast fan can trigger Abnormal Temp. Control-Bed on the J1.
0-2 mm; do not exceed 2 mm on the J1.
140 °C standby in dual-extruder jobs.

entries.title: PLA and Breakaway PLA settings for the J1
entries.summary: Snapmaker's J1 values for PLA: nozzle 190-220 °C, bed 50-65 °C, 10-200 mm/s, retraction 0-2 mm at 20-50 mm/s, part fan on, standby 150 °C, dry at 55 °C for 6 h; prints on PEI or glass. Breakaway PLA (support material): nozzle 220-230 °C, bed 25-65 °C, only 20-40 mm/s, retraction 0-2 mm, fan on, standby 120 °C, dry 55 °C for 6 h, PEI side; pairs with PLA or TPU.

settings.advice: PLA 190-220 °C; Breakaway PLA 220-230 °C. Raise PLA by 10-15 °C for high-speed profiles.
PLA 50-65 °C; Breakaway PLA 25-65 °C.
Keep within 0-2 mm; longer retractions risk jams at the PTFE section of the standard hot end.
20-50 mm/s for both.
Standby: PLA 150 °C, Breakaway PLA 120 °C in dual-extruder jobs.
Part cooling fan on for PLA and Breakaway PLA.

facts: PLA pairs with Breakaway PLA or PVA for supports.
In a closed J1, remove the top panel for PLA to avoid heat-related clogs.

entries.title: PVA water-soluble support on the J1
entries.summary: PVA is the J1's water-soluble support material: nozzle 215-225 °C, bed 25-60 °C, 30-40 mm/s, retraction 0-1 mm at 10-30 mm/s, fan on, standby 100 °C, PEI side. It pairs with PLA, PETG, TPU and the nylons (CoPA, PA6-CF, PA12-CF, PA6-GF). It soaks up moisture quickly: dry at 80 °C for 12 h, store below 25% RH and print it from a filament dryer.

settings.advice: Short: 0-1 mm at 10-30 mm/s.
Enable so PVA is treated as a soluble support material.
Assign PVA to the interface (or all support) for mark-free surfaces.
100 °C standby while the other head prints.

entries.title: TPU and flexible filament on the J1 (90A minimum, no retraction)
entries.summary: The J1 handles TPU of 90A or harder; softer TPU twists inside the extruder and clogs it, and any flexible filament can buckle if fed too fast. Library values: TPU90 and TPU95 210-230 °C, bed 25-60 °C, TPU90 30-60 mm/s, TPU95 20-40 mm/s; TPU95-HF 200-220 °C, bed 25-50 °C, 40-100 mm/s. All grades: 0 mm retraction (15 mm/s), fan on, standby 120 °C, glass side, dry at 65-70 °C for 8 h, store below 25% RH.

settings.advice: 0 mm for every TPU grade on the J1.
TPU90/TPU95/TPU-Foam 210-230 °C; TPU95-HF 200-220 °C.
Stay inside the grade's range (TPU95 20-40 mm/s, TPU90 30-60 mm/s) to avoid buckling in the extruder.
Same limits as walls; only TPU95-HF tolerates up to 100 mm/s.
120 °C standby in dual-extruder jobs.

facts: TPU-Foam: 210-230 °C, bed 25-60 °C, 0 mm retraction, glass side, dry 70 °C for 8 h.
TPU pairs with Breakaway PLA or PVA for supports.

sources.title: Choosing the proper build plate side

entries.title: Unloading and changing filament on the J1 (aided and manual)
entries.summary: To change J1 filament, unload the current spool and then load the new one. Heat the extruder first (default 200 °C; Load and Unload unlock near the set temperature). Aided unloading: tap Unload, wait about 20 seconds, tap Stop Unloading and pull the filament out of the filament entry. Manual unloading: unclip the guide tube, open the idler latch and draw the filament out of the hot extruder.
steps: Control > Extruder: set the temperature for the left or right head and tap Heat.
Aided: at temperature tap Unload, wait about 20 s, tap Stop Unloading, then pull the filament back out through the filament entry.
Manual: unclip the guide tube, press the idler latch to open it, pull the filament out of the extruder at temperature and then out of the guide tube.
Take the spool off its holder and load the new filament (aided or manual).
Avoid touching the hot nozzle; insulated gloves are recommended.

entries.title: Updating J1/J1s firmware via Wi-Fi or USB drive
entries.summary: Keep J1/J1s firmware current, at least every three months, because the factory version can lag behind fixes (the filament sensor false-trigger fix, for example, needs 2.7.2 or later). Update over Wi-Fi from Settings > Firmware Update, or put the firmware from the Snapmaker website on a USB drive and pick it from the touchscreen's USB file list. Redo calibration afterwards.
steps: Wi-Fi: connect the printer to a network, tap Settings > Firmware Update > Download > Update and wait for Complete.
USB: download the firmware file to a USB flash drive, insert it, power on, tap the blank area of the home screen, tap USB, then tap the firmware file.
After updating, run the calibration steps again.
