entries.title: Assembling a backlit lithophane frame with light guide plate and USB-C backlight
entries.summary: Snapmaker provides STL and 3MF files for the frame, a light-blocking strip and a light guide plate; the backlight board is bought separately (a 156 × 120 mm USB-C board is recommended). After printing, clean supports and burrs off the lithophane edges. From back to front the stack is backlight board, light guide plate, then the lithophane with its image facing the viewer.
steps: Deburr the lithophane edges and check you have the print, guide plate, both frame halves, backlight and USB-C cable.
Seat the light guide plate in the frame in front of the backlight and behind the print; a little glue keeps it from falling out.
Fit the backlight into the frame back, lit side toward the guide plate, USB-C port lined up with the rear hole, held flat under the clips.
Route the USB-C cable through the rear hole for portrait or landscape use, plug it in and press it into the cable slot so it isn't pinched.
Insert the lithophane image side forward, line up the clips and press the front frame on gently; push a tight print in slowly from behind.
Power it from a 5 V source such as a phone charger or power bank and view in dim light; swap prints without removing the guide plate or backlight.

entries.title: Printing a CMYK color lithophane in Snapmaker Orca (Lithophane Makers workflow)
entries.summary: Color lithophanes use the SnapSpeed PLA CMYK Lithophane bundle. Create the model at the third-party Lithophane Makers site from a JPG or PNG (layer 0.1, first layer 0.15, size 144 × 108 mm), unzip the five STLs and drag them into Orca, answering Yes to load them as a multi-part object. Assign the CMYK filaments by part name, use fine layers and solid rectilinear infill, then slice; slicing takes a while.
steps: In Lithophane Makers choose the photo, set layer height 0.1, first layer 0.15 and size 144 mm × 108 mm, enter an email and click Create .stl.
Unzip the download to get 5 STL files, drag them all into Orca and choose Yes to load them as one multi-part object.
Add four filaments in Filament Management: SnapSpeed Cyan #0086D6, Vivid Magenta #EC008C, Lemon Yellow #FCE300 and Pure White #FFFFFF.
In the Objects list give each part the color named in its file name.
In Global settings use a 0.4 mm nozzle (0.2 mm gives better detail), layer height 0.08 or 0.1 mm and first layer 0.15 mm.
Set top shell layers to 3, sparse infill density 100% and pattern Rectilinear, then slice and be patient.

settings.advice: Use 0.08 or 0.1 mm for color lithophanes.
Set 0.15 mm to match the generator's first layer.
Set to 3 for lithophanes.
Use 100% so light passes through solid, evenly layered color.
Use Rectilinear for lithophanes.
0.2 mm gives finer image detail; 0.4 mm works with less detail.

entries.title: Exporting Snapmaker Orca log files for support
entries.summary: Many Snapmaker Orca errors are written to its log, so sending logs helps support find the root cause faster. On Windows open the main menu and choose Help > Export Logs; on macOS use Help > Export Logs in the menu bar. For U1 connection or camera problems, export the printer's logs as well and note roughly when the problem occurred.
steps: Windows: Menu > Help > Export Logs.
macOS: Help > Export Logs.
For printer-side issues also export the U1 logs and send both with the approximate time of the error.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca how to export log files
Snapmaker Orca camera fails to open

entries.title: Applying a Full Spectrum mixed color: paint regions or change a whole object's filament
entries.summary: Save a mix first (it appears in Filament Management > Color Mixing). To color only part of a model, open Color Painting and paint with the mixed color. To color the whole model, use Change Filament and choose the mix; regions already painted keep their paint. Then enable layer subdivision for smoother blending and slice.
steps: Partial: on the Prepare page select the model and click Color Painting in the top bar (or the painting icon next to the object under Process > Objects).
Partial: in the Filaments section of the painting menu choose the mixed color and paint the area.
Whole model: right-click the model (or its color block in the Objects list), pick Change Filament and choose the mixed color.
Enable Subdivide Mix Layer for painted mixes, plus Full domain when the whole model uses the mix, then slice and send to the U1.

entries.title: Color Mixing Match: converting a multicolor model to Full Spectrum mixes automatically
entries.summary: Color Mixing Match (Orca V2.3.6+) computes mixing ratios that approximate a multicolor model's original colors with your filaments and applies them to the model; it is meant for models with 4 or more colors. Auto mode assumes the official Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum bundle with each color between 0% and 70%; Manual mode uses up to 4 filaments from your own Filament list. Afterwards select the 0.10 mm color-mixing process for the U1 and slice.
steps: Open the multicolor model in Orca V2.3.6 or later.
Under Process enable Objects and give every object a specific filament instead of Default, or matching may skip it.
Click Color Mixing Match next to Filament Management.
Choose Match Mode: Auto (official bundle; V2.4.0+ lets you pick its colors) or Manual, then set up to 4 filaments in Filament Setup.
Click Start Matching and inspect the Matched view, changing Plate and View to compare before and after.
Hover each pair in Color Mapping to see its ΔE rating; a smaller ΔE is a closer match.
Click Confirm to save the mixes into Filament Management > Color Mixing and apply them to the model.
Enable Global under Process, pick 0.10mm Color Mixing @Snapmaker U1 (0.4 nozzle) as the preset, then slice and print.

entries.title: Full Spectrum color reference setup: toolhead order and base colors (F1-F4)
entries.summary: Snapmaker's color reference recipes assume a fixed loading order: Toolhead 1 Cyan (F1), Toolhead 2 Magenta (F2), Toolhead 3 Yellow (F3), Toolhead 4 White or Gray (F4) from the PLA Full Spectrum bundle. Load the spools that way, set all four project filaments to the Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum profile, and give them the matching colors in Filament Management > Filament, otherwise prints will not match the published ratios.
steps: Load cyan, magenta, yellow and white/gray into toolheads 1-4 in that order.
In Filament Management > Filament click each filament name and select Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum.
Click each color box and set Filament 1 to Cyan, 2 to Magenta, 3 to Yellow and 4 to White (or Gray).
Add mixes via Filament Management > Color Mixing > + using the ratios from the reference.
facts: White Edition colors: Cyan #00C3FF, Magenta #F54399, Yellow #FAE727, White #F5F4F2.
Gray Edition colors: Cyan #08ABFB, Magenta #D93B90, Yellow #F9ED3D, Gray #9199A4.
Best results come from two base colors, each between 33% and 67% of the mix.

entries.title: Finding a Full Spectrum mix: 39-color reference table and 177-color swatch print
entries.summary: Orca's preview can't fully predict printed color, so Snapmaker publishes swatches calibrated from real prints. Either look up one of 39 common mixes in the reference table, or print the 177-color swatch 3MF in Orca V2.3.6+ with all four filaments set to Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum, find the physical swatch you like and read its recipe under Filament Management > Color Mixing in that file. Recreate the ratio in Ratio or Cycle Mode, paint, print and fine-tune.
facts: Example: color A54 is 50% F1 Cyan plus 50% F3 Yellow (a green); in Ratio Mode pick Cyan and Yellow and drag to 50/50.
The 39-color table includes each pure color, every two-color pair at 20, 33, 50, 67 and 80%, four three-color mixes at 34/33/33, and A155 with all four at 25%.
The 177-swatch print takes a long time but covers far more ratios.
Monitors, lighting, geometry and settings cause differences, so print a test swatch before the final model.

entries.title: Full Spectrum Gradient mode: two-color gradients along the model height
entries.summary: Gradient Mode creates a continuous transition between exactly two filament colors over the model's height. Pick the two colors and use Swap Filaments to reverse the direction; the bottom of the color block corresponds to the bed end of the model and the top to its top. Preview the estimate in Mix Effect, and after slicing switch the Preview page to an orthographic view to judge the gradient.
facts: Mixing Recommendations suggest gradient pairs based on the colors you have configured.

entries.title: Full Spectrum Match mode: mixing toward a target color with a minimum mix ratio
entries.summary: Match Mode works out the ratio of your available filaments that comes closest to a target color. Click the Target Color block and use Define Custom Colours, or type a Hex value and press Enter. Fine-tune the generated ratio with the slider while watching the layer Preview and Mix Effect, and raise Min Mix Ratio so no single color is reduced to a tiny share, which keeps the print closer to the prediction.
facts: If unsure of a target, the Mixing Recommendations section proposes reachable colors and ratios from your filaments.
V2.3.5 fixed 25% suggestions still appearing when Min Mix Ratio was 30%.
V2.3.6 fixed an incorrect ratio display after switching tabs in the Color Mixing window.

entries.title: Full Spectrum color mixing on the U1: how it works and what you need
entries.summary: Full Spectrum is Snapmaker Orca's color-mixing workflow for the U1. Instead of only switching between solid filaments, it stacks alternating thin layers of different colors along Z so the eye sees a blend (red with blue reads as purple, yellow with blue as green). Thinner layers and more frequent alternation give smoother results. Use Orca V2.3.6 or later, current firmware, and translucent high-TD filaments such as the Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum bundle.
facts: Create mixes under Filament Management > Color Mixing (+ button) with Ratio, Cycle, Match or Gradient mode; Color Mixing Match converts a whole multicolor model.
Mixed colors are virtual: the U1 still prints with at most 4 physical filaments, without extra hardware.
Mix filaments of the same family (PLA with PLA); pairs like PLA with PETG or PVA can look very different from the preview.
Moderately to fully translucent filaments blend best; opaque ones weaken the effect and make layer transitions obvious.
Avoid extreme ratios; Orca warns when a mix becomes too unbalanced.
Experienced users sometimes try PLA with TPU for special textures, but results are experimental.
Final color depends on filament, geometry, settings and lighting, so it is not meant for exact or repeatable color matching.
The feature started in the community and was refined jointly with Snapmaker.

entries.title: Full Spectrum Ratio and Cycle modes: mixing by proportion or by layer sequence
entries.summary: Ratio Mode blends 2 or 3 base filaments: choose them under Filament Selection, drag the ratio slider and check the layer-stack Preview and the Mix Effect swatch; Mixing Recommendations suggest combinations from your configured filaments. Cycle Mode takes a typed sequence of filament index numbers (confirm with Enter) that repeats layer after layer, for example yellow and blue alternating for a green, and lists the resulting share of each color.
facts: Use the + and - buttons in Ratio Mode to add or remove base colors (2 to 3 supported).
In Cycle Mode Subdivide Mix Layer has no effect, so your sequence is preserved and layers never drop below the nozzle's minimum height.
The preview only estimates the color; translucency, layer height and other settings change the real result.
Click OK to save a mix; saved mixes are listed in Filament Management > Color Mixing.

entries.title: Subdivide Mix Layer, Full domain and subdivision of infill for smoother color mixing
entries.summary: Thick layers make mixed colors band and gradients break up, so Orca can slice mixed regions with finer sublayers. Turn on Global and Advanced, then in Process > Multimaterial > Color Mixing tick Subdivide Mix Layer for painted mixed areas, add Full domain when large regions or whole objects use a mix via Change Filament, and Apply Subdivision to Infill so infill inside mixed areas follows the wall layering (more tool changes and time).

settings.advice: Lower toward 0.08-0.1 mm for mixed colors; thinner layers alternate colors more often and show less striping.
Shown as 'Subdivide all mix layers' in this build; enable to slice mixed-color regions with finer sublayers.
Shown as 'Full domain for all mixes'; enable when big areas or whole objects use a mixed color so the entire mixed region is subdivided.
Enable for translucent filaments where inner color shows through; costs extra tool changes and print time.

facts: Also lower the base layer height in Process > Quality > Layer height; 0.08 mm is recommended.
Without Full domain only painted mixed areas are subdivided; regions colored via Change Filament keep the normal layer height.
Mixes made in Cycle Mode are never subdivided.
V2.3.5+ warns if Variable Layer Height and Subdivide Mix Layer are enabled together.
V2.4.1 fixed the first layer being subdivided and brims disappearing with Subdivide plus Full Domain.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca network test tool (Help > Open Network Test)
entries.summary: From V2.2.1 Snapmaker Orca includes a network test for diagnosing device connection, login and upload problems. Open the menu, then Help > Open Network Test, run the relevant test and send a screenshot of the results to Snapmaker technical support.
facts: Test LAN Device: with the printer in LAN mode, enable it, enter the device IP, click Confirm and read the log.
Test Cloud Server: with the printer in Cloud mode, enable it and read the log output.
Test Login API: checks the login interface when you cannot sign in.
Test Upload API: checks the file-upload interface when sending print files fails.
The connection troubleshooting guide uses Start Test Multi-Thread with the printer's IP.
The V2.2.1 notes say the tool may still need tuning in some scenarios.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca quick start for Artisan, Snapmaker 2.0 and J1/J1s
entries.summary: Get Snapmaker Orca from Snapmaker's website or from the Assets section of a GitHub release and install it. The Setup Wizard appears on first install to choose login region, printers with nozzles, and filaments; reopen it later from Help > Setup Wizard. Then create a New Project, drag in or import a model, select printer, filament and process presets, edit as needed and click Slice plate. Start the job over Wi-Fi or from a USB flash drive and watch first-layer adhesion.
facts: Printers and filaments shown in the preset lists can be changed later with the edit icon beside Printer or Filament.
A print can be started from Orca or from the machine's touchscreen.
For Snapmaker 2.0, Artisan and J1, Orca's Wi-Fi sending relies on Luban being open and connected to the machine.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.1.1 and V2.1.2 release highlights
entries.summary: V2.1.1 (Nov 6, 2025) bundled profile version 02.02.39.02 and let the U1 accept M220 B and M220 R speed commands during a print. It added per-material bed temperatures by plate type, Cloud Mode download progress, firmware compatibility checks and region-mismatch warnings for PIN binding. V2.1.2 (Nov 26, 2025) fixed G-code containing characters the printer couldn't read under European language settings, and connection failures on PCs without Unicode language support.
facts: V2.1.1 fixes: Snapmaker 2.0 bed temperature shown as 0 °C, filament mapping on the device page, weak-network handling, first-launch monitoring failures.
V2.1.1 Cloud Mode fixes: intermittent failures uploading or printing large files and an MQTT termination popup.
V2.1.1 improved filament mapping for printing local files and encrypted real-time monitoring data.
V2.1.1 known issues: UI problems on Ubuntu 22.04 and occasional calculation errors when slicing with several filaments.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.2.1 release highlights (OrcaSlicer 2.3.1 base, network test)
entries.summary: V2.2.1 (Dec 31, 2025) merged upstream OrcaSlicer work through the official 2.3.1 release, so its slicing features match OrcaSlicer 2.3.1. It added error reporting during use, a User Experience Improvement Program, support for the printer's AI detection and a network testing tool under Help > Open Network Test.
facts: Binding and connecting with the printer were streamlined; device control and slice uploads became more reliable on unstable networks.
Switching between Cloud and LAN binding modes or logging out on the touchscreen is handled more smoothly; camera start-up improved.
Estimated print times are more accurate in certain cases.
Known issues: the network test may need work in some situations and the Linux version was not yet fully compatible.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.2.3 Beta and V2.2.4: Rib wipe tower fix, PETG HF/TPU 95A HF
entries.summary: V2.2.3 Beta (Jan 29, 2026) and V2.2.4 (Feb 9, 2026) fixed Rib wipe tower extrusions or travel leaving the build plate, Bambu Lab printers that couldn't be selected on Prepare, and filament-sync bugs: Snapspeed PLA arriving with density 0 (blocking jobs) and Generic PETG getting a 0 °C first-layer bed temperature on the PEI steel sheet (poor first layers). Both added hot updates for presets and web resources and separate update channels per region.

settings.advice: Rib towers could print paths off the plate before V2.2.3/V2.2.4; update Orca if Rib tower moves leave the bed.

facts: V2.2.4 added a brim chamfer for the prime tower to steady the Rib tower.
V2.2.4 introduced PETG HF and TPU 95A HF materials, each with a Snapmaker and a Generic profile.
V2.2.4 fixes: launch failure on some Windows 11 PCs, process migration when changing printer model, device reporting the wrong IP, frequent forced logins, crashes.
V2.2.4 speeds up monitoring and file uploads when PC and printer share a local network.
Both versions improved the warning about spiral lift near the edge of the build plate.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.0 release highlights (Model Library)
entries.summary: V2.3.0 (Mar 24, 2026) added the Model Library, where you can download 3MF or G-code files and start prints online (some creators share only G-code). It also added new official material types and color choices for third-party materials.
facts: Fixed a crash with filaments assigned to a transparent channel.
Sporadic slow HTTP requests and wrong page jumps when changing, adding or deleting printer models were fixed.
Fixed U1 disconnecting in LAN mode.
Polymaker filament names were corrected.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.1 and hotfix V2.3.12: new nozzles, Graphic Effect Plate
entries.summary: V2.3.1 (Apr 15, 2026) added 0.2, 0.6 and 0.8 mm nozzles, a Graphic Effect Plate option, and Smooth High Temp Plate is now called Smooth PEI Plate. It added Silk Dual-Color PLA profiles and plate selection for Model Library Print Now, and dropped the camera countdown in Cloud Mode and the 5-minute camera limit in LAN Mode. Hotfix V2.3.12 (Apr 17, 2026) let users map extra preset filaments when more than 4 were available on Print Preprocessing.

settings.advice: Bed temperature used when the Graphic Effect Plate (added in V2.3.1) is selected.
Applies to the U1 Smooth PEI Plate, which was called Smooth High Temp Plate before V2.3.1.

facts: V2.3.1 fixes: failed web resource and process profile updates, Cloud Mode devices receiving piles of stale server messages, some U1s not reading filament info after connecting.
V2.3.12 installs as a configuration package: restart, accept Configuration update, restart (or Help > Check for Web Resource Updates).

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.3: Full Spectrum color mixing introduced, prime tower ribs
entries.summary: V2.3.3 (Jun 1, 2026) introduced Full Spectrum color mixing for the U1 with Ratio, Cycle, Match and Gradient modes and the options Subdivide mixing layers, Full domain and Apply subdivision to infill. Prime tower ribs are now constrained to a square footprint using quadratic programming for better stability, and local-file printing assigns filaments to nozzles correctly even when density is 0.
facts: Full Spectrum needs Orca V2.3.3+ and current firmware; at launch translucent high-TD filaments such as Polymaker Panchroma PLA translucent yellow/cyan/magenta/grey were suggested.
Fixes: first prime tower layer exceeding limits; 3MF files with more filaments than extruders failing to save, slice or map correctly.
Fixes: Upload and Upload and Print unavailable while port 13619 was used by another process; mapping failures when printing from the built-in model library.
Full Spectrum began in the community; Reddit user beybladetable (Ratdoux) is credited as its original developer.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.4 bug fixes (painted domes, fuzzy skin painting, first-layer infill)
entries.summary: V2.3.4 (Jun 11, 2026) was a fix release. It repaired filament mapping on Print Preprocessing when Generic Support for PLA was chosen, slicing of painted dome-shaped models that produced maze patterns, islands or missing geometry, Fuzzy Skin painting that skipped painted areas and hit unpainted ones, and misaligned sparse infill on the first layer.

settings.advice: If painted fuzzy skin appears in the wrong places, update to V2.3.4 or later.

facts: Infill options under Process > Multimaterial > Filament for Features were enabled again.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.5: filament sync, Top Cover controls, color mixing checks
entries.summary: V2.3.5 (Jul 15, 2026) added Top Cover controls, syncing filament info from the printer via Match Mapping or Direct Override, an official filament color library with dual-color filaments, Snapmaker PVA support and refined Snapmaker PLA-CF and TPU profiles. In Color Mixing, incompatible filament combinations now block slicing with an error, and a warning appears when Variable Layer Height and Subdivide Mix Layer are both on.

settings.advice: Can be enabled without turning off the wipe tower from V2.3.5; it is unchecked by default.
Avoid combining mix-layer subdivision with Variable Layer Height; V2.3.5+ warns when both are active.

facts: The wipe tower outer wall now has an opening.
Fixes: wrong filament types after reopening a saved project with fewer filaments; 25% suggestions despite a 30% Match minimum; subdivision hitting single-color areas with Full Domain.
Fixes: wrong wipe tower filament estimates, wipe tower brim overlapping the model brim, hot-updated resources not loading, unresponsive startup on some PCs.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.3.6: time-lapse export, AI detection, Color Mixing Match
entries.summary: V2.3.6 (Aug 31, 2026) added time-lapse video export (printer firmware V1.6.0+; tick Time-lapse in print preferences before sending, download after the print), Spaghetti and Foreign Object Detection preferences, one-click auto-zoom/pan, Color Mixing Match Mapping for models with many colors, Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum profiles, and a color-mixing preset named 0.10mm Color Mixing @Snapmaker U1 (0.4 nozzle).

settings.advice: Never leave it at 0; from V2.3.6 Orca refuses to slice in that case.

facts: PLA Full Spectrum: use a 0.4 mm or smaller hot end with layers of 0.1 mm or less; bigger values leave visible layer lines.
With several filaments needing different bed temperatures, the higher temperature is now used.
Slicing is blocked with an error if a filament's flow ratio is 0.
Going from Prepare to Preview slices only the selected plate again (V2.3.5 sliced every plate).
A memory guard now warns before full-bed slicing; crashes with Full Bed Arrangement, emoji or special-character filenames on Windows, and repeated G-code import were fixed.
Viewport culling of off-screen geometry improves responsiveness; filament-sync color matching was improved.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.4.0: new U1 filaments, high-flow hot end, merged presets
entries.summary: V2.4.0 (Sep 21, 2026); update printer firmware to V2.0.0 or later first. It added selection highlighting, a level-of-detail renderer, manual color choice in Color Mixing Match Auto mode, High-Flow Hot End parameters for some filaments and profiles, six new U1 filaments and extra colors for many others. Presets sharing a layer height but differing only in quality label (e.g. Fine, High Quality) were merged into Standard presets.

settings.advice: Filled with a default model automatically from V2.4.0 when small area flow compensation is enabled.
Don't set 0 with Tree Hybrid supports on versions before V2.4.0; slicing could hang at 70%.

facts: New U1 filaments and nozzles: Snapmaker TPU and PEBA 90A (0.4/0.6/0.8 mm), PLA Glow (0.6/0.8), PLA Rainbow (0.2-0.8), Support for PLA (0.2), PETG-CF (0.6/0.8).
Turning on small area flow compensation now fills in a default Flow Compensation Model.
OpenSSL upgraded to 3.5.7; large-model slicing and G-code upload/print stability improved.

Fixes: slicing stuck at 70% with base pattern spacing 0 and Tree Hybrid; crash for 3MFs that once used Organic support; colors lost importing OrcaSlicer multi-color G-code; wrong layer change markers.
Fixes: Windows connection status after the screen turned off, re-login prompt after 24 h, macOS white screens and Snapmaker Space links, calibration failing on a parameter type mismatch.
Fixed missing official PETG HF colors and an old palette for the 0.4 mm nozzle.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.4.1: official filament bed temperature changes per U1 plate
entries.summary: V2.4.1 revised official filament bed temperatures per plate type. A 0 °C value now means the filament isn't supported on that plate: PETG Translucent, PLA CF and PVA can no longer be used on the Graphic Effect Steel Plate. Several PLA variants and PVA got higher values. It also fixed G-code bed temperatures not matching the filament settings and a Textured PEI label appearing for a cold steel plate.

settings.advice: 0 means the filament is unsupported on the Graphic Effect plate; switch plates rather than forcing a temperature.
Smooth PEI plate on the U1; since V2.4.1 PVA uses 70 °C and Snapspeed PLA (0.6/0.8 mm) 65 °C.
Textured PEI plate; since V2.4.1 PVA uses 70 °C and PLA Matte (0.6 mm) 65 °C.

facts: Now disabled on the Graphic Effect plate: PETG Translucent (was 80 °C), PLA CF (was 65 °C), PVA (was 65 °C).
PVA on Smooth PEI and Textured PEI: 65 to 70 °C.
PLA Matte 0.6 mm: Graphic Effect 0 to 65 °C, Textured PEI 45 to 65 °C; PLA Matte 0.8 mm Graphic Effect 0 to 65 °C.
Graphic Effect plate 65 to 70 °C: PLA Wood 0.4 mm, PLA Translucent, Support for PLA, PLA Glow 0.4 mm; PLA Wood 0.6/0.8 mm went from 0 to 70 °C.
PLA Snapspeed 0.6/0.8 mm on Smooth PEI: 55 to 65 °C.
Ten new PETG HF colors (SKUs 34152-34156 and 34171-34175), e.g. Chestnut Red #7E2D40, Sage Green #A3B2A4, Navy Blue #1A4E8A.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.4.1: notable slicing and app bug fixes
entries.summary: V2.4.1 fixed many slicing defects. Notable ones: Pressure Advance still active after being disabled, the cooling fan causing a Z height drop, gap fill printed before outer walls, the first layer ignoring Inner/Outer/Inner wall order, the first layer being subdivided with Subdivide Mixing Layers, and colors lost or bleeding after slicing multi-color 3MF files.

settings.advice: Before V2.4.1 PA could still apply after being turned off; update if disabling it has no effect.
Inner/Outer/Inner is respected on the first layer too from V2.4.1.
Was ignored before V2.4.1; update if base layers still use the interface filament.
Keep enabled so the first layer stays unsplit when mixed-color layer subdivision is on.

facts: Supports: interfaces now form continuous surfaces via a new overhang classification; missing tree supports, Organic tree plus raft empty layers, lost contact areas with Variable Layer Height and flat models without supports were fixed.
First layer: elephant foot compensation deleting the first layer on special models, missing first layer after a 45° rotation, and slow-layer count offset with a raft were fixed.

Multi-color: missing colors for filament IDs above 16, lost brim with painted brim plus Subdivide and Full Domain, per-object skirt working on one object only, skirt overlapping the prime tower skirt.

Other: a prompt for unexpected patterns at 100% sparse infill, gaps with External bridge density above 100%, Avoid interface filament for base ignored, Boolean ops on mirrored objects, emboss Lock rotation.
App: optional cache clearing in the Windows uninstaller (off by default), Linux login persistence, time-lapse download stuck at Waiting for device upload, Linux Z camera-fit shortcut.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.4.1: prime tower rework and new tower interface parameters
entries.summary: V2.4.1 (Oct 28, 2026) reworked the prime tower: filaments are auto-grouped by adhesion type so incompatible materials don't share a section, the toolhead detours around the tower and enters through the outer-wall opening on tool changes, the default position moved from top-left to left-center, and the pre-slice preview now matches the sliced tower size. New filament parameters, visible in Developer mode (Preferences > Developer mode), tune the tower interface.

settings.advice: Set per filament; from V2.4.1 the larger of this and the Prime Tower page value is used.
Values other than 100% caused gaps before V2.4.1; the first layer now always prints purge lines at 100%.
Moved to Developer mode in V2.4.1.

facts: Interface Layer Pre-extrusion Distance: an extra path along the tower's outer edge before printing that builds nozzle pressure for better interface adhesion.
Interface Layer Pre-extrusion Length: extra filament pushed after the loading retraction; 10 mm retraction plus a 10 mm setting gives 20 mm in total.
Interface Layer Print Temperature: nozzle temperature for the tower interface; -1 uses the filament's highest recommended temperature; needs Enable Tower Interface Features.
Adhesiveness Category: different values put materials in separate tower zones, e.g. PLA 100 and PETG 300 places PLA lower and PETG higher to stop collapse.
New Prime Tower options: Cool Down from Interface Boost During Prime Tower plus Enable Tower Interface Features (both Developer mode), and Internal Ribs (Advanced mode).
Brim chamfer and Max chamfer width were removed; No Sparse Layer is now a Developer-mode option.
First-layer purge lines always use 100% spacing; non-SEMM towers now honor per-filament minimum purge, using the larger of the filament and tower values.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca V2.4.1: support, bridge and first-layer default changes
entries.summary: V2.4.1 changed defaults: Bridge Flow 0.8 to 1.0, External Bridge Density 80 to 100 (limit raised to 120%), Max Bridge Length 10 mm to 0 mm so bridges get full support, a 1° minimum support threshold angle and First Layer Expansion -1 (Auto). It added a tree Support Transition type with its own speed and flow, a Minimum Support Contact Area, First Layer Travel acceleration and jerk, and Top/Bottom Paint Penetration Layers to stop light/dark color bleed into infill.

settings.advice: Default raised from 0.8 to 1.0 in V2.4.1; reduce only if bridges sag from too much material.
Default now 100 (was 80) and may go up to 120% to close gaps on bridge surfaces.
Default now 0 mm so bridges are fully supported; raise it if you prefer unsupported bridging.
Can now be set as low as 1°.
Lightning isn't supported with Organic style; Rectilinear is used instead.
In multi-filament prints use a soluble material or Default for the support base; other choices trigger a warning.

facts: New warnings: Organic support with a Lightning base pattern falls back to Rectilinear; Organic with Support Wall Loops 2 and a non-default/hollow base also warns.
Multi-filament warnings: a non-soluble Support/Raft base can be reset to Default; PLA/PETG supporting each other with non-default base or interface patterns prompts a reset.
Projects saved by V2.4.1 show an error prompt when opened in older Snapmaker Orca versions.
The G-code template was changed to avoid nozzle collisions with the print during sequential printing, filament changes or pauses.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca release history and latest version
entries.summary: Snapmaker advises always running the newest Snapmaker Orca. According to the release notes index, the latest version is V2.4.1, released 2026-10-28. Before installing V2.4.0 or later, update the printer firmware to V2.0.0 or newer.
facts: 2026 releases: 2.4.1 on Oct 28, 2.4.0 on Sep 21, 2.3.6 on Aug 31, 2.3.5 on Jul 15, 2.3.4 on Jun 11, 2.3.3 on Jun 1.
Earlier 2026 releases: 2.3.12 hotfix on Apr 17, 2.3.1 on Apr 15, 2.3.0 on Mar 24, 2.2.4 on Feb 9, 2.2.3 Beta on Jan 29.
2025 releases: 2.2.1 on Dec 31, 2.1.5 on Dec 16, 2.1.2 on Nov 26, 2.1.1 on Nov 6.
V2.2.1 brought Snapmaker Orca in line with official OrcaSlicer V2.3.1.

entries.title: U1 camera won't open in Orca: 'Device not online' or 'Failed to start camera monitor'
entries.summary: When the U1 camera won't open in Orca, the cause is usually a broken Orca-to-printer connection, an unstable network (typical in Cloud Mode), or a bug in older Orca builds. Choose the fix by the message shown.
symptoms: Message 'Camera not on'
Message 'Device not online'
Message 'Failed to start camera monitor'
An error showing a long IPv6 URL ending in /server/files/camera/monitor.jpg
causes: Abnormal connection between Orca and the U1
Unstable network, especially in Cloud Mode
Known bug in some older Orca versions
steps: 'Device not online': restart Orca and the computer and reconnect; if it continues, export U1 and Orca logs and contact support.
'Failed to start camera monitor' in Cloud Mode: suspect the network; compare stability using a phone hotspot.
'Failed to start camera monitor' in LAN Mode: export both sets of logs and send them with the approximate time of the error.
Long IPv6 address error: update Orca; the wiki points to a beta build containing the camera fix.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca camera fails to open

entries.title: Binding a U1 to Snapmaker Orca in Cloud Mode (PIN code or nearby search)
entries.summary: Cloud Mode routes Orca's traffic through Snapmaker's servers, so the computer and the U1 do not have to share a LAN. You can bind with the PIN code shown on the touchscreen, by searching for nearby devices and approving on the printer, or by scanning the QR code with the Snapmaker App. The printer's region must match the region chosen in Orca, and the PIN must be used before its 180 s countdown runs out.
steps: Connect the printer and computer to the internet and power on the U1.
On the touchscreen open Settings > Account and check that the region matches the software region.
Log in to your account in Snapmaker Orca.
Click Add Device on the Home page or the Devices page.
Choose PIN Code Binding and enter the current PIN before the 180 s timer expires; a correct PIN binds automatically.
Or choose Search Device, pick the printer, and grant the authorization request on the touchscreen.
facts: In very dim or bright light, tap the touchscreen to enlarge the QR code before scanning it with the app.
A green indicator on the Home/Device page means communication is working; gray means disconnected.
Orca V2.1.1 added an alert when the PIN-binding region does not match.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: Orca or Snapmaker App can't connect to the U1 in Cloud Mode (Cloud Connection Error)
entries.summary: Sort the problem into one of three cases: the U1 has no IP address; it has an IP but the region or the PC's network blocks it; or it worked before and now fails with 'device connection failed'. The U1 only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, and firmware, Orca and the App should all be up to date (on 2025-12-18 that was firmware 0.9.4, Orca 2.1.5 and App 2.1.5).
symptoms: Orca cannot discover or connect to the U1 through the cloud
Cloud Connection Error icon in the top-right corner of the touchscreen
Snapmaker App cannot find or bind the U1
causes: Printer has no IP address (5 GHz network, router compatibility)
Printer region differs from the software region
Computer firewall, VPN or proxy blocking Orca
Stale Wi-Fi session after a timeout
steps: Open Settings > Wi-Fi on the touchscreen and check for an IP address; without one, enable Maximum Compatibility and retry, or test on a 2.4 GHz phone hotspot.
Set Settings > Account > Region (International for anywhere outside Mainland China) and use the same region in Orca.
Make sure the computer's firewall lets Orca access the network and that no VPN or proxy is active.
If it used to work, hold a finger on the saved Wi-Fi entry for over 3 s so the printer forgets it, then join again.
If nothing helps, export U1 and Orca logs and send them to support with the time of the failure.
Success: the printer shows an IP and Orca displays Connected in its top-right corner.
facts: If the firmware can't update online, use the local update method described in the U1 firmware release notes.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca disconnects from the U1 in Cloud Mode: router, PC and server checks
entries.summary: In Cloud Mode Orca's commands travel from the computer over the internet to Snapmaker's cloud server and on to the printer, so both ends need working internet. Check the router first, then the computer's own connection, then the server link using Orca's network test (V2.2.1 or later).
symptoms: Orca shows the U1 as disconnected in Cloud Mode
Other devices on the same Wi-Fi also lag
causes: Overheating or unstable router
Router WAN/internet connection down
Computer on the wrong network or cable unplugged
Communication problems with the cloud server
steps: Touch the router: warm is normal; if too hot to hold your hand on, unplug it for 5 minutes, then power it back on.
Check the router's WAN light, or browse external websites from a phone or PC on that network.
Confirm the computer is on the right Wi-Fi network, or that its Ethernet cable and wired connection are active.
In Orca open Help > Open Network Test, click Start Test Multi-Thread, enter the U1's IP address and review the result.
If the problem remains, export U1 and Orca logs and send them with screenshots or videos to support.
Afterwards rebind via PIN code to confirm the connection works.

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca disconnects from the U1 in LAN Mode: router, PC and printer checks
entries.summary: In LAN Mode data stays local, flowing computer to router to printer without the internet, so test each link. After checking the router and the computer's connection, confirm the U1 still has an IP address, ping it from the computer, and restart or factory-reset the printer if it still won't connect.
steps: Check the router for overheating (cool it for 5 minutes if it's too hot) and confirm it works.
Make sure the computer's Wi-Fi or wired connection is active on the same network as the printer.
On the touchscreen open Settings > Wi-Fi and look for an IP address at the bottom.
If none is shown, enable Maximum Compatibility at the bottom of the Wi-Fi page and tap Scan again.
If the U1 has an IP but Orca still can't connect, run ping with that IP from the computer.
Restart the printer, or do a Factory Reset if it still fails.
If unresolved, export U1 and Orca logs plus screenshots for support; afterwards rebind by IP address.
facts: V2.3.0 fixed a bug where the U1 disconnected in LAN mode.
V2.2.4 fixed the device reporting a different IP than its real one, which broke material retrieval and printing from Print Preprocessing.

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0529-0000-0014: Unable to parse move 'G1 X-nan Y-nan'
entries.summary: This error appears when a G-code file is started from the touchscreen. With more than four filaments in a project, Orca could map filaments to the wrong extruders, so slicing math produced invalid coordinates. Trim the project to four filaments or point the wipe tower at a specific filament, then slice again.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows Unable to parse move 'G1 X-nan Y-nan' (code 0003-0529-0000-0014) when starting a file
causes: Project uses more than four filaments, causing wrong extruder mapping and undefined slicing results
steps: Move the model on the plate and slice again.
In the Multimaterial settings change Wipe tower from the default to a specific filament.
Delete filaments after the first four, or merge them into one of the first four.
If it still happens, send the .3mf file to Snapmaker support.

settings.advice: Pick a specific filament instead of the default to avoid the X-nan error on projects with many filaments.

facts: V2.3.3 fixed several problems with 3MF files holding more filaments than extruders: unsaved extra filaments, failed slicing and wrong mapping on Print Preprocessing.

sources.title: Unable to parse move 'G1 X-nan Y-nan'

entries.title: Binding a U1 to Snapmaker Orca in LAN Mode (IP address or nearby search)
entries.summary: LAN Mode keeps all communication on the local network without any cloud service, which suits confidential models or places without internet; sending files, managing jobs and camera monitoring still work. The computer and printer must be on the same network. Turn it on at Settings > LAN Mode > Enable LAN Mode on the printer, then bind in Orca by IP address or by nearby-device search and confirm on the touchscreen.
steps: Put the U1 and the computer on the same network.
On the touchscreen go to Settings > LAN Mode and enable LAN Mode.
In Orca click Add Device and either type the printer's IP address or search for nearby devices.
Approve the binding prompt on the U1 touchscreen.
facts: An account login is needed before binding in Cloud Mode but not in LAN Mode.
The Snapmaker App can also bind in LAN Mode by IP address or nearby search.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: Using the built-in Model Library in Snapmaker Orca (Download & Open vs Print Now)
entries.summary: Since V2.3.0 Snapmaker Orca has a Model Library: click Model in the left navigation of the home page to browse models Snapmaker recommends. Each model page has photos, a print profile (time, nozzle, filaments, plates) and a description. Download & Open fetches the 3MF and opens it on the Prepare page for editing; Print Now prints the creator's G-code as-is through Print Preprocessing and only works in Cloud Mode.
facts: If Download & Open is greyed out, the author only shared G-code, so use Print Now.
Print Now does not allow custom settings: choose the printer, edit material info, check preferences, then Send.
Print Now needs the printer bound in Cloud Mode (PIN code or nearby-device search).
Since V2.3.1 Print Now offers plate selection on the Print Preprocessing page.
V2.3.3 fixed filament mapping failures when printing directly from the model library.

sources.title: Model Library Guide for Snapmaker Orca

entries.title: Multi-color printing on the U1: filament list, painting tools and filament mapping
entries.summary: A multi-color U1 job takes three steps: add a filament per color, assign or paint them on the model, then slice and print. In the left filament panel use + and - to add or remove filaments and set each one's color and type. Assign a filament per part in the Object List or by right-clicking the part, or paint with the Circle, Sphere, Triangle, Height Range, Fill and Gap Fill tools. When sending, the printer matches each project filament to a loaded one of the same type and closest color, which you can change.
facts: New filaments are added to the end of the list and - removes the last one.
Filaments loaded and edited on the printer's touchscreen can be mapped into the project list automatically (Sync Filament).
Filament type can come from the printer's loaded filaments or from user or system presets.
In the Edit Filament mapping view the top row shows the model's filaments and the bottom row the matched filaments in the printer.
V2.3.5 added filament sync with two options, Match Mapping and Direct Override.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: U1 keeps disconnecting when several Snapmaker Orca instances connect at once
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca does not support more than one instance being connected to the same U1 at the same time. When two or more copies, on one computer or on different machines in the network, connect to one printer, the link keeps dropping and reconnecting; the Wi-Fi icon in Orca flips between red and green.
symptoms: Wi-Fi indicator in Orca alternates between red and green
Repeated disconnects and reconnects to the U1
causes: More than one Orca instance connected to the same U1 simultaneously
steps: Keep a single Orca instance connected to each U1.
Close or disconnect other Orca copies on the same computer or network that point at that U1.
facts: V2.4.1 fixed connection status getting out of sync in multi-process LAN mode.

sources.title: Connection instability when running multiple Snapmaker Orca instances

entries.title: Network ports Snapmaker Orca uses to reach the U1 (firewall and router rules)
entries.summary: If a firewall, router or security tool blocks Snapmaker Orca from talking to the U1, allow these protocols. The HTTP/HTTPS API uses TCP 80, 443 and 8080 in both Cloud and LAN Mode; MQTT uses TCP 1884 in LAN Mode; MQTTS uses TCP 8883 in both modes; Bonjour device discovery uses UDP 5353 in both modes.
facts: HTTP/HTTPS API: TCP 80 / 443 / 8080, Cloud and LAN Mode.
MQTT: TCP 1884, LAN Mode only.
MQTTS: TCP 8883, Cloud and LAN Mode.
Bonjour: UDP 5353, Cloud and LAN Mode.
Before V2.3.3, Upload and Upload and Print were greyed out when another program occupied local port 13619; V2.3.3 fixed this.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca with the U1: install, setup wizard, slicing and sending a job
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca is Snapmaker's Orca-based slicer with extra U1 features such as remote monitoring and device control. On first launch choose a login region, the printer and nozzle (Snapmaker U1 by default) and the filaments to list, then sign in by email with a code or password. Import a model, pick printer, filament and process presets, click Slice Plate (or Slice All), then Print to upload, upload-and-print, or export G-code.
steps: Download from snapmaker.com/snapmaker-orca (Linux builds come from GitHub) and install.
In the first-start wizard select login region, printer/nozzle and the filaments you want in the preset list; these can be changed later.
Register or log in (email + verification code or email + password); registration needs acceptance of the User Agreement and Privacy Policy.
Create a project on the home page and add models via File > Import, the first toolbar icon, or drag and drop.
Choose the printer and nozzle, the filament type and the process preset (quality, strength, speed).
Click Slice Plate (Slice All for multi-plate files); the preview then shows filament use, colors and estimated time.
Click Print and choose Upload (file only), Upload and Print (pick printer, edit filament mapping and preferences, then Send), or Export G-code File for a USB drive.
facts: System requirements: Windows 10+, macOS 12.0+, Ubuntu 20.02+ or Fedora 36+, OpenGL 2.0, 2 GHz Core 2/Athlon 64 class CPU, 8 GB RAM recommended (4 GB minimum), 2 GB free disk.
Supported import formats: .3mf, .stl, .stp, .step, .amf, .obj.
The Device button opens real-time monitoring and remote control of a bound printer.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: Remote printing, camera view and control panel for the U1 in Snapmaker Orca
entries.summary: With the U1 bound and showing a green status, slice, click Print > Upload and Print, select the printer and the loaded filaments, and click Send. The Device page then shows progress and remaining time with Pause and Stop, a Camera button for live video, and a control panel. The camera view is unavailable when the printer is off or the network is down.
facts: Control panel: home, move X/Y/Z, attach/detach toolheads, extrude/retract, nozzle and bed temperature, LED light, fan speed, and print speed (print speed only during a job).
Official RFID filaments can be viewed remotely; third-party filament details can be edited.
V2.3.1 removed the camera countdown in Cloud Mode and the 5-minute viewing limit in LAN Mode.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Quick Start Guide for U1

entries.title: 'Unrecognized Gcode type' on the U1 touchscreen: filament density 0 or unsupported type
entries.summary: This touchscreen error after sending a job from Orca comes from wrong filament settings in the slice: either a filament type the U1 can't use, or a filament Density of 0, which is not a valid value. Correct the filament profile and slice again.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows 'Unrecognized Gcode type' after a job is sent from Snapmaker Orca
causes: Density set to 0 in a filament profile
Filament type not compatible with the U1
steps: Open the 3MF project in Snapmaker Orca.
Check Density in every filament profile and replace 0 with the real value (for example 1.24 g/cm³ for Snapspeed PLA (RFID)).
Re-slice and send the job again.

settings.advice: Must be a real non-zero value (about 1.24 g/cm³ for SnapSpeed PLA); 0 makes the U1 reject the file.

facts: V2.2.4 fixed a filament-sync bug where Snapmaker PLA Snapspeed could arrive with density 0 and block sending.
V2.3.3 made local-file printing assign filaments to nozzles correctly even when density is 0.

entries.title: U1 gets no IP or drops Wi-Fi: 2.4 GHz only, Maximum Compatibility, Wi-Fi 6/7 routers
entries.summary: The U1's Wi-Fi works only on the 2.4 GHz band; 5 GHz is not supported. Some access points with advanced features, and some Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 7 routers, keep the printer from getting an IP or from reconnecting after a reboot. Turning on Maximum Compatibility on the U1, or using a simpler 2.4 GHz mode on the router, usually solves it.
symptoms: No IP address under Settings > Wi-Fi
U1 often fails to join Wi-Fi after power-up or reboot
Orca cannot find the printer
causes: 2.4 GHz band disabled on the router
802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) or 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7) features the printer's module doesn't handle
Faulty router or access point
steps: Make sure the router has its 2.4 GHz network enabled.
At the bottom of the touchscreen Wi-Fi page enable Maximum Compatibility (off by default), scan again and rejoin the network.
If the router offers a dedicated IoT network, connect the U1 to that.
Turn off Wi-Fi 6/7 for 2.4 GHz or choose a legacy mode, e.g. 802.11b/g/n mixed instead of 802.11b/g/n/ax mixed.
Check the router with a phone or PC, and test whether the U1 gets an IP from a 2.4 GHz phone hotspot.

entries.title: Updating Snapmaker Orca process presets and web resources (hot update)
entries.summary: Since V2.2.3/V2.2.4 Snapmaker Orca can hot-update its process presets and web resources without a full reinstall, with separate update channels for Mainland China and other regions. Restart Orca, accept the Configuration update dialog, and restart again once the package is installed. If no dialog appears, use Help > Check for Web Resource Updates.
steps: Restart Snapmaker Orca.
When the Configuration update dialog appears, click OK; restart after the package installs.
If no prompt shows, choose Help > Check for Web Resource Updates in the top bar, click OK, then restart.
facts: Hotfix V2.3.12 was delivered this way.
V2.3.1 and V2.3.5 fixed cases where web resources or process profiles failed to update or load after a hot update.

entries.title: Orca can't reach SM2/Artisan/J1 over Wi-Fi: Error 7, connection refused on port 5000
entries.summary: On Snapmaker 2.0, Artisan and J1 machines, Snapmaker Orca sends jobs over Wi-Fi through Luban. A 'Connection refused [Error 7]' message when connecting to 127.0.0.1 port 5000 means Luban isn't running or isn't connected to the machine, or something else holds port 5000; on a Mac this is usually the AirPlay Receiver.
symptoms: Error 7: connection refused on 127.0.0.1 port 5000
Snapmaker Orca cannot send jobs over Wi-Fi
causes: Luban closed or not connected to the machine over Wi-Fi
Port 5000 occupied by the macOS AirPlay Receiver
steps: Open Luban and connect it to the Snapmaker machine over Wi-Fi, following the Orca Wi-Fi setup guide.
On macOS switch off AirPlay Receiver in system settings, then restart Luban.
Or update Luban to 4.15 or later and change the port to 5008 under Settings > Port Settings.
If it still fails, open a support ticket with photos or videos of what you tried.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca Wi-Fi is unable to connect to SM2/Artisan/J1

entries.title: Snapmaker Artisan printer profile in Snapmaker Orca: build volume and motion limits
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca's bundled Artisan profile uses a 400 x 400 mm printable area and 400 mm printable height, with machine limits of 300 mm/s on X and 5,000 mm/s2 acceleration.
facts: Printable area 400 x 400 mm.
Printable height 400 mm.
Machine limits: X speed 300 mm/s, X acceleration 5,000 mm/s2.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca bundled profile: fdm_a400 (Artisan base)

entries.title: Snapmaker J1/J1s printer profile in Snapmaker Orca: build volume
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca's bundled J1 profile (shared IDEX base) uses a 324 x 200 mm printable area and 200 mm printable height. In duplication and mirror modes each head prints a copy, so the usable width per copy is roughly half of the X range.

settings.advice: Comes from the J1 printer preset; keep copies within half the width when using duplication or mirror mode.

facts: Printable area 324 x 200 mm in the slicer profile.
Printable height 200 mm.
Extruder clearance radius 35 mm for sequential printing checks.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca bundled profile: fdm_idex (J1 base)

entries.title: Choosing J1 IDEX duplication, mirror or backup mode from the plate name in Snapmaker Orca
entries.summary: The bundled J1 start G-code reads the plate name and switches the printer's IDEX mode: a name containing IDEXDupl or IDEXCopy sends M605 S2 (duplication), IDEXMirr sends M605 S3 (mirror), and IDEXBack sends M605 S4 (backup). Any other plate name prints in normal mode. Rename the plate before slicing to pick the mode.
steps: Arrange a single copy of the model on the left half of the plate for duplication or mirror printing; the duplication command offsets the second head by 162 mm (M605 S2 X162).
Rename the plate so its name contains IDEXDupl (or IDEXCopy), IDEXMirr or IDEXBack.
Slice and check the G-code start: it should contain the matching M605 S2, S3 or S4 line.
Print; the second head copies or mirrors the first head's moves.

settings.advice: The J1 profile's start G-code holds the plate-name checks; keep them if you customise it.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca bundled profile: fdm_idex start G-code

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 A250/A350 printer profiles: build volume for single, dual, Quick Swap and Bracing Kit variants
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca ships a separate printer profile for each Snapmaker 2.0 configuration. The bed area depends only on the frame size (A350 320 x 350 mm, A250 230 x 250 mm); the printable height drops with the dual extrusion module, the Quick Swap Kit (about 15 mm) and the Bracing Kit (about 6 mm). Pick the profile that matches the installed hardware instead of editing the build volume.

settings.advice: Set by the chosen 2.0 variant profile; switch to the QSKit/BKit profile when a kit is installed.

facts: A350: area 320 x 350 mm; height 325 single, 310 QS, 319 BK, 304 QS+BK.
A350 Dual: height 285; 270 QS, 279 BK, 264 QS+BK.
A250: area 230 x 250 mm; height 230 single, 215 QS, 224 BK, 209 QS+BK.
A250 Dual: height 190; 175 QS, 184 BK, 169 QS+BK.
The Quick Swap and Bracing Kit profiles keep the full bed area; only the height changes.

entries.title: Snapmaker U1 printer profile in Snapmaker Orca: build volume and motion limits
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca's bundled U1 profile defines a 270 x 270 mm printable area and about 270 mm printable height. It inherits the tool-changer base profile, whose machine limits allow 500 mm/s travel on X (200 mm/s in the silent limit set) and 20,000 mm/s2 acceleration. Objects that exceed these limits are reported outside the plate.

settings.advice: Comes from the selected U1 printer preset; do not enlarge it, the plate checks rely on it.
270 mm on the U1; taller models are flagged as exceeding the build height.

facts: Printable area 270 x 270 mm (plate origin offset 0.5 mm in X and 1 mm in Y).
Printable height 270 mm (270.05 in the profile).
Machine limits: X speed 500 mm/s normal, 200 mm/s silent; X acceleration 20,000 mm/s2.
Extruder clearance radius 72.5 mm, used for sequential (by-object) printing collision checks.

sources.title: Snapmaker Orca bundled profile: Snapmaker U1 (0.4 nozzle)

entries.title: Acceleration settings per feature
entries.summary: Orca can send a different acceleration for each feature, overriding firmware values, capped by the printer's Motion ability limits. Lower outer wall and top surface acceleration improves surface quality and reduces ringing; inner walls, infill and travel can use higher values. Setting default acceleration to 0 stops Orca sending acceleration commands and disables the others.

settings.advice: Base acceleration for printing and travel; 0 leaves firmware values in control.
Lower than default for cleaner walls and less ringing.
Higher than outer wall to save time.
Similar to outer wall for smooth tops.
Can be high; percentage values follow default acceleration.
Low value improves first-layer adhesion.
High to shorten travel and reduce oozing.
Klipper only; keep enabled so deceleration is gentler than acceleration.

facts: Bridge acceleration as a percentage is based on outer wall acceleration; sparse and solid infill percentages use default acceleration
On Klipper, Accel to decel sends ACCEL_TO_DECEL as a percentage (default 50%) of each acceleration
High acceleration with high pressure advance can make the extruder skip

entries.title: Adaptive bed mesh settings in the printer profile
entries.summary: Orca can compute an adaptive bed mesh area that covers only the printed objects and pass it to the start G-code through variables (adaptive_bed_mesh_min/max, bed_mesh_probe_count, bed_mesh_algo), for Marlin, Klipper and RRF. This speeds up probing while keeping first-layer compensation where it matters. Limit the area to what the probe can reach, set probe spacing, and add a margin.

settings.advice: Lowest XY the probe can reach; prevents probing off the bed.
Highest XY the probe can reach.
Smaller spacing probes more points for warped beds; larger is faster.
A few mm of margin around objects so skirts and brims are also compensated.

facts: Bed mesh min/max default to no limits; set them to the probe-reachable area
Default probe point distance is 50 mm in X and Y
Klipper users should pass ADAPTIVE=0 and ADAPTIVE_MARGIN=0 because Orca already applies the margin
Orca selects lagrange interpolation below 4 probe points per axis, bicubic otherwise
Klipper notes adaptive meshes work best on beds whose full-mesh variance is within about one layer height

entries.title: Adaptive pressure advance settings
entries.summary: The ideal PA value drops as volumetric flow and acceleration rise, so one value is a compromise between slow outer walls and fast infill. Adaptive PA fits a model from measured triplets (PA, flow, acceleration) and sends the best value per feature. It mostly helps high-flow hotends on fast CoreXY printers; if your test values barely change, it is unnecessary. Keep a sensible normal PA value as fallback for tool changes and the prime tower.

settings.advice: Enable after running PA tests at several speeds and accelerations.
Paste PA,flow,acceleration triplets, one per line, at least 3 flows and 3 accelerations.
Start near half the normal PA if lines after bridges look thin.
Leave off until the model is accurate; can cause uneven walls around overhangs.
Keep a median value as fallback when adaptive PA is on.

facts: Tested mainly on Klipper; Klipper versions before the July 2024 fix may show artifacts with dynamic PA
Pressure advance for bridges: about half your usual PA reduces under-extrusion right after bridges; 0 disables
Adaptive PA for overhangs is experimental; enable only after the main model is well calibrated
Measurements are entered one triplet per line, e.g. 0.04,3.96,3000

sources.title: OrcaSlicer wiki - Material flow ratio and pressure advance

entries.title: Arc fitting (G2/G3): when to use it
entries.summary: Arc fitting replaces many short straight moves with G2/G3 arcs, mainly shrinking G-code files and easing load on slow connections. It is not a print-quality feature: arcs can slightly change paths, may print slower because firmware splits them back into lines, and can stress 8-bit controllers. Orca recommends leaving it off on Klipper. It is disabled while extrusion rate smoothing is on.

settings.advice: Leave off on Klipper; consider on only for slow serial/SD workflows on firmware with good arc support.

entries.title: Avoid crossing walls (travel detours) to hide strings and blobs
entries.summary: Avoid crossing walls routes travel moves around perimeters instead of across them, keeping ooze inside the part and reducing surface blobs and visible strings. It is especially helpful for stringy materials like PETG and TPU. It adds some travel time and slicing time. Max detour length limits how far the detour may go, in mm or as a percentage of the direct path; 0 means unlimited.

settings.advice: Enable for PETG, TPU and cosmetic prints.
0 for unlimited detours; set a limit (mm or %) if travel time grows too much.

entries.title: Bridge flow, density, thick bridges and bridge speed
entries.summary: Bridges span gaps in mid-air. For external bridges that sag, reduce bridge flow slightly; for internal bridges, a higher flow can strengthen them and improve the layers above. Bridge density above 100% (up to about 125%) overlaps lines for smoother bridges; below 100% cools faster but sags. Thick bridges use nozzle-diameter-high lines for reliable long spans at the cost of looks, and are recommended for internal bridges.

settings.advice: Lower slightly below 1.0 if external bridges sag or droop.
Raise slightly for stronger internal bridges and flatter tops.
100-125% for smoother bridges; lower only for faster cooling on easy spans.
Enable for long or difficult external bridges; disable for nicer short bridges.
Keep enabled for reliable internal bridges over sparse infill.
Keep external bridges slow, with strong cooling, for less sagging.
Can be faster than external bridges to save time.
0 for automatic; set an angle only to force a direction.

facts: Bridge flow is multiplied by filament flow ratio; internal bridge flow is also multiplied by bridge flow
Bridge density changes line spacing, not flow per line
Disabling thick external bridges looks better but suits only short spans or large nozzles
Internal bridge speed defaults to 150% of the external bridge speed in Orca
Bridge angle 0 lets Orca choose the direction automatically

entries.title: Brim type, width and gap for adhesion and warping
entries.summary: A brim adds flat loops around the base to enlarge contact area, holding down warp-prone materials and tall or small-footprint parts. Auto brim sizes width from height, footprint, speed and material. Mouse ears put small pads only at sharp corners for easier cleanup. A small brim-object gap makes removal easier; zero gap holds best. Try a brim before a raft.

settings.advice: Auto for most prints; Outer only for ABS/ASA/PC or tall thin parts; Mouse ears for corner lifting with easy cleanup.
Manual width; go wider for warp-prone materials and tall thin parts (Auto brim computes up to 18 mm).
A small or zero gap holds best; raise slightly for easier removal.
Ears are placed at corners sharper than this angle; 0 disables ears.

facts: Auto brim width is capped at 18 mm and skipped when the computed width is under 5 mm
Auto brim uses wider brims for ABS, PC and CF materials and narrower for TPU; PETG counts as more adhesive
Outer brims are easier to remove than inner brims
Elephant foot compensation can make the brim look detached in preview
Default brim width and gap in this slicer: 0 mm (brim type default Auto)

entries.title: Chamber temperature control for engineering materials
entries.summary: A warm, stable chamber reduces warping and cracking and improves layer bonding for ABS, ASA, PC and nylon. When chamber temperature control is enabled, Orca sends M191 (set and wait) before the start G-code and M141 to switch the heater off at the end; it also exposes a chamber_temperature variable for start macros. For PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA keep it off: a hot chamber softens filament at the heat break and causes clogs.

settings.advice: Enable only if the printer has an active chamber heater or a heat-soak macro.
Orca lists about 50-70 C for ABS/ASA and higher for PC/PA if supported; 0 for PLA, PETG, TPU.
Softening temperature; when the bed is at or above it, open the door to avoid clogs.

facts: Orca's typical chamber ranges: ABS and ASA 50-70 C, PC 80-100 C, nylon 70-100 C, PLA and TPU ambient
A higher chamber temperature reduces air filtration efficiency for ABS/ASA
Bambu recommends opening the door or removing the top glass when printing PLA/TPU with bed above 45 C, and PETG above 60-70 C

sources.title: Bambu Lab wiki - Filament guide material table

entries.title: Elephant foot compensation for flared first layers
entries.summary: Elephant foot is the first layer(s) spreading wider than the rest because of squish, weight above and bed heat. Compensation shrinks the first layer by the set distance, tapering linearly to zero over the set number of layers, so the finished base matches the model. About 0.1-0.2 mm suits a 0.4 mm nozzle. If a large lip remains, also lower bed temperature, raise Z offset slightly or lower first-layer nozzle temperature.
causes: Too much first-layer squish (nozzle too low)
Bed temperature too high
High first-layer nozzle temperature
Weight of layers above on soft lower layers

settings.advice: Start at 0.1-0.2 mm for a 0.4 mm nozzle; raise until the base edge matches the walls.
1-2 layers for most cases; more if the flare spans several layers.

facts: Prusa: about 0.2 mm works well for a 0.4 mm nozzle; you should not need more than about half the first-layer line width
Not applied when printing on a raft
Preview shows a smaller footprint and the brim may look detached; the printed part is correct
Default in this slicer: 0 mm over 1 layer
Example with 0.25 mm over 2 layers: layer 1 shrinks 0.25 mm, layer 2 0.125 mm

sources.title: Prusa Knowledge Base - Elephant foot compensation

entries.title: Extra bridge layers and internal bridge filtering against pillowing
entries.summary: Extra bridge layers print a second bridge layer over bridges so solid infill above is better supported, reducing pillowing and bridge separation, especially on fast printers. Orca suggests at least External bridge only. Filtering of small internal bridges can let solid infill curl on heavily sloped or curved tops; Limited filtering adds internal bridges where needed. Counterbore bridging adds partial or sacrificial bridges so counterbored holes print without support.

settings.advice: External bridge only as a baseline; Apply to all if tops pillow over sparse infill.
Limited filtering for sloped or curved tops that pillow; keep filtering otherwise.
Partially bridged for clean counterbores without support; sacrificial layer for maximum reliability.

facts: Extra bridge layer options: Disabled (default), External bridge only, Internal bridge only, Apply to all
Internal bridges count toward the top shell layers
No filtering creates internal bridges everywhere and usually too many
Sacrificial layer counterbore mode closes the hole; break it out after printing

entries.title: Extrusion rate smoothing (ERS) to soften sudden flow changes
entries.summary: Extrusion rate smoothing limits how fast the volumetric flow may change (mm3/s2) by ramping speed before and after sudden slowdowns, such as entering an overhang. It reduces bulges that appear when the extruder cannot follow a big speed drop at high acceleration. It only affects slicer-commanded speed changes, not firmware cornering. A value of 0 disables it; any value above 0 turns arc fitting off.

settings.advice: Start at 60-80% of the acceleration-derived maximum; lower 10% if overhang bulges remain.
Keep 3; raise if the printer stutters or Klipper reports timer errors.
Enable to smooth only outer and overhang walls and keep other features fast.

facts: Suggested starting ERS for 0.42 mm lines at 0.16 mm layers: 35-50 mm3/s2 at 1k accel, 70-100 at 2k, 145-200 at 4k
Increase about 25% at 0.2 mm layers
Bowden Marlin printers without pressure advance: about 8-10 mm3/s2
ERS segment length default 3; lower is smoother but makes larger G-code and can overload slow controllers

entries.title: Initial (first) layer height for bed adhesion
entries.summary: A slightly thicker first layer sticks better and hides small bed-height errors, because the extra plastic is more forgiving of a nozzle that is a little high or low. Orca recommends about 0.25 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle (around 62% of nozzle diameter) and no more than about 65%. Thicker first layers are also easier to keep consistent on large beds.
steps: Set the first layer to roughly 60% of nozzle diameter (0.25 mm for 0.4 mm)
Pair it with a wider first-layer line width (about 120%) for more contact area
Fine-tune squish with live Z adjustment while printing a few square patches

settings.advice: Use about 0.2-0.25 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle; raise slightly for uneven or textured beds, but stay under about 65% of nozzle diameter.
A wider first-layer line (around 120% of nozzle) improves adhesion; it also sets brim and skirt width.

facts: Orca guideline first-layer heights: 0.2 mm nozzle 0.12 mm, 0.4 mm nozzle 0.25 mm, 0.6 mm nozzle 0.35 mm, 0.8 mm nozzle 0.45 mm
Ellis' tuning guide suggests 0.25 mm or more because thicker first layers are less sensitive to Z errors
With a raft, the first layer height applies to the raft, not to the object

sources.title: Ellis' Print Tuning Guide - First Layer Squish

entries.title: First layer speeds and slow layer ramp-up
entries.summary: Printing the first layer slowly improves adhesion, reduces warping and tolerates small leveling errors. Initial layer speed covers walls and brim on layer one; initial layer infill speed covers the rest, mainly solid infill. Number of slow layers ramps speed up linearly over several layers instead of jumping to full speed, which helps small-footprint or warp-prone parts.

settings.advice: Default 30 mm/s; lower if the first layer does not stick or lines pull up.
Keep moderate; fast first-layer solid infill adds stress and warping risk.
Use a few layers for tall thin parts or warp-prone materials so speed ramps up gradually.
Usually 100% of travel; reduce only if travel knocks parts loose.
Lower than normal printing acceleration to improve adhesion.

facts: Default first-layer speed in this slicer: 30 mm/s
Initial layer travel speed rarely affects quality and can be a percentage of travel speed
Lower first-layer acceleration and jerk also help adhesion

entries.title: No cooling for the first layers and full fan speed layer
entries.summary: Keeping the part fan off for the first layer(s) helps plastic stay hot and stick, reducing early warping. Full fan speed at layer then ramps fan linearly from 0 up to the maximum by the chosen layer instead of switching on abruptly. If the full-fan layer is not above the no-cooling count, the fan reaches full speed on the next layer.

settings.advice: 1 by default; a few more for warp-prone materials or poor adhesion.
Set a few layers above the no-cooling count to ramp the fan gently; 0 disables the ramp.

facts: Default in this slicer: no cooling for the first 1 layer
The auxiliary fan, if present, also stays off for the no-cooling layers
Prusa suggests PETG with the fan off for the first few layers, then about half power

entries.title: Filament flow ratio and per-object flow ratio
entries.summary: Flow ratio (extrusion multiplier) scales all extrusion for a filament. Too low gives gaps, weak layers and rough tops; too high gives ridges, blobs and oversized parts. The normal range is about 0.95-1.05, and filament profiles are usually close, so calibrate with the flow test. The process flow ratio multiplies on top of the filament value; top and bottom surface flow ratios can be fine-tuned separately for smoother surfaces.

settings.advice: Set from the flow ratio calibration; typically 0.95-1.05.
Leave at 1 unless a specific object needs a correction.
Reduce slightly for smoother tops after flow is calibrated.
Adjust if the first solid layers look over- or under-filled.

facts: Final flow = filament flow ratio x object flow ratio (and x surface-specific ratios where they apply)
Calibrate extruder E-steps or rotation distance in firmware before flow ratio
Tune pressure advance before or alongside flow ratio; if flow changes a lot, rerun PA

sources.title: OrcaSlicer wiki - Material flow ratio and pressure advance
Ellis' Print Tuning Guide - Extrusion Multiplier

entries.title: Flushing volumes, flush multiplier and flushing into infill/objects
entries.summary: Flushing volumes set how much plastic is purged for each from/to color pair; changing from dark to light needs much more than similar colors. The multiplier scales all pairs at once; too low shows as discolored layers. To cut waste, flush into infill or support (hidden material), or into sacrificial objects. Fewer layers (taller layer height) and fewer colors per layer also reduce the number of changes and the waste.

settings.advice: Lower in small steps to save filament; raise if colors bleed after changes.
Raise individual pairs (dark to light) that show contamination; lower similar-color pairs.
Enable for opaque parts with enough walls; avoid with translucent or light walls.
Enable to reuse purge in supports that will be removed.
Set on sacrificial or color-insensitive objects to absorb purge.

facts: Bambu suggests trying a multiplier of 0.8-0.9 and test printing to check for color bleed
Flushing into infill can show through light, translucent or thin-walled parts
Flush into this object is a per-object setting; the object's color will be mixed
Bambu example: 0.28 mm instead of 0.2 mm layers cut filament changes and waste by about 26%
Adding identical multi-color copies to one plate shares the same per-layer waste

sources.title: Bambu Lab wiki - Reduce waste during filament change

entries.title: Fuzzy skin texture: where, how thick and how dense
entries.summary: Fuzzy skin jitters the wall path to give a rough, matte texture that hides layer lines and adds grip, at the cost of dimensional accuracy and extra time. Thickness sets how far points move; point distance sets how dense the bumps are. The classic Displacement mode moves the nozzle and weakens walls; Extrusion mode varies flow instead (half as pronounced, no extra motion) and Combined mixes both. Avoid it on the first layer for adhesion.

settings.advice: Contour for outer surfaces only; All walls only when you want texture everywhere.
Default 0.2 mm; larger is rougher but less accurate. Keep below the outer wall line width.
Smaller gives finer, denser texture; larger is coarser and faster.
Displacement for strongest texture; Extrusion to keep walls strong and speed unchanged.
Classic for random roughness; Perlin or Billow for organic textures.
Leave off to protect bed adhesion.

facts: Defaults in this slicer: thickness 0.2 mm, point distance 0.3 mm
Keep thickness at or below about the outer wall line width
Extrusion and Combined modes require the Arachne wall generator
Painted only mode applies fuzzy skin just where painted with the fuzzy skin tool
Noise types include Classic, Perlin, Billow, Ridged Multifractal and Voronoi

entries.title: Gap fill: where it is applied and filtering tiny gaps
entries.summary: Gap fill prints thin lines into spaces too narrow for a full line. Apply gap fill controls whether solid surfaces get it everywhere, only on top and bottom surfaces, or nowhere. Filter out tiny gaps skips gap fill shorter than a threshold. With the Classic generator, gap fill between walls is separate and adds strength; switching to Arachne is the better way to remove excessive wall gap fill.

settings.advice: Top and bottom surfaces avoids pinholes without extra internal fill; Everywhere for maximum strength.
Raise to drop tiny gap fill segments that cause blobs; 0 keeps all gap fill.
Keep moderate since gap lines have irregular width.

entries.title: Infill combination to print sparse infill in thicker layers
entries.summary: Infill combination prints the sparse infill of several layers at once as one thicker layer while walls keep the normal layer height. It saves time mainly at fine layer heights. The max layer height limits the combined thickness: use about 80% of nozzle diameter to keep infill strong, or 100% for maximum time savings, but never more than the nozzle diameter.

settings.advice: Enable with thin layer heights to cut print time.
About 80% of nozzle diameter for strength; must not exceed nozzle diameter.

entries.title: Beam interlocking for multi-material bonding (e.g. TPU + rigid)
entries.summary: Beam interlocking builds a woven beam structure where two different filaments meet, so materials that bond poorly hold together mechanically. It is useful for soft-plus-rigid parts such as TPU grips on PETG or PLA. Fewer beam layers is stronger but more prone to defects; too shallow a depth gives poor adhesion. Some pairs, like TPU with ABS/ASA/PC, are still not recommended for structural bonding.

settings.advice: Enable for multi-material parts whose materials do not fuse well.
Wider beams are sturdier; narrower follow small interfaces.
Fewer layers is stronger but more defect-prone.
Increase if the materials still separate.
Keeps beams away from the outer surface so they do not show.

facts: Defaults in this slicer: beam width 0.8 mm, 2 beam layers, depth 2 cells, boundary avoidance 2 cells
Snapmaker lists TPU + PLA, PA, PETG or PET as bondable with beam interlocking
When interlocking is enabled, segmented region width/depth settings are ignored

entries.title: Ironing for smooth flat top surfaces
entries.summary: Ironing passes the hot nozzle over a finished top surface a second time with very low flow and tight spacing, filling gaps and smoothing it. It suits flat tops such as badges, lids and boxes, not curved or sloped surfaces, and adds noticeable time. Slow filament flow during ironing raises heat creep and clog risk, especially with PLA in warm rooms. Use Monotonic top surfaces for best results.

settings.advice: Topmost surface for single flat tops; Top surfaces for stepped parts. Avoid All solid layers unless needed.
Raise a few % if gaps remain; lower if ridges or over-extrusion appear.
Default 0.1 mm; keep at or below nozzle diameter. Tighter is smoother but slower.
Slow speeds give the best finish (default 20 mm/s).
Rectilinear for most surfaces; concentric for round tops.
Offset from the top infill direction; 0, 45 or 90 deg give different finishes.
Increase to keep ironing away from edges if edges get blobs.

facts: Types: Top surfaces, Topmost surface only, All solid layers
Defaults in this slicer: flow 10%, spacing 0.1 mm, speed 20 mm/s
Line spacing should be at or below the nozzle diameter
Lower layer heights may need a higher ironing flow
