Use fans or air conditioning to cool a hot room; an enclosure or heating for a cold one.
Use a dehumidifier or humidifier to stay in range.

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 Power Module dead (no LED, fan not spinning)
entries.summary: If the Power Module shows no LED and its fan does not turn at power-on, check the mains voltage, then the AC cord, before concluding the module has failed.
causes: Input voltage out of range
AC power cable broken
Power Module faulty
steps: Confirm the mains input is within 88-264 V AC.
Try another standard AC power cable; if that fixes it, replace the cable.
If voltage and cable are fine, the Power Module needs replacing.

sources.title: What should I do if the Power Module does not work?

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 power supply making a loud grinding or rattling noise
entries.summary: A loud power supply is either its small rear fan or its internal fan. Disconnect the rear fan to tell which, then get a replacement fan or power supply from support.
causes: Rear fan of the power supply failing
Internal power supply fan failing
steps: Power off and remove the four backplate screws (H1.5 hex key).
Ease the backplate out without fully removing it and unplug the rear fan.
Refit the backplate and power on. If the noise is gone, ask support for a new rear fan.
If it is still loud, the internal fan (a 6012, 60 mm 12 V) is the cause; ask support for a new power supply. Only qualified people should replace the internal fan because of shock risk.

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 3D Printing Module crashes into the Print Sheet during calibration or printing
entries.summary: If the nozzle digs into the Print Sheet, check the firmware, how the Y-axis linear modules and support platform are mounted, the Y/Z cable ports on the Controller, and the probe (proximity) sensor. The sensor LED must light as it nears the bed, and the nozzle tip should sit about 1 mm below the sensor.
causes: Outdated firmware
Y-axis linear modules not seated in the base plate grooves
Y and Z linear module cables in the wrong Controller ports
Support platform mounted upside down (its screws should face down)
Faulty probe sensor
Nozzle or probe sensor mounted at the wrong height
steps: Install the latest firmware.
Confirm both Y-axis linear modules sit fully in the grooves of the base plate.
Check the screws on the support platform face downward; if not, reinstall them.
Verify the Y and Z cables are in the correct ports on the Controller.
Test the sensor: hold a palette knife under the module, or run Calibration > Start, and watch whether the LED lights as it approaches. No light means the sensor must be replaced.
If the LED works, loosen the hot end set screw, push the nozzle fully in and retighten.
Lower the module until the nozzle touches the sheet, loosen the sensor screw, rest the sensor on a card about 1 mm thick and tighten it.
Run calibration again.

sources.title: What should I do if the 3D Printing Module pushes into the Print Sheet?

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 3D Printing Module not detected (toolhead cable, CAN bus, PCBA, M1029 E2)
entries.summary: If the 3D Printing Module is not recognized, suspect the toolhead cable, the Controller's toolhead port, a linear module disturbing CAN communication, or the module's own PCBA. Swap cables and toolheads to isolate the part; Addon-1 can be remapped as a temporary toolhead port.
causes: Toolhead cable broken
Controller toolhead port broken
Printing module PCBA damaged (often after a reversed cable)
A linear module disrupting CAN communication
steps: Power off, swap the toolhead cable for one of the interchangeable cables and power on. If the module is found now, the cable was faulty.
If not, try the laser and CNC modules. If only the printing module fails, its PCBA is likely damaged; it can be replaced with H1.5/H2.0 tools (video guide).
If nothing is detected, unplug everything from the Controller except Power Module and Touchscreen, connect only the printing module and power on; success means a linear module is upsetting CAN.
To test the toolhead port, connect Luban over USB serial, send M1029 E2 then M500, power off and plug the toolhead cable into Addon-1.
Always power off before plugging cables and insert them the right way round.
facts: Signs of a damaged module PCBA: not recognized at power-on, or filament cannot be loaded/unloaded from the screen.

sources.title: Replacing the PCBA of the 3D Printing Module

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 circles and holes print out of round: linear module backlash
entries.summary: Round features coming out oval are caused by backlash in a linear module's lead screw nut, or a loose slider. With the module removed, press the anti-backlash nut down about 3 mm, re-grease the lead screw and reassemble.
symptoms: Printed circles or holes are not round
causes: Backlash in the linear module
Loose linear module slider
steps: Remove the module. Tools: dust-free cloth, 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm screwdrivers.
Remove the steel strip pressure blocks (2.0 mm) and end cover (2.5 mm); slide the slider out and scrape its grease onto the cloth to reuse.
Unscrew the limit trigger block (two 2.0 mm screws), take it out and slide the slider about two-thirds out.
Press the nut down roughly 3 mm with a screwdriver to remove backlash, then slide the slider in until the lead screw just shows, avoiding the limit switch contact.
Confirm the nut sits below the top of the slider cylinder, then refit and tighten the limit trigger block.
Move the slider back 1-2 cm, spread the saved grease on the lead screw, refit end cover and steel strip, and adjust the strip.

sources.title: What should I do if the processed object is not round

entries.title: Replacing the Snapmaker 2.0 printing module proximity sensor or air passage (blower vent)
entries.summary: Replace the proximity sensor when it stays triggered during calibration, lets the nozzle press into the bed (after mounting and cabling are ruled out), or was damaged by a knock. The Single Extrusion Module and the 2.0 Dual Extrusion Module use the same sensor. After fitting, set the sensor about 1 mm above the nozzle tip.
steps: Power off and remove the module. Tools: H2.0 and H1.5 screwdrivers, tweezers.
Loosen the hot end screws (H2.0), remove the hot end, then unbolt the print cooling vent.
Remove the left cover (H1.5), unscrew the PCBA (H2.0) and unplug the sensor connector from it.
Remove the right cover (H1.5) and the blower vent bolts (H2.0); lift out vent and sensor and ease them apart with tweezers.
Press the new sensor into the vent (hot glue or glue if it is loose), route its cable into the module, refit the vent and the right cover.
Plug the sensor into the PCBA, fix the PCBA, refit the left cover and the print cooling vent.
Refit the hot end, leaving clearance between each side of it and the cooling vent.
Loosen the blower vent bolt, set the sensor about 1 mm higher than the nozzle (a credit card makes a handy gauge) and retighten.

sources.title: 3D printing module Air Passage and Proximity Sensor replacement guide
SM 2.0 Dual Extruder proximity sensor replacement guide

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 Quick Swap Kit: setup, install status and reduced travel for 3D printing
entries.summary: The Quick Swap Kit adds brackets so toolheads and platforms slide in and lock with a handle. It cuts Y and Z travel by about 15 mm, so the printing module must be recalibrated and the install status set correctly on the Touchscreen; a mismatched status causes leveling failures. Use the original support platform for 3D printing; the kit's new support platform is for CNC only.
steps: Update software (Luban 4.8.1+, choose Snapmaker 2.0 Quick Swap Kit in Machine Settings) and firmware to 1.16.5 or later.
At first boot tap Installed > Let's Create!, or later set Settings > Quick Swap Install Status.
Mount the brackets with the original M4 x 8 screws; with a printing module fitted you only need to unplug the heated bed, not remove it.
Recalibrate: bed leveling for the single module, full calibration for the dual module.
If the kit is removed, set the status to Not Installed and recalibrate again.
To change toolheads, use Settings > Park for Easy Swap, then power off and unplug before swapping.

settings.advice: Select the matching QSKit printer profile in Snapmaker Orca; it already lowers the printable height by 15 mm (21 mm with the Bracing Kit too) and keeps the bed area.

sources.title: Quick Start Guide for Snapmaker 2.0 Quick Swap Kit

entries.title: Resetting the Snapmaker 2.0 Touchscreen or Controller (Developer Mode, M502/M500)
entries.summary: The Touchscreen is reset from a hidden Developer Mode; the Controller is reset to defaults by sending M502 followed by M500 from Luban over a USB serial connection.
steps: Touchscreen: open Settings > About Machine and tap the image at the top five times; confirm Enter Developer Mode with OK.
In Developer Mode tap Experiment > Preference > Reset All.
Controller: power on, connect Luban via USB (Serial Port > COM > Connect).
In the console send M502, then M500 to save; the Controller is now reset.

sources.title: How to reset the touchscreen or controller

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 Dual Extruder 'Hardware Abnormal Detected - Result 7' during auto leveling
entries.summary: Result 7 aborts auto bed leveling with the Dual Extrusion Module. Either the Quick Swap Kit install status on the Touchscreen does not match the hardware, or the dual module has a hardware fault such as the right nozzle not lifting.
symptoms: Auto leveling stops midway
Alert: Hardware Abnormal Detected - Result 7
causes: Quick Swap Kit installed but not selected (or the reverse)
Dual Extruder hardware fault, e.g. right nozzle not lifting
steps: Open Settings > Quick Swap Install Status and choose the option that matches the machine.
With the kit set as installed, a green Quick Swap icon appears on the home screen; without it, no icon.
Check the right extruder lifts: confirm the lead screw nut is positioned correctly and the lifting motor works.
For hardware faults, contact support with photos or video.

sources.title: How to fix the Dual Extruder 'Result 7' error?

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 routine 3D printing maintenance schedule
entries.summary: Look at the nozzle before every print and clean the bore or tip if blocked. Monthly, wipe the linear modules, clean the extruder gear, and clear the vents and dust nets on the printing module's two side covers so internal parts do not overheat.
steps: Before each print: inspect the nozzle and clean the bore or tip if it is blocked or crusted.
Monthly, machine off: wipe the linear module surfaces with a dry cotton cloth without pressing on the steel strip.
Do not open the linear modules yourself; that voids the Limited Warranty.
Monthly: clean the extruder gear and U-shaped bearing bracket with a swab or vacuum.
Monthly: swab or vacuum the vents and dust-proof nets on both side covers of the Single Extrusion Module.
facts: Blocked side-cover vents reduce airflow and can make the module overheat and malfunction.
Clean linear modules move with less friction and noise.

sources.title: Cleaning the nozzle of the Single Extrusion Module
Cleaning the linear modules for Snapmaker 2.0
Cleaning the gear of the Single Extrusion Module
Cleaning the side covers of the Single Extrusion Module

entries.title: Safety labels on Snapmaker 2.0 3D printing parts and the Dual Extrusion Module
entries.summary: Labels on the printing module, heated bed and Print Sheet warn of hot surfaces; the heated bed also warns not to print directly on it, which would damage it. The Dual Extrusion Module carries hot-surface and hand-crush warnings. The A150's heated bed has no labels, but the same precautions apply.
facts: 3D Printing Module: do not touch the nozzle or hot end during or right after printing.
Heated bed: hot surface; never print directly on the bed, always use the Print Sheet; wait several minutes or use heat-insulated gloves.
Print Sheet: hot surface during and immediately after printing; no bare hands.
Dual Extrusion Module: hot surface warning and a warning to avoid crushing hands.
The Snapmaker 2.0 A150 heated bed carries no labels.

sources.title: Warnings & Labels of the Dual Extrusion Module

entries.title: Sending G-code to the Snapmaker 2.0 and starting a print (Wi-Fi, USB drive, USB cable)
entries.summary: G-code can be sent to the Touchscreen over Wi-Fi, copied over on a USB flash drive, or streamed from Luban's Workspace over Wi-Fi or a USB cable. Prints started from the Touchscreen can be tuned live by swiping left. A print streamed over the USB cable stops if the cable is pulled.
steps: Wi-Fi to the screen: send the file to the device, tap Got It on the Touchscreen, open Files > Local, preview, check settings and tap Start.
USB drive: save the .gcode file to the drive, plug it into the Controller, open Files > USB, preview and tap Start.
While printing, swipe left on the print screen to adjust settings such as Z Offset.
Luban Workspace over Wi-Fi: load the G-code to Workspace, connect and press Run. If Wi-Fi drops, the screen asks whether to keep printing; ignore it to continue or tap Confirm to stop.
Luban over USB serial: pick the machine model and toolhead when prompted, press Run, and keep the cable connected until the job finishes.

sources.title: Transferring G-code file and start printing

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 keeps showing 'Filament Runout' (Single Extrusion Module); M412 workaround
entries.summary: If the Touchscreen shows Filament Runout while filament is loaded, or the sensor fails to stop a print when filament really runs out, the filament sensor is misadjusted or broken. Remove the fan and adjust the switch, or replace the sensor. To print in the meantime, turn runout detection off with M412 S0 from the Luban console over USB.
symptoms: Filament Runout screen at print start with filament present
Print pauses for no reason
Filament runs out but the machine keeps printing in the air
causes: Filament sensor not seated correctly
Filament sensor damaged
steps: Remove the module fan and readjust the filament switch (wiki videos).
If the sensor is damaged, replace it: power off, remove the module; tools H2.0, H2.5, tweezers, 1.5 hex key (video guide).
Interim: connect the machine by USB, open the Luban console and send M412 S0 to disable detection.
Send M412 S1 to re-enable detection, or M412 alone to report its current state.
facts: M412 S1 enables, M412 S0 disables, and M412 reports filament runout detection.

sources.title: What should I do if the Touchscreens keeps showing Filament Runout?
Filament runout sensor and linear module limit switch replacement guide
Replacing the limit switch of the linear module and the filament sensor of the 3D printing module

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module: filament won't load or come out of the nozzle
entries.summary: Nothing coming out of the nozzle can mean a jammed hot end, filament not inserted properly, a faulty module, a broken toolhead cable or a dead Controller port. Clear the hot end at temperature first; then watch whether the drive gear turns on Load/Unload to separate mechanical from electrical faults.
causes: Jammed nozzle/hot end
Filament not inserted correctly
3D Printing Module fault
Controller toolhead port broken
Toolhead cable broken
steps: Heat the nozzle (225 C for PLA, 265 C for ABS) and push the old filament out through the module with a metal rod.
If it will not push through, the hot end is clogged: replace the hot end.
Otherwise open the module latch, set the nozzle to 200 C in Control > Nozzle, wait, then tap Load or Unload and watch the gear.
Gear turns: module, Controller and cable are fine. Reinsert the filament properly, close the latch and load again.
Gear does not turn: check the Controller toolhead port by connecting the 1.6W laser module and testing it, or remap the port to Addon-1 (M1029 E2, then M500).

sources.title: What should I do if the filament won't load?

entries.title: Filaments for the Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module (PLA, ABS, PETG, TPU; no nylon)
entries.summary: The Single Extrusion Module is meant for PLA, ABS, PETG and TPU. Snapmaker says its brass nozzle is not hard enough for nylon. PLA and PETG pick up moisture and should be kept dry; ABS gives off odors and particles, so print it with ventilation and a mask. Data sheets are reference values only.

settings.advice: Stay within the filament's range and below the module's 275 C maximum.
Keep around 9 mm³/s or lower, the module's rated flow.

facts: Supported: PLA, ABS, TPU, PETG (others under testing per the FAQ).
Nylon is not recommended: the standard brass nozzle is too soft.
Single module max nozzle temperature 275 C.
Bed above 80 C is possible on A/AT/F models but takes about 20-30 minutes.

sources.title: Filament library for Single Extrusion Module

entries.title: Cleaning the Snapmaker 2.0 Single Extrusion Module extruder gear (stops slipping)
entries.summary: Once a month, clear out the plastic shavings the drive gear scrapes off the filament. Built-up debris cuts the grip between filament, gear and the U-shaped bearing bracket, so the extruder slips and under-extrudes, and loose shavings can fall into the nozzle and clog it.
symptoms: Extruder slips or clicks
Weak or inconsistent extrusion
Repeated nozzle clogs
causes: Filament shavings accumulated on the gear and U-shaped bearing bracket
steps: Power the machine off.
Open the 3D printing module.
Clean debris off the U-shaped bearing bracket with a cotton swab or a vacuum.
Swab the gear and the area around it.
Close the module.

sources.title: Cleaning the gear of the Single Extrusion Module

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 toolhead cable plugged in reversed or hot-swapped: possible damage and checks
entries.summary: Plugging the toolhead cable in backwards, or connecting or disconnecting it with the power on, can destroy the toolhead PCB, the Controller's level-conversion or communication chip, and (when hot-swapping) the proximity sensor. Always power off before touching cables.
symptoms: Toolhead not recognized or not working
Toolhead smoked and the machine stopped
causes: Toolhead cable inserted the wrong way
Cable plugged or unplugged while powered
steps: Plug the toolhead in; if it is not detected, try another toolhead. If only the affected one fails, its internal PCB is damaged.
Check the Controller: heat the nozzle and use Load/Unload. The gear should turn clockwise to load and counterclockwise to unload; no or reversed rotation means Controller damage.
If no printing module can be detected, use a laser module: a yellow camera icon, or a laser that ignores Laser Status ON/OFF, also indicates Controller damage.
On F-series machines with only the printing module, remap the toolhead port to Addon-1 (M1029 E2, then M500 via Luban over USB serial) to keep printing.
facts: Addon-1 works as a toolhead port only for 3D printing and CNC modules.

sources.title: What could happen if I plugged in the toolhead cable reversely or hot-swapped?
Installing the toolhead on A350T & Quick Swap Kit Bundle
Installing the platform on A350T & Quick Swap Kit Bundle

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 'Machine is not responding', black or flashing Touchscreen
entries.summary: The 'Machine is not responding. Would you like to reconnect?' warning before or during prints, and a screen that stays black at power-on, are diagnosed the same way: the Type-C link between screen and Controller, Controller firmware or hardware, old firmware with a new Dual Extrusion Module, or a faulty screen. A flickering, flashing screen means the Touchscreen itself needs replacing.
causes: Poor contact at the screen or Controller Type-C connector
Controller firmware corrupted
New Dual Extrusion Module on old firmware
Loose internal connections or damaged screen hardware
Power Module or DC cable fault (black screen)
steps: Unplug the screen cable at the Controller, flip the Type-C plug 180 degrees and reinsert it firmly.
If only the rubber boot, not the metal, enters the port, trim about 1 mm off the rubber.
Push the cable backward (Controller mounted left) or inward (Controller mounted right); if it reconnects, the Controller's Type-C socket is loose and the Controller should be opened and checked.
Secure the screen cable (a printable cable fixture is shared on the forum) so tugging does not loosen the socket.
Check the status light on the back of the Controller: it should pulse slowly. A steady light means a Controller fault; contact support.
No light at all: connect Luban by USB and see whether it can move the axes.
After fitting a new Dual Extrusion Module: unplug it, update firmware, then reconnect it.
Flashing screen: replace the Touchscreen.

sources.title: What should I do if the Touchscreen shows not responding?
What should I do if the Touchscreen is black?
What should I do if the Touchscreen flashes?

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 cannot read files on a USB flash drive (FAT32, 16 GB limit, toolhead)
entries.summary: The machine only reads FAT32 drives, and drives larger than 16 GB can cause problems. Files are also hidden unless the toolhead is detected (green dot on the home screen) and the file type suits it: G-code for the 3D printing module.
causes: Faulty USB drive
Drive not formatted FAT32
Drive larger than 16 GB
Toolhead not recognized
File type does not match the attached toolhead
steps: Test the drive in a computer and try a different drive in the machine.
Reformat to FAT32 (this erases the drive, back up first). Windows, under 32 GB: in an admin PowerShell run format /FS:FAT32 /Q X: with your drive letter; larger drives need a FAT32 formatting tool.
macOS: run diskutil list to find the disk number, then sudo diskutil eraseDisk FAT32 USB MBRFormat /dev/diskX.
Use a drive of 16 GB or less where possible.
Check the home screen shows the toolhead with a green dot; fix toolhead detection first if not.
Make sure the files match the toolhead: .gcode for printing (laser NC files will not show).

sources.title: What should I do if the machine can't read the file of my USB flash drive?

entries.title: Snapmaker 2.0 Y-axis clunk or linear module noise (lead mismatch, travel mismatch, steel strip)
entries.summary: A clunk as the bed moves back and forth usually means mismatched linear modules: the wrong lead on an AT-series machine, or two Y modules whose travel differs. A loose stainless steel strip on a module also makes noise while it moves; tension or replace it.
symptoms: Clunk sound as the Y axis moves
Rattling or noise from a linear module in motion
causes: Module with the wrong lead in a Y or Z position (AT series)
Two Y modules with different travel distances
Loose or broken stainless steel strip
steps: AT series: check the lead label on each module; X 20 mm, Y 20 mm, Z 8 mm.
Compare Y travel: power off, remove heated bed and support platform, slide both Y sliders to the front and lay a laser platform panel against both with no gap.
Power on, jog Y to the far end and see whether a gap opens between either slider and the panel.
If so, swap one Y module with the X module and repeat; keep the two with the closest travel as the Y axes.
Inspect each module's stainless steel strip; tension a loose strip or replace a broken one (wiki videos).

sources.title: The Y-axis Linear Modules make a clunk sound when moving back and forth
The stainless steel strip of the linear module is broken or loose

entries.title: U1 Auto-Refill: switching to a backup spool when filament runs out
entries.summary: With Auto-Refill on, a toolhead that runs out hands over to another toolhead holding matching filament and the print carries on. Backups are used in ascending toolhead order (start on T2: then T1, T3, T4). Handy for long single-color jobs, or as a spare for the most-used color in multicolor prints.
steps: Update firmware to V1.5.2 or later and enable Settings > Print Preferences > Auto-Refill
Load a backup with the same brand, material and color, or enable Allow auto-refill with different colors to accept same brand and material in another color
Feed the backup into an empty feeder until its white light stays on; rigid filament can be added before or during the print
Flexible filament cannot auto-load, so load the TPU backup manually before starting (otherwise you must pause)
Set filament info on the Filament page; RFID Snapmaker spools fill in automatically
If no backup exists the print pauses: tap OK, put a new spool on the original holder, wait for the steady white light, edit filament info, then press the play icon in the Print Workspace to resume
facts: No auto-refill between nozzles of different diameters (firmware 1.3.0+)
Known issue: after loading a flexible backup you must re-enable Auto Loading, otherwise Auto-Refill does nothing
Release notes say Auto-Refill is on by default since V1.1.0, while the guide asks for V1.5.2+

entries.title: U1 heated bed leveling: auto leveling and manual handwheel leveling
entries.summary: Auto leveling is normally enough. If the bed is badly out of level or the first layer is still uneven, level by hand with the yellow handwheels under the bed first, then run auto leveling again.
steps: Auto: Settings > Device Calibration, enable Heated Bed Leveling, tap Start at the top right, check the estimated time and tap Start; tap OK when finished
Manual: Settings > Maintenance > Manual Leveling; the bed rises and the screen shows which handwheel to turn
Turn the yellow handwheels on the leveling screws beneath the bed by hand; an optional printable helper (heated-bed-nut_helper-tool) fits over them for more leverage
Run auto leveling again afterwards from Settings > Device Calibration
facts: Firmware 1.0.0+ flashes icons to show whether to loosen or tighten each screw
Firmware 1.1.1+ detects abnormal bed unevenness and offers guided manual leveling
Since the V1.5.x first-layer fix, Snapmaker advises keeping Heated Bed Leveling enabled before every print

sources.title: U1 model warps, detaches or collapses

entries.title: U1 build plates: Smooth PEI vs carbon-fiber textured, glue and temperature limits
entries.summary: On the Smooth PEI plate, use glue stick or liquid glue as a release layer for every material except PLA, otherwise strong adhesion can tear the PEI film. On the carbon-fiber textured plate never use glue, since it fills the texture that creates the patterned bottom surface. Keep smooth PEI below 105 °C and the carbon-fiber plate below 80 °C.
steps: Start with a clean plate and seat it on the magnetic bed aligned with the edges
In Snapmaker Orca 2.3.1+ pick the plate type (Smooth PEI Plate or Graphic Effect Plate) so bed temperatures, Z-offset and glue prompts match
Firmware 1.3.0+ reads the plate type from the G-code and applies a -0.07 mm Z-offset (same for both plates)
Use a moderate first-layer speed and apply glue when the slicer prompts
Remove prints only once the plate is at room temperature: take it off and flex it. A scraper at 15-30° is fine on textured plates, never on smooth PEI
Clean after prints and when adhesion drops; never use acetone-based cleaners

settings.advice: Choose the plate actually installed (Textured PEI, Smooth PEI or Graphic Effect Plate) so the right bed temperatures and Z-offset are used.
Bed temperature for the Smooth PEI Plate; stay below the plate's 105 °C rating (the bed itself tops out at 100 °C).
Bed temperature for the carbon-fiber textured (Graphic Effect) plate; keep it under 80 °C.

entries.title: Removing filament residue from the outside of a U1 nozzle
entries.summary: Filament stuck to the outside of the nozzle can interrupt extrusion lines and reduce how well the first layer contacts the plate. Heat the nozzle to soften the residue and brush it off.
steps: Control > Toolheads, select the toolhead and tap Attach Toolhead
Tap Nozzle Temp. and set your usual print temperature (about 200 °C for PLA, about 240 °C for ABS and PETG)
Wearing heat-resistant gloves, brush the residue away gently with the toolbox wire brush; scrubbing hard can damage the nozzle
Reheat if needed and tap EXTRUDE; a smooth, steady stream means cleaning is complete
Also check the nozzle wiper brush is still attached

entries.title: U1 extruder cleaning and gear greasing (rust marks on prints)
entries.summary: Clean and grease the extruder when dust or filament debris builds up, or when the gears rust and leave rust-colored marks on prints. Rust happens when the gear plating wears off from running without lubrication.
symptoms: Rust-colored marks on printed parts
Visible rust on extruder gears
Dust or filament chips inside the extruder
causes: Normal debris buildup over long use
Gear plating worn through by dry meshing, exposing metal that rusts
steps: Open the extruder following the Toolhead Disassembly and Reassembly guide; the hotend and hotend cooling fan can stay in place
Blow or brush dust and debris off the extruder parts
Brush grease onto the helical gear teeth while turning the gears
Do not let grease run into the filament guide channel, it will disturb extrusion
Reassemble the extruder and toolhead

entries.title: U1 false filament runout alarm (0002-0523-0000-0000 to 0002-0523-0003-0000)
entries.summary: A runout pause while filament is present (codes 0002-0523-0000-0000 for toolhead 1, -0001- for toolhead 2, -0002- for toolhead 3, -0003- for toolhead 4) usually means a loose or damaged runout sensor cable or a software misread. Reload first, then test the sensor by hand using the Edit Filament icon.
symptoms: Print pauses with a filament runout error although filament is loaded
causes: Loose runout sensor cable connection
Damaged runout sensor cable
Software recognition error
Leftover filament piece holding the sensor
steps: Unload completely (feeder and toolhead), reload and see whether the alarm clears
If not, unload again, open the Load Filament page and push a short piece of filament into the toolhead by hand
Normal: the Edit Filament page becomes available with filament inserted and unavailable once it is removed
Reversed behaviour: reseat the sensor cable at both ends and inspect it for damage; if it is fine, the runout sensor needs replacing (contact support)
Correct behaviour but the alarm persists: export the logs and send them to support
Edit page available whether or not filament is inserted: remove leftover filament blocking the sensor

entries.title: Auto loading PLA, PETG and other rigid filament on the U1
entries.summary: Auto Loading is the default and recommended method for rigid filaments; TPU and other flexible filaments must be loaded manually. The feeder pre-loads the filament, then the printer picks the toolhead, heats, extrudes and purges by itself.
steps: Snip the filament end at about 45° to reduce feeding resistance
Hang the spool so filament leaves from the bottom of the spool
Push filament into the feeder until the white light comes on; blinking means still feeding, steady means pre-load finished
On the Filament page, RFID Snapmaker spools are detected; for third-party or non-RFID spools tap the icon below the slot, pick type and color, Save
Tap Loading Mode, select the filament and tap Load
Wait while the toolhead is picked, filament fed, nozzle heated and old material purged, then tap Done; the slot shows Loaded

entries.title: Auto unloading rigid filament from the U1
entries.summary: Rigid filaments (PLA, PETG) are unloaded automatically: the printer heats each selected toolhead and the extruder gears push the filament back up. Use Manual Unloading for TPU.
steps: Filament page > Unloading Mode, select the toolheads to empty, tap Unload
Each toolhead is picked and heated, then the filament is retracted; toolheads are processed one after another. Tap OK when all are done
Turn the spool backwards to wind filament out of the tube until the feeder's white light goes off
Thread the loose end through the two locking holes on the spool so it cannot unwind, then take the spool off

entries.title: Manually loading TPU or flexible filament on the U1
entries.summary: Flexible filament such as TPU cannot go through the feeder and must be loaded by hand straight into the toolhead tube. Auto Loading has to be disabled for that toolhead first.
steps: Cut the filament end at about 45° and hang the spool so it unwinds from the bottom
Press the round latch on the end of the feeder and pull out the tube that runs to the target toolhead
Turn off Auto Loading for that toolhead in Settings > Print Preferences > Auto Loading
Filament page > Loading Mode > Filament Loading Guide > Switch to Manual Loading, pick the toolhead, tap Manual Loading
Push the filament through the tube into the toolhead; easiest is to unplug the tube at the top of the toolhead and press the exposed filament down onto the extruder gears
Tap Next; the nozzle heats and extrudes. If filament appears tap Extruded > Done, otherwise reinsert it and tap Retry Extrusion
After automatic nozzle wiping tap Done and push the tube back into the top of the toolhead
Enter filament type and color unless an RFID spool is recognized

entries.title: Manually unloading TPU or flexible filament from the U1
entries.summary: TPU and other flexible filaments need manual help to unload: after the nozzle heats, you pull the filament out by hand directly from the filament tube, since TPU does not use the feeder.
steps: Filament page > Unloading Mode, select the toolheads, tap Unload and then Confirm
When the nozzle reaches temperature an on-screen guide appears; tap Next and pull the filament outward by hand
Pull it straight out of the filament tube (the on-screen feeder illustration does not apply to TPU)
Tap OK when finished, rewind the spool, secure the end through the spool's two holes and remove the spool

entries.title: How to update U1 firmware over Wi-Fi or from a USB flash drive
entries.summary: U1 firmware can be installed over the air via Wi-Fi or from a USB flash drive. When the printer is online, the touchscreen prompts when a new version exists. Calibration and leveling data survive the update.
steps: Wi-Fi: connect the printer to Wi-Fi and make sure LAN mode is switched off
On the touchscreen open Settings > About > Firmware Version
If a newer version is offered tap Download Now, then Update Now once the download completes
USB: download the latest package from the U1 Firmware Release Notes page and copy it onto a USB flash drive
Plug the drive into the printer and open Settings > About > Firmware Version > Local Update
Pick the firmware file and confirm the pop-up

entries.title: U1 firmware V0.9.0: status display, USB backup and connection fixes
entries.summary: V0.9.0 (2025-11-06) adds home-screen indicators for timelapse recording, camera errors and LAN/cloud connection state, shows download progress for remote jobs, and copies files printed from USB to local storage. It needs Snapmaker Orca 2.1.1+ or Snapmaker App 2.1.0+.
facts: Home screen shows timelapse status (recording or camera error) and connection mode: LAN, cloud connected, cloud disconnected or cloud abnormal
Remote jobs display file download progress; LAN-sent files do not yet
Files printed from a USB drive are automatically backed up to internal storage
More reliable remote control; fixed PIN code retrieval, OTA info retrieval and recovery after cloud drops
Auxiliary and part cooling fans now stop while a print is paused, for quieter idle
Better pause/resume handling gives cleaner layers where printing resumes
Fixed: LAN reconnection error from Orca/App, speed changes failing in multicolor prints, wrong file names or thumbnails, possible freeze when leaving Wi-Fi setup

entries.title: U1 firmware V0.9.4: tangle sensitivity, pick/park coordinates, 170 °C minimum
entries.summary: V0.9.4 (2025-12-16) adds an adjustable filament tangle detection sensitivity and adjustable toolhead attach/detach (pick and park) coordinates, lengthens the auto-load purge and fixes several stability bugs. It requires Snapmaker Orca 2.1.5+ or App 2.1.5+.
facts: Auto-loading purges more filament to stop old and new colors mixing
Fans switch off before vibration compensation calibration so the measurement is accurate
The active toolhead's minimum temperature while printing is set to 170 °C
New 15-minute screen timeout, now the default
Snappier UI, faster USB file scan, better cloud connection on weak networks, connection-failure notices and cloud status icons
Fixed: auxiliary fan not controllable during bed leveling, cloud failures from config load errors, Klipper shutdowns on abnormal move commands, print timer resetting at toolhead changes

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.0.0: AI monitoring, homing calibration, maintenance reminders
entries.summary: V1.0.0 (2025-12-31) introduces AI monitoring with spaghetti and foreign-object detection, a homing calibration for failed homing or pick/park, maintenance reminders for the SnapSwap system and a filament auto-mapping switch. It requires Snapmaker Orca 2.2.1+ or App 2.2.1+.
facts: AI monitoring needs Snapmaker Orca 2.2.1 (push notifications); Snapmaker App 2.2.2 shows pop-up alerts for detections
Homing calibration targets cases where homing or toolhead picking/parking fails; homing logic was also improved
Filament auto-mapping is on by default and can be turned off in Settings > Print Preferences
Low-storage warnings added
Manual leveling screen now flashes icons to show which screw to loosen or tighten
Fixed failures when downloading large files

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.1.0: per-toolhead flow calibration, QR error help, Z torque
entries.summary: V1.1.0 (2026-01-26) lets you run flow calibration only on chosen toolheads, puts QR codes linking to official fixes on some error screens and adds more RFID filament types. It raises Z motor current for more torque and turns Auto-Refill on by default. Requires Snapmaker Orca 2.2.1+ or App 2.2.1+.
facts: Selective flow calibration skips toolheads that are already calibrated
Idle toolhead fans run quieter during printing; AI detection has fewer false positives
Print completion time now excludes paused time
Higher Z motor current increases torque to fix quality defects caused by weak Z drive
Tangle detection gains a medium sensitivity level
Fixed: firmware shutdown when start G-code lacked a layer count command; nozzle temperature changing unexpectedly during pre-extrusion

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.1.1: bed flatness check, log export to Fluidd, HF filaments
entries.summary: V1.1.1 (2026-02-09) detects abnormal heated bed unevenness and guides you through manual leveling, adds a log export path into the Fluidd G-code logs folder and adds HF filament types. Requires Snapmaker Orca 2.2.4+ or App 2.2.3+.
facts: Log export: About > System Log > Export logs to Local Storage puts logs in the logs folder of the Fluidd G-code directory
New filament types: PETG HF and TPU 95A HF, each in a Snapmaker and a Generic version
Fixed longer print times caused by restricted motion parameters after flow calibration
Fixed toolhead wrongly reported as loaded during a runout pause
Updated built-in filament parameters, smoother resume after pause, screen wakes and stays on for alerts
Resuming after runout no longer requires re-entering material info

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.2.0: Skip Objects, Ethernet adapter support, root SSH access
entries.summary: V1.2.0 (2026-03-23) adds on-screen Skip Objects, wired networking through a USB-to-Ethernet adapter (preferred over Wi-Fi when connected) and optional root access for SSH. Requires Snapmaker Orca 2.2.4+ or App 2.2.3+.

settings.advice: Turn on so the U1 touchscreen can skip individual failed objects during a print (firmware 1.2.0+).

facts: Skip Objects requires Exclude objects (Snapmaker Orca: Process > Global > Others > G-code output) to be switched on
Wi-Fi gains WPA3 support; DNS caching avoids repeated lookups
Wider range of material colors selectable
Improved spaghetti and static foreign-object detection; log export now includes AI monitoring photos by default (can be unticked)
Warns when a G-code file sets the bed temperature to 0 °C

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.3.0: 0.2/0.6/0.8 mm nozzle support and nozzle rules
entries.summary: V1.3.0 (2026-04-14) adds support for 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm nozzles with editable nozzle info per toolhead, plus safety rules against mixing diameters. It also reads the build plate type from sliced files and connects to hidden SSIDs. Snapmaker Orca 2.3.1+ or App 2.3.2+ recommended.

settings.advice: Set to the nozzle actually fitted; every toolhead used in the print must share it or the printer will not map the job.

facts: Edit nozzle size at Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Info > choose the toolhead > Save
After changing a nozzle, run Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and Heated Bed Leveling
Auto-refill is not allowed between toolheads with different nozzle diameters
A G-code nozzle diameter cannot be mapped onto a toolhead fitted with a different size
Plate type from the sliced file selects the matching Z-offset (-0.07 mm for smooth PEI and carbon-fiber textured plates)
Fixed a lingering Unedited Filament error and cloud-mode control problems on weak networks (unexpected parameter commands, delayed jobs)
Updated AI model, fewer false Pogo Pin continuity pauses, improved extrusion flow calibration

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.4.0: LED off after print, 64-object Skip Object limit
entries.summary: V1.4.0 (2026-05-25) adds Traditional Chinese and Russian, an option to switch the LEDs off after printing (Settings > Print Preferences) and raises Skip Object to 64 objects. Snapmaker Orca 2.3.1+ or App 2.3.2+ recommended.
facts: Skip Object now lists every object and avoids the occasional overlong extrusion seen after skipping
Updated AI defect detection workflow
Better performance and stability with fewer MCU control timeout errors

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.4.1: runout pause and filament recognition fixes
entries.summary: V1.4.1 (2026-06-11) is a bug-fix release. It repairs runout detection not pausing a job, AI detection misbehaving with a blocked camera, and filament info being lost after a restart.
facts: Runout could fail to pause a new print started after cancelling the previous one
AI defect detection now handles an obstructed camera correctly
Filament info could go unrecognized after reboot when Auto Loading was off and the slot showed Loaded

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.5.0: Top Cover support and different-color Auto-Refill
entries.summary: V1.5.0 (2026-07-01) adds Top Cover functions, an option to auto-refill with a different color, uploading of AI detection data, German and Hebrew, and Snapmaker TPU 90A and PLA Silk filament types. It introduced a first-layer squish bug, so Snapmaker says to go directly to V1.5.2.
facts: Top Cover: setup wizard on first connection, prompt to redo Vibration Compensation, fan speed on the Control page, filter run time and replacement guide under Settings > Maintenance > Usage Statistics; needs Snapmaker Orca or App 2.3.5
Allow auto-refill with different colors is set in Settings > Print Preferences
Fixed stray circular icons on Filament Setup and inaccurate X/Y/Z coordinates on the Control page
Fewer Timer too close errors

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.5.1: first-layer squish fix and required follow-up
entries.summary: V1.5.1 (2026-07-03) is a maintenance release fixing over-squished first layers on prints started without Heated Bed Leveling enabled. The fix was incomplete, so Snapmaker recommends V1.5.2 instead.
symptoms: First layer pressed too thin on V1.5.0
steps: After updating, unload filament from every toolhead and rerun Multi-Toolhead Offset Calibration
Keep Heated Bed Leveling enabled so the printer levels automatically before each print

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.5.2: final fix for over-squished first layers
entries.summary: V1.5.2 (2026-07-30) fully fixes the V1.5.0 bug that over-squished the first layer when Heated Bed Leveling was off (on V1.5.1 it still appeared after long idle periods). It also fixes false nozzle diameter mismatch warnings and heaters staying on after load/unload, and is the baseline for full Top Cover support.
symptoms: First layer too squished after upgrading to V1.5.0 or V1.5.1
Print will not start because of a false nozzle diameter mismatch
Nozzle stays hot after loading or unloading
steps: If you were on V1.5.0 or V1.5.1: unload all toolheads and rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration
Enable Heated Bed Leveling before printing
Coming from a version older than V1.5.0 needs no extra steps
If first layers are still poor, work through the warp/detach troubleshooting guide; for support send a first-layer photo, firmware version, the print file and whether bed leveling was on
facts: First-layer quality also depends on bed mesh data, offset calibration, plate flatness, filament condition and first-layer settings, so it can vary between printers on identical firmware

entries.title: U1 firmware V1.6.0: 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle option, faster loading
entries.summary: V1.6.0 (2026-08-25) adds a 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle choice in toolhead info editing, selectable filament types on the Filament Details page and a post-print AI monitoring report (cloud mode only). Loading and unloading are faster and filament tip forming on unload is better.
steps: If you fit the 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle, set it in Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Info
Then rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and Heated Bed Leveling
facts: Improved tip forming during unload reduces failures caused by swollen filament ends

Fixed: Z not moving in 0.1 mm steps, Wi-Fi Management page jumping after the Enter key, unused channels checking filament after resuming a client-started job, enclosure setup guide not showing after the initial setup wizard

entries.title: U1 firmware V2.0.0: rainbow filament display, high-flow warning change
entries.summary: V2.0.0 (2026-09-15), the newest listed release, adds rainbow filament display and French. Standard-flow G-code sent to a toolhead with a high-flow nozzle now only triggers a warning rather than blocking the print.
steps: After updating, confirm nozzle settings in Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Info
Rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and Heated Bed Leveling
facts: Fixed the printer waiting for chamber heat-up while the Top Cover ran in external circulation mode
Fixed abnormal system shutdown with G-code file names starting with #
Fixed glitches in the LAN monitoring view and slow login status after QR-code app binding on a new Wi-Fi network
Startup filament guidance skips its animation if the toolhead is already loaded; faster target temperature refresh on the Control page

entries.title: Snapmaker U1 firmware versions and the Snapmaker Orca versions they need
entries.summary: Snapmaker advises always running the newest U1 firmware; the latest listed is V2.0.0 (2026-09-15). Updating keeps calibration and leveling data, so a full recalibration is normally not needed, although a few releases ask for specific follow-up calibrations. Most releases name a minimum Snapmaker Orca and Snapmaker App version.
facts: Feature minimums: Top Cover needs firmware 1.5.2+ with Orca/App 2.3.5+; plate-type auto Z-offset needs firmware 1.3.0+ with Orca 2.3.1+; Auto-Refill guide asks for firmware 1.5.2+; official TPU profiles need Orca 2.3.4+
V1.5.0 and V1.5.1 had a first-layer over-squish bug; Snapmaker recommends jumping straight to V1.5.2 or newer

entries.title: U1 flow ratio calibration with the YOLO flow test
entries.summary: The slicer's flow value may not match what actually comes out of the nozzle. Print Snapmaker Orca's YOLO flow test, pick the flattest block and add its correction to the current flow ratio.
steps: Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended) generates the test model
Select the filament you print with, slice and print
Choose the block whose top shows the fewest bulges (too much flow) and gaps (too little); its number is the correction
In the filament settings under Flow ratio and Pressure Advance, set flow ratio = current + correction (e.g. 1 + -0.01 = 0.99)

settings.advice: Add the YOLO correction to the existing value.

entries.title: Reducing color bleeding and muddy colors in U1 Full Spectrum prints
entries.summary: Unintended blending or muddy colors in Full Spectrum prints are reduced by accurate toolhead alignment, filaments of suitable translucency, enough wall thickness and keeping mixing off large flat top surfaces.
symptoms: Colors look contaminated or blurred
Mixed colors not crisp
steps: Run XY offset calibration before Full Spectrum printing
Choose filaments with moderate to moderately high TD; very high or very low TD hurts clarity
Keep default or thicker walls
Avoid mixing effects on large flat Z-plane surfaces

settings.advice: Keep default or increase for cleaner color mixing.

entries.title: U1 Full Spectrum color mixing: modes, material rules and preview accuracy
entries.summary: Full Spectrum in Snapmaker Orca stacks thin layers of up to four loaded PLA filaments to make blended colors. It offers Ratio, Cycle, Match and Gradient modes and suits beginners. Mix only within one material family: no PLA with PETG or PVA. The preview only shows color trends, so print a small swatch first.
facts: Ratio: set filament proportions. Cycle: define the filament order per layer. Match: enter a target color to get a suggested combination and ratio. Gradient: smooth transitions between chosen colors
Final color depends on filament color and TD (transmission distance), mix ratio, layer height, geometry, toolpaths, flow and printing conditions
Other PLAs can be blended with Full Spectrum filament but results are not guaranteed
May use extra filament and time depending on mode and model; check the slicer estimate
Beginners can start from mixed-color models on Snapmaker Space
If the gradient is not visible in Preview, confirm orientation and slicing settings first

entries.title: Recommended filament and settings for U1 Full Spectrum prints
entries.summary: Use the Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum Filament Bundle with the built-in Snapmaker PLA Full Spectrum profile, a 0.4 mm or smaller nozzle and layers of 0.1 mm or less. Thinner layers give smoother transitions and fewer horizontal stripes; bigger nozzles and thicker layers expose the layered structure.

settings.advice: 0.1 mm or lower for smooth blends.
0.4 mm or smaller.
Stay within 190-230 °C.
Keep at or below 200 mm/s.

facts: Nozzle temperature 190-230 °C, bed 25-65 °C
Speed no higher than 200 mm/s; keep part cooling running
Dry at 55 °C for 6 hours if needed

entries.title: Uneven gloss (shiny and matte patches) on U1 prints, especially Silk PLA
entries.summary: Shiny and dull regions on one part, most obvious with Silk filament, come from different print speeds between layers. Check Preview > Speed in Snapmaker Orca, then even out speeds by turning off overhang slowdown (use supports for overhangs instead) and the cooling slowdown.
symptoms: Some areas glossy, others matte on the same model
Bands of different shine on Silk prints
causes: Overhang slowdown printing those walls slower
Layer-cooling slowdown reducing speed on small layers
steps: Slice and open Preview > Speed to spot layers printed at different speeds
Disable Slow down for overhangs (Process > Speed > Overhang speed) and support overhangs instead
In the filament's Cooling > Part cooling fan group, untick Slow printing down for better layer cooling
Re-slice and print

settings.advice: Turn off for Silk filaments so overhang walls run at the same speed as the rest.
Turn off to keep speed uniform between small and large layers.

sources.title: U1 significant gloss variation across different regions of the model

entries.title: U1 layer separation and interlayer cracking
entries.summary: Gaps or splits between layers, appearing during printing or as the part cools, leave it weak and ugly. Typical causes on the U1 are a nozzle that is too cool, layers too thick, too much part cooling, excessive speed, or cold drafts. Fix the temperature first with a temperature tower.
symptoms: Visible cracks or gaps between layers
Part splits along layer lines under light force
causes: Print temperature too low to fuse layers
Layer height too large
Part cooling fan too strong
Printing too fast for layers to bond
Large ambient temperature difference or drafts
steps: Print a temperature tower (Calibration > Temperature) and set the best block's value for first and other layers
Keep layer height between 20% and 80% of nozzle size (0.08-0.32 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle)
Lower the part cooling fan maximum speed
Reduce outer and inner wall speeds
Enclose the printer, for example with the U1 Top Cover

settings.advice: Raise toward the best temperature-tower value; cold layers do not fuse.
Set to the same calibrated temperature.
Lower it; stay within 20-80% of nozzle diameter.
Reduce so layers stay warm long enough to bond.
Reduce to give each line more heat and pressure.
Reduce together with the outer wall speed.

entries.title: Which filaments to print on the U1 Liber high-flow hotend
entries.summary: The Liber high-flow hotend handles PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PA, PC, PVA, support and other engineering filaments. Avoid high-flow printing with CF-, GF- or wood-filled filaments, whose fibers can tangle or char and clog at high rates, and with TPU, which feeds unstably. Use a standard hotend for those, hardened steel for CF/GF.
facts: ABS, ASA, PA and PC should be printed with the Top Cover fitted
Same 0.4 mm presets as stock hotend apply

sources.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber High Flow Hotend for U1

entries.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber high-flow hotend for U1: specs and setup
entries.summary: The Liber is an optional U1-only hotend that melts filament faster for higher throughput. It pays off on large parts with long continuous paths, batch jobs and strength settings (thick walls, dense infill); on detailed parts with many corners or direction changes the gain is small. Max 300 °C, 0.4 mm nozzle, heater pre-installed.
steps: Install it exactly like the stock hotend
On the touchscreen set the 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle in Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Info (firmware 1.6.0+)
Rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and Heated Bed Leveling
Slice with the Liber system parameters in Snapmaker Orca; existing 0.4 mm filament presets can be reused

settings.advice: Stays 0.4 mm with the Liber hotend; use the Liber system profile rather than standard-flow.

facts: Sold as 4-pack or single; you can upgrade only some toolheads
Not compatible with any other Snapmaker printer
Heater uses the same spec as the stock hotend, so a stock heater can replace a damaged one

sources.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber High Flow Hotend for U1

entries.title: Mixing high-flow and standard hotends or nozzle sizes on one U1
entries.summary: Different toolheads may carry high-flow and standard hotends, and different materials, but all toolheads used in one print must share the same nozzle diameter. The flow type and diameter in the sliced file must match what each toolhead has fitted. Sources differ on flow-type mismatches: the Liber FAQ says the print is blocked, while firmware V2.0.0 only warns when standard-flow G-code meets a high-flow nozzle.

settings.advice: Must equal the nozzle installed on every toolhead the print uses.

facts: Firmware 1.3.0+: G-code nozzle diameter cannot be mapped to a toolhead with a different nozzle, and auto-refill never crosses diameters
V1.5.2 fixed false nozzle diameter mismatch warnings that stopped prints
Record nozzle changes in Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Info, then rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and Heated Bed Leveling

sources.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber High Flow Hotend for U1

entries.title: U1 cold pull to clear a clogged nozzle (230 °C extrude, 70 °C pull)
entries.summary: Use a cold pull for clogs too stubborn for the cleaning needle. The toolhead must already have filament loaded: heat to 230 °C and extrude, park the toolhead and let it cool to 70 °C, then pull the filament out so the debris comes with it.
steps: Control > Toolheads, select the toolhead and tap Attach Toolhead
Tap Nozzle Temp., set 230 °C, Done, and wait for it to heat
Tap EXTRUDE and let filament flow out
Tap Detach Toolhead, then set the nozzle to 70 °C
At 70 °C, press the round clamp on the toolhead and pull the filament tube out
Hold the orange lever, grip the filament above the toolhead and pull steadily with moderate force
If it will not come out, repeat the 230 °C extrude and 70 °C cool cycle rather than forcing it
A good pull leaves a funnel-shaped tip matching the inside of the nozzle
Rotate the spool holder to retract the filament without tangling, cut off the deformed end and reload

entries.title: Checking and replacing the U1 nozzle wiper cleaning brush
entries.summary: The brush on the nozzle wiper scrubs each nozzle automatically whenever a toolhead is picked up or parked. If the brush wears out or falls off, filament collects on the nozzle exterior, which can disturb extrusion and weaken first-layer adhesion.
steps: Inspect the brush on the nozzle wiper; a little cleaned-off filament on it is normal
If it is damaged or detached, peel the old brush off and stick a spare brush from the U1 toolbox in the same place
Replacement wipers: Toolhead 1 uses the Left Nozzle Wiper, toolheads 2, 3 and 4 use the Right Nozzle Wiper

entries.title: Cleaning the U1 PEI steel build plate
entries.summary: Dust, skin oil and leftover brims or supports weaken adhesion and spoil the next bottom layer. Wipe after prints, wash with dish soap every 5-10 prints, scrape off stubborn residue as needed, and clean before big jobs. Always let the plate cool below about 40 °C and take it off the printer first.
steps: Quick clean: wipe with a lint-free cloth dampened with a little ethanol
Wash: rinse under water, scrub with a sponge and dish soap (focus on fingerprints and residue), rinse all soap off, dry with a towel and let it air-dry
Residue (textured plate): lay it flat, hold the supplied scraper at 15-30°, slide the blade under the edge of the residue and push forward evenly without prying up, then wipe
facts: Never use acetone; it permanently damages the PEI surface
Avoid steel wool, abrasive pads and sharp metal tools such as knives or screwdrivers
Never use a scraper on the smooth PEI plate, neither to clean it nor to remove prints
A sponge reaches into the textured grooves better than a cloth

sources.title: How to clean your PEI steel sheet

entries.title: Easy-to-remove supports on the U1 using PLA and PETG as interface material
entries.summary: Pair materials that stick poorly to each other (PLA with PETG, or PLA with TPU) so one forms the support interface. Print the support base in the model material, because PLA and PETG want different bed temperatures, and use the other filament only for the interface. Dry the filaments first; damp support material bonds too hard or too weakly.
steps: Example: Filament 1 Generic PETG HF for model and support base, Filament 2 Snapspeed PLA for the interface; enable supports
Top Z distance 0, base pattern Rectilinear grid, 3 top interface layers, interface pattern Rectilinear Interlaced, top and bottom interface spacing 0
Snapmaker's tested values: PLA at 230 °C, PETG bed at 65 °C
Reversed (PLA model, PETG interface): PETG 265 °C, bed 65 °C, max volumetric speed 10 mm³/s; PLA 230 °C
Assign the wipe tower to the model filament so the tower does not delaminate

settings.advice: Set 0 when the interface is a non-bonding material for a tight, smooth underside.
Rectilinear grid.
3 layers of the contrasting material.
Rectilinear Interlaced.
0 for a dense interface.
0 as well.
Use the model filament for the support base.
Use the contrasting filament (PLA under PETG, or PETG under PLA).
10 mm³/s for PETG used as interface.
Set to the model filament for a stable tower.

entries.title: U1 poor first-layer adhesion: lifting, shifting or dragged first layer
entries.summary: When the first layer does not stick, edges lift, the part shifts or the nozzle scrapes it loose. Main causes: dirty plate, filament stuck on the nozzle (or a missing wiper brush), unlevel bed, first layer printed too fast, and bed too cool for the plate type.
symptoms: First layer lifts at edges
Part slides off during printing
Nozzle catches and tears the first layer
causes: Dust, oil or fingerprints on the plate
Residue on the nozzle exterior reducing extrusion
Bed not level
First layer speed too high
Bed temperature too low
steps: Cool and remove the plate, wipe with a lint-free cloth and a little ethanol; deep-clean PEI if needed
Brush residue off the hot nozzle and check the nozzle wiper brush
Run auto leveling; if that is not enough, level manually with the handwheels, then auto level again
Lower first layer and first layer infill speed and add more slow layers
Confirm Printer > Bed type matches the installed plate, then raise that plate's first-layer bed temperature in the filament profile

settings.advice: Lower so the line is pressed onto the plate before it cools.
Lower along with initial layer speed.
Increase to ramp speed up gradually over the first layers.
Must match the installed plate so the right bed temperature is used.
Raise a few degrees for the Textured PEI Plate if edges lift.
Raise for the Smooth PEI Plate if edges lift; keep under 100 °C bed max.

entries.title: U1 pressure advance calibration with the PA Line test
entries.summary: Pressure advance adjusts extrusion pressure ahead of speed changes: less before slowing to avoid blobs, more before speeding up to avoid thin lines. The U1 has a direct drive extruder (DDE); print the PA Line pattern and use the value of the most even line.
steps: Calibration > Pressure Advance: choose DDE and PA Line mode, keep the default start, end and step, click OK
Select your filament and enable pressure advance in its Flow ratio and Pressure Advance settings
Slice; Preview > Speed shows each line accelerating then decelerating
Print and pick the line with uniform width from end to end; the number beside it is the PA value
Too low: thin at acceleration, thick at deceleration. Too high: the opposite
Enter the value as Pressure Advance in the filament profile

settings.advice: Turn on before printing the PA test and for normal use.
Set to the most uniform PA Line value.

entries.title: Preventing U1 prime/wipe tower collapse with TPU or mixed materials
entries.summary: TPU towers are floppy, and towers built from materials that do not bond (TPU with PLA, PLA with PETG) delaminate and fall over. Stiffen the tower with wider, longer ribs and print its walls from a single filament, ideally the model's material.
symptoms: Prime tower topples or breaks mid-print
Tower splits along layers
causes: Low stiffness of TPU
Poor bonding between different materials in the tower walls
steps: Process > Global > Multimaterial: increase tower rib width and rib length
Process > Global > Multimaterial > Filament for Features: assign one filament to the wipe tower (the model's filament when using a different support material)

settings.advice: Increase for a sturdier rib-wall tower.
Increase to widen the tower's footprint and stability.
Set to a single filament (the model material) so tower walls always bond.

sources.title: Using a Different Filament for Support (PLA and PETG)

entries.title: Bubbles, bulges or dents on the U1 Smooth PEI plate
entries.summary: The Smooth PEI plate is a PEI film bonded with adhesive to spring steel, so heat cycles and adhesion gradually raise small bubbles, soft bumps or shallow dents. These are normal wear and rarely affect prints, but heating the plate can flatten them.
symptoms: Small round or irregular raised spots that feel springy
Bubbles more visible when the bed is hot
Shallow dents in the print area
steps: Place the plate on the bed with the bulging side facing down
Control > Control > Heated Bed Temp., set 100 °C, Done
Wait 20-30 minutes without touching the plate
Inspect: small remaining bumps settle with use; contact support if severe ones still affect printing
Before touching, set the bed to 0 °C and wait until the plate reaches room temperature

sources.title: U1 Common Issues with Smooth PEI Steel Plate

entries.title: Model outlines and gloss marks left on the U1 Smooth PEI plate
entries.summary: Outlines, light or dark patches or gloss changes matching earlier prints are normal aging of the Smooth PEI plate and do not affect function. They can be reduced with a release agent, regular cleaning, tight hotend screws and suitable bed temperatures.
symptoms: Outlines of previous parts on the plate
Color or gloss differences between used and unused areas
Slight texture changes
steps: Apply a glue stick or liquid glue release layer when printing PETG, TPU and ABS
Clean the plate regularly
Check the hotend fixing screws are tight; a loose hotend lets the nozzle run too close to the plate
Keep the bed reasonably warm: PLA about 50-65 °C, PETG about 70-80 °C, ABS/ASA higher

settings.advice: For the Smooth PEI Plate use about 50-65 °C for PLA and 70-80 °C for PETG.

sources.title: U1 Common Issues with Smooth PEI Steel Plate

entries.title: Torn, scratched or stretched film on the U1 Smooth PEI plate
entries.summary: The flexible PEI film is damaged by strong pulling, impacts or hard tools. Damage usually happens when strongly adhering materials are printed without a release layer, or prints are pried off hot or with metal tools.
symptoms: White stretch marks
Scratches or local damage
Film deformed or torn-looking in the print area
causes: PETG, TPU or ABS printed without glue as a release agent
Removing prints before the plate has cooled
Prying parts off with sharp metal tools
steps: Apply glue stick or liquid glue before printing PETG, TPU or ABS (see the Build Plate Guide or the filament TDS)
Wait for the bed to return to room temperature before removing parts
Do not scrape the smooth plate; for stubborn parts spray alcohol around the base and let it soak under before lifting

sources.title: U1 Common Issues with Smooth PEI Steel Plate

entries.title: Snapmaker U1 specifications
entries.summary: The U1 is a CoreXY toolchanger with four independent direct-drive toolheads (SnapSwap), a build volume of 270 x 270 x 270 mm and firmware built on Klipper, Moonraker and Fluidd. Stock hotends are 0.4 mm stainless steel rated to 300 °C, the bed reaches 100 °C, and motion peaks at 500 mm/s and 20000 mm/s². Out of the box it is rated for PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA and PCTG; ABS, ASA, PA, PC and PET need the Top Cover, and fiber-filled filaments also need hardened steel hotends.
facts: Build volume 270 x 270 x 270 mm. Machine 584 x 499 x 730 mm and 18.2 kg; with Top Cover 584 x 510 x 751 mm and 21.8 kg
4 toolheads, up to 4 filaments or colors per print. Each filament keeps its own nozzle, so there is no flush between colors, only a small prime tower to clear degraded material from standby nozzles
Ships with 4 x 0.4 mm stainless steel hotends plus 1 spare. Heatsink, heat break, heater block and nozzle form one unit and cannot be replaced individually. Hardened steel hotends are optional
Firmware V1.3.0+ supports 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8 mm nozzles; V1.6.0+ adds a 0.4 mm high-flow (Liber) option. All toolheads used in one print must share one nozzle diameter
Max nozzle 300 °C; max heated bed 100 °C. Bed is 6.5 mm thick (1.5 mm base + 5 mm ribs) with mesh variation generally within 0.4 mm. Parked toolheads idle at about 70 °C
Max toolhead speed 500 mm/s, acceleration up to 20000 mm/s². Dimensional accuracy up to ±0.1 mm, repeatability ±0.04 mm on every axis. No hotend PID tuning
Layer height range per the FAQ: 0.08-0.24 mm, default 0.2 mm (the interlayer-cracking guide instead allows 20-80% of nozzle diameter, i.e. 0.08-0.32 mm on 0.4 mm)

Materials: base PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, PCTG; with Top Cover add PET, ABS, ASA, PA, PC; with Top Cover plus hardened steel hotends add CF- and GF-reinforced. Third-party 1.75 mm filament works but RFID recognition does not

Plates: one textured PEI steel plate included; smooth PEI (keep below 105 °C) and carbon-fiber textured (keep below 80 °C) plates on a magnetic bed. Firmware applies -0.07 mm Z-offset for both add-on plates

Sensors and safety: toolhead probe for automatic bed leveling, per-toolhead filament runout sensors, tangle detection, RFID spool recognition, power-loss recovery, thermal runaway shutdown, 2 MP camera (about 1 Hz) for AI spaghetti and foreign-object detection

Motion: CoreXY with carbon-fiber X rod, all-metal Y and Z, belts plus lead screws. Spool holder takes 52-60 mm hub, up to 70 mm wide and 1 kg. SnapSwap rated 1,000,000 swaps; each toolhead's pogo pins 250,000 (clean contacts every 100,000)

Power 100-240 V: max 1150 W / 6 A at 220-240 V, 400 W / 4 A at 100-120 V. Noise 55 dB at 1 m (under 50 dB with Top Cover). Operate at 15-30 °C ambient. Connects via Wi-Fi, USB drive and, from firmware V1.2.0, Ethernet through a USB adapter

sources.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber High Flow Hotend for U1

entries.title: Giving the U1 a static IP address with a router DHCP binding
entries.summary: If the U1 keeps going offline, fails to bind, or gets a new IP after a reboot (painful when several printers share a LAN), reserve its address in the router by binding its MAC address to its current IP. Menu names differ by router brand; the wiki example uses a Ruijie RG-X60 PRO.
steps: Connect your phone, tablet or computer to the same router as the printer
Open the router's management address in a browser (usually printed on the router label) and log in
Open the connected client list and find the U1 by its IP address
Bind the printer's MAC address to that IP (in the example, click Unbind next to the device and confirm with OK)
To undo, remove the binding again (Bind then confirm in the example)

sources.title: U1 How to set a static IP address

entries.title: Removing a U1 screw with a stripped head
entries.summary: Covers screws whose drive recess (slot, Phillips, hex or Torx) is worn so the driver spins without turning the screw. Try gentle methods first and move to cutting or an extractor bit only if needed.
causes: Driver of the wrong size or type, loading only a few edges of the recess
Too little downward pressure or turning at an angle, so the bit slips at peak torque
A worn, rounded driver bit
Continuing to force a screw that will not turn
steps: Lightly stripped: lay a rubber band, balloon or piece of nitrile glove over the head and press the driver through it while unscrewing
Grip the outside of the head with screw removal pliers and turn it out
Cut a straight slot across the head with a rotary tool cutting disc and use a flat screwdriver (not for low-profile or hard stainless screws)
Use a screw extractor bit: drill in with one end, extract with the other, keeping firm pressure; check which rotation direction your tool needs

entries.title: Finding the best nozzle temperature on the U1 with a temperature tower
entries.summary: Each filament has its own sweet spot, so print Snapmaker Orca's temperature tower, in which identical blocks are printed at stepped temperatures, and use the value of the best-looking block.
steps: In the Prepare tab select the filament you will print with
Calibration > Temperature, choose the filament type and keep or set Start temp and End temp (defaults differ per material)
Click OK to generate the tower, then print it on the U1
Discard blocks with poor quality and read the number on the best one (e.g. 200 means 200 °C)
Edit the filament: Filament > Print temperature > Nozzle, set first layer and other layers to that value

settings.advice: Set to the best tower block.
Set to the same calibrated value.

entries.title: Fitting the U1 toolhead USB cable without over-tightening the screws
entries.summary: The toolhead cable's connector housing is soft plastic, so cranking its two screws can strip the threads or damage parts inside. It supplements User Manual section 5.19 (p. 55).
steps: Use the supplied H2.0 hex key; do not use an electric screwdriver
Turn both fixing screws until you feel clear resistance, then stop
Wiggle the USB connector gently; if it still moves, give each screw another half turn (180°), alternating, and check again
Stop tightening as soon as the connector no longer moves
facts: Correct: the screw head sits flush on the plastic step. Over-tightened: head sits sunk below the plastic surface
For a support ticket choose Issue Type Toolhead and description Issue Caused by USB Cable

entries.title: U1 Top Cover internal vs external circulation by filament type
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca chooses the Top Cover mode from the selected filaments' chamber needs and writes it into the G-code; it cannot be switched on the touchscreen. Internal circulation (heat retention): PEBA, ASA, ABS, PC, PA, PETG. External circulation (heat removal): PLA, TPU, PVA, PLA support.
facts: Several filaments in one print: same mode on all is fine (ABS + ASA, PLA + TPU)
Filaments needing different modes are normally blocked from slicing; for some pairs the more heat-sensitive one decides, e.g. PETG + PLA uses external circulation
Plan multi-material jobs with filaments that share a circulation mode
If the exhaust fan runs for a high-temperature filament, or recirculation for a heat-sensitive one, update Snapmaker Orca or install its hotfix (profile configuration bug)
Firmware 2.0.0 fixed the printer waiting for chamber heat-up in external mode

entries.title: Replacing the U1 Top Cover exhaust (external circulation) fan
entries.summary: Easy job, about 20 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. The fan sits in the external circulation assembly inside the upper housing.
steps: Unplug the Top Cover cable, remove the magnetic front door and lift the cover off the printer
Turn the cover over and release the clips
Remove the 3 ST3x8 screws holding the external circulation assembly; flip the upper housing, remove the 2 ST3x8 adapter board screws, lift the board and unplug the ribbon cable
Remove 1 ST3x8 screw and take off the air duct, then remove the 4 ST3x35 fan screws
Fit the new fan, pass its cable through the opening and fasten with 4 ST3x35
Refit the duct with the fan facing the same way as the housing air outlet (1 ST3x8)
Seat the assembly with the cable clear of the outlet (3 ST3x8)
Plug the ribbon cable into the adapter board, lay it in its slot, align the locating pins and fasten 2 ST3x8
Reinstall the Top Cover per its installation guide

sources.title: U1 Top Cover Exhaust Fan Replacement Guide

entries.title: U1 Top Cover: replacing the fan adapter unit or the cover cable
entries.summary: Easy job, about 20 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. The Fan Adapter Unit joins the Top Cover cable to the internal and external circulation fans.
steps: Unplug the Top Cover cable, remove the front door, lift the cover off, turn it over and release the clips
Flip the upper housing and remove the 2 ST3x8 screws holding the Fan Adapter Unit
Lift the unit and unplug its three connectors: Top Cover cable, internal circulation fan and external circulation fan
Fit the new unit or cable, reconnect all three and fasten the 2 ST3x8 screws
Reinstall the Top Cover

sources.title: U1 Top Cover Fan Adapter Unit and Top Cover Cable Replacement Guide

entries.title: U1 Top Cover fan speed limits, temporary overrides and overheat protection
entries.summary: Fan speeds can be changed during a print from the touchscreen Top Cover page, Snapmaker Orca or the App, but this never changes the mode and is not saved: the next job again follows the G-code. Per-filament fan speeds cannot be stored.
facts: Internal mode: recirculation fan can go down to 10% (lower may weaken filtration); exhaust fan stays off to hold heat
External mode: exhaust fan adjustable but cannot be switched off (slower may hurt quality); recirculation fan free
Standby: both fans independently adjustable
External mode overheat protection automatically speeds up the exhaust fan if the chamber gets too hot, overriding a lowered setting, to stop softened filament clogging the nozzle
With PLA the right-side exhaust fan starts by itself, pulling air in at the bottom inlet and pushing hot air out through the vent

entries.title: When to replace the U1 Top Cover air filter
entries.summary: The U1 logs how long the Top Cover filter has run and automatically shows a replacement guide on the touchscreen when it is due. Filter status can also be checked under the usage statistics menu.
facts: Top Cover guide path: Settings > Device Maintenance > Usage Statistics; V1.5.0 notes call it Settings > Maintenance > Usage Statistics
The filter sits behind a filter cover in the Internal Circulation Kit

sources.title: U1 Top Cover Recirculation Fan Replacement Guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 Top Cover upper or lower housing
entries.summary: Easy job, about 20 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. The lower housing comes free once the clips are released; the upper housing needs both circulation kits and the adapter board moved over.
steps: Unplug the Top Cover cable, remove the front door, lift the cover off, turn it over and release the clips; the lower housing can now be swapped
When rejoining, seat the Top Cover cable in the rear groove, line the upper housing up with the holes in the lower housing and press it home
Upper housing: flip it, remove the 2 ST3x8 adapter board screws and the 6 ST3x8 screws of the internal and external circulation kits, then lift the kits out
Mount both kits on the new upper housing with the 6 ST3x8 screws, keeping the external kit's cable clear of the air outlet
Lay the adapter board cable in its slot, align the locating pins, fasten 2 ST3x8 and reinstall the Top Cover

sources.title: U1 Top Cover Housing Replacement Guide

entries.title: U1 Top Cover enclosure: features, requirements and first setup
entries.summary: The Top Cover is an add-on enclosure that uses heat from the bed to warm the chamber for ABS, ASA and similar filaments. It runs internal circulation (recirculation fan through a three-stage filter, keeps heat, cuts odors and particles) or external circulation (exhaust fan, no filter, vents heat). It also lowers noise to under 50 dB.
steps: Update to firmware 1.5.2+, Snapmaker Orca 2.3.5+ and Snapmaker App 2.3.5+
Assemble per the Top Cover User Manual and plug in its cable; a Top Cover control card appears on the touchscreen (if not, check the cable)
Follow the setup guide shown on first connection (it appears only once)
Redo Vibration Compensation, because the cover changes the machine's resonance
facts: Parts: housing with magnetic front door, Internal Circulation Kit (recirculation fan and filter), External Circulation Kit (exhaust fan, no filter)
With cover the U1 needs 584 x 510 x 751 mm and weighs 21.8 kg
Adds PET, ABS, ASA, PA and PC to the supported materials

entries.title: Replacing the U1 Top Cover recirculation (internal circulation) fan
entries.summary: Easy job, about 20 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. The fan is mounted under the filter box of the Internal Circulation Kit.
steps: Unplug the Top Cover cable, remove the front door and lift the cover off; open the filter cover and take out the filter
Turn the cover over and release the clips
Remove the 3 ST3x8 screws of the Internal Circulation Kit; flip the upper housing and remove the 2 ST3x8 adapter board screws
Remove the 3 ST3x8 filter box screws, lift off the box and separate the fan from its base
Fit the new fan and route its cable through the opening
Align the filter box with the blower base locating pins and fasten 3 ST3x8
Put the kit back (3 ST3x8) and reinstall the filter
Reconnect the adapter board cables, fasten its 2 ST3x8 screws and reinstall the Top Cover

sources.title: U1 Top Cover Recirculation Fan Replacement Guide
