entries.title: TPU alternating over- and under-extrusion on the U1
entries.summary: TPU reacts strongly to resistance in the filament path: pressure drops cause gaps or dents, then built-up pressure releases as surface bumps. Clear the external path first, then purge more to flush TPU residue from the nozzle.
symptoms: Gaps or dents followed by bulges on the surface
Inconsistent extrusion with TPU
causes: Bent or loose filament tube
Tight dryer box outlet
Spool holder not turning freely
TPU buildup partly clogging the nozzle
steps: Check the tube for bends or looseness, the dryer outlet for tightness and the spool holder for free rotation
Increase prime volume in Process > Global > Multimaterial > Prime Tower
Add skirt loops so the nozzle extrudes continuously before the model starts

settings.advice: Increase to flush partially stuck TPU after each tool change.
Add loops to prime the hotend steadily before the part.

entries.title: Unmelted TPU squeezing out of gaps in the U1 toolhead
entries.summary: TPU is hard to push and retract, so high resistance makes it bunch up inside the toolhead and even escape through small gaps. Slow down, shorten the toolchange retraction, and ease the extruder tension.
symptoms: Unmelted TPU visible squeezing out of the toolhead
TPU jams at the extruder
causes: Excess resistance during feeding and retraction
steps: Lower outer and inner wall speeds (Process > Global > Speed > Other layers speed)
Shorten Retraction Length (Toolchange) in the filament's Setting Overrides
Back off the toolhead's side screws a little to ease feeding resistance

settings.advice: Reduce for TPU to lower feed pressure.
Reduce as well.
Reduce (set as a filament override for TPU) so less soft filament is pulled back and buckled at tool changes.

entries.title: Reliable TPU printing workflow on the U1 (TPU 95A HF and 90A)
entries.summary: TPU is the hardest common filament on the U1. Snapmaker offers TPU 95A HF (stiffer, faster, easier) and TPU 90A (softer, more demanding). Dry it and keep it sealed, load it manually, use Snapmaker Orca 2.3.4+ with the official TPU profiles, and switch off dynamic flow calibration when starting the job.
steps: Prefer Snapmaker TPU 95A HF or 90A with their built-in profiles
Dry the spool (e.g. SnapDryer) and keep it sealed for the whole print
Load manually and enter filament info by hand (RFID is not read when feeding from the dryer)
Update Snapmaker Orca to 2.3.4+; if the profile is missing, import Snapmaker TPU 90A / TPU 95A HF via the Filament Management settings icon
Optionally start from a tested Library model (e.g. Squishy TPU Donut), which loads matching presets
Turn off dynamic flow calibration when sending the print; compressible TPU makes it unreliable
To tidy strings, sweep a heat gun at about 200 °C from 5-10 cm, briefly; not for large surfaces
facts: The Liber high-flow hotend is not recommended for TPU; use a standard hotend

sources.title: Snapmaker x Phaetus Liber High Flow Hotend for U1

entries.title: TPU stringing, color bleeding and heavy layer lines on the U1
entries.summary: Stringing and color bleed with TPU are usually moisture boiling in the hotend, so dry or replace the spool first, then lower temperature. Pronounced layer lines come from nozzle drag on soft walls: slow the outer wall and increase part cooling.
symptoms: Fine strings between features
Colors smearing into each other
Very visible layer lines on walls
causes: Wet filament producing bubbles
Print temperature too high
Many small isolated features causing travel
Outer walls not solidifying before the nozzle drags them
steps: Dry the TPU thoroughly or swap to a fresh spool
Reduce the Other layers nozzle temperature
Simplify or merge small isolated features to cut travel moves
For layer lines lower outer wall speed and raise part cooling fan speed

settings.advice: Lower in small steps if stringing persists with dry filament.
Lower to reduce drag lines on soft TPU walls.
Increase so outer walls set faster.
Increase together with minimum fan speed.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 active extruder gear assembly
entries.summary: The active (driving) extruder gear sits inside the U1 extruder unit, which must come out of the toolhead. The job is easy (2/5, about 20 minutes) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys. After reassembly, make sure all three gears mesh and turn smoothly when you rotate the active gear.
steps: Remove the toolhead from the dock (see toolhead removal entry)
Remove the 3 top cover screws and the back cover; disconnect the extruder unit cables and the two PCB screws (H1.5 and H2.0)
Free the cables from the extruder unit clips and remove its 4 screws (two H1.5, two H2.0)
Remove the bearing block (4 screws), then the spring screw, compression spring and spring block
Remove 2 H1.5 screws and take out the filament runout sensor, driven gear assembly and active gear assembly
Fit the new active gear, then the driven gear; turn the active gear to confirm all three gears mesh and spin freely
Refit the runout sensor, spring with the spring block on top, and bearing block
Reinstall the extruder unit and PCB, routing its 3 cables as originally, reconnect, then refit covers and the toolhead
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes
Tools: H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys

sources.title: U1 active extruder gear assembly replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 auxiliary cooling fan
entries.summary: The U1 auxiliary cooling fan sits between the left panel and the left inner panel. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 15 minutes) with an H2.0 hex key: remove the left side panel (unload toolheads 1 and 2 first), unplug the fan, remove its 3 screws, fit the new fan and reassemble.
steps: Remove the left side panel (see side panel removal entry)
Unplug the auxiliary cooling fan cable
Remove the 3 fan screws and lift the fan out
Fit the new fan with the 3 screws and reconnect its cable
Reinstall the left panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 15 minutes
The auxiliary fan cable plugs into the RFID board

sources.title: U1 auxiliary cooling fan replacement guide

entries.title: U1 heated bed not heating or heating slowly (error 0003-0526-0000-0001)
entries.summary: Use this when the U1 bed temperature reads normally but the bed will not heat or heats slowly, or an error such as 0003-0526-0000-0001 appears while heating. Work through three scenarios: the bed control cable (watch the AC Board indicator), an open heating element (L-N should measure 46-52.3 Ohm), and wrong PID behavior from a misdetected supply voltage, fixed on firmware 1.2 or later.
symptoms: Bed temperature displays normally but does not rise, or rises slowly
Error during bed heating
causes: Bed control cable loose or faulty
Heating element open circuit or loose L/N cables
AC Board fault
Supply voltage misdetected, giving wrong PID parameters (older firmware)
steps: Power off, remove the right side panel and the power supply enclosure (4 screws; unplug its cooling fan)
Reconnect the toolhead cable to the Hub Adapter Board, power on and set the bed to 100 C; watch whether the AC Board indicator lights
Indicator off: reseat both ends of the bed control cable and retry; still off means contact support
Indicator on but the bed cannot reach 100 C: reseat the bed L and N cables and retry
Power off and measure L to N resistance: 46-52.3 Ohm is normal, so replace the AC Board; out of range means replace the heated bed
Check your local mains voltage, send QUERY_POWER_LOSS_CHECK_INFO and compare the voltage the printer reports; if they differ, update to firmware 1.2 or later
Done when the bed reaches 100 C without errors
facts: Bed heater L-N reference resistance: 46-52.3 Ohm
Difficulty 3/5, 30-50 minutes; tools: H2.0 hex key, multimeter

entries.title: U1 heated bed temperature error 0003-0526-0000-0000 reading above 110 C
entries.summary: If the reading that triggered U1 error 0003-0526-0000-0000 is above 110 C, isolate the bed by unplugging its control cable from the main control board. If the reading then drops below -10 C the bed NTC side is suspect; if it stays above 110 C the fault is on the board, often the ESD protection device, which the wiki has you cut out before resorting to a main board replacement.
symptoms: Bed temperature reads above 110 C
Error 0003-0526-0000-0000 with a high instantaneous temperature
causes: Faulty ESD protection device on the main control board bed NTC input
Faulty heated bed NTC
Main control board fault
steps: Power off and unplug; remove the right side panel and the power cover (4 screws, H2.0)
Disconnect the bed control cable from the main control board, reconnect power and switch on
Reading falls below -10 C: measure the bed NTC resistance (80-120 kOhm at 25 C) and contact support
Reading stays above 110 C: with diagonal pliers cut the indicated ESD tube so its two solder pads are no longer connected, removing any leftover bits with the pliers or tweezers
If the error clears, the ESD protection part was the fault; otherwise request a Main Control Board replacement
Verify by restarting and heating the bed to 100 C with no error
facts: Normal bed reading window: -10 C to 110 C

sources.title: U1 heated bed temperature exceeds limit

entries.title: U1 heated bed temperature error 0003-0526-0000-0000 reading below -10 C (open NTC circuit)
entries.summary: Error 0003-0526-0000-0000 fires when the U1 bed reading leaves the -10 C to 110 C window. Tap the code to see the reading that triggered it. A value below -10 C usually means the bed NTC signal is lost: a loose or damaged bed control cable, a bad pin on the main control board (pin 2 is the bed NTC signal) or AC board, a twisted harness, or a failed NTC (should read 80-120 kOhm at 25 C).
symptoms: Bed temperature shows a negative value
Error 0003-0526-0000-0000 with an instantaneous temperature below -10 C
causes: Bed control cable not fully seated at either end
Loose, burnt or blackened pin on the main control board bed connector (pin 2 = bed NTC signal)
Loose connector base or cable on the AC board
Bed harness twisted or damaged where it flexes
Heated bed NTC failed
steps: Power off and unplug; remove the right side panel, then the power cover (4 screws, H2.0)
Disconnect the power supply cooling fan wire, unplug both ends of the bed control cable and plug them back firmly
Leaving the panels off, plug the toolhead USB cable back into the Hub Adapter Board and fasten it, then power on and see whether the reading is back in range
If still wrong, inspect the main control board bed connector pins, the two connector bases on the AC board, and gently wiggle the bed NTC terminal
Raise the bed to the top and look for a twisted or damaged bed harness
Measure the bed NTC on the 200 kOhm range: about 80-120 kOhm at 25 C is normal; outside that, the Heated Bed Assembly needs replacing
A damaged board connector means that board needs replacing via support; verify the fix by heating the bed to 100 C without error
facts: Normal bed reading window: -10 C to 110 C
Difficulty 3/5, 20-40 minutes; tools: H2.0 hex key, tweezers, diagonal pliers, multimeter
Do not touch the main board, power supply or other live parts while powered

sources.title: U1 heated bed temperature exceeds limit

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0523-0000-0002: disabling a faulty toolhead in printer.cfg
entries.summary: A blob wrapped around a U1 hotend can damage its thermistor cable, giving abnormal (even negative) nozzle readings and error 0003-0523-0000-0002 that survives reboots and blocks all printing, even with healthy toolheads. Until the part is replaced, back up printer.cfg and edit the faulty head's block in Fluidd so the printer ignores it, then restore the original file after the repair.
symptoms: Error 0003-0523-0000-0002 that returns after every restart
Abnormal or negative nozzle temperature on one toolhead after a blob
causes: Thermistor cable damaged by a filament blob around the hotend
steps: Touchscreen: Settings > Maintenance > Advanced Mode, tick Agree to enable it
Open the printer IP in a browser (Fluidd), go to Configuration, right-click printer.cfg and Download a backup
Find the head's section with Ctrl+F: toolhead 1 = extruder, 2 = extruder1, 3 = extruder2, 4 = extruder3
Sensor pin line: comment it out with #, paste a copy below and change its last two characters to PC5
Max temperature line: comment it out, paste a copy and set the maximum to 999
Hotend fan block (example: heater_fan e1_nozzle_fan): set its temperature to 999 and its speed above 260 C to 0 so it does not run flat out constantly
Save and restart, then confirm the other toolheads work
After replacing the damaged part, undo the edits or upload the backup (named printer.cfg) to overwrite the modified file

sources.title: U1 how to bypass a faulty toolhead 0003-0523-0000-0002

entries.title: Replacing the U1 camera (camera kit with FPC cable) and fixing no camera image
entries.summary: The U1 camera is on the right inner panel, so the right side panel must come off. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 15 minutes) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys. Afterward check the feed in the Snapmaker App or Snapmaker Orca; if there is no image, the flat cable is usually not fully inserted or its latch is not closed.
steps: Remove the right side panel (unload toolheads 3 and 4 first; see side panel removal entry)
Remove the 2 H2.0 screws holding the camera base
Open the black latch on the FPC connector and unplug the cable, then take out camera and base
Remove the 2 H1.5 screws to separate camera from base and fit the new camera to the base
Mount the base with its 2 H2.0 screws and reconnect the FPC cable, closing the latch
Power on and check the camera in the Snapmaker App or Snapmaker Orca; if no image, reseat the cable fully and press the clip down
Reassemble the panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables, then reload filament
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 15 minutes

sources.title: U1 camera kit with FPC cable replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 hotend ceramic heater and thermistor
entries.summary: The U1 ceramic heater (also called heater core or heater module) and thermistor sit in the hotend heating block. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 15 minutes) with an H2.0 hex key. Cool the nozzle below 40 C, remove the hotend from the toolhead, swap both parts using thermal grease, and reconnect heater to the left port and thermistor to the right.
steps: Unload the toolhead via Unload mode and wait until the nozzle is below 40 C; power off and unplug
Release the toolhead from the swapper by pressing an H2.0 key into the middle hole between its two locating pins until it clicks
Remove the toolhead rear cover, release the hotend cable clips, remove the 2 hotend screws and take the hotend out
Remove the silicone sock, heater clamp spring and wire press strip, then the old heater and thermistor
Bend the new thermistor tip 90 degrees, dip the probe in thermal grease and spread grease on the heater seat
Fit heater and thermistor, then the clamp spring, press strip and sock (sock notch aligned with the press strip)
Reinstall the hotend (2 screws); heater cable to the left port, thermistor cable to the right; press both into the clip and fold the thermistor lead into the extruder unit slot
Refit the rear cover; set the latch with an H2.0 key until two red marks show (toolhead 1 left limit, 2/3/4 right limit), push the toolhead onto the swapper pin and seat both side pins
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 15 minutes
Heater cable: left port; thermistor cable: right port

sources.title: U1 ceramic heater and thermistor replacement guide

entries.title: U1 motion system maintenance schedule: shafts, carbon rods, lead screws, belts, pogo pins
entries.summary: Snapmaker's U1 upkeep plan: clean and lubricate linear shafts/bearings monthly, clean the X carbon rod assembly monthly (never oil or grease it, which accelerates wear), check belt tension and clean belts monthly, grease lead screws/nuts and steel pins/balls quarterly, and clean pogo pins every 4-6 months. Always power off and let the bed and hotend cool first. Use white lithium grease NLGI 2-3 sparingly and never WD-40.
steps: Power off and wait until the heated bed and hotend are fully cool

Linear shafts: wipe with a lint-free cloth lightly wetted with high-purity isopropanol or ethanol (keep alcohol out of bearings), then add a little light lithium grease or 1-2 drops of synthetic spindle oil and move the axis through its full travel; wipe off excess to leave a thin film
X carbon rods: wipe only with a cloth and 70% isopropanol or ethanol; no lubricant on rods or bushings
Lead screws: brush or blow debris out of the threads, apply a thin layer of the included white lithium grease, run Z through full travel several times and wipe away surplus so it cannot drip
Steel pins/balls: clean with alcohol, then grease the marked contact points
Timing belts: watch for the screen prompt that tension needs adjusting, re-tension per the XY belt guide, and dry-wipe dust off the teeth
Pogo pins: see the separate pogo pin cleaning entry; never scrape them with hard tools
facts: Linear shaft/bearing: monthly; white lithium grease NLGI 2-3 or fully synthetic high-speed spindle oil
X carbon rod assembly: monthly cleaning only, no oil or grease
Lead screw/nut: quarterly; white lithium grease NLGI 2-3, non copper-corrosive
Steel pin/ball: quarterly; white lithium grease NLGI 2-3
Timing belt: monthly tension check and cleaning
Pogo pins: every 4-6 months, lint-free cloth and alcohol
Keep oil and grease off the timing belts
WD-40 is a penetrant/rust remover: it strips grease, attracts dust and can make parts seize
Too much lubricant collects dust into an abrasive paste that speeds wear

entries.title: U1 0003-0528-0000-0027 Corexy home unstable / 0003-0530-0000-0027 Homing Calibration Failed
entries.summary: Corexy home is unstable (0003-0528-0000-0027) and Homing Calibration Failed (0003-0530-0000-0027) are fixed by updating to the latest U1 firmware and running Homing Calibration. If the error blocks the first-run wizard, skip setup by holding the top-left of the screen for 6+ seconds, then redo the skipped Device Calibration once homing works.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows Corexy home is unstable (0003-0528-0000-0027)
Touchscreen shows Homing Calibration Failed (0003-0530-0000-0027)
steps: Hold the top-left corner of the touchscreen for at least 6 seconds to skip the initial setup
Connect to Wi-Fi and update to the latest firmware (Settings > About)
Run Homing Calibration (Settings > Maintenance); if a toolhead is still attached and blocks calibration, release it manually first
Avoid overtightening the screws in the area shown on the wiki; stop once resistance rises noticeably
Once resolved, run the Device Calibration you skipped (Settings > Device Calibration)
If it persists, open a ticket through the Snapmaker App with photos or video

entries.title: Replacing a U1 docking Hall sensor board (toolhead dock detection)
entries.summary: Each U1 toolhead docking bracket has a Hall sensor board that is reachable once the toolhead is moved off it. Replacement is very easy (1/5, about 5 minutes) with an H1.5 hex key.
steps: On the touchscreen select the matching toolhead and tap Detach Toolhead
Power off, unplug, and slide the toolhead away from the sensor board by hand
Remove the 2 fixing screws (H1.5), hold the connector clip and pull the cable out
Plug the cable into the new board and fasten it with the 2 screws
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes

sources.title: U1 docking Hall sensor board replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 driven (idler) extruder gear assembly
entries.summary: The driven extruder gear assembly sits in the U1 extruder unit opposite the active gear. Swapping it is easy (2/5, about 20 minutes) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys and follows the active-gear procedure, except only the bearing block and spring need to come off.
steps: Remove the toolhead from the dock and take off its top cover (3 screws) and back cover
Disconnect the extruder unit cables, remove the PCB screws, free the cables and remove the 4 extruder unit screws
Remove the bearing block (4 H2.0 screws), the spring screw, compression spring and spring block
Lift out the old driven gear assembly and fit the new one
Refit spring with the spring block on top, tighten the spring screw, then the bearing block
Reinstall the extruder unit and PCB, route the 3 cables as before, refit covers and reinstall the toolhead
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes

sources.title: U1 driven extruder gear assembly replacement guide

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0522-0000-0000 / 0003-0522-0000-0002 (System Anomaly prompt)
entries.summary: A System Anomaly prompt on the U1 touchscreen with code 0003-0522-0000-0000 or 0003-0522-0000-0002 is attributed by Snapmaker to a backlog of server messages, which they are fixing on the server side. The -0000 variant does not affect the print: tap Confirm and carry on. For -0002, update the firmware from a USB flash drive and send logs to support if it keeps coming back.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows a System Anomaly message asking you to check details and contact support
causes: Accumulated messages from the Snapmaker cloud server (server-side issue being optimized by Snapmaker)
steps: 0003-0522-0000-0000: tap Confirm; the print can continue normally
0003-0522-0000-0002: update the U1 firmware with the USB flash drive update procedure
If -0002 still appears after updating, export the machine logs (Settings > About > System Log) and open a support ticket

entries.title: Exporting U1 log files for Snapmaker support (USB or Fluidd)
entries.summary: U1 errors are recorded in logs that support uses to diagnose problems. Export them from Settings > About > System Log, either to a USB drive (FAT32/EXT2/EXT4, 64 GB max) as collection.tar, or, on firmware V1.1.1 or later, to local storage and download from Fluidd's logs folder. The file is encrypted and only readable by Snapmaker.
steps: USB method: plug a FAT32, EXT2 or EXT4 drive of 64 GB or less into the rear USB port
Go to Settings > About > System Log > Export logs to USB, then copy collection.tar from the drive
Local method (firmware V1.1.1+): Settings > About > System Log > Export logs to Local Storage; tick Include AI Detected Photos for AI detection issues
Find the printer IP under Settings > Wi-Fi and open it in a browser to reach Fluidd
In Fluidd's Jobs section open the logs folder, right-click the archive and choose Download
Send the file to support; for large files share a Google Drive link with access set to Anyone with the link
facts: Stuck on the first-run setup? On the language selection screen press and hold the upper-left corner for 6-7 seconds to skip setup
Log archives are encrypted and cannot be read locally

sources.title: U1 how to export log files

entries.title: U1 top cover External Circulation Kit air duct misaligned with the air inlet cover
entries.summary: Shipping knocks can shift the External Circulation Kit air duct out of line with the Heat Dissipation Air Inlet Cover in the U1 top cover. If nothing is cracked or deformed, it is only a position shift and can be realigned in about 10 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. Send the top cover SN and Verification Code to support as well.
symptoms: External Circulation Kit air duct does not line up with the Heat Dissipation Air Inlet Cover
causes: Handling, vibration, compression or impact during transport shifting parts slightly
steps: Unplug the top cover cable, remove the magnetic front door, lift off the top cover, flip it and unlatch the clips to remove the lower housing
Remove the 3 ST3 x 8 screws holding the External Circulation Kit, flip the upper housing and remove the 1 ST3 x 8 duct screw
Separate the duct from the inlet cover and inspect the cover's clips; contact support if any are damaged
Realign the duct with the inlet cover (fan facing the same way as the cover's outlet) and seat the cable in its slot
Tighten the duct screw, check it is back in its original position, place the kit (cable clear of the outlet) and fit the 3 screws
Reinstall the top cover per the U1 Top Cover Installation Guide
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 10 minutes

sources.title: U1 Top Cover External Circulation Kit Misalignment Adjustment

entries.title: Replacing the U1 extruder housing assembly
entries.summary: The extruder housing is the frame of the U1 extruder unit; replacing it (easy, 2/5, about 20 minutes, H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys) means stripping every part off the old housing and moving it to the new one: bearing block, spring, runout sensor, both gear assemblies, motor and motor heat shield.
steps: Remove the toolhead, its top and back covers, the PCB and the extruder unit
Take off the bearing block (4 screws), spring screw, compression spring and spring block
Remove 2 H1.5 screws and lift out the runout sensor, driven gear assembly and active gear assembly
Remove 2 H2.0 screws to free the extruder motor and its heat shield
On the new housing fit heat shield and motor in the original orientation, then active and driven gears; spin the active gear to confirm all three gears mesh smoothly
Refit runout sensor, spring (spring block on top), bearing block, then reinstall the unit, PCB with correct 3-cable routing, covers and toolhead
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes

sources.title: U1 extruder housing assembly replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 extruder motor (pancake stepper)
entries.summary: Replace the U1 extruder motor (also called the extruder stepper or pancake stepper) when it is damaged. It lives in the extruder unit; the job takes about 20 minutes with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys (rated 3 stars but labelled easy). Afterward confirm loading and unloading work and that the active extruder gear turns, as seen from the right side of the toolhead.
steps: Unload, power off, remove the toolhead and its top and back covers
Unplug the six PCB cables and remove the PCB (M2x6 and ST2.6x6 screws)
Remove the extruder unit (2 M2 screws with H1.5, 2 M3x8 with H2.0) after moving the surface cables aside
Remove the bearing block (4 screws) and the pressure spring screw and spring
Remove 2 H2.0 screws and take out the motor and heat shield
Fit heat shield and new motor with the motor cable positioned as originally, flip and tighten the 2 screws
Refit spring, bearing block, extruder unit and PCB, reconnect and route cables, refit covers and dock the toolhead
Test loading/unloading and watch the active gear rotate
facts: The removal step lists 2 M2x8 screws but the install step lists 2 M2x10 screws for the extruder unit; reuse the original screws

entries.title: Replacing the complete U1 extruder unit
entries.summary: The whole U1 extruder unit (extruder assembly) can be swapped when it is damaged, in about 20 minutes with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys. Remove the toolhead, its covers and the PCB, take out the four extruder unit screws, fit the new unit and reconnect the six PCB cables in their original positions.
steps: Unload the toolhead, power off and remove the toolhead from the dock
Remove the top cover (3 screws) and back cover, unplug the PCB cables and remove the PCB (M2x6 with H1.5, ST2.6x6 with H2.0)
Remove the 4 extruder unit screws (H1.5 and H2.0) and lift the unit out
Install the new unit with the 4 screws
Refit the PCB and reconnect motor, filament detection, calibration sensor, fan, heater and thermistor cables; tidy the routing
Refit covers and dock the toolhead, then reload filament
facts: Difficulty rated 3 stars but labelled easy; about 20 minutes

entries.title: U1 shuts down with Mainboard or Toolhead MCU detected power-off signal
entries.summary: The U1 may halt saying the mainboard MCU, or toolhead 1-4 MCU, detected a power-off signal and shut down for protection. Mainboard cases point to unstable mains: weak grid, a shared strip with heavy loads, loose plugs, or an over-sensitive detection threshold in 100-130 V regions. Toolhead cases point to a loose toolhead USB cable or a loose 16-pin cable between mainboard and HUB board.
symptoms: Error saying the mainboard MCU saw a power-off signal, followed by a protective shutdown
Error naming one toolhead (1-4) whose MCU saw a power-off signal, followed by a protective shutdown
causes: Unstable mains supply
Printer shares a power strip with high-load devices
AC cable or power strip not fully plugged in
Power loss detection threshold too sensitive (more likely on 100-130 V supplies)
Loose toolhead USB cable (toolhead MCU message)
Loose 16-pin cable between mainboard and HUB board (toolhead MCU message)
steps: Mainboard message: check the wall socket and push both ends of the AC cable fully home; move the printer off strips shared with heavy loads
If you are on 100-130 V mains or other printers show similar issues, consider a UPS sized for 1150 W peak
If it continues, enable Advanced Mode and raise the power loss detection threshold from the default 0.022 s to 0.04-0.05 s (never above 0.05 s)
Toolhead message: make sure the toolhead USB cable is locked; swap USB cables between toolheads to see whether the fault follows the cable
Remove the right side panel and reseat the 16-pin mainboard-to-HUB cable; the mainboard end is glued, so pick the white glue away with tweezers before unplugging
facts: U1 power draw: 1150 W peak, 200-400 W average
Power loss detection threshold default 0.022 s, maximum recommended 0.05 s

entries.title: Replacing a U1 filament feeder (autofeeder)
entries.summary: The U1 has two filament feeders (also called autofeeders or feeder units) at the rear of each side, pushing filament from the spools to the toolheads. The left one serves toolheads 1-2 and the right one 3-4. Swapping one takes about 5 minutes and needs no tools.
steps: Unload Mode: select toolheads 1 and 2 (left feeder) or 3 and 4 (right feeder), tap Unload, then turn the spools back to withdraw the filament
Press the feeder clip and slide the feeder out
Disconnect the feeder cable and press the quick connectors to pull the filament tubes
Connect and route the new feeder's cable, line up the clips and push the feeder home
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes, no tools needed

entries.title: U1 Filament Loading Anomaly 0002-0525-000x-0032 (broken runout sensor cable)
entries.summary: The Filament Loading Anomaly message (codes 0002-0525-0000-0032 through 0002-0525-0003-0032) can appear during automatic or manual loading. The page blames a broken Filament Runout Sensor cable inside the toolhead, typically from overtightening the toolhead USB cable. Open the toolhead top cover to inspect the cable; if broken, send a photo and the SN to Snapmaker support.
symptoms: Filament Loading Anomaly during automatic loading after the filament has reached the feeder
Filament Loading Anomaly during manual loading or later in the print even though filament is in the toolhead
causes: Filament Runout Sensor cable broken by excessive force when fastening the toolhead USB cable
steps: Automatic loading: the toolhead parks at the front waiting for filament to trigger the runout sensor; an error at this point points to the sensor cable
Manual loading: confirm the filament is fully inserted into the toolhead; if the error persists, suspect the cable
Remove the three screws on the toolhead top cover with a 2.0 mm hex key and inspect the runout switch cable for damage
If it is broken, photograph it, note the SN from Settings > About, and contact Snapmaker support
When refitting the USB cable, do not overtighten it

entries.title: Filament moisture sensitivity and drying temperatures (PLA, PETG, TPU, ABS/ASA, PA, PC, PVA)
entries.summary: How quickly filaments soak up moisture, and how to dry them, per Snapmaker's U1 guidance. PVA/BVOH and nylon saturate within hours, TPU in about a day, PETG in days and PLA in 1-2 weeks. Wet PETG pops and pits, TPU turns foamy, and nylon or PVA can fail outright. Drying temperatures range from 45-50 C for PLA up to 120 C for PC.
symptoms: PLA: brittle, more stringing, sandy or fuzzy surface
PETG: heavy stringing, cloudiness in clear filament, popping, pits, bubbly infill
TPU: whitening, steam, foam-like pinholed surface
ABS/ASA: oozing, layer cracks, matte surface, pores, burnt smell
Nylon: violent steam, large holes, spongy weak parts; PVA/BVOH: softens and may dissolve in the tube
facts: Time to saturation: PLA/PLA+ 1-2 weeks; PETG 3-5 days; TPU/TPE 12-24 h; ABS/ASA about 1 week; nylon under 6 h; PVA/BVOH under 1 h
PLA/PLA+: dry 45-50 C for 4-6 h; never above 55 C or it softens and jams
PETG: 60-65 C for 4-6 h; below 60 C is ineffective
TPU 95A: 50-55 C for 6-8 h; too hot makes the filament stick together
ABS/ASA: 80-85 C for 4-6 h
Nylon (PA): 70-80 C for 12+ h, keep in a dry box while printing
PC: 120 C for 6-8 h, beyond most household dryers
Store opened spools sealed with desiccant

sources.title: U1 how to avoid pitting and pockmarks in prints

entries.title: U1 filament loaded but not extruding: locating an extruder or hotend clog
entries.summary: If a U1 toolhead has filament loaded but parts come out partly or wholly missing, the filament is jammed either in the extruder or in the hotend. Move the hotend aside and drive the extruder from Fluidd: if filament comes through the extruder freely, the hotend is clogged (clear it with the needle and a cold pull); if not, open the extruder and inspect the sensor inlet, gears, motor and bearing-base outlet.
symptoms: Filament is loaded but nothing comes out of one toolhead
Part of the model missing in that toolhead's color, or no model at all
causes: Hotend clog
Extruder clog: debris at the runout sensor inlet, on the gears or motor, or in the bearing-base outlet
steps: Unload the affected toolhead and wait until it is below 40 C; release it from the swapper with a hex key in the side hole, then unscrew the hotend (H2.0) and move it aside without unplugging
Open Fluidd at the printer IP (the screen's extrude function needs the toolhead picked up); Extruder, Extruder1, Extruder2, Extruder3 = toolheads 1-4
Select the extruder, heat it to 180 C, set 200 mm, click Extrude and hand-feed filament into the extruder
Filament passes: hotend clog. Heat to the last filament's print temperature (e.g. 230 C for PLA) and, wearing heat-resistant gloves, push the cleaning needle up and down through the nozzle
Reinstall the hotend and do a cold pull; also do one before switching filament in that toolhead

Filament does not pass: extruder clog. Disassemble and check the runout-sensor inlet passes filament easily, drive gear free of debris with the silver gear not slipping on the orange gear, driven gear spins freely, motor pulley spins freely, bearing-base outlet channel clear
Contact support if it persists or parts are needed
facts: The included cleaning needle is about 0.3 mm, so it is not usable on a 0.2 mm hotend

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead filament runout sensor
entries.summary: The U1 filament runout sensor is the inlet of the extruder unit inside each toolhead. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 25 minutes) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys. You remove the toolhead, PCB and extruder unit, take off the bearing mount (keep track of the bearing), and swap the sensor held by two H1.5 screws.
steps: Unload the toolhead and wait until the nozzle is below 40 C

Pull the filament tube, remove the 3 top cover screws, click the toolhead free by pressing an H2.0 key into the middle hole between the locating pins, then unplug the toolhead cable and remove the top cover
Remove the rear cover, unplug 4 cables on top of the PCB and 2 latched cables at the bottom, remove the PCB screws and the PCB
Free the cables and remove the extruder unit (H1.5 screws upper-left and lower-right, H2.0 upper-right and lower-left)
Remove the 4 bearing mount screws without losing the bearing, then the 2 H1.5 sensor screws, and fit the new sensor
Reassemble; reconnect runout sensor, motor, hotend fan, calibration sensor, heater and thermistor cables with proper routing, pushing spare thermistor cable into the extruder unit hole
Set the latch until both red marks show, dock the toolhead, connect its cable, refit the top cover (one of the 3 screws differs and goes in the marked hole) and the tube
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 25 minutes

sources.title: U1 filament runout sensor replacement guide

entries.title: U1 filament sticking to the outside of the nozzle: causes and slicer fixes
entries.summary: When molten filament clings to the U1 nozzle exterior you get stringing, rough surfaces or under-extrusion, and in bad cases clogs or failed prints. Work through, in order: damp filament (dry it, e.g. in a SnapDryer), a worn nozzle (replace the hotend), flow ratio too high, print temperature too high, print speed too slow, and retraction or Z-hop settings.
symptoms: Molten filament collects on the nozzle's outer wall
Stringing, rough surfaces or under-extrusion
Nozzle clogs or extrusion stops in severe cases
causes: Filament has absorbed moisture
Worn nozzle
Extrusion flow ratio too high
Nozzle temperature too high
Print speed too slow, especially walls
Unsuitable retraction length, speed or Z-hop
steps: Dry the filament (SnapDryer at its recommended settings) and store opened spools sealed with desiccant
Replace a worn nozzle via the U1 hotend replacement procedure
Run Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended) in Snapmaker Orca and apply the best correction to the filament flow ratio
Print a temperature tower (Calibration > Temperature) and set first-layer and other-layer nozzle temperatures to the best level
Turn on Process > Advanced and raise wall speeds under Speed > Other layers speed, keeping outer wall slower than inner wall
In the filament's Setting Overrides adjust retraction length, retraction speed, Z-hop height and Z-hop type
Power off and unplug before any hardware check

settings.advice: Lower it to the calibrated value if extrusion is excessive; excess flow pushes material onto the nozzle.
Lower toward the best temperature-tower result if filament is too runny and sticks to the nozzle.
Raise moderately if printing very slowly; keep it below inner wall speed for surface quality.
Raise moderately; slow printing lets heat-softened filament accumulate on the nozzle.
Tune via filament overrides to cut oozing and stringing onto the nozzle.
Tune together with retraction length.
Adjust Z-hop height so travels do not drag the nozzle through printed material.
Try a different Z-hop type if the nozzle keeps picking up material on travels.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead filament tube (6 x 4.6 x 650 mm)
entries.summary: The tube from the U1 top panel to each toolhead is 6 mm OD, 4.6 mm ID and 650 mm long, held by quick-release fittings at both ends. Swapping it takes about 5 minutes and needs no tools.
steps: Unload the toolhead via Unload Mode and turn the spool back to retract the filament
Press the quick connectors at both ends and pull the tube out, then lift it from the tube holder
Push the new tube fully into both connectors and press it into the holder
Clip the tube and the toolhead USB cable together
facts: Tube: 6 mm OD, 4.6 mm ID, 650 mm long
Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes

entries.title: Finding the Snapmaker U1 serial number (SN)
entries.summary: The full U1 serial number is 16 digits plus a 4-character verification code. The original SN is on a sticker on the side of the shipping box and on the lower rear panel of the printer; the current SN is under Settings > About on the touchscreen. If you can see all three, check that they match.
steps: Look for the SN sticker on the side of the outer box
Check the sticker low on the printer's rear panel
On the touchscreen open Settings > About
Compare the values; quote all 16 digits plus the 4-character code to support

sources.title: How to Find the Printer Serial Number

entries.title: U1 firmware update failed or stuck (unpacking at 1%, toolhead update at 18-75%)
entries.summary: A failed U1 firmware update is diagnosed by the progress stage. At 1% the file failed to unpack: re-download the official firmware and copy it to a FAT32 USB drive (OTA failures go to support). Between 18% and 75% a toolhead failed to update; swapping USB cable ends and ports shows whether the fault is the machine-side port (16-pin cable/HUB board), the USB cable or the toolhead PCB. On firmware 1.3+, a silent hang warrants a restart and retry.
symptoms: Touchscreen reports firmware update failure
Older firmware hangs at one stage without an error message
causes: Corrupt or improperly prepared update file (1% stage)
Toolhead USB cable fault
Machine-side port fault: loose or bad 16-pin cable or HUB board
Toolhead PCB fault
steps: Note the stage: 1% = unpacking failed, 18-75% = toolhead update failed, anything else = contact support
1% on a local update: work in a non-encrypted environment, download the latest firmware from the release page, format the USB drive FAT32, copy the file to the root, eject safely and retry
Stage tells which toolhead failed: 18% toolhead 1, 37% toolhead 2, 56% toolhead 3, 75% toolhead 4 (earlier ones succeeded)
Reverse the failed toolhead's USB cable end-for-end and retry
If the stage is unchanged, swap the machine-side USB ports of the failed and a good toolhead and retry
If the failure stays with the same port, reseat both ends of the 16-pin cable behind the right panel and retry; if still failing, replace the 16-pin cable and HUB board
If the failure moves with the toolhead, fully swap the two cables: failure follows the cable = replace the USB cable; failure stays with the toolhead = replace the toolhead PCB
facts: Firmware update runs in 8 stages
During retries the side and top panels can stay off; only the USB cables need reconnecting

entries.title: U1 first layer not sticking to the build plate / print detaching
entries.summary: If the U1 first layer lifts or the part breaks free and prints in mid-air, check the model's contact area (tall narrow parts, uneven AI-generated bottoms), slicer adhesion settings, the load-cell based bed leveling on the affected toolhead and on toolhead 1 (all heads use its calibration data), and wear on the PEI sheet.
symptoms: Plastic blob forms at the nozzle
Model breaks off and the printer extrudes in mid-air
causes: Small or uneven footprint (tall thin parts, rough bottoms from AI-made models)
No brim or poor orientation for small/complex parts
Bed leveling disturbed by a loose hotend, debris or too little clearance between heatsink fins and the copper sensing plate
Worn PEI coating (pulled areas, bumps, craters)
steps: Add a brim, or paint Hybrid Tree supports to steady tall narrow models
Use Lay on Face or reorient the part to maximize contact; sink an uneven bottom slightly below the plate or trim it with the Cut tool
Try a higher first-layer bed temperature
Use the 1+1 check: inspect the problem toolhead and also toolhead 1 for tight hotend screws, no debris between heatsink fins and copper plate, and enough gap for the plate to flex
Run Settings > Maintenance > Manual Leveling, then Settings > Device Calibration > Heated Bed Leveling, then test
Inspect the PEI sheet and flip to the fresh side if worn

settings.advice: Enable a brim for small-footprint or tall parts to add contact area.
Increase for tall, narrow or sharp-cornered parts that tend to lift.
Raise slightly for the first layer on the textured PEI plate if adhesion is poor.
Raise slightly on the smooth PEI plate if adhesion is poor.
Use supports (e.g. painted hybrid tree) to anchor tall thin models.
A hybrid tree style is what the wiki suggests for stabilizing tall parts.

facts: All U1 toolheads rely on calibration data from toolhead 1 (leftmost)

sources.title: U1 first layer printing troubleshooting guide

entries.title: U1 first layer bad on only some toolheads or only with PETG
entries.summary: If one U1 toolhead lays a poor first layer after calibration, inspect that head and toolhead 1 for bed-leveling sensor problems. If several heads fail while at least one is fine, run Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration, then calibrate and test each head separately. If PLA works but PETG or other filaments fail, check the filament profile and heat soak the bed 5 minutes, as hotter beds take longer to settle.
steps: One toolhead bad: check its hotend screws, heatsink-to-copper-plate debris and clearance, and do the same on toolhead 1
Several toolheads bad but at least one good: run Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration from Settings > Device Calibration and complete the on-screen steps
If that does not fix it, calibrate and test each toolhead individually
Only PETG/other materials failing: confirm the correct filament profile is assigned to the part
Heat soak the bed for 5 minutes before starting

sources.title: U1 first layer printing troubleshooting guide

entries.title: U1 first layer problems: pre-flight checks (plate cleaning, leveling, wet filament)
entries.summary: Snapmaker says over 90% of bad U1 first layers come from three things, in order: a dirty build plate, stale bed leveling or Z data, and compromised (usually wet) filament. Wash the plate with dish soap, clear debris under it, check the silicone wiper and nozzle, rerun Heated Bed Leveling, use dry filament, then test with a simple 0.2 mm-tall box before blaming the model.
symptoms: First layer fails to stick, wrinkles or shows gaps
Bubbles, popping or extra stringing at the nozzle (wet filament)
causes: Fingerprints or residue on the build plate
Plate moved, flipped or parts pulled off while hot, so the saved mesh no longer matches
Debris between plate and heated bed
Damaged or detached silicone wiper on the nozzle cleaning bracket
Plastic buildup on the nozzle
Wet or brittle filament
steps: Hand-wash the plate with dish soap like a dish, keep water contact brief to avoid rust, and dry with a lint-free cloth (Snapmaker prefers soap to isopropyl alcohol, which is flammable and not safe on every surface)
Remove debris from under the plate and replace a damaged or loose silicone wiper
Heat the nozzle (200 C for PLA, 230 C for ABS) and brush off buildup with the included brush
Run Settings > Device Calibration > Heated Bed Leveling (start button top right) for a fresh mesh
Use fresh dry filament; if it snaps when bent it is probably wet, so dry it per the maker's guidance
Load filament, heat the extruder and extrude to confirm smooth, even flow
In the slicer add a primitive box 0.2 mm tall with the right profiles and print it to test the first layer in isolation

sources.title: U1 first layer printing troubleshooting guide

entries.title: U1 first layer wrinkles or gaps between lines: bed mesh range and z_offset tuning
entries.summary: Wrinkles or waves mean the nozzle is too close; sparse, translucent lines with gaps mean it is too far; over 10% of the area affected is a fail. Print a full-plate 0.2 mm square. Widespread wrinkles usually mean firmware Z_offset is too high: lower it in printer.cfg (-0.05 to -0.07 to -0.09). For gaps, raise it (-0.05 to -0.03 to -0.01). Local issues point to plate flatness: check the mesh Range in Fluidd.
symptoms: Waves, wrinkles or buildup in the first layer (nozzle too close)
Gaps, translucent or broken first-layer lines (nozzle too far)
causes: Firmware Z_offset too high (wrinkles over a large area) or too low (gaps)
Debris between plate and heated bed
Bed not flat: mesh Range above 0.5 mm, glue or bumps around the bed magnets
Bed deformation restricted by the plastic bed shell (helped by heat soaking)
steps: Scale a 0.2 mm primitive to cover the whole plate and print it to see if the problem is local or global
Check flatness: open Fluidd at the printer IP, Tune, read Range (top right); under 0.5 mm is normal
If wrinkles follow red mesh peaks, look for excess glue or bumps around the magnets under the plate
If Range exceeds 0.8 mm and raised corners match the wrinkles, do Settings > Maintenance > Manual Leveling, then Heated Bed Leveling; if still bad, flip the cleaned PEI sheet
To change Z_offset (smooth/textured PEI only; other plates use G-code): enable Advanced Mode, open printer.cfg in Fluidd, change Z_offset by no more than 0.05 per step, save and power cycle
If the first layer gets worse, go the other way
Heat soak the bed at 65 C for at least 5 minutes before printing; if wrinkles shrink, the bed shell was restricting bed deformation
facts: Lower (more negative) firmware Z_offset moves the nozzle away from the plate; higher moves it closer
Mesh Range under 0.5 mm is normal; above 0.8 mm calls for manual leveling
The blob guide recommends 0.01 steps, this guide allows up to 0.05 per step; smaller steps are safer

sources.title: U1 first layer printing troubleshooting guide

entries.title: U1 gaps on sloped top surfaces: flow, line width, walls, top pattern, variable layer height
entries.summary: Gaps on sloped U1 top surfaces come from weak top-layer extrusion, thin walls, a poor top pattern, stair-stepping at large layer heights, and sagging on steep slopes. Calibrate flow (YOLO), widen outer wall and top surface lines slightly, add walls and top layers, use denser or more supportive infill, choose Monotonic or Concentric tops, use adaptive variable layer height, and add cooling with overhang slowdowns.
symptoms: Holes or open lines on inclined top surfaces
causes: Under-extrusion or unstable extrusion
Too few walls or top layers
Sparse or weak infill under the slope
Top surface pattern poor at filling small or irregular areas
Large uniform layer height causing stair-stepping
Steep overhang angle letting material sag
steps: Run Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended): 11 blocks spanning -0.05 to +0.05 in 0.01 steps; add the smoothest block's value to the current flow ratio
Set outer wall width to 105-120% of the nozzle (0.42-0.48 mm on 0.4) and top surface width to 100-105% (0.40-0.42 mm)
Increase wall loops (Process > Strength > Walls) and top shell layers
Raise infill density (decorative 10-20%, functional 30-50%, high strength 60%+); patterns such as Line, Adaptive Cubic, Honeycomb or Hilbert Curve support slopes better than Rectilinear
Set the top surface pattern to Concentric, Monotonic or Monotonic line
Open Variable layer height in the top toolbar, set the quality/speed slider, click Adaptive, then Smooth as needed
For steep slopes: lower nozzle temperature a little, raise part cooling and/or auxiliary fan, enable slowdown for overhangs and curled perimeters

settings.advice: Raise to the YOLO-calibrated value if top lines are thin or open.
Increase slightly within 0.42-0.48 mm for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
Keep within 0.40-0.42 mm for a 0.4 mm nozzle; slightly wider helps closure without over-extrusion.
Increase (e.g. 1 to 2 or more) for a sturdier edge under sloped tops.
Increase to close gaps on top surfaces.
Increase if large internal voids leave tops unsupported.
Try Line, Adaptive Cubic, Honeycomb or Hilbert Curve instead of Rectilinear for better support under slopes.
Use Concentric, Monotonic or Monotonic line to fill small and irregular areas.
Increase part cooling for steep slopes to reduce sagging.
Increase auxiliary fan speed on steep slopes and overhangs.
Enable to slow down on overhangs.
Enable to slow down where perimeters curl.

facts: The wiki's worked example (0.98 current, smoothest block -0.1, result 0.97) is arithmetically inconsistent; the block offsets are in 0.01 steps, so it should read -0.01

sources.title: U1 how to avoid gaps on sloped top surfaces

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0529-0000-0001 G-code parsing failed (Snapmaker Orca German/French decimal commas)
entries.summary: Error 0003-0529-0000-0001 on the U1 comes from multi-color G-code sliced in Snapmaker Orca before V2.1.2 with the UI language set to Deutsch or Francais, which wrote commas instead of decimal points. Fully quit and reopen Orca after changing language (the in-app restart is only a soft restart), update to the latest Orca, and if needed temporarily turn off Enable change pressure advance when wiping.
symptoms: Touchscreen shows 0003-0529-0000-0001 G-code parsing failed on a multi-color file
causes: Snapmaker Orca older than V2.1.2 running in German or French wrote decimal commas into the G-code
steps: Close Snapmaker Orca completely and reopen it after switching language; the language-change restart does not fully reload
Download and install the latest official Snapmaker Orca
If it still fails, temporarily disable Enable change pressure advance when wiping and re-slice

settings.advice: Temporarily disable if G-code parsing error 0003-0529-0000-0001 persists after a full Orca restart.

sources.title: U1 Known issues and quick fixes

entries.title: Replacing the U1 front glass door
entries.summary: The U1 glass door is held to the front panel by 4 screws. Swapping it takes about 5 minutes with an H2.0 hex key: remove the 4 screws, fit the new door with its rubber gaskets in place, and tighten the screws again.
steps: Remove the 4 door screws with an H2.0 hex key and lift off the old door
Position the new door and stick the rubber gaskets at the marked spots
Refit and tighten the 4 screws
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes

entries.title: U1 heated bed cover loose or corners sagging: normal floating design
entries.summary: The white plastic shell around the U1 heated bed (marked BUILD VOLUME 270 x 270 x 270 mm) deliberately floats: its screws sit on soft silicone pads and the corners are unscrewed, so they can be pressed down slightly. This lets the aluminum plate expand freely and settle flat sooner. Plastic expands more than aluminum when hot, so the shell may loosen, sag or make some noise; this is expected.
symptoms: Four corners of the bed cover droop or press down
Cover feels loose after heating, sometimes with unusual noise
causes: Intentional suspended mounting of the cover
Plastic cover expanding more than the aluminum bed plate when heated
facts: U1 build volume: 270 x 270 x 270 mm
Cover screws are cushioned by silicone pads; the four corners have no screws

entries.title: Replacing the U1 heated bed (and avoiding bed cable wear)
entries.summary: Replacing the U1 heated bed is medium difficulty (3/5) and takes about 80 minutes with an H2.0 hex key and a spare spool as a prop. The bed cable lands on four terminals in the power supply box (N, L, NTC, PE). Route the new cable without excess slack near the lead screw, check it does not twist through the Z travel, and always do manual bed leveling afterward to avoid nozzle scraping.
steps: Power off, unplug, let parts cool and remove the right side panel
Pull the bottom timing belt left to raise the bed; remove the 4 nuts under the bed, pressing each corner down with a spool underneath so it cannot drop (fitting the PEI sheet first helps)

Remove the bed cable clamp (2 screws) and the power supply housing (4 screws, unplug its fan), press the terminal tabs to release N, L, NTC and PE, loosen the 4 PSU screws and pull the cable out behind the PSU
Fit the PEI sheet to the new bed, seat the bottom springs in the raised holes and route the cable through the sheet metal
Press each corner down over a spool and tighten the nuts until the screw end is flush with the nut bottom
Clamp the cable, route it behind the PSU and over the screw post to the bottom-right, avoiding slack between lead screw and inner panel
Reconnect N, L, NTC, PE; with panels off, reconnect USB, power on and test heating
Power off, tighten the PSU screws, run the bed up and down to check the cable is not twisted, tidy wiring, refit fan, enclosure and panel
Do manual bed leveling
facts: Difficulty 3/5, about 80 minutes
Bed cable terminals: N, L, NTC, PE
Too much slack between the lead screw and inner side panel lets the cable wear as the bed moves

entries.title: U1 homing anomaly 0002-0528-0000-0000 (XY/Z homing or sensor calibration failed)
entries.summary: Code 0002-0528-0000-0000 means the U1 could not home XY or Z, or failed sensor calibration. Causes are binding or poorly tensioned XY or Z belts, debris on belts or lead screws, an uneven or soft surface under the printer, or a disturbed detection system: dirty nozzle or plate, a loose hotend, or the heatsink fan cable or debris between the heatsink fins and the copper induction piece.
symptoms: XY axis fails to return to origin
Z axis fails to return to origin
Sensor calibration fails
causes: XY belt tension wrong or debris on the XY belt causing drag
Z axis drag: debris on lead screws or smooth rods, loose Z belt, sticking Z pulley
Printer on a soft pad, cardboard or uneven surface interfering with Z
Filament residue on the nozzle or PEI sheet
Hotend fixing screws loose or hotend not seated
Heatsink fan cable or a foreign object between the heatsink fins and copper induction piece
Faulty calibration sensor
steps: Re-tension the XY belts; if already done once during assembly, repeat the adjustment three more times
Power off and push the toolhead by hand along X and Y, feeling for sticking
Clean the Z lead screws and smooth rods; with power off lift the front slightly and pull the Z belt to check the bed moves freely; re-tension a loose Z belt
Set the printer on a flat, firm surface (no soft pads or cardboard)
Clean residue from the nozzle tip and outer wall and from the PEI sheet
Open the rear cover: clear anything between heatsink fins and copper induction piece, reroute the heatsink fan cable, and retighten the two hotend screws
Retry homing; if it still fails, film the error, export logs and contact support

entries.title: Replacing the U1 hotend cooling fan (heatsink fan)
entries.summary: The U1 hotend cooling fan (also called hotend fan, heatsink fan or nozzle cooler) sits inside the toolhead behind the hotend. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 15 minutes) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys. Afterward heat the hotend from the touchscreen: the fan should start once the temperature passes 60 C.
steps: Unload the toolhead, power off and remove the toolhead from the dock
Remove the top cover (3 screws) and back cover and unplug the fan cable
Remove the 2 hotend screws (H2.0), move the hotend aside, remove the 3 H1.5 screws and lift out the fan with its base
Mount the new fan on the base in the marked orientation (watch the cable direction) with 2 H1.5 screws, without overtightening into the plastic base
Refit the fan base (3 screws) and the hotend (2 screws), plug the fan into the PCB and route its cable
Refit covers, dock the toolhead, reconnect USB and filament
Heat the hotend and confirm the fan spins once it exceeds 60 C
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 15 minutes
Hotend fan switches on above 60 C

sources.title: U1 hot end cooling fan replacement guide

entries.title: Re-gluing a detached copper sheet on top of the U1 hotend
entries.summary: The copper sheet on top of the U1 hotend heatsink can come unstuck from vibration or impact, poorly cleaned surfaces, or too little glue at the factory. It can be reattached with an instant metal adhesive such as Loctite 401: clean both faces with ethanol, use a small amount of glue, press 5-6 seconds, clear any glue from the positioning holes, and confirm both edges sit flush.
symptoms: Copper sheet at the top of the hotend is loose or has fallen off
causes: Adhesive cracked by vibration or impact in use or shipping
Bonding surfaces not cleaned of oil or dust before gluing
Too little adhesive applied
steps: Wearing nitrile gloves, wipe both bonding faces with ethanol on a lint-free cloth, removing old glue and dirt
Apply a small amount of Loctite 401 (or similar metal-bonding instant glue) to the heatsink face, avoiding excess
Align the copper sheet and press firmly for 5-6 seconds
Clean any glue that seeped into the heatsink positioning holes (adhesive remover with nitromethane/acetone, or nail polish remover)
Check both sides sit flush with the heatsink; if not, remove the glue and redo it

entries.title: U1 hotend cooling fan whistling or abnormal noise
entries.summary: A whistling sound from a U1 toolhead is often the hotend cooling fan, caused by blades hitting wiring, a loose fan or a failed fan. Rule out the part cooling and auxiliary fans, confirm by taping the hotend fan blades still while heating, then check wiring clearance and screw tightness behind the rear cover. A faulty fan or mount needs replacement.
symptoms: Whistling or abnormal noise that starts when the hotend fan spins up during heating
causes: Wires touching the fan blades
Fan or fan mount not secured
Fan hardware failure
steps: Turn off the part cooling fan and auxiliary fan to isolate the noise
Heat the noisy toolhead and listen as the hotend fan starts
Stop heating, tape the hotend fan blades so they cannot turn, heat again; if the noise stops, the hotend fan is the source
Remove the toolhead rear cover, move any wires away from the blades, and tighten the fan and fan mount screws
If the noise remains, record your results and contact support to replace the fan or fan mount

sources.title: U1 abnormal noise of hotend cooling fan

entries.title: Replacing a U1 hotend (hot end / nozzle heatsink assembly)
entries.summary: The U1 hotend (nozzle and heatsink assembly) sits behind the toolhead rear cover and swaps in about 15 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. Cool below 40 C, click the toolhead off the swapper, unplug heater and thermistor, swap the hotend held by 2 screws, reconnect heater left and thermistor right, and re-park. Run Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration afterward for multi-color work.
steps: Unload the toolhead (Unload mode) and wait until the nozzle is below 40 C; power off and unplug
Free the toolhead by pressing an H2.0 key into the middle hole between its 2 locating pins until it clicks
Remove the rear cover and release the hotend cable latches with the hex key
Remove the 2 screws, swap the hotend, tighten the screws
Connect the ceramic heater to the left port and thermistor to the right; press both into the clip and fold the thermistor end into the extruder unit slot
Refit the rear cover; set the latch until two red marks show (toolhead 1 at left limit, 2/3/4 at right limit)
Align the latch hole with the swapper pin, push in to the stop and wiggle until both side pins seat
Run Settings > Device Calibration > Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration before multi-color printing
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 15 minutes
Also called hotend, extruder, nozzle or nozzle heatsink assembly

entries.title: U1 Hub board not detected / connection interrupted (0003-0522-0101-0006, 0003-0522-0100-0008)
entries.summary: The U1 Hub board links the toolheads to the main control board and handles toolhead power, firmware updates and dock detection. Not detected means it had no power at startup; connection interrupted means it lost power afterward. Usual causes are a loose mainboard USB cable or the Hub board being squeezed. Normally the toolhead indicator lights stay on; if all are off with 0003-0522-0100-0008, follow the No Toolhead Detected guide.
symptoms: Screen error Hub board not detected
Screen error Hub board connection interrupted
causes: Mainboard USB cable to the Hub board is loose
Hub board is under mechanical compression
steps: Never plug or unplug cables with the printer powered
Power off and remove the right side panel
Scrape the adhesive off the mainboard USB connector, then unplug and firmly reseat the cable
Take out the screws on each end of the Hub board so it is no longer clamped
With the panel still off, reconnect the toolhead USB cables and restart
If it persists, export logs and contact support
facts: All toolhead indicator lights off together with 0003-0522-0100-0008 means every toolhead lost power: use the No Toolhead Detected procedure

sources.title: U1 Hub board not detected / connection interrupted

entries.title: Replacing the U1 HUB board (rear panel)
entries.summary: Replacing the U1 HUB board is medium difficulty (3/5, about 40 minutes, H2.0 hex key) because the top, side and rear panels must come off. When wiring the new board, plug the docking sensor cables in left to right without crossing them, and remember the middle HUB board screw is shared with the rear panel, so fit it only once the panel is back.
steps: Unload all toolheads, rewind and remove the spools and holders, power off and unplug
Disconnect the 4 mm tubes at the back and remove both feeders; remove the 8 M2.5 x 16 toolhead USB screws and unplug all 4 cables
Release the 6 mm tubes at the top, remove the tube holder and the toolheads, then the top panel (4 ST3 x 8 under the silicone plugs)
Remove screw groups 1-9 except group 5 (front panel); lower the bed via the bottom belt if it is in the way
Unplug RFID cables 1-4, remove both side panels, lift the rear cover behind the bracket, remove group 11 (6 x M3 x 6) and the rear panel
Unplug and remove the old HUB board; fit the new one and restore wiring, docking sensor cables in order left to right, uncrossed
Fit only the two outer group-4 screws; refit the rear cover and rear panel (top center hole under the HUB board) and tighten group 11, then the middle group-4 screw, then group 3
Route feeder cables, reconnect RFID, refit side panels (groups 6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 2 in order), the top panel and plugs, then the accessories
facts: Difficulty 3/5, about 40 minutes
Toolhead USB screws: M2.5 x 16 (8 pcs); HUB board screws: M3 x 6 (3 pcs, middle one shared with rear panel)

entries.title: Replacing the U1 chamber LED strips
entries.summary: The U1 has two LED strips on the right inner panel. Replacement is rated easy (2/5) and takes about 20 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. Remove the right side panel (unload toolheads 3 and 4 first), unclip the three terminal blocks, unscrew the four strip screws, fit the new strips, and reassemble, then reload filament into the matching feeder ports.
steps: Remove the right side panel (see the side panel removal entry; unload toolheads 3 and 4)
Hold the release clip and pull the three terminal blocks out to disconnect the strip cables
Remove screws 1-4 and take out the old strips
Mount the new strips with the four screws and reconnect the cables
Reinstall the right panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables, then power on and load filament into each feeder port in order
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes
Tools: H2.0 hex key

entries.title: Replacing the U1 main control board (back up toolhead swap coordinates first)
entries.summary: The U1 main control board (mainboard) is on the right inner panel; replacement is moderate (3/5, about 20 minutes, H2.0 hex key). A new board ships with default toolhead swap coordinates, which can rarely cause tool-change problems, so first download extruder_config.json and, if present, homing_calibrated_origin.json from Fluidd's persistent folder and upload them again afterward.
steps: Find the IP in Settings > Wi-Fi, open Fluidd, Configuration > persistent, and download extruder_config.json and homing_calibrated_origin.json (if it exists)
Remove the right side panel (unload toolheads 3 and 4 first)
Unplug all 16 board cables, slowly lifting the black flip latches on FFC connectors 2, 3 and 16
Remove the 4 screws and the old board, fit the new board with the 4 screws
Reconnect all 16 cables to their numbered sockets
Reassemble the panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables, power on and reload filament
Upload the backed-up files to /persistent
facts: Board sockets 1-4: LAVA Wi-Fi antenna, camera control (FFC), screen control (FFC), light strip control
Sockets 5-8: USB transfer, mainboard-to-HUB board cable, chamber temperature NTC, left motor
Sockets 9-12: right motor, Z-axis motor, main board power, heated bed control
Sockets 13-16: USB expansion, CAN board expansion, filament feeder, RFID transfer (FFC)
Difficulty 3/5, about 20 minutes

sources.title: U1 main control board replacement guide

entries.title: Manually releasing a U1 toolhead from the swapper with the power off
entries.summary: If a toolhead is still attached to the swapper while the U1 is off, you can park it by hand. Working from the back, line up the toolhead hole with the positioning pin, push toolhead and swapper inward to the stop, then slide sideways until the pin seats in the backing-bracket hole. Toolhead 1 sits against the right inner wall and slides left; toolheads 2/3/4 sit against the left wall and slide right. An H2.0 hex key in the release hole also frees it.
steps: Power off and stand at the back of the printer

Toolhead 1: hold it against the right inner wall with its hole aligned to the positioning pin, push toolhead and swapper inward until they stop, then move left until the pin enters the hole on the backing bracket and the toolhead lets go
Toolheads 2/3/4: same motion but held against the left inner wall and moved right at the end
Alternative for any toolhead: insert an H2.0 hex key into the release hole on the swapper to unlatch it

sources.title: U1 How to manually detach the toolhead

entries.title: U1 multi-color misalignment: colors offset, gaps or overlaps at color boundaries
entries.summary: U1 multi-color accuracy depends on calibrated offsets between toolheads. Shifted colors, gaps or overlaps at color changes, or multi-part assemblies that do not fit usually mean bad offset data or a mechanical issue: filament stuck under a nozzle during calibration, a loose hotend, a copper plate too far from the calibration sensor (should be 0.1-0.4 mm), or dry steel balls. Fix these, then rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration.
symptoms: Visible misalignment between colors
Gaps or overlaps where colors meet
Multi-color parts do not fit together or show spacing
causes: Filament residue under a nozzle changing its trigger height during calibration
Hotend not fully tightened
Gap between hotend copper plate and calibration sensor too large, delaying the trigger and skewing Z references
Steel balls lacking grease, raising resistance and positioning error
steps: Update firmware, unload the toolheads, run Manual Leveling then Heated Bed Leveling
Park all toolheads, remove each one (toolhead 1 slides right, 2-4 slide left; they are held magnetically) and check the nozzle tip; heat and pick off residue with tweezers or a wire brush
Power off, remove the toolhead top cover (3 screws), wiggle the toolhead; if the hotend moves, remove the rear cover and tighten its 2 screws
Check the copper plate to calibration sensor gap is 0.1-0.4 mm (about a sheet of A4 paper); if larger, loosen the 2 hotend screws, push the hotend up and retighten
Clean pogo pins and steel balls with alcohol and apply an even film of the included white lithium grease to the balls
Run Settings > Device Calibration > Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration, then print a four-color test and check boundaries, gaps and overlap
facts: Copper plate to calibration sensor gap: 0.1-0.4 mm
Recalibrate after moving the printer, replacing a toolhead or hotend, or major maintenance; lubricate moving parts quarterly

entries.title: U1 no toolhead detected (error 0003-0522-0100-0006)
entries.summary: Error 0003-0522-0100-0006 means the U1 sees no toolhead. Look through the gap in the toolhead for its internal indicator: if it is lit, contact support; if dark, connect toolheads one at a time to find the bad one, then isolate the toolhead PCB (often a capacitor pierced by a wrong or overtightened USB screw), hotend or ceramic heater. If every toolhead stays dark, suspect the 16-pin cable that carries toolhead power control.
symptoms: Toolhead internal indicator light off
causes: Toolhead PCB capacitor pierced by a wrong (correct is ST2.6 x 10) or overtightened USB cable screw
Toolhead PCB failure
Shorted hotend, often the ceramic heater
Loose 16-pin cable between mainboard and HUB board cutting power to all toolheads
Toolhead power supply fault
steps: Power off for every plug/unplug step
Connect one toolhead at a time and power on; a toolhead whose indicator stays dark is faulty
Remove that toolhead's PCB and inspect for damaged capacitors
If the capacitors are fine, unplug everything but USB from the PCB and power on: no light means the PCB is bad
If it lights, plug in both hotend cables: light goes out means the hotend is bad; then try only the thermistor (right port), and if it lights now the ceramic heater is faulty

If no toolhead lights individually: remove the top and right side panels, reconnect toolhead USB, and reseat both ends of the 16-pin cable, supporting the inner panel behind the main board as you plug it in
Measure the two 24 V test points shown on the wiki with a multimeter (DC); typical faulty readings are 24 V/0 V or 0 V/0 V; share results and logs with support
facts: Toolhead-side USB cable screws must be ST2.6 x 10
Difficulty 3/5, 10-30 minutes; tools: H2.0 hex key, multimeter

entries.title: U1 filament blob wrapped around the nozzle/hotend: causes and prevention
entries.summary: A blob forms when molten filament collects on the outside of the U1 nozzle and gradually encases the hotend, often alongside the part lifting in early layers, the nozzle plowing into the print, or layer shifts. Main causes: a leaking hotend (heat break or nozzle joint), the nozzle running too close to the bed or part (uneven bed, firmware z_offset too large), weak plate adhesion, and poor process settings.
symptoms: Filament builds up on the nozzle exterior and spreads around the hotend
Print detaches in the first few layers
Nozzle scrapes the model
Layer shift
Burnt black plastic on the nozzle
causes: Hotend leakage at the heat break or nozzle joints from assembly gaps
Uneven bed: the nozzle hits raised areas and peels the part off while still extruding
Firmware z_offset too large, so the nozzle sits too close and filament squeezes up around it
Dirty or worn PEI sheet giving poor adhesion
Over-high flow combined with too large a z_offset (edge buildup, scraping)
Short retraction with fast travel, or damp filament with too hot a nozzle (stringing, whiskers, pitting)
steps: If the hotend still heats, clean the blob off (Snapmaker has a video); if a nozzle temperature error appears or the hotend is damaged, swap in a new hotend or move a new ceramic heater and thermistor onto the spare hotend from the accessory box
Measure from the hotend top to the nozzle tip with calipers: it should be 48 +/- 0.2 mm; replace the hotend if outside
Wire-brush burnt plastic off the nozzle; if it keeps coming back, replace the hotend
Enable Auto Leveling before every print, and level the bed manually if that is not enough
Keep first layer speed at or below 50 mm/s
After replacing a hotend rerun Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration; on third-party plates recalibrate z_offset
Clean the PEI sheet regularly and replace it when adhesion stays poor
For third-party filament, calibrate temperature and flow from the generic profile and tune pressure advance and retraction; stop the print early if the first layer looks wrong

settings.advice: Keep at or below 50 mm/s so the nozzle is less likely to catch and peel the first layer.
Run a flow calibration and lower it if edges show material buildup or the nozzle drags through the part.
Increase if stringing or whiskers feed material onto the nozzle; the wiki flags short retraction as a blob contributor.
Lower it if pitting and stringing appear together, and dry the filament; damp filament plus high temperature is a listed cause.
Tune from real prints, especially for third-party filament.
Select the correct plate type before slicing; with the official plate no z_offset calibration is normally needed.

facts: Hotend top-to-nozzle-tip reference length: 48 +/- 0.2 mm
Leaks most often occur at the heat break and nozzle assembly joints

entries.title: U1 toolhead keeps retrying filament load: clearing a clogged nozzle
entries.summary: If a U1 toolhead cycles through filament loading several times without finishing, the nozzle is likely clogged. Heat it 10-20 C above the filament's normal print temperature, gently work the supplied cleaning needle up and down in the nozzle, then load filament again to confirm flow.
symptoms: Toolhead repeatedly attempts to load filament and never completes
causes: Clogged nozzle
steps: Heat the nozzle 10-20 C above normal: PLA 200 to 210-220 C, PETG 240 to 250-260 C, ABS 240 to 250-260 C
At temperature, gently insert the supplied cleaning needle and move it up and down several times
Use light force so the needle does not bend or scratch the nozzle bore
Load filament again to confirm the nozzle is clear; if not, see the filament-not-extruding guide to separate hotend and extruder clogs
facts: Snapmaker's pages give different PLA reference temperatures for clog clearing (200 C base here, 230 C in the not-extruding guide); use the filament's actual print temperature plus 10-20 C

sources.title: U1 Known issues and quick fixes

entries.title: U1 Nozzle Diameter Mismatch when printing a local G-code file
entries.summary: A Nozzle Diameter Mismatch error on a local U1 G-code file can occur because the file's metadata was scanned by older firmware and no longer matches what the current firmware expects. Press and hold the file in the file list, release to trigger a metadata rescan, and start the print again once it finishes.
symptoms: Nozzle Diameter Mismatch error when starting a G-code file stored on the printer or USB drive
causes: File metadata cached by an earlier firmware version
steps: Press and hold the G-code file on the touchscreen, then release to rescan its metadata
Wait for the scan to finish and start the print again
If the error remains, submit a support ticket

entries.title: U1 nozzle scraping or hitting the build plate
entries.summary: When the U1 nozzle scratches or bumps the bed, makes friction or impact noises, or leaves wear marks on the plate, check in order: the bed (residue, deformation, leveling), the hotend (filament stuck on the nozzle, loose hotend or dislodged heater block, copper plate gap over 0.1-0.4 mm), then the Z offset. In printer.cfg a larger z_offset moves the nozzle closer, so lower it in 0.02 mm steps if it scrapes.
symptoms: Nozzle scratches or collides with the bed while moving
Friction or knocking noise from the toolhead
Scratches, coating damage or local wear on the plate
causes: Filament residue on the PEI sheet or a deformed bed
Bed not leveled
Filament stuck on the nozzle tip
Loose hotend or heating block slipped down
Gap between hotend copper plate and calibration sensor too large
Firmware Z offset too high so the nozzle starts too low
steps: Scrape residue off the PEI sheet; replace the bed if it has bulges or warping
Run Manual Leveling (Settings > Maintenance), then Heated Bed Leveling (Settings > Device Calibration)
Unload the toolhead, heat the nozzle and clean off residue with tweezers or a wire brush
Power off, remove the toolhead and hotend, shake the hotend; if it moves, pull the silicone sock to see whether the heating block has slipped
If the hotend is damaged, move the ceramic heater and thermistor onto the spare hotend from the tool kit
Check the copper plate to calibration sensor gap is 0.1-0.4 mm (about one A4 sheet); if larger, loosen the 2 hotend screws, push it up and retighten
Enable Advanced Mode, open printer.cfg in Fluidd and lower z_offset in 0.02 mm steps (e.g. -0.05 to -0.07 to -0.09), save and restart
Verify with a single-layer test print: no contact, no odd noise, even nozzle height
facts: In U1 printer.cfg, a larger z_offset puts the nozzle closer to the bed
Scraping guide suggests 0.02 mm steps; other U1 pages suggest 0.01 or up to 0.05

sources.title: U1 Nozzle Scraping the Build Plate

entries.title: U1 errors 0003-0523-0000-0006 / 0003-0523-0000-0036: bad heating command or temperature over 300 C
entries.summary: 0003-0523-0000-0006 means the U1 did not understand the G-code's toolhead heating command; 0003-0523-0000-0036 means the requested extruder temperature is out of range.
