Both point to the G-code: slice with Snapmaker Orca and its U1 profile, and keep every nozzle temperature at or below the 300 C hotend limit.
symptoms: Print stops with 0003-0523-0000-0006 (heating command not recognized)
Print stops with 0003-0523-0000-0036 (extruder temperature out of range)
causes: G-code from a slicer or profile not compatible with the U1
Temperature values in the G-code above the allowed range
steps: Re-slice the model in Snapmaker Orca using the official U1 printer profile
Check the filament temperatures in the slicer, including initial layer, and make sure none exceed 300 C
If the error persists, send the G-code file to Snapmaker support

settings.advice: Keep at or below 300 C, the U1 hotend maximum; higher values trigger 0003-0523-0000-0036.
Also must not exceed 300 C on the U1.

facts: U1 hotend maximum temperature: 300 C

sources.title: U1 nozzle temperature is abnormal (caused by incorrect slicing parameters) 0003-0523-0000-0006

entries.title: Replacing the U1 nozzle wiper (left for toolhead 1, right for 2-4)
entries.summary: The U1 has two nozzle wipers under the toolhead nozzles: the left one (far left) serves toolhead 1 and the right one serves toolheads 2, 3 and 4. A damaged or detached wiper can hurt first layers. Replacement is very easy (1/5, about 5 minutes) with an H2.0 hex key.
steps: Select the matching toolhead and tap Detach Toolhead on the touchscreen
Lower the print platform to its bottom limit
Power off, unplug and push the toolhead away from the wiper by hand
Remove the 2 wiper screws, fit the new wiper and tighten the 2 screws
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes

sources.title: U1 first layer printing troubleshooting guide

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca cannot connect to the U1 while the app and Fluidd can
entries.summary: If Snapmaker Orca fails to connect to a U1 that the Snapmaker App and Fluidd reach normally, the cause is a known connection bug in Snapmaker Orca v2.1.1 and earlier. Install the latest official Snapmaker Orca.
symptoms: Snapmaker Orca cannot connect to the U1
Snapmaker App and Fluidd connect fine
causes: Connection bug in Snapmaker Orca v2.1.1 and older
steps: Download and install the latest official Snapmaker Orca release
Reconnect to the printer

sources.title: U1 Known issues and quick fixes

entries.title: Snapmaker Orca flow ratio calibration (YOLO) for U1 filaments
entries.summary: Slicer flow values do not always match real extrusion, so calibrate per filament. In Snapmaker Orca use Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended), print the generated blocks with your filament selected, and pick the block with the fewest bumps and gaps. Add its number to the current flow ratio: e.g. 1 + (-0.01) = 0.99.
symptoms: Bulging, ridged top surfaces (flow too high)
Gaps between top lines (flow too low)
steps: Select the filament you will print with in the Filament section of the sidebar
Click Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO (Recommended) to generate the test model, then slice and print it
Choose the flattest block, with the fewest bulges and gaps; its label is the flow correction
Open the filament's ... > Edit and find Filament > Flow ratio and Pressure Advance > Flow ratio
Set new flow ratio = current flow ratio + correction (1 + (-0.01) = 0.99) and save

settings.advice: Set to the current value plus the YOLO correction of the flattest block.

entries.title: Finding the best print temperature with a Snapmaker Orca temperature tower (U1)
entries.summary: Each filament has its own sweet spot. In Snapmaker Orca's Prepare tab select the filament, open Calibration > Temperature, keep or adjust the preset start and end temperatures, and print the generated tower, whose identical sections each print at a different temperature. Pick the best-looking section and set both first-layer and other-layer nozzle temperatures to its value.
steps: In the Prepare tab choose your filament in the sidebar
Click Calibration > Temperature, select the filament type and set Start temp and End temp (the presets per material are fine)
Click OK to generate the tower, then print it on the U1
Discard sections with stringing or poor surfaces and note the temperature labelled on the best one (e.g. 200)
Open the filament's ... > Edit, go to Filament > Print temperature > Nozzle, and set First layer and Other layers to that value

settings.advice: Set Other layers to the best temperature-tower value.
Set First layer to the same calibrated value, per the wiki example.

entries.title: Replacing a U1 parking tool on the toolhead docking bracket
entries.summary: The U1 docking bracket carries four parking tools: one left parking tool (leftmost, toolhead 1) and three right parking tools. Replacing one is easy (2/5, about 20 minutes, H2.0 hex key) but requires taking all four toolheads off and removing the bracket, which has four docking Hall sensor cables behind it.
steps: Power off and unplug; slide all 4 toolheads off the bracket (No.1 to the right, No.2/3/4 to the left) and rest them on the bed
Remove the 4 bracket screws, ease the bracket out, flip it and unplug the 4 docking Hall sensor cables while pressing their clips
Remove the 2 screws holding the parking tool, fit the new one and tighten
Reconnect the 4 sensor cables and refit the bracket with its 4 screws
Set the sliders (No.1 far left, No.2/3/4 far right, red marks visible) and remount each toolhead on its locating pins
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes
Each parking tool is held by 2 screws

entries.title: Replacing the U1 part cooling fan adapter board
entries.summary: The part cooling fan adapter board is inside the U1 toolhead swapper behind the fan cover. It swaps in about 5 minutes (1/5) with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys.
steps: Detach the toolhead from the swapper and power off
Move the swapper by hand to a convenient spot and slide off the air duct
Remove the 2 cover screws (H2.0) and the cover, then unplug the fan cable
Remove the 4 board screws (H1.5), replace the adapter board and refit the screws
Reconnect the fan, refit the cover (2 screws) and slide the duct onto the swapper guide rails
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 5 minutes

sources.title: U1 part cooling fan adapter board replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 part cooling fan and part cooling duct kit
entries.summary: The U1 part cooling fan lives in the toolhead swapper behind the part cooling fan cover; the duct kit is the cover plus the air duct. Replacement is very easy (1/5, about 10 minutes) with an H2.0 hex key. Do not run the fan cable through the cable groove when refitting.
steps: Park the active toolhead, power off and unplug, then move the swapper to a convenient spot
Slide off the air duct, remove the 2 cover screws and the fan cover
Unplug the fan, remove its 2 screws and take it out
Fit the new fan with 2 screws and plug it in, keeping its cable out of the cable groove
Refit the cover (2 screws) and slide the duct onto the guide rails under the swapper
facts: Difficulty 1/5, about 10 minutes

sources.title: U1 part cooling fan and part cooling duct kit replacement guide

entries.title: U1 part cooling fan does not spin
entries.summary: A U1 part cooling fan that will not turn is usually electrostatic damage. Clean the pogo pins and solid pins with alcohol for good contact, try driving the fan from the touchscreen, and spin the blades by hand 2-3 turns to feel for resistance. Report the results and the fan's age to support; a damaged fan gets replaced.
symptoms: Part cooling fan does not rotate
causes: Electrostatic damage to the fan
Poor pogo pin contact
steps: Clean the pogo pins and solid pins with alcohol on a lint-free cloth
Command the fan from the touchscreen and see whether it runs
Turn the blades by hand 2-3 revolutions and note any resistance
Send the results and how long the fan has been used to support; replace the part cooling fan if confirmed damaged

sources.title: U1 part cooling fan cannot rotate

entries.title: U1 pitting, pockmarks and popping sounds: wet filament or excessive retraction
entries.summary: Pits on U1 prints come in two forms: burst pockmarks with outward-curled edges and popping or crackling at the nozzle, and random fine pits about 0.1-0.3 mm across. The usual cause is moisture in the filament flashing to steam in the hotend; dry it. If the filament is dry, retraction that is too long or too fast sucks air in through the nozzle: keep retraction at 0.5-1.5 mm (never over 2 mm) and speed at 25-45 mm/s.
symptoms: Holes with burst, outward-curled edges
Popping or crackling from the nozzle while extruding
Scattered fine pits about 0.1-0.3 mm on outer walls
causes: Moisture in the filament turning to steam bubbles that burst at the nozzle exit
Retraction distance too long, pulling air in through the nozzle
Retraction speed too high (above about 60 mm/s) causing cavitation in the melt
steps: Check whether the material is likely wet (see the moisture sensitivity entry) and dry it, for example in a SnapDryer
If the filament is dry, reduce retraction length in 0.5 mm steps until slight stringing appears, then increase it a little
Keep retraction within 0.5-1.5 mm for the direct-drive toolhead and never above 2 mm
Lower retraction speed to 25-45 mm/s
Print a test model and confirm no popping and no continuous pits; favor surface quality over a little stringing, which a heat gun can clean up

settings.advice: Reduce in 0.5 mm steps; keep 0.5-1.5 mm and never above 2 mm on the U1 direct drive.
Lower to 25-45 mm/s; speeds above about 60 mm/s can draw vacuum bubbles.

sources.title: U1 how to avoid pitting and pockmarks in prints

entries.title: Cleaning the U1 toolhead pogo pins
entries.summary: Clean the U1 pogo pins every 4-6 months so no dust or grease sits on the contact tips. Use a lint-free cloth barely dampened with alcohol, wipe each tip in one direction only, and let it dry. Do not scrape the pins with anything hard, which damages the plating.
steps: Put about 1-2 drops of alcohol on a dust-free cloth; it should be damp, not dripping, so no alcohol runs into the spring housing
Wrap the cloth around the pin tips and wipe in a single direction (base toward tip), not back and forth, to avoid leaving lint
For heavily soiled tips, press lightly so the spring pins retract and contact the cloth better
Let the alcohol evaporate for 10-20 seconds or pat dry with a clean dry cloth
facts: Interval: every 4-6 months
Never scrape pogo pins with hard objects (coating damage)

entries.title: U1 Pogopin contact anomaly after a print
entries.summary: A Pogopin contact anomaly shown after a U1 print finishes usually comes from dirty pogo pins or solid pins, a stuck pogo pin (replace the toolhead PCB), or too little pogo pin compression, from a protruding screw or debris on the swapper. Clean the pins with alcohol, press each of the three pins per pogo connector to check spring return, and inspect the swapper.
symptoms: Pogopin contact anomaly error on screen after a print completes
causes: Contaminated pogo pins or solid pins
A pogo pin stuck down or not springing back
Insufficient pogo pin compression travel: protruding screw on the back of the swapper or debris in its 3 pin slots
steps: Clean pogo pins and solid pins with alcohol on a lint-free cloth wrapped tightly around a finger, keeping it away from the greased steel balls
Press each of the three pins in every pogo connector; if one will not press or does not spring back, replace the toolhead PCB
With a caliper: remove the toolhead top cover and part cooling fan cover, pick up the toolhead and measure the reference distance shown on the wiki; out of range means contact support
Without a caliper: check the rear of the toolhead swapper for any screw sticking out, and the 3 pin slots for foreign objects
For remote help, send order number, SN plus verification code, labelled photos of each toolhead's pins, and the error count from Snapmaker's toolhead swap test G-code

entries.title: U1 poor bridging: sagging, stringing or broken bridges
entries.summary: Bridges on the U1 sag, string or break when the strand cannot cool before gravity pulls it down. In Snapmaker Orca slow the bridge speed to about 15-30 mm/s, raise the auxiliary part cooling fan and the max fan speed, lower nozzle temperature in 5 C steps (not below the filament minimum), and fine-tune the bridge flow ratio.
symptoms: Bridged lines sag or droop
Stringing in bridged areas
Bridge strands break or fail to anchor at both ends
causes: Bridge speed too high
Not enough cooling
Nozzle temperature too high
Bridge flow ratio unsuitable
steps: Lower bridge speed to the 15-30 mm/s range depending on filament and span
Raise the auxiliary part cooling fan speed for bridges
Raise the max fan speed threshold in the filament cooling settings
Lower the Other layers nozzle temperature by 5 C at a time, staying above the filament's minimum recommended temperature
Adjust the bridge flow ratio so strands carry enough material without sagging or stringing
Reprint and check the bridges

settings.advice: Lower to about 15-30 mm/s so the strand cools before it sags.
Increase the auxiliary part cooling fan for bridges.
Raise the max fan speed threshold for better bridge cooling (filament-dependent).
Keep high so bridges and overhangs get strong cooling.
Lower in 5 C steps, but not below nozzle_temperature_range_low.
Fine-tune: lower slightly if bridges sag, raise slightly if strands are thin or break.

entries.title: U1 poor overhangs: sagging, collapse, stringing or curling
entries.summary: Overhang problems on the U1 come from gravity winning before the plastic cools. Add supports beyond about 45 degrees, lower nozzle temperature in 5 C steps, cut overall speed to 60-80% or enable Slow down for overhangs, raise the auxiliary fan and max fan speed, and use a smaller layer height or adaptive (variable) layer height on overhang regions.
symptoms: Overhangs sag or collapse
Stringing on overhang surfaces
Overhangs warp or deform
causes: Overhang angle too steep (over about 45 degrees) without support
Nozzle temperature too high
Print speed too high
Insufficient cooling
Layer height too large, adding weight to unsupported sections
steps: Enable supports for overhangs steeper than about 45 degrees
Lower Other layers nozzle temperature by 5 C steps, staying above the filament minimum
Reduce overall speed to 60-80% of current in Prepare > Process
Under Speed enable Slow down for overhangs and set overhang speeds
In Filament > Edit > Cooling raise the auxiliary part cooling fan and the max fan speed threshold
Lower the layer height, or use the adaptive layer height tool in the top toolbar to thin layers only on overhangs

settings.advice: Turn on for overhangs steeper than about 45 degrees.
Lower in 5 C steps, not below the filament's minimum recommended temperature.
Enable to slow down only on overhang regions, more effective than slowing the whole print.
Reduce for steep overhang segments when Slow down for overhangs is on.
Reduce for the steepest overhang segments.
Increase the auxiliary part cooling fan to set overhangs faster.
Raise the max fan speed threshold (values are filament-dependent).
Reduce; thinner layers make unsupported sections lighter and less prone to sag.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 power supply and AC heated bed control board wiring
entries.summary: The U1 power supply sits in the power supply box behind the right side panel, with the AC heated bed control board mounted on it. Replacement is moderate (3/5, about 40 minutes) and needs an H2.0 hex key and a PH2 Phillips screwdriver. Note the nine AC board cable positions before unplugging so they go back correctly.
steps: Power off, unplug, let parts cool, and remove the right side panel
Remove the PSU cover (screws 1-4), unplugging its fan first
Loosen the 7 Phillips terminal screws on the AC heated bed control board and disconnect its cables; press the latch to pull cables 1, 2, 4 and 5
Remove screws 1-5 to take out the power supply box, then the screws under the AC board to remove it
Remove the 3 screws on the right of the box and swap the power supply
Loosen the 7 terminal screws on the new unit, fit the AC board at an angle, fix it from below, refit the box (screws 1-5)
Reconnect all 9 cables, tighten the 7 terminal screws and tidy wiring; refit the fan and cover, then reassemble
facts: AC board cables 1-5: AC red, AC black, AC and heated bed yellow, heated bed red, heated bed blue
AC board cables 6-9: heated bed NTC, HUB board power, main control board power, heated bed control
Difficulty 3/5, about 40 minutes

entries.title: U1 power switch not lighting up (power cable, blown fuse, PSU or bed short, switch fault)
entries.summary: If the U1 power switch stays dark when switched on, first rule out the obvious (plugs, power strip, switch). Then try a known-good IEC power cable, check the fuse in the holder under the switch, and if it is blown look for a short in the power supply (burn marks or smell, about 84 kOhm across input points) or heated bed (damaged cable, about 50 Ohm across the heater). An intact fuse points to a loose wire or failed power switch.
symptoms: Power switch light stays off after plugging in and switching on
causes: Faulty power cable
Blown fuse from a short circuit in the power supply
Blown fuse from a short in the heated bed or its cable
Loose neutral (black) or line (red) wire on the power switch, or a failed switch
steps: Check both ends of the power cable, the power strip and the switch
Swap in a compatible power cable from a PC, monitor or kitchen appliance; if the switch lights, ask support for a new official cable
Power off, pry the fuse holder out from under the switch with diagonal-pliers tips and inspect the fuse
Fuse blown: remove the right side panel and power cover; look for burning or a burnt smell at the PSU and for damaged or creased bed cables
With a multimeter on the wiki's labelled points: PSU input points 1-2 about 84 kOhm, and with the bed cables (4, 5) unplugged, 1-3 and 2-3 open circuit; otherwise the PSU is shorted
Bed: 4-5 about 50 Ohm, and 4-3 and 5-3 open circuit; otherwise the bed is shorted; send readings to support for fuse plus PSU or bed replacement

Fuse intact: remove side and rear panels and the power cover, remove screws 1-3 by the rear switch, unplug the two switch cables, and check the black and red wires are tight; reseat, or replace the switch via support
facts: Difficulty 3/5, 10-40 minutes; tools: H2.0 hex key, diagonal pliers, multimeter

entries.title: U1 prime tower shifting, collapsing or breaking (multi-color)
entries.summary: A U1 prime tower that shifts or falls is fixed by one change at a time, ideally after watching a timelapse. For same-material prints, enlarge and stabilize the tower: squarer width, wider brim, more purge-line spacing, and the Rib wall type with longer, wider ribs. For mixed materials such as PLA with PETG, assign one filament to the tower shell. For adhesion problems, clean the plate, raise first-layer bed temperature, cut early cooling, and enclose warp-prone materials.
symptoms: Prime tower shifts during printing
Prime tower partly or completely topples
Tower delaminates at the boundary between different materials
causes: Tall narrow tower with a small footprint
Nozzle collisions knocking a weak tower
Poor adhesion between different filament types inside the tower
Poor bed adhesion: dirty plate, wrong plate type, cold bed or too much fan, drafts with ABS/ASA/PA
steps: Examine the failed tower (timelapse helps) and change one parameter at a time
Set the tower width so its footprint is close to square
Increase the tower brim width and the purge line spacing
Choose Rib as the wall type; lengthen ribs for a wider base and avoid small rib widths
For mixed-material prints, specify a single filament for the tower shell
Confirm the plate type in the slicer and wash the plate with warm water and dish soap
Raise bed temperature and reduce fan speed for the first layers; enclose and cool less for ABS/ASA/PA or a cold room

settings.advice: Adjust so the tower is roughly square, giving a stable footprint.
Increase to improve tower adhesion.
Increase purge line spacing to enlarge the tower volume.
Set to Rib to resist tipping and nozzle knocks on tall towers.
Increase for a larger, more stable base.
Do not set small; enough width bonds the outer wall to the inner infill.
Assign one filament to the tower shell when mixing poorly bonding materials such as PLA and PETG.
Increase to keep cooling off for more of the first layers when the tower lifts.
Make sure the selected plate type matches the installed plate.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 power supply cooling fan
entries.summary: The U1 power supply cooling fan is mounted on the power supply cover behind the right side panel. Replacement is easy (2/5, about 20 minutes) with an H2.0 hex key: remove the right panel, take off the PSU cover (4 screws, unplug the fan first), and swap the fan held by 2 screws.
steps: Remove the right side panel (unload toolheads 3 and 4 first; see side panel removal entry)
Remove screws 1-4 on the power supply cover, ease it out and unplug the fan cable before lifting it away
Remove the 2 fan screws and fit the new fan with them
Plug in the fan cable and refit the cover with its 4 screws
Reassemble the panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables and reload filament
facts: Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes

sources.title: U1 power supply cooling fan replacement guide

entries.title: U1 fails to get QR code or PIN code (cloud binding, firmware before 0.9.0)
entries.summary: On U1 firmware older than V0.9.0, cloud connection problems stop the setup wizard, or later the settings, from fetching a QR or PIN code. Exit the wizard, update the firmware from a USB flash drive and restart; if binding still fails, the network is probably weak, so retry several times.
symptoms: QR code fails to load in the first-start wizard
QR code or PIN code fails to load later in normal use
causes: Cloud connection issues in firmware before V0.9.0
Weak network connection
steps: In the wizard tap Set Up Later to reach Device Calibration, long-press the indicated screen spot for 5 seconds, release, then keep tapping Set Up Later to leave the wizard
Update the firmware from a USB flash drive and restart
If the cloud still fails, retry the connection several times on a stronger network

sources.title: U1 Known issues and quick fixes

entries.title: Replacing the U1 RFID board (left inner panel)
entries.summary: The U1 RFID board is on the left inner panel. Replacement is moderate (3/5), about 30 minutes with an H2.0 hex key. After removing the left side panel (unload toolheads 1 and 2), unplug the board's three cables, opening the FFC connector's black flip latch first, then swap the board held by four screws.
steps: Remove the left side panel (see the side panel removal entry)
Unplug its three cables: the filament feeder lead, the auxiliary cooling fan lead, and the FFC ribbon to the main control board (flip up the black latch before pulling the ribbon)
Remove the 4 screws and take out the old board
Fit the new board with the 4 screws and reconnect all three cables
Reassemble the left panel, feeder, spools, top cover and USB cables
facts: Difficulty 3/5, about 30 minutes
RFID board connectors: auxiliary cooling fan cable, main control board FFC, filament feeder cable

entries.title: Replacing U1 RFID antenna coils (red wire terminal above black)
entries.summary: RFID antenna coils are glued and taped to the inside of the U1 left panel (toolheads 1-2) and right panel (toolheads 3-4). Replacement is easy (2/5, about 20 minutes) using an H2.0 hex key, scraper, tape and glue. When fitting a new coil, match the original position and wire routing, and place the red-wire terminal above the black-wire terminal.
steps: Unload the affected toolheads (all four if doing both sides), power off and unplug
Remove the 8 USB cable screws, the filament feeder(s), the top cover and the relevant side panel(s), disconnecting the RFID cables
Scrape off the glue holding the old coil and peel away its fixing tape
Position the new coil and route its wires like the original, red-wire terminal above black, and tape it down
Glue the coil in place
Reinstall panels, top cover, feeders, spools and USB cables in reverse order
facts: Left coils serve toolheads 1 and 2; right coils serve toolheads 3 and 4
Difficulty 2/5, about 20 minutes

entries.title: U1 cannot read filament type/color from RFID (RFID information not updating)
entries.summary: When the U1 does not pick up filament type and color, the cause is usually a bad spool chip, runout detection switched off, leftover filament in the toolhead, a faulty runout sensor, or an RFID antenna/cable fault. Test the spool in another channel, restore factory settings, check sensors in Fluidd, then force a read with FILAMENT_DT_UPDATE CHANNEL=0-3. Only Snapmaker-store spools carry RFID chips.
symptoms: Filament type and color are not detected after loading a spool
causes: Faulty RFID chip on the spool, or a non-Snapmaker spool without a chip
Toolhead filament runout detection disabled
Residual filament left inside the toolhead
Toolhead filament runout sensor fault or misinstalled filament tube
RFID antenna coil, connector or wiring problem
steps: Move the spool to a channel that does recognize filament; if it still fails, try a known-good chipped spool to separate chip from channel faults
Run Restore Factory Settings from the touchscreen settings page; if this fixes it, runout detection was likely off, so watch for recurrence
Open the toolhead and remove any leftover filament
Open Fluidd (printer IP from Settings > Wi-Fi) and confirm all Runout Sensors are enabled under Tune
Remove the tube above the toolhead, insert filament (Fluidd should show a green check), pull it out (orange exclamation mark)
Feed the spool into the auto feeder and send FILAMENT_DT_UPDATE CHANNEL=0 (channel 1) to CHANNEL=3 (channel 4) in the Fluidd console, one channel at a time
If the command still cannot read the tag, open the side panel, reseat that channel's connector, check for bent pins, and confirm the coil's red-wire terminal sits above the black one
facts: FILAMENT_DT_UPDATE CHANNEL=n uses zero-based numbering: CHANNEL=0 is channel 1

sources.title: U1 RFID information cannot be updated

entries.title: U1 touchscreen rear cover feels loose
entries.summary: The U1 screen rear cover is designed to pop off quickly, so its plastic clips can sit slightly loose in the metal panel. It does not affect function. To firm it up, remove the cover and add tape at the four clip points, either two layers on the cover's clips or one to two layers on the matching spots of the front panel.
steps: Remove the screen rear cover
Add two layers of tape over the four clips on the cover, or one to two layers at the four matching positions on the front panel
Snap the cover back on

sources.title: U1 Known issues and quick fixes

entries.title: Removing a U1 left or right side panel (for RFID, LED, fan repairs)
entries.summary: Several U1 repairs (RFID board and coils, LED strips, auxiliary cooling fan) need a side panel off. The left side serves toolheads 1-2 and the right side toolheads 3-4. You unload those toolheads, unplug power, pull the filament feeder, free the four toolhead USB cables, lift the top cover and remove eight panel screws, disconnecting the RFID cables before the panel comes away. Only an H2.0 hex key is needed.
steps: Touchscreen: Unload Mode, select toolheads 1+2 (left) or 3+4 (right), tap Unload, then wind back the remaining filament and remove those spools and holders
Turn off the printer and unplug the power cable
Press the feeder clip and slide the filament feeder out, then disconnect its cable
Remove the 8 screws holding the 4 toolhead USB cables and unplug them
Pop out the 4 silicone corner plugs on the top cover and remove the 4 screws under them
Shift the top cover slightly, remove the 4 marked panel screws, screws 5 and 6 inside the spool holder holes, and screws 7 and 8 on the inner panel
Thread the feeder cable through the panel opening, disconnect the two RFID cables, and lift the panel off
Reassemble in reverse: RFID cables, feeder cable routing, 8 panel screws, feeder (align clips and push in), spools, top cover screws and plugs, USB cables (8 screws)

sources.title: U1 auxiliary cooling fan replacement guide

entries.title: Removing a stripped U1 heated bed transport screw
entries.summary: Three screws lock the U1 heated bed for shipping. If one spins without coming out, take out the other two to release tension, then pull the Z timing belt under the printer to the left. The rising bed presses against the stuck screw head, adding friction so the threads catch and it backs out as you turn it.
symptoms: Heated bed shipping screw spins in place and will not come out
steps: Remove the other bed transport screws with an H2.0 hex key to release the belt-to-bed tension
Power off and tilt or lay the printer on its side to reach the Z timing belt underneath
Pull the belt steadily to the left so the bed rises
Meanwhile keep turning the stuck screw with the hex key under steady torque until it backs out
facts: The U1 heated bed is secured by three screws to prevent shifting in transport

sources.title: U1 how to remove stripped heated bed mounting screws

entries.title: U1 Tangled Filament Detected (0002-0523-000x-0038): feeder odometer, tangles, broken filament
entries.summary: Tangled Filament Detected means the U1 feeder judged the filament stuck and paused the print; the 12th digit of the code gives the channel (0-3 = toolheads 1-4, e.g. 0002-0523-0000-0038 is toolhead 1). The first time, dismiss and resume. If it repeats, check for a tangled spool, set air printing detection sensitivity to Low, look for broken filament in the guide tube, and test the feeder odometer wheel for slipping.
symptoms: Print pauses with a tangled filament or feeding-stuck error
causes: Filament tangled or knotted on the spool
Air printing detection sensitivity set too high
Broken filament blocking the guide tube
Feeder odometer wheel slipping so it does not register movement
steps: If tangled, cut the filament at the feeder inlet, remove and untangle the spool, cold-pull the leftover filament from the toolhead, reload and Resume Print
Settings > Print Preferences: set air printing detection sensitivity to Low
Inspect the guide tube; two strands visible side by side mean filament broke inside it and must be cleared
Remove the feeder (keep its springs and magnets safe) and identify the odometer wheel for the channel in the code (channel 1 = upper wheel in the wiki photo)
Push a 20 cm piece of rigid filament through, curve facing that wheel; the wheel should turn in step, and little or no turning means it slips
To fix slipping, remove the 2 H2.0 screws on the filament guide bracket, shift it toward the slipping wheel within its play, retighten and reassemble
facts: The feeder compares the G-code extrusion length with odometer wheel rotation to detect tangles
12th digit of the code: 0, 1, 2, 3 = toolhead 1, 2, 3, 4

entries.title: U1 toolhead not heating or heating slowly (nozzle temperature anomaly)
entries.summary: If a U1 toolhead shows a nozzle temperature anomaly along with no heating or slow heating, inspect the ceramic heater terminals and wires, re-apply thermal grease to the heater and thermistor seats (skip if it does not heat at all), and measure the heater: 10.5-13 Ohm is normal, anything else means replace the ceramic heater.
symptoms: Nozzle temperature anomaly message
Toolhead does not heat or heats slowly
causes: Ceramic heater terminal not fully inserted
Damaged or broken heater wires
Dried out or missing thermal grease (slow heating)
Failed ceramic heater
steps: Check the ceramic heater connector is fully seated and the wires are intact
For slow heating, re-apply thermal grease evenly to the thermistor probe and ceramic heater seats (per the heater and thermistor replacement guide)
Measure heater resistance with a multimeter: 10.5-13 Ohm is normal
Out of range: replace the ceramic heater
facts: U1 ceramic heater reference resistance: 10.5-13 Ohm

entries.title: U1 toolhead PCB cable map (motor, filament detection, calibration sensor, fan, heater, thermistor)
entries.summary: The U1 toolhead PCB takes six cables, useful to know when reseating connectors or checking for a damaged lead: extruder motor (4 wires), filament detection (3 wires), calibration sensor (2 black wires, called the inductive coil cable in one table), hotend fan (4 wires), ceramic heater (2 white) and thermistor (2 white). The PCB is held by one M2x6 (H1.5) and one ST2.6x6 (H2.0) screw.
facts: 1 Motor cable: 4 wires green, black, blue, red
2 Filament detection cable: 3 wires red, yellow, black
3 Calibration sensor cable (also labelled inductive coil cable): 2 black wires
4 Fan cable: 4 wires red, black, blue, yellow
5 Ceramic heater cable: 2 white wires
6 Thermistor cable: 2 white wires
On the hotend, the ceramic heater plugs into the left port and the thermistor into the right port
PCB screws: M2x6 (H1.5 hex key) and ST2.6x6 (H2.0 hex key)

entries.title: Removing and reinstalling a U1 toolhead on the docking bracket
entries.summary: Many U1 repairs start by taking a toolhead off its docking bracket. Unload its filament, power off, slide the toolhead until the locating pin shows, unclip and pull the filament tube, then remove the two USB screws and unplug. On reinstall, set the slider first (No.1 far left, No.2/3/4 far right, red mark visible) and seat the toolhead on both locating pins before fastening USB.
steps: Touchscreen: Unload Mode, select the toolhead and tap Unload; wait for it to finish
Power off and unplug the printer
Slide toolhead No.1 rightward (No.2/3/4 leftward) until you can see the whole locating pin
Unclip the three cable clips, then push the quick-release collar and withdraw the tube together with the filament
Remove the two USB screws with an H2.0 hex key, unplug the USB cable and lift the toolhead off
To reinstall: use a hex key to set the slider (No.1 far left, No.2/3/4 far right) with its red mark showing
Slide the toolhead hole onto the long locating pin until it stops, illustrated side facing inward, and engage the two locating pins (hole left of the pins for No.1, right of the pins for No.2/3/4)
Plug in USB and tighten its two screws, then insert filament while pressing the release and reconnect the filament tube

sources.title: U1 active extruder gear assembly replacement guide

entries.title: U1 toolhead temperature reading abnormal: over 310 C, high at idle, or below -10 C
entries.summary: A U1 toolhead reading abnormally high at idle or exceeding the 310 C maximum safe limit usually means the thermistor insulation is damaged and its copper wire is shorting to metal. Pull the probe out of the heater block, separate its wires and reboot; if the reading normalizes, insulate the bare spot as a stopgap and replace the thermistor. A reading below -10 C points to a loose thermistor terminal or broken wire.
symptoms: Abnormally high toolhead temperature while idle
Toolhead exceeds max safe limit (310 C)
Toolhead below minimum safe temperature (-10 C)
causes: Damaged thermistor insulation letting copper wire touch metal parts (overtemperature)
Thermistor terminal not fully inserted, or damaged or broken thermistor wires (undertemperature)
steps: Overtemperature: remove the thermistor probe from the heater block, separate its two wires, restart and see if the reading returns to normal
If it does, slide the brown insulation sleeve over the bare copper or wrap it with a little insulating tape as a temporary fix
Replace the thermistor for a permanent fix
Undertemperature: check the thermistor connector is fully inserted and the wires are not damaged or broken
facts: Toolhead max safe limit 310 C; minimum safe reading -10 C

entries.title: Adjusting U1 XY timing belt tension
entries.summary: Check the U1 XY belt tension monthly. The U1 tensions its XY belts automatically: loosen the designated screws with an H2.0 hex key and tighten them again, and the mechanism sets the tension. Run Vibration Compensation Calibration afterward. Because manual tensioning varies, the homing guide suggests repeating the adjustment several times.
steps: Loosen the designated XY belt tension screws with an H2.0 hex key
Let the automatic tensioner take up the slack, then retighten the screws
If homing or quality issues persist, repeat the loosen/retighten cycle (the homing guide suggests three extra rounds)
Run Vibration Compensation Calibration after any belt adjustment
facts: Recommended check interval: monthly

sources.title: U1 adjusting the xy-axis timing belt tension

entries.title: When to run U1 Multi-toolhead (XYZ) Offset Calibration
entries.summary: The U1 needs its XYZ (multi-toolhead) offset calibrated so colors from different toolheads line up. Run it after replacing or swapping a hotend or toolhead, after a hotend has been knocked or had a filament blob removed, or whenever colors print visibly shifted. Start it from Settings > Device Calibration > Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration > Start and follow the screen.
symptoms: Colors from different toolheads are offset from each other in multi-color prints
causes: Hotend or toolhead replaced or swapped between positions
Hotend bumped or slightly shifted
Filament lump cleared from a hotend
steps: On the touchscreen open Settings > Device Calibration
Select Multi-toolhead Offset Calibration and tap Start
Follow the on-screen instructions until the calibration finishes, then reprint the multi-color model

entries.title: Replacing and tensioning the U1 Z-axis timing belt
entries.summary: The U1 Z-axis belt runs under the machine and is tensioned by a spring-loaded swing arm. Replacement is rated difficult (4/5, about 40 minutes, H2.0 hex key); lay the printer on its back. To re-tension any time, loosen screws 3 and 4 until the swing arm moves freely, let the spring set tension, then retighten.
steps: Power off, unplug, and lay the printer on its back
Pull the bottom belt to the right to drop the bed to its lowest point
Remove the 4 screws: 1 and 2 have no washers, 3 and 4 have washers; screw 4 carries Nylok threadlocker, so do not mix it up with 3
Remove the pressure block, then carefully take out the swing arm with belt and the compression spring (the spring can jump out)
Fit the new swing arm and spring, press the arm fully down, refit the pressure block with its 2 screws
Route the belt around the 3 pulleys; turn each pulley clockwise to its stop and hold it there while routing
Push the arm against the spring and loop the belt over the motor pulley, snug screw 4 lightly, pull the belt both ways to check the bed moves smoothly, then tighten 3 and 4
Final tension: loosen 3 and 4 until the arm swings freely, let the spring tension the belt, then tighten 3 and 4
facts: Difficulty 4/5, about 40 minutes
Z belt tension is set automatically by a compression spring on the swing arm

sources.title: U1 Z-Axis timing belt replacement guide

entries.title: Calibrating U1 firmware z_offset for third-party build plates
entries.summary: With the official plate and the right bed type selected, the U1 rarely needs z_offset tuning. Third-party plates can differ in stiffness, so print a 270 x 270 x 0.2 mm single layer and read it: visible gaps mean z_offset is too small, wrinkles or waves mean too large, smooth with flaws under about 10% is correct. Default is -0.05; adjust in 0.01 steps with Heated Bed Leveling on. On the U1 a larger z_offset brings the nozzle closer.
symptoms: First layer lines sparse with gaps (z_offset too small)
First layer wrinkled or wavy (z_offset too large)
steps: Import a 270 x 270 x 0.2 mm model in Snapmaker Orca, choose Snapspeed PLA and 0.20 Standard @Snapmaker U1, enable bed leveling and print (example uses a PEI textured sheet)
Judge the layer and change z_offset by 0.01 per test; always keep Heated Bed Leveling enabled or the new value cannot be verified
Option 1: enable Advanced Mode (does not affect warranty), open Fluidd at the printer IP, edit printer.cfg, search Z_offset (around line 787), then SAVE & RESTART

Option 2: in the Orca-generated G-code (open in Fluidd, near lines 145 and 151) insert a line z_offset -0.03 below G28 Z, and a line z_offset=-0.03 below the BED_MESH_CALIBRATE PROBE_COUNT=11,11 command (space in the first, equals sign in the second), substituting your own value
Put the calibrated lines into the machine start G-code and save a user preset for that plate
If both places are set, the start G-code value wins

settings.advice: Add the calibrated z_offset lines after G28 Z and after BED_MESH_CALIBRATE, then save as a user printer preset for the third-party plate.
Pick the correct plate type before slicing; with the official plate this usually removes the need to calibrate.

facts: Default U1 firmware z_offset: -0.05
This is the firmware value (printer.cfg or start G-code), not Orca's own Z offset printer setting; do not assume the same sign convention
Start G-code z_offset overrides the printer.cfg value

entries.title: U1 automatic loading does nothing: filament feeder light stays off
entries.summary: If the U1 feeder's indicator never lights when you load filament, automatic loading may be switched off, the toolhead filament runout sensors may be disabled, or the feeder's connector may not be seated. Check them in that order; swapping the left and right feeders isolates a faulty feeder.
steps: On the touchscreen go to Settings > Print Preferences > Auto Loading, enable Automatic Loading and try again.
Find the printer IP under Settings > Wi-Fi, open it in a browser on the same network to reach Fluidd, enable the filament runout sensor for every toolhead and try again.
Power off and remove the feeder: press the release point (top for the left feeder, bottom for the right), slide it toward the front and lift it from its slots.
Push the connector fully and squarely into its socket, refit the feeder, power on and try again.
If the light still stays off, swap the left and right feeders to see whether the fault moves with the feeder.

entries.title: U1 auto loading red light: errors 0525-xxxx-0015, -0011, -0032, -0051 by loading stage
entries.summary: A red feeder light means automatic loading failed in one of three stages: pre-loading (feeder pushes filament close to, but not into, the toolhead), feeding (toolhead waits in front of the bed for its runout sensor to see filament) and extruding (toolhead near its park position; success is judged using the feeder mileage wheel together with the eddy current sensor). The last group of the code names the failure.
steps: ...-0015 (pre-loading, residual filament): if the filament status shows '?', filament is left in the toolhead; unload it with the rigid or flexible unloading procedure and load again.

...-0011 (pre-loading): lower the loading resistance: untangle the spool, use spools of 1 kg or less, clear filament stuck in the feeder (cut off chewed sections) and make sure the tube is not kinked. With a SnapDryer, mount just one dryer on the side to limit tube bending.

...-0032 (feeding): if it happens right after first assembly, see U1 filament loading anomaly; otherwise make sure the filament tube is fully inserted and cut the filament tip at about 45 degrees, then retry.
...-0051 (extruding): filament reaches the nozzle but cannot purge; troubleshoot it as a nozzle clog, then retry.
Success check: inserting filament finishes pre-loading with a white feeder light, and the toolhead extrudes normally once printing.
facts: The wiki's examples all use third group 0003; in the error table that group is the feeder number (0000-0003 = feeder 1-4), so the same fixes apply to every feeder.

The error table words 0011 as a feeder motor speed anomaly (check the feeder cable) and 0012 as an encoder wheel speed anomaly (tangle or blocked path), slightly different from this guide's advice for 0011.

entries.title: U1 axis movement anomaly 0003-0528-000X-0002 to -0006: homing or sensor calibration failed
entries.summary: These codes mean the U1 could not reach the XY or Z origin or could not calibrate its sensor. Likely causes: resistance in XY motion (belt tension, debris on the belt, a loose front cover), resistance in Z (belt tension, sticking Z pulley, soft surface under the printer) or a detection problem (dirty nozzle or PEI, fan cable or debris at the copper induction piece, faulty calibration sensor).
causes: XY belt tension wrong or debris on the XY belt
Machine front cover loose
Z belt tension wrong or Z synchronous pulley sticking
Heatsink fan cable interfering at the copper induction piece
Filament residue on the nozzle or PEI sheet
Faulty calibration sensor
steps: Re-tension the XY belt; if done once at assembly, repeat the procedure three more times.
With power off, move the toolhead through X and Y by hand and feel for sticking.
If the front cover protrudes, press it back into place.
Inspect the Z lead screws and smooth rods for debris; with power off, lift the front slightly and pull the Z belt to drive the bed up and down, feeling for binding.
Re-tension a loose Z belt (U1 Z-Axis timing belt replacement guide) and stand the printer on a flat, solid surface with no pads or cardboard underneath.
Clean filament off the nozzle tip and outer wall and off the PEI sheet.
Open the toolhead rear cover and make sure nothing, including the heatsink fan cable, sits between the copper induction piece and the hotend heatsink fins.
Run a homing test; if it still fails, film the error and export the logs for Snapmaker Support.
facts: Table hints: 0004 asks to check that axis for obvious resistance; 0006 asks to check belt tension, smooth XY travel and obstructions at the XY homing positions.

entries.title: Clearing filament that snapped inside a U1 filament tube
entries.summary: When filament breaks inside a U1 tube and cannot be pulled out, take the tube off and push the fragment out with a small plug of cotton driven by a length of rigid filament.
steps: Turn the spool backward to retract the filament.
Remove the affected tube: for the 6 mm tube press the quick-release fittings at both ends and lift it from its support; for the 4 mm tube press its two quick-release fittings.
Stuff a little cotton, for example from a cotton swab, into one end of the tube.
Push the cotton through with rigid filament (not flexible) so it drives the broken piece out of the far end.

sources.title: U1 how to clean filament breakage in the filament tube

entries.title: U1 calibration anomaly 0003-0530-000X-0000 / -0001: calibration sensor faults
entries.summary: Calibration anomalies 0003-0530-0000..0003-0000 (Toolhead 1-4 sensor possibly disconnected) and -0001 (sensor reading out of range) are checked like the axis movement anomaly: XY and Z mechanical resistance first, then the detection system: a dirty nozzle or PEI sheet, a badly fitted hotend silicone sock, the heatsink fan cable or debris at the copper induction piece, or a faulty sensor.
causes: Debris on XY belts or rails, or wrong XY belt tension
Z belt tension wrong or Z pulley sticking
Filament residue on nozzle or PEI sheet
Hotend silicone sock installed incorrectly
Heatsink fan cable interfering at the copper induction piece
Faulty calibration sensor
steps: Check the XY belts and smooth rods for foreign objects, move the toolhead by hand with power off to feel for binding, and re-tension loose XY belts (U1 XY Timing Belts Replacement Guide).
Inspect the Z lead screws and rods, pull the Z belt by hand with power off and the front raised slightly to check smooth travel, re-tension a loose Z belt, and use a flat, firm surface.
Clean the nozzle tip and outer wall and remove filament from the PEI sheet.
Check that the hotend silicone sock is fitted correctly.
Under the toolhead rear cover, clear anything between the heatsink fins and the copper induction piece, including the fan cable.
Run a homing test; if it fails again, record a video, export logs and contact Snapmaker Support.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead docking bracket and refitting the nozzle wipers
entries.summary: The toolhead docking bracket is on the U1's rear beam and holds the four nozzle wipers and the docking Hall sensor boards. Replacing it is easy (about 20 minutes, H2.0 hex key): take off the toolheads, the wipers and the 4 bracket screws, move the 4 Hall sensor cables to the new bracket, then refit everything with the toolhead sliders set correctly.
steps: Power off and unplug. Slide Toolhead 1 to the right and Toolheads 2/3/4 to the left until the locating pin is fully exposed, then rest them on the print bed.
Remove the 8 screws and the 4 nozzle wipers.
Remove the 4 bracket screws, ease the bracket outward and flip it, and unplug the 4 Hall sensor board cables while pressing their clips.
Plug the 4 cables into the new bracket and fasten it with its 4 screws.
Refit the wipers: the single left wiper serves Toolhead 1 at the far left, the other 3 go on the right side.
Set the sliders before docking: Toolhead 1 slider fully left, Toolheads 2/3/4 fully right, red mark showing (move them with a hex key).

Push each toolhead onto the long locating pin until it stops, illustrated side facing in, then engage its two pins in the mount holes (hole left of the pins for Toolhead 1, right of the pins for 2/3/4).

sources.title: U1 toolhead docking bracket replacement guide

entries.title: U1 0522 system errors: System Failed to Start, MCU disconnects, timeouts, power-off signal
entries.summary: Severity-0003 codes in module 0522 stop the print for system faults. Toolhead MCU codes (sub-module 0002-0005 = Toolheads 1-4) with issue 0006 (could not connect at start), 0008 (connection lost) or 0016 (control timed out) usually mean powering off and checking that toolhead's cable. Host or mainboard MCU faults, configuration load failures and power-off signals mostly need firmware updates or Snapmaker support.
steps: Note the full code and which MCU or toolhead it names.
For toolhead MCU codes, power off, reseat or swap that toolhead's USB-C cable and restart.
For other codes, update firmware, export logs and contact Snapmaker support.
facts: 0000, 0001, 0002: generic System Anomaly; read the details and contact support.
0003/0004: configuration failed to load at start; contact support or restore factory settings. 0005: communication protocol failed to load; update firmware or contact support.
0006: MCU connection failed at start (0000 host, 0001 mainboard, 0002-0005 Toolheads 1-4). 0003-0522-0100-0006: no toolhead detected. 0007: abnormal MCU connection.
0008: MCU connection interrupted, same mapping; for a toolhead, power off, check its cable and restart.
0009/0010: accelerometer storage or device ID fault; power cycle and contact support if it returns. 0011: motor driver anomaly.
0014: ADC sensor configuration over limit; 0015: heating module failed to heat. Both shut the system down; export logs for support.
0016: MCU control timed out ('timer too close' for toolheads); check the toolhead cable. Host and mainboard versions need support.
0017: an MCU detected a power-off signal (0000 mainboard, 0001-0004 Toolheads 1-4); see U1 false power-off signal triggered.

entries.title: U1 toolhead errors 0003-0523: nozzle temperature, thermistor/heater and extrusion limits
entries.summary: Severity-0003 toolhead codes (sub-module 0000-0003 = Toolheads 1-4) stop the print for hotend or G-code problems: extrusion below 170 C (0001), thermistor fault (0002), heater or thermistor fault (0003), a single extrusion move that is too long (0004), extrusion volume above the maximum (0005), a toolhead the printer does not recognize in the G-code (0006) and a nozzle temperature outside the allowed range (0036).
steps: 0001: the nozzle must be above 170 C before anything is extruded.
0002: power off and check the thermistor connection of the named toolhead.
0003: power off and check that toolhead's ceramic heater and thermistor connections.
0004, 0005, 0006: the G-code contains bad moves or settings; re-slice in Snapmaker Orca with the U1 profile instead of using third-party G-code.
0036: the sliced nozzle temperature is out of range; correct the filament temperature and re-slice (see the wiki article on abnormal nozzle temperature from incorrect slicing parameters).

settings.advice: Keep within the toolhead's allowed range and above 170 C to avoid 0036 and 0001.
Same limits as other layers; an out-of-range first layer value also triggers 0036.
If 0005 appears, check this has not been raised above the U1 preset; excessive flow in the G-code triggers the error.

entries.title: U1 0523 notices: runout -0000, printing anomaly -0038, filament info -0039, maintenance -0037
entries.summary: Several module 0523 codes pause the print for filament or upkeep reasons rather than hardware faults: runout detected on a toolhead (0000), a printing anomaly pointing to broken, tangled or clogged filament (0038), missing filament information for a toolhead (0039), a maintenance reminder after many tool swaps (0037) and a flow calibration anomaly (9000).
steps: 0000 runout: reload filament for the named toolhead and tap play to resume; if filament is actually present, see U1 false filament runout detection.
0038: check that toolhead for filament snapped in the tube, a tangled spool or a clogged nozzle, fix it and tap to resume.
0039: open the filament page, set the filament information for that toolhead and tap to resume.
0001-0523-0000-0037: clean the pogo pins on both sides and grease the toolhead's steel balls and steel pins (U1 core components maintenance guide).
0002-0523-000X-9000: flow calibration anomaly on that toolhead; contact technical support.

entries.title: U1 toolhead swap, pick and park failures 0002-0523-000X-0007 to -0035 and -0040 to -0047
entries.summary: Module 0523 warnings in the 0007-0035 and 0040-0047 range pause the print when a tool change fails. The sub-module names the toolhead being handled (0000-0003 = 1-4) and the issue code mostly tells you which docked heads to inspect for dropping or tilting. Reseat misplaced heads, clear obstructions, clean pogo pins when asked, then tap to resume.
steps: Inspect every docked toolhead and push any dropped, tilted or misplaced head fully back onto its bracket.
Remove debris from the dock and work area.
For pogo pin codes, clean the contacts on both the toolhead and the swapper.
Tap to resume; if a code repeats, follow the toolhead picking failure and pick-and-park coordinate guides or contact support.
facts: Picking failures follow the same pattern: 0024-0029 pairs, 0030-0033 triples, 0034 all heads. The table lists heads 2+4 for both 0028 and 0029 (3+4 seems missing).
0019: parking failed; 0021 and 0022: picking failed. Retry, then contact support.
0018, 0020, 0023, 0035: swap anomaly; confirm the active head is properly picked or placed and each idle head is seated, then resume.
0040/0043/0046: Toolhead N detached; 0041/0044/0047: placement anomaly. Reinstall the head in its dock and resume. 0042: return failed, probably an obstruction in the dock or work area.
0045: pogo pin contact anomaly; wipe the pogo pins on the toolhead and on the swapper with a dust-free cloth, then resume.

entries.title: U1 filament feeder error codes 0525: pre-loading, loading, extrusion and unloading faults
entries.summary: Module 0525 codes come from the U1 filament feeders, with sub-module 0000-0003 = feeder or toolhead 1-4. The issue number gives the stage: 0010-0015 pre-loading (notice), 0030-0035 loading into the toolhead (warning), 0050-0051 extrusion, 0070 unloading, 0090 manual loading. Most point to tangles, blocked or detached tubes, loose feeder cables, residual filament or a clog.
steps: Read the stage from the issue code and the feeder from the sub-module.
Untangle the spool and check tubes are seated and not kinked.
Reseat the feeder cable for motor speed codes.
Unload residual filament before loading again.
For 0051, clear the extruder gears or the nozzle clog.
Tap play to resume if a print was running; see U1 automatic loading failure for details.
facts: 0011 / 0031: feeder motor speed anomaly; make sure the feeder cable is properly connected.
0012 / 0032: encoder wheel speed anomaly; tangle or blocked path. Fix it, then reload or resume.
0013 / 0033: no filament detected in the feeder; 0003: no filament entry detected. Insert filament.
0014 / 0034: feeding timeout from a tangle or obstruction. 0035: feeding stroke overrun, the tube has probably come off the feeder.
0015 and 0008: residual filament in the toolhead; unload it first, then load again.
0004: extrusion blocked at the toolhead drive gear; clean and retry. 0005/0006: loading timed out; blocked path or detached tube.
0051: feeding failure; tangle, filament jammed in the extruder gears, or clogged nozzle.
0000, 0001, 0010, 0030, 0050, 0070, 0090: generic feeder or stage anomaly; tap the code for details, support recommended. 0002: loading anomaly; check for tangles or loose connectors.

entries.title: U1 heated bed and chamber temperature errors 0003-0526 and 0003-0527
entries.summary: 0003-0526-0000-0000 means the heated bed went over its temperature limit and 0003-0526-0000-0001 that bed heating behaved abnormally; both stop the print and need Snapmaker technical support. 0003-0527-0000-0000 reports the chamber temperature over its limit; check the chamber sensor connection first, then contact support.

entries.title: U1 homing anomaly codes 0528: homing order, belts, obstructions, homing sensor not triggered
entries.summary: Module 0528 covers homing. Warnings ask you to home in order (XY before Z), report an unavailable toolhead, or say XY homing met resistance (check belt tension, smooth XY travel and obstructions at the homing spots). Severity-0003 versions cover axis movement faults, shutdown protection, sensor activation and Z homing sensor faults (sub-module 0003).
facts: 0002-0528-0000-0000: home X and Y before Z. 0002-0528-0000-0010: home XY before this operation.
0002-0528-0000-0001: current toolhead unavailable, cannot home; restart and retry.
0002-0528-0000-0011/0012 and 0003-0528-0000-0006: check XY belt tension, free XY motion and nothing blocking the XY homing positions.
0003-0528-0000-0007/0008: system in shutdown protection, cannot home or level; restart the printer.
0003-0528-0000-0009: sensor failed to activate; retry.
0003-0528-0003-0002/0003: homing anomaly; retry. 0003-0528-0003-0004: homing sensor not triggered; clean residual filament off the nozzle (see U1 Homing Sensor Not Triggered).
0002-0528-000X-0013: toolhead detached; 0002-0528-000X-0014: toolhead placement anomaly. Reinstall the head in its dock and resume.

entries.title: U1 G-code errors 0003-0529 and slicing file notices 0001-0531
entries.summary: 0003-0529 codes mean the printer rejected a G-code command: missing or unparsable parameters, values below the minimum or above the maximum, duplicate command registration, or a line that cannot be parsed. 0001-0531 notices concern the print file: file list not retrieved, file operations while printing, unsupported M28/M29/M30, file cannot be opened, or power-loss resume failed. Slicing with Snapmaker Orca's U1 profile avoids most G-code errors.

settings.advice: If custom start G-code was edited, remove M28/M29/M30 and malformed commands that trigger 0529/0531 errors.
Same check for custom end G-code.

facts: 0529 issues: 0000 missing parameter; 0001 parameter parsing failed; 0002/0003 value below minimum / above maximum; 0004/0005 value must be greater / less than a set bound; 0006 command registered twice; 0007 mux command key error; 0008 G-code cannot be parsed; 0009 invalid parameter.

0531 issues: 0000 file list not retrieved; 0001 cannot handle slicing files while printing (wait until idle); 0002 M28, M29, M30 unsupported, remove them; 0003 file cannot be reset while it is being parsed.
0531 issues continued: 0004 file cannot be opened; 0005 resume after power outage failed; 0006 power-off data cannot be deleted during a print.

entries.title: U1 detection and calibration codes 0003-0530: homing first, obstructions, PEI sheet presence
entries.summary: Module 0530 handles calibration and detection. Apart from the calibration sensor faults (0000/0001), it reports calibrating before homing, bad parameters, failed or obstructed calibration, toolheads in the wrong dock numbers, a mismatched calibration module, and build plate checks: PEI sheet missing when printing (0010), still fitted when calibration needs it off (0011), or not seated correctly (0017).
facts: 0002: home before calibrating. 0004: toolhead not positioned properly; return it home by hand and retry.
0005: toolheads do not match their dock position numbers; put each head in its own numbered slot.
0008 (sub-module 0000 X, 0001 Y, 0002 Z): obstruction on that axis or residue on the nozzle; clean and retry.
0003, 0006, 0009, 0012: bad calibration parameters, module mismatch, system anomaly or bed detection fault; contact support. 0007: probe command used axes other than X, Y, Z.
0010: place the PEI sheet and retry printing. 0011: take the PEI sheet off and retry calibration. 0017: seat the PEI sheet correctly.
0013: attach any one toolhead and retry. 0014 detached / 0016 placement anomaly: reinstall the head in its dock. 0015: clean pogo pins on toolhead and swapper.

entries.title: How to read U1 error codes: severity, module, sub-module and issue
entries.summary: U1 error codes are four groups of four digits: severity, main module, sub-module and issue. Severity 0001 is a notice, 0002 a warning that pauses the print and needs your action, 0003 a high-risk error that stops the print. The module says which system raised it, and the sub-module usually identifies the toolhead, feeder or axis involved.
steps: Search the full code on the Snapmaker wiki for a dedicated article.
If there is none, use the U1 error code reference table, or note the code and contact Snapmaker support.
facts: Severity: 0000 invalid; 0001 notice (no safety risk, sometimes needs user action); 0002 warning (medium-low risk, print paused, action required); 0003 error (high risk, print stopped, action required).
Modules: 0522 motion control/system, 0523 toolhead, 0525 filament feeder, 0526 heated bed, 0527 chamber temperature, 0528 homing, 0529 G-code, 0530 detection/calibration, 0531 slicing file.
In 0523, 0525 and 0530 codes, sub-module 0000-0003 means Toolhead or feeder 1-4.
In 0522 MCU codes (issues 0006, 0008, 0016): 0000 host MCU, 0001 mainboard MCU, 0002-0005 Toolheads 1-4. In 0522 issue 0017: 0000 mainboard, 0001-0004 Toolheads 1-4.
Wiki example: 0002-0528-0003-0013 is a homing anomaly.
The code shown may not always be the true root cause, and some checks are still being refined, so keep firmware up to date.

entries.title: U1 filament cannot be pulled out of the feeder after unloading: feeder port recovery
entries.summary: If filament stays clamped in a U1 feeder port after unloading, the swing arm gear inside the feeder has not returned to neutral. Use the recovery icon for that port under Settings > Maintenance > Filament Feeder. If it keeps happening, open the feeder and look for a protruding or missing internal clip.
steps: From the home screen go to Settings, scroll to Maintenance and choose Filament Feeder.
Tap the recovery icon next to the stuck port; when it stops spinning, pull the filament out.
If this recurs often, unplug the feeder's tube and remove the feeder from the machine.
Remove cover screws 1 and 2 and the inner screw 3 with an H2.0 key; screw 3 is the shorter one.
Press any protruding clip back into place; if a clip is missing or something else looks wrong, contact Snapmaker Support.
Refit the three screws and reinstall the feeder.

sources.title: U1 unable to pull filament from the filament feeder during unloading

entries.title: U1 severely tilted heated bed: reseat the bed plate on the Z guide blocks
entries.summary: The heated bed's metal base plate is tied to the Z lead screws through 3 guide blocks. When the blocks sit at different heights the plate is bent and the bed ends up badly tilted. Fix it by releasing the Z belt, pushing every block to its bottom stop, refitting the plate, then putting the belt back in Snapmaker's specified order so no block gets lifted again.
symptoms: Heated bed visibly tilted or uneven
causes: Height difference between the 3 guide blocks connecting the bed's metal plate to the Z lead screws, warping the plate
steps: Take the heated bed off following the Heated Bed Replacement Guide.
Remove the 6 screws with an H2.0 hex key and lift off the bed's metal plate.
Loosen the 2 screws on the Z belt tension lever arm and press the arm to slacken the Z timing belt so it comes off the Z pulley.
Press each guide block down to its lowest limit.
Refit the metal plate and tighten its screws.
Refit the timing belt on the Z pulley in the order shown in the guide, then tighten the lever arm screws.
Reinstall the heated bed.
facts: The belt order matters: done wrong, the Z pulley can turn counterclockwise and raise a guide block, recreating the height difference; the correct order tends to turn it clockwise, which only presses the blocks against their bottom stop.

entries.title: U1 X/Y layer shifting: CoreXY resistance, belt tension and toolhead coordinates
entries.summary: Horizontal layer offsets on the U1 (staircase steps, sometimes with knocking or collision noises) come from three sources: resistance in the CoreXY motion (dirty carbon rods, wrong belt tension), wrong toolhead attach/detach coordinates, or the nozzle striking the part. Clean and re-tension first, run vibration compensation, then adjust coordinates.
symptoms: One or more layers offset horizontally in X and/or Y
Visible staircase steps on an otherwise intact print
Knocking, collision or sharp noises from the toolhead while moving
causes: Debris on the carbon rods
XY belt too loose (slips) or too tight (extra load, missed steps)
Incorrect toolhead attach/detach coordinates
Nozzle colliding with the model
steps: Note your current print settings and consider enabling timelapse to document the shift.
With power off, wipe the carbon rods with a cloth and alcohol. Never lubricate the X-axis carbon rods.
Press the middle of each XY belt (upper and lower) and judge the rebound; re-tension if loose.
To re-tension: loosen the 2 screws at the back of the toolhead swapper, move the swapper by hand around the path shown in the guide for two full loops (some resistance is normal), then retighten.
Run Settings > Device Calibration > Vibration Compensation > Start.
With firmware V0.9.4 or later, run Settings > Maintenance > Toolhead Attach/Detach Coordinate Adjustment and follow the prompts.
If shifts continue, check for nozzle collisions (see the nozzle collision entry).
After fixing, reprint the same model and raise speed back gradually, about 10% at a time, to find a stable limit.

entries.title: U1 layer shift from the nozzle hitting the print: warping, nozzle residue, Z-hop, supports
entries.summary: If the U1 nozzle strikes the print, the motors can skip and shift layers. Usually the part has curled above its planned height (overhang curl or lifted edges), which Snapmaker calls the most common cause, or filament stuck to the nozzle changes its shape. Fix adhesion and overhang support, keep the nozzle clean, and in Snapmaker Orca enable Z-hop, slow down and add supports.
causes: Overhangs curling up from lack of support
Model edges lifting from poor bed adhesion
Filament residue on the nozzle catching the surface
steps: Overhang curl: add supports, especially for overhangs steeper than about 45 degrees, or reorient the model to shorten unsupported spans.
Edge lifting: clean the PEI sheet, apply a thin, even coat of 3D printing glue if needed, and raise the bed temperature slightly within the filament's range.
Remove nozzle residue with the supplied wire brush; pre-dry sticky or stringy filaments.
Enable the wipe (prime) tower to cut down filament dragging on the nozzle.
In Snapmaker Orca, click Edit beside the printer, select the extruder and enable Z-hop so the nozzle lifts over the part during travel.
Lower print speed to soften impacts and give each layer time to cool.

settings.advice: Use a non-zero lift so travel moves clear the printed surface.
Turn on for overhangs steeper than about 45 degrees to stop curling into the nozzle path.
Enable to reduce filament dragging on the nozzle.
If edges lift, raise slightly within the filament's recommended range (use the field for the plate in use).
Same as above when a smooth or high-temperature plate profile is selected.
Reduce to lower impact force and give layers more cooling time.
Reduce together with outer wall speed when collisions shift layers.

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0522-0001-0016: mainboard MCU control timeout
entries.summary: This system anomaly shuts the U1 down for protection when the mainboard MCU does not respond in time. Newer firmware contains fixes for it, so update first. If it happens again, export the printer logs and the G-code file that was printing (downloadable from Fluidd) and send both to Snapmaker Support.
steps: Update the U1 to the latest firmware and try the print again.
If it recurs, export the log files (U1 how to export log files).
Find the printer IP under Settings > Wi-Fi and open it in a web browser to reach Fluidd.
On Fluidd's home page scroll to Jobs, right-click the G-code that was running and choose Download.
Send the logs and G-code to Snapmaker Support.

sources.title: U1 error 0003-0522-0001-0016: mainboard MCU control timeout

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead male mount (left type for Toolhead 1, right type for 2/3/4)
entries.summary: The male mount is the toolhead's front cover. The left version fits Toolhead 1 and the right version fits Toolheads 2/3/4. Replacing it (about 20 minutes, H1.5 and H2.0 keys) means removing the toolhead, freeing the PCB, extruder unit, hotend and hotend cooling assembly from the old mount and fastening them to the new one.
steps: Unload the toolhead: tap the filament area on the touchscreen > Unload Mode > select the toolhead > Unload, and wait for it to finish.
Power off and unplug; slide the toolhead off its pin (Toolhead 1 to the right, 2/3/4 to the left).
Remove the 3 cable clips, press the quick-release fitting to pull out filament and tube, remove the 2 USB screws (H2.0), unplug the cable and lift the toolhead off.
Remove the top cover (3 screws) and the back cover.
Undo PCB screws 1 (H1.5) and 2 (H2.0) and raise the board so its centre hole sits over the runout sensor.
Undo the extruder unit screws (1-2 with H1.5, 3-4 with H2.0) and the 2 hotend screws (H2.0); move the hotend aside, undo the 3 hotend cooling assembly screws (H1.5) and take off the old mount.
Fit the new mount and tighten in order: cooling assembly, hotend, extruder unit, PCB; refit both covers.

Set the slider (Toolhead 1 fully left, 2/3/4 fully right, red mark visible), dock the toolhead, screw the USB cable back on, then press the release, push filament in to the end and reconnect the tube.

sources.title: U1 toolhead male mount replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 nozzle cleaning brush and nozzle parking pad
entries.summary: Each U1 nozzle wiper, located right under a docked toolhead's nozzle, carries a silicone cleaning brush that wipes the nozzle and a parking pad that stops an idle toolhead from leaking filament. Replace either one when it looks worn; the job takes about 5 minutes.
steps: Power off and unplug the U1.
Remove the toolhead above the wiper being serviced.
Peel off the old brush, clean the holder surface, and press the new self-adhesive brush on firmly.
Pull the old parking pad outward to unclip it, push the new pad into the holder and check it is held securely.

sources.title: U1 nozzle cleaning brushes & parking pads kit replacement guide

entries.title: Calibrating U1 toolhead pick and park X/Y coordinates (Fluidd, extruder_config.json)
entries.summary: After homing, the U1 moves the swapper to each toolhead's stored X/Y position, slides sideways so the pull pin engages the pull bolt, then moves outward with the head; parking runs this in reverse. X is calibrated from the screen (homing calibration under Settings > Maintenance). Y is calibrated afterwards in Fluidd by jogging until the toolhead's side pin lines up with the dock slot, then saved in extruder_config.json.
steps: Enable Advanced Mode (using it only for XY calibration does not affect warranty) and connect the computer to the printer's Wi-Fi network.
Calibrate X first with the on-screen homing calibration under Settings > Maintenance.
Open the printer's IP in a browser to reach Fluidd and click Dashboard > Extruder > Home XY.
Pick the problem head with macro T0, T1, T2 or T3 (Toolheads 1-4; T1 picks Toolhead 2).
Jog Y with the lower-left movement controls (e.g. step 1; the up arrow moves swapper and head back 1 mm) until the side pin is centred on the dock slot, and read the Y value shown.
Verify in the console: G91 then G1 X-8.5 F3600 for Toolhead 1, or G1 X8.5 F3600 for Toolheads 2-4; the side pin should slide smoothly into the slot.
Enter the value for that toolhead in extruder_config.json, save and restart the firmware.
If the toolhead falls off, the Y value is too small (too much clearance to lock); increase it. After a collision, restart and redo the calibration carefully.

sources.title: U1 How to adjust the pick & park coordinates

entries.title: Cleaning U1 toolhead pogo pins with alcohol
entries.summary: Dirty pogo pins cause toolhead picking failures and pogo pin contact anomalies. Clean them with a dust-free cloth only slightly damp with alcohol, wiping in a single direction, and let them dry before resuming the print.
steps: Put about 1-2 drops of alcohol on a dust-free cloth so it is damp but not dripping; excess can seep into the pin housing and affect the springs.
Wrap the cloth around the pin tips and wipe one way only, for example base to tip, not back and forth, so no lint is left behind.
For heavy dirt, press gently so the spring-loaded pins retract and contact the cloth better.
Let the alcohol evaporate for 10-20 seconds, or pat dry with a clean dry cloth.
Resume the print and check that the error has cleared.

entries.title: Calibrating pressure advance for the U1 in Snapmaker Orca (PA Line and PA Tower)
entries.summary: Snapmaker Orca's Calibration > Pressure Advance prints test patterns so you can choose the PA value that keeps extrusion even while the nozzle speeds up and slows down. The U1 has a direct drive extruder (DDE). In PA Line mode pick the line whose width stays constant; in PA Tower mode measure the height with the sharpest corners and multiply by 0.002.
steps: In Prepare, select the exact filament you will print with in the Filament section.
Open Calibration > Pressure Advance, choose DDE and PA Line mode (PA Tower or V-shaped also work), keep the preset start, end and step values or set your own, and click OK.
Click ... > Edit beside the filament and tick Enable pressure advance under Filament > Flow ratio and Pressure Advance.
Slice; Preview > Speed shows each test line speeding up and then slowing down, each with its own PA value.
Print on the U1. For PA Line, choose the line that is the same width from end to end and read the value printed beside it.
For PA Tower, find the height where the 5 corners look sharpest, measure it from the base in mm and multiply by 0.002.
Enter the result in the filament's Pressure Advance field and save the profile.

settings.advice: Turn on in the filament profile before running the test and for normal printing.
Set to the value found with PA Line or PA Tower for that specific filament.

facts: PA too low: line thin at acceleration and thick at deceleration. PA too high: thick at acceleration and thin at deceleration.
PA Tower formula given by Snapmaker: PA = 0.002 x measured height in mm; 8 mm gives 0.016.
Snapmaker Orca's default start, end and step values for PA Line can be used directly.

entries.title: Reducing U1 Z-axis acceleration to 200 mm/s² in printer.cfg via Fluidd
entries.summary: Snapmaker suggests lowering the U1's Z acceleration from 500 to 200 mm/s² to quieten Z thumps; the step loss guide also recommends a lower Z acceleration to ease the motor's load. It needs Advanced Mode and two edits to printer.cfg in Fluidd.
steps: On the touchscreen enable Settings > Maintenance > Advanced Mode.
Read the IP under Settings > Wi-Fi and open it in a computer browser to reach Fluidd.
Click Configuration and open printer.cfg.
Use Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on Mac) to find max_z_accel: 500 and replace the value so it reads max_z_accel: 200.
Find SET_MAX_Z_ACCEL A=500 and edit it to read SET_MAX_Z_ACCEL A=200.
Click SAVE & RESTART at the top right.

sources.title: U1 z-axis noise (thumping sound) explanation and temporary solutions

entries.title: U1 screen black or abnormal at power-on: switch, PSU, AC board and FFC cable checks
entries.summary: If the U1 display is black or wrong from the moment it powers on, narrow the fault with three indicator lights: the power switch, the motherboard LED and the power supply LED. Depending on which are lit, the problem is AC input or the switch, a loose or shorted AC board cable, a failed power supply, or the screen path (FFC cable, motherboard connector, touchscreen).
steps: Check whether the power switch is lit; if not, suspect the AC input, AC power cable or switch and contact support.
If lit, remove the right side panel and check whether the motherboard LED blinks; if it blinks, go straight to the screen path checks.
If it does not blink, remove the power supply cover. PSU LED on: power off and reseat the AC board-to-motherboard power cable; if still dead, that cable or the motherboard is likely faulty.

PSU LED off: power off, tighten the AC board screws and reseat its two cables. If still off, unplug both AC board cables and power on: LED now on means one of those cables is shorted; LED still off means the power supply has failed.
Screen path: power off, pull off the touchscreen rear cover (no tools) and remove the right side panel.
Inspect the FFC cable for creases, breaks or a loose fit; replace it if damaged, otherwise reseat it straight and firmly and restart.
Inspect the metal contacts of the screen connector on the motherboard for oxidation, bending or breaks; replace the motherboard if damaged.
Otherwise replace the touchscreen; if a new screen does not fix it, contact Snapmaker Support.

entries.title: U1 visible seam marks: seam position, seam gap and wipe settings in Snapmaker Orca
entries.summary: Each layer outside vase mode has a start and end point, so some seam on U1 prints is unavoidable; it hides well on sharp or concave corners and shows most on smooth curves such as cylinders. Snapmaker attributes prominent seams to three things: retraction settings, an uncalibrated pressure advance value, and the seam settings themselves (position, gap, wipe speed, seam painting).
symptoms: Vertical line, dots, bulge or small divot where every layer begins and ends
Seam very obvious on cylinders and other smooth curved walls
causes: Retraction length, speed or Z-hop not matched to the filament
Pressure advance not calibrated for the filament
Seam position or seam gap poorly suited to the model
steps: Tune retraction: in Prepare, click ... > Edit beside the filament, open Setting Overrides and adjust retraction length, retraction speed, Z-hop height and Z-hop type.
Calibrate pressure advance with Calibration > Pressure Advance and enter the result under Filament > Flow ratio and Pressure Advance.
