Choose a seam position under Process > Quality > Seam. Aligned, Aligned Back or Back usually look best; Random spreads the weak spot for stronger parts; Nearest minimizes travel.
Back puts the seam at the rearmost (min Y) point of each layer; Aligned Back keeps it off the front while still looking for hidden corners, handy for figurines with a clear front view.
Set seam gap to roughly 0-15% of the nozzle size on a well-tuned printer: a bigger gap reduces bulging, a smaller gap makes the seam less visible.
Enable Role base wipe speed so the wipe runs at the speed of the feature just printed; if disabled, set wipe speed as an absolute value or a percentage of travel speed.
If automatic placement is still poor, use Seam Painting to put the seam on a hidden edge.

settings.advice: Aligned, Aligned Back or Back for looks; Random when strength matters because the weak point is distributed.
Keep around 0-15% of nozzle size; increase if the seam bulges, decrease if a visible gap appears.
Turn on so wiping matches the print speed of the feature.
Only used when role-based wipe speed is off; absolute speed or percentage of travel speed.
Set from a PA calibration print; a value that is too low leaves extra material where the nozzle slows down, such as at the seam.
Adjust in the filament's Setting Overrides if blobs or gaps form at the seam.

entries.title: U1 spool claw came off the filament holder: reset or replace
entries.summary: The spool claw on a U1 filament holder can pop out if the holder is fitted or removed the wrong way, or if the holder falls after being pulled. When the internal spring clip is still in place the claw can be clipped back by hand; if the spring clip has shifted or come out, or the claw is damaged, Snapmaker support replaces the filament holder.
symptoms: Spool claw assembly detached while installing or removing the filament holder
Claw loose or crooked after the filament holder dropped
causes: Filament holder removed improperly
External pulling or wrong installation making the holder lose its support and fall
steps: Look at the spring clip inside the filament holder first.
If the clip is seated: tilt the claw slightly, line both clip ends up with their slots, then press firmly until the white locating clips on each side snap fully in.
Squeeze and release the claw several times; it should move smoothly and spring back without sticking.
If the clip is displaced or detached, or the claw is damaged, open a support ticket with photos or video and what you already tried; a replacement holder will be arranged.
Refit the holder (U1 Quick Start Guide, chapter 5) and run automatic loading to check filament feeds smoothly into the tube.
To avoid a repeat, remove the holder as described in U1 How To Remove The Filament Holder.

entries.title: U1 stringing or oozing: wet filament, worn nozzle, temperature, travel speed, retraction
entries.summary: Stringing (fine strands left along travel moves) and oozing (uncontrolled leaking from the nozzle) on the U1 have five causes in Snapmaker's guide, checked in this order: moisture in the filament, a worn nozzle, a nozzle temperature that is too high, travel that is too slow, and retraction settings.
symptoms: Thin strings between parts or features along travel paths
Blobs or small bumps from filament leaking out
Rougher surface and worse dimensional accuracy in bad cases
causes: Filament has absorbed moisture
Worn nozzle
Print temperature too high for the filament
Travel speed too low
Retraction length, speed or Z-hop not suited to the filament
steps: Dry the filament, for example in the Snapmaker SnapDryer at its recommended settings, and keep opened spools sealed with desiccant such as silica gel.
Replace a worn nozzle following U1 Hot End replacement and configuration.
Print a temperature tower (Calibration > Temperature) and note the temperature of the cleanest block.
Enter that value for both First layer and Other layers under Filament > Print temperature > Nozzle.
Raise travel speed moderately under Process > Speed > Travel speed.
Adjust retraction length, retraction speed, Z-hop height and Z-hop type in the filament's Setting Overrides.

settings.advice: Lower toward the best temperature tower result if strings persist.
Set to the same calibrated temperature, as the guide does for both fields.
Increase moderately so the nozzle spends less time oozing over open gaps.
Tune in the filament's Setting Overrides; adequate retraction limits leaking during travel.
Tune together with retraction length in the filament overrides.
Part of the retraction tuning the guide recommends; adjust height in the filament overrides.

entries.title: U1 toolhead cannot be picked or parked during first setup after unboxing
entries.summary: If a freshly assembled U1 fails to pick up or park a toolhead during its first calibration or print, check in order: a left or right inner panel pushed out while fitting the filament holder, a latch still showing its red mark, XY belt tension, and finally the pick-and-park coordinates using the on-screen adjustment (firmware 0.9.4 or newer).
causes: Inner panel popped out by excess force when installing the filament holder, blocking the toolhead's return
Latch set wrong when docking (red mark should show before docking and be hidden afterwards)
XY timing belt not tensioned correctly
Wrong pick-and-park coordinates
steps: Check for a popped left or right inner panel and refit it firmly.
With all four toolheads docked, confirm no red latch indicator is visible.
Re-tension the XY belt; if you already did it once at assembly, repeat the procedure three more times, since manual tensioning varies.
Update firmware to 0.9.4 or later and run Maintenance > Toolhead Attach/Detach Coordinate Adjustment for the affected toolhead.
If correcting X does not help, calibrate the Y coordinate too (see the pick and park coordinates guide).
For remote help, run Snapmaker's pick-and-park test G-code (it picks Toolheads 1-4 repeatedly, homing after each, for 100 cycles by default), film it from above, and stop once every pick is recorded.

sources.title: U1 toolhead swapping anomaly during first-time setup after unboxing

entries.title: U1 tangled filament spool: spool will not turn or filament pulled tight
entries.summary: A tangle shows as a spool that cannot rotate, filament stuck or under tension, or coils visibly crossing each other. It usually starts when coils loosen after the spool is dropped, squeezed or moved, or when a loose end springs under other coils during unloading. Unload, free the trapped strand, rewind neatly, then reload and resume.
symptoms: Spool blocked from turning
Filament stuck or drawn tight
Coils crossing over one another
causes: Coils shifted after the spool was moved, dropped or squeezed
Free end not held during unloading or filament change, slipping under or across other coils
steps: If printing, tap Pause and return to the home screen.
Unload the filament with automatic unloading and take the spool off.
Find where an outer strand runs beneath an inner coil and pull it back out the same way it went in; repeat until the spool is free.
Rewind the filament onto the spool one coil at a time.
Feed it back into the feeder and tap Resume Print.
Prevention: hold the free end while rewinding and lock it in the spool's hole; avoid dropping, squeezing or shaking spools, and straighten loose outer coils before use.

entries.title: U1 error 0003-0522-000X-0012 'Tap Home first' before moving X, Y or Z: wrong printer profile
entries.summary: These axis movement anomalies appear as a print starts and ask you to home before moving X (0000), Y (0001) or Z (0002). The cause is G-code sliced for a different printer, which lacks the homing command the U1 expects. Re-slice in Snapmaker Orca with Snapmaker U1 selected as the printer and send the new file.
causes: Model or project sliced with a printer other than Snapmaker U1; external model files may carry another printer preset
steps: Add the model to Snapmaker Orca again.
Under Prepare > Printer, select Snapmaker U1 from the drop-down; do this manually because imported files may be preset to another machine.
Set your parameters and slice again.
Send the new G-code to the U1 and print; contact Snapmaker Support if the error remains.

settings.advice: Must be the Snapmaker U1 profile so the generated G-code contains the U1's homing sequence.

sources.title: U1 Tap Home first, then move the X / Y / Z axis

entries.title: Finding the best nozzle temperature with a temperature tower in Snapmaker Orca (U1)
entries.summary: Calibration > Temperature in Snapmaker Orca builds a tower of identical blocks, each printed at a different temperature between your start and end values using Orca's default step. Print it on the U1, rule out the blocks with defects and use the temperature marked on the best block in the filament profile.
steps: In Prepare, pick the filament you will print with in the Filament section.
Open Calibration > Temperature, choose the filament type, and keep Orca's preset Start temp and End temp or set your own.
Click OK to generate the tower.
Print it and compare blocks; the label on the best block is the temperature to use, e.g. a block marked 200 means 200 C.
Click ... > Edit beside the filament and set Filament > Print temperature > Nozzle First layer and Other layers to that value.

settings.advice: Set to the temperature of the best tower block.
The guide sets the first layer to the same calibrated value.

entries.title: U1 'timer too close' error 0003-0522-000X-0016: toolhead cable or MCU timeout
entries.summary: 'timer too close' during a print means an MCU did not respond in time and the printer shut down for protection. Codes 0003-0522-0002/0003/0004/0005-0016 point to Toolheads 1/2/3/4; 0000 and 0001 are the host and mainboard MCUs. Check the toolhead cable screws, then swap or replace the cable to see whether the fault follows it; if it stays with the toolhead, the main MCU is suspect.
causes: Loose toolhead cable
Damaged toolhead cable
Faulty main MCU causing a communication timeout
steps: Check the two screws holding the toolhead cable and retighten them if loose.
Make sure each end has its own screw type; the two ends of the cable use different screws.
Identify the toolhead from the code: 0002 = Toolhead 1, 0003 = Toolhead 2, 0004 = Toolhead 3, 0005 = Toolhead 4.
Fit a spare USB toolhead cable, or swap cables between the failing toolhead and one that works.
If the error moves with the cable, replace that cable.
If it stays on the same toolhead even with a new cable, the main MCU is likely at fault; collect your results and contact Snapmaker Support.
facts: In the error table, 0003-0522-0000-0016 is a host MCU control timeout and 0003-0522-0001-0016 a mainboard MCU control timeout, which has its own guide.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead USB-C cable
entries.summary: Each U1 toolhead cable (USB-C) runs from the top of the toolhead to the HUB board under the machine's top panel. Swapping one is easy and takes about 5 minutes with an H2.0 hex key; the only trap is that the two cable ends use different fixing screws.
steps: Switch off the U1 and unplug the power cable.
Unclip the cable from its retaining clips.
Take out the 4 fixing screws with the H2.0 key and remove the old cable.
Plug the new cable into the HUB board and the toolhead and screw both ends down, using the correct screw type at each end.
Press the cable back into the clips.
facts: Sold as the Toolhead USB Cable 2-pack for Snapmaker U1.
Per the toolhead disconnected guide, the longer screws go at the HUB board end and the shorter ones at the toolhead end.

entries.title: U1 'Toolhead N detached' error although all toolheads are docked: Hall sensor and 16-pin cable
entries.summary: Before picking a toolhead the U1 confirms every idle head is docked. Each bracket position has a Docking Hall Sensor Board that senses a magnet in the docked toolhead; its signal goes to the HUB board and on to the main control board. If 'Toolhead 1/2/3/4 detached' appears while every head really is docked, that signal path is faulty: check the 16-pin cable, then swap Hall sensor boards.
symptoms: Toolhead Swapping Anomaly: Toolhead 1/2/3/4 detached, while the toolheads sit correctly on their brackets
causes: Bent pins or poor contact in the 16-pin cable between the HUB board and main control board
Faulty Docking Hall Sensor Board at the reported position
steps: Remove the top panel and right side panel (U1 Video Guide: How to Remove the Side Panels).
Clean leftover adhesive from the 16-pin connector, unplug the 16-pin cable and inspect it for bent pins.
Reconnect both ends, supporting the inner panel while working on the main control board end.
Plug the toolhead USB cable back into its HUB port, power on and check whether the error has cleared.
If not, swap the Hall sensor board at the failing position with another position (Docking Hall Sensor Board Replacement Guide), power on and see whether the error position moves.
Send your findings to Snapmaker Support if unresolved.
facts: Error table codes reporting 'Toolhead N detached' include 0002-0523-000X-0040/0043/0046, 0002-0528-000X-0013 and 0003-0530-000X-0014, where X = 0-3 for Toolheads 1-4.

sources.title: U1 toolhead detached error after proper installation

entries.title: U1 toolhead disassembly and reassembly order (cover, board, hotend, cooling, extruder)
entries.summary: A U1 toolhead consists of five parts: cover, male mount, extruder unit, hotend and control board. Taking it apart is moderately hard (about 40 minutes with H1.5 and H2.0 hex keys) and must follow a fixed order; reassembly reverses it with checks on gear mesh, thermistor bend, sock orientation and cable routing.
steps: Remove the 3 cover screws (H2.0) and lift off the top and rear covers.

Unplug the 6 board cables (extruder motor, filament runout sensor, calibration sensor, hotend cooling fan, ceramic heater, thermistor), remove screw 1 (H1.5) and screw 2 (H2.0) and lift out the board.
Remove the 2 hotend screws (H2.0); take off the silicone sock, the heater spring clip and the cable holder, then the ceramic heater and thermistor.
Remove the hotend cooling assembly (3 x H1.5) and then its fan (2 x H1.5).

Remove the extruder unit (4 screws, H1.5 and H2.0), then its bearing holder (4 x H2.0), the spring screw with compression spring and spring block, the runout sensor and both gear assemblies (2 x H1.5), and finally the motor and heat shield (2 x H2.0).
Reassemble in reverse. After fitting the driving and driven gear assemblies, turn the driving gear and check that all 3 gears mesh and the other two spin freely.
Seat the spring block on top of the compression spring, and mount the motor with its cable facing as shown in the guide.
Bend the thermistor probe tip 90 degrees when fitting it, and install the silicone sock with its notch on the same side as the cable holder.
Route the runout sensor cable before seating the control board, then reconnect all 6 cables and dress them.
On the top cover, screw 3 is a different size from screws 1 and 2.

sources.title: U1 toolhead disassembly and reassembly guide

entries.title: U1 toolhead disconnected / System Failed to Start 0003-0522-000X-0006 and -0008
entries.summary: If the U1 takes over 30 seconds to start, toolhead lights blink 2-3 times, the setup wizard stops at 'System Failed to Start', or bed and nozzle temperatures read '--', a toolhead has lost its connection. Codes 0003-0522-0002..0005-0006 (at startup) and -0008 (interrupted) name Toolheads 1-4. Work from the toolhead LEDs through cable, HUB port and PCB swaps.
causes: Loose toolhead USB cable
Faulty USB cable
HUB board failure
Toolhead PCB failure
Faulty cable between HUB board and mainboard
Mainboard failure
steps: Look through each toolhead's top cover: a connected head shows a white LED. Note any that are dark.
For a dark head, check the USB cable is firmly attached at both the toolhead PCB and the HUB board.
Check screw types: long screws at the HUB end, short at the toolhead end; a long screw at the toolhead end can cause poor contact.
If all four LEDs are off, one bad head may be the cause: power off, unplug one head's USB, power on, wait about 2 minutes and see if the others light; repeat head by head.
Reinsert the problem head's USB-C cable rotated 180 degrees.
Swap its cable with a working head's cable; if the fault follows the cable, replace the cable.
If not, plug it into another head's HUB port; if it now works, the original HUB port is bad and the HUB board should be replaced.
Swap toolhead PCBs to check for a faulty PCB.
If nothing isolates it, suspect the HUB-to-mainboard cable or the mainboard and contact support with your results.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 toolhead PCB (pogo pins rated 250,000 swaps) with cable color map
entries.summary: The toolhead PCB lives inside the toolhead housing and includes the pogo pins, each set rated for 250,000 swaps. Replace it when the board fails or the pogo pins are worn. The job is easy (about 15 minutes, H1.5 and H2.0 keys): remove the toolhead, open the covers, move six cables to the new board and reassemble.
steps: Unload the toolhead from the touchscreen (Unload Mode), then power off and unplug.
Slide the toolhead off its dock pin, release the filament tube, remove the 2 USB screws, unplug and lift the toolhead off.
Remove the top cover (3 x H2.0) and the back cover.
Unplug the 6 cables and remove the M2x6 screw (H1.5) and the ST2.6x6 screw (H2.0) to free the board.
Fit the new board, tighten both screws, reconnect each cable to its numbered socket and tidy the wiring.
Refit the covers, set the slider, dock the toolhead, screw the USB cable back on and reload filament.
Verify: the PCB indicator lights at power-on, the toolhead is recognized, and heating and printing work.
facts: Cable 1 motor: 4 wires orange, black, blue, red. Cable 2 filament detection: 3 wires red, yellow, black.
Cable 3 calibration sensor: 2 black wires. Cable 4 fan: 4 wires red, black, blue, yellow.
Cable 5 ceramic heater: 2 white wires. Cable 6 thermistor: 2 white wires.

entries.title: U1 toolhead picking failure 0002-0523-000X-0021 to -0035 (Toolheads 2, 3 and 4)
entries.summary: A picking failure stops the print when the U1 cannot attach a toolhead. Snapmaker gives four causes: a homing failure (debris at the homing contact points or a lifted inner panel), toolheads in the wrong slot or not latched, dirty pogo pin contacts, and pogo pins that do not touch properly or are badly worn. The same checklist covers Toolheads 2, 3 and 4 (sub-module 0001, 0002, 0003).
causes: Homing failure from filament or debris at the homing contact points
Inner panel lifted, blocking X homing
Toolhead placed in the wrong dock or not latched
Dirty pogo pin contacts
Pogo pins not contacting properly or badly worn
steps: Homing order is Y, then X, then Z. Clean where the Y-axis slider meets the front pillar and where the toolhead swapper cover meets the Y-axis slider; stuck filament there causes errors.
Check whether an inner panel has been lifted, for example by force when fitting the filament holder.
Make sure each head is in its own numbered dock (e.g. Toolhead 3 not in slot 4) and the slider's red mark is hidden after docking.
Before tapping Got it, wipe the pogo pin contacts using alcohol on a dust-free cloth so no dust or grease remains.
If the job will not resume or a head keeps failing to park, power off, return the head to its dock by hand, power on and retry.
Test for housing interference with white paper: it should not slide between the solid pins of the head on the carbon rods and the pogo pins of the other head; if it does, adjust the cover screws.
Press each pogo pin with a cloth or glove; it should spring straight back.
Inspect the solid pins on the carbon tube side and replace the part if clearly worn.
facts: The cached Toolhead 3 page repeats Toolhead 2's codes (0002-0523-0001-xxxx) in its table although its title gives 0002-0523-0002-0021/0022/0023; per the error table, Toolhead 3 uses sub-module 0002.

entries.title: Replacing a complete U1 toolhead (Toolhead 1 vs Toolheads 2/3/4)
entries.summary: U1 toolheads are numbered 1-4 from left to right on the docking bracket, and Toolhead 1 is a different part from Toolheads 2/3/4. A full toolhead swap takes about 8 minutes with an H2.0 hex key: unload, let the nozzle cool below 40 C, release the old head, set the new head's latch, dock it and reconnect cable and tube.
steps: Tap the filament info area on the home page > Unload mode > choose the toolhead > Unload, then tap OK when finished.
Watch the nozzle temperature (upper-left of the home page) and wait until it is below 40 C.
Power off and unplug; press the quick connector and pull out the filament tube.
Remove the 2 cable screws (H2.0) and unplug the toolhead cable.
Push the H2.0 key into the middle hole between the 2 locating pins until it clicks, then lift the toolhead off.
On the new head, turn the latch with the H2.0 key until two red marks show: Toolhead 1 latch at its left limit, Toolheads 2/3/4 at their right limit.
Line the latch hole up with the swapper's locating pin, push in to the stop, and shift the head slightly so its 2 side pins drop into the bracket holes.
Reconnect and screw down the cable, then insert the filament tube.
facts: Other U1 guides release a docked toolhead by sliding it sideways (Toolhead 1 right, 2/3/4 left) until the locating pin shows; this guide uses the hex-key click release instead.

entries.title: U1 touchscreen freezes, goes black or displays garbage during use
entries.summary: When the U1 touchscreen stops responding, blacks out or shows a corrupted image after running for a while, start with a forced restart and a screen-saver change, then rule out static (cut out the ESD tube) and a loose power connection before inspecting the FFC cable, motherboard connector and the screen itself.
symptoms: Touch stops working or the screen goes black during use
Image corrupted while touch still works, sometimes right after waking from the screen saver
causes: Electrostatic interference or a frozen UI
Loose power connection
Loose or damaged touchscreen FFC cable, damaged motherboard connector or faulty touchscreen
steps: Press and hold the top centre of the screen for about 5 seconds to force-restart the touchscreen.

Unresponsive or black: turn on the screen saver in Settings. If it recurs, remove the right side panel and snip out the marked ESD tube with diagonal cutters so the upper and lower solder joints are no longer bridged; scrape away any leftover piece.
Display wrong after waking from the screen saver: turn the screen saver off first.
Display wrong at other times: force-restart and turn the screen saver on.
If still faulty, power off, check the power connection and restart.
If it persists, inspect the FFC cable, the motherboard screen connector and the touchscreen (see the power-on screen entry).
facts: Do not plug or unplug cables while powered unless told to; avoid deep disassembly on machines still under warranty.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 3.5-inch touchscreen
entries.summary: The U1 touchscreen sits between the front panel and a black rear cover that pulls off by hand. Swapping it takes about 5 minutes and no tools beyond a hair dryer to soften the adhesive.
steps: Power off and unplug the printer.
Pull the black touchscreen rear cover off by hand.
Unplug the FFC cable, warm the screen edges gently with a hair dryer and pry the screen out from its edges.
Clean any leftover adhesive off the mounting surface.
Peel the backing off the new screen, pass its FFC connector through the window in the frame first, and stick the screen to the front panel in the correct orientation.
Reconnect the FFC cable, stick it to the metal frame with its adhesive patch, and refit the rear cover.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 X carbon rod assembly (very difficult, about 180 minutes)
entries.summary: The X carbon rod carries the toolhead swapper and is the hardest U1 repair (5/5, about 180 minutes). You unload and remove spools and feeders, strip the casing including the front panel, dismantle the swapper and free the XY belts, swap the rod, then re-route the belts and rebuild. Tools: H1.5 and H2.0 keys, tweezers or flat screwdriver, strong needle-nose pliers, fine or copper wire, zip ties.
steps: Unload all toolheads (Unload Mode, select all), wind back the filament and remove the 4 spools with their holders.
Power off; release the 4 mm tubes at the rear and take out both feeders, unplugging their cables.
Unscrew and unplug the 4 USB cables (8 screws), remove the top cover screws under the silicone plugs, and remove both plastic side panels (8 screws each, unplugging 2 RFID cables per side).
Remove the screen rear cover and FFC cable, then the 10 front panel screws and 2 glass door hinge screws to take off the front panel.
Dismantle the swapper: part cooling duct and shroud, fan, fan adapter board, swapper base, then the 8 screws joining X-axis slider-1 and slider-2 (keep the 4 anti-backlash springs).
Remove the end tensioning movable blocks (2 screws with lock nuts) and their torsion springs, and push out the belt fixing block to free the belt ends.
Free both ends of the upper and lower belts without pulling them out of the frame.

Remove the 8 side frame screws through the access holes; the rod's clamp plates will drop. Fit the new rod with its arrow end toward the front, square to the Y axis, and with the front Y slider aligned to its linear bearing.
Hold the clamp plates up with wire threaded through the frame holes, tighten the 2 lower screws per side, remove the wire, then tighten the 2 upper screws.
Re-route the belts (U1 XY Belt Path Guide), rebuild the swapper, refit casing, feeders and spools, then load all toolheads via Load Mode, setting type and color for unrecognized filament.

sources.title: U1 X carbon rod assembly replacement guide

entries.title: U1 XY timing belt routing: upper and lower belt path
entries.summary: The U1 has two open-ended XY belts, upper and lower, each anchored at both ends inside the printhead adapter and wrapped around 6 idler pulleys and one motor pulley. Re-routing needs the side, front and rear panels and the toolhead docking bracket removed. Keep the belt from twisting: smooth side on idler 1, toothed side on the motor pulley.
steps: Stand at the front of the printer and centre the X axis.
Run the belt around idler 1 with its smooth side against the pulley, then around idler 2 and through or around idler 3.
Wrap it around the motor pulley with the teeth against the pulley.
Continue around idler 4, through the Y-axis slider, then around idlers 5 and 6.
For the lower belt, turning the machine upside down helps with idler 3, the motor pulley and idler 4; set it upright again after idler 4.
Check by pulling the belt left and right: it should run smoothly and turn the motor pulley in step.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 XY timing belts (2GT-6RF, at least 175 cm each)
entries.summary: U1 XY motion uses an upper and a lower 2GT-6RF belt; each replacement must be at least 175 cm long. The job is difficult (about 120 minutes). Snapmaker's method glues each new belt to the cut end of the old one and pulls it through the path, then rebuilds the swapper's tensioning blocks and torsion springs.
steps: Tap Detach Toolhead for the attached head, power off and unplug, and move the swapper to the centre.

Cut both belts at the marked line but do not pull them out. Glue a new belt to one old end with teeth facing the same way, let it dry, pull the other old end until the new belt comes through, then cut off the joint. Repeat for the second belt.
Dismantle the swapper: cooling duct and shroud, part cooling fan, adapter board, swapper base, then the 8 screws joining X-axis slider-1 and slider-2 (keep the 4 anti-backlash springs).
Remove the 2 end tensioning movable blocks (screws with lock nuts) and torsion springs, and push out the belt fixing block to free the old ends.
Press the upper belt's left end and the lower belt's right end into the tensioning blocks, teeth meshed and nothing sticking out; zip-tie the other two ends to the carbon rod.
With the machine front-down, mount the blocks at the left and right limits of slider-2 and tighten their screws and lock nuts.

Release each zip-tied end, thread it through, pull it straight and tight while holding slider-2 still, and press the fixing block (groove up) flush with slider-2's inner face; tug both belts to check, then trim the excess.
Refit the torsion springs: long arm into the block's middle hole, short end twisted into its groove with strong pliers, using two partly driven screws in the post to stop the spring popping out.
Place the 4 anti-backlash springs, slide the oil-free bearing into slider-2, cover with slider-1 and tighten the 8 screws.
Loosen the 2 tensioning block screws by 180 degrees, run the slider around the illustrated path, then retighten.
Refit the male mount, adapter board, part cooling fan and part cooling assembly.

sources.title: U1 XY timing belts replacement guide

entries.title: U1 stripped XY belt tensioning screw: replacing it with an M3x16 screw
entries.summary: If an XY belt tensioning screw's hex socket rounds out, dismantle the toolhead swapper and replace it with a new M3x16 hex socket screw (about 20 minutes, H1.5 and H2.0 keys, needle-nose pliers). To avoid stripping, use the long arm of the L-shaped key for more leverage.
steps: Remove group 1 (2 x ST3x8) and group 2 (4 x ST3x8) screws with an H2.0 key, then the cooling duct, part cooling fan enclosure and toolhead female base.
Unplug the part cooling fan; remove group 4 (4 x ST2x6, adapter board) and group 5 (2 x ST2.6x10, fan) and take off the adapter board and fan.
Lay the machine face down, remove the 8 x ST3x10 screws (group 6) and lift off X-axis slider-2, keeping the 4 springs under the oil-free bearing.
Grip the stripped screw head with needle-nose pliers and turn it out; hold the metal block so the torsion spring cannot fling it, and do not lose the loose nut under X-axis slider-1.
Fit a new M3x16 hex socket screw.
Refit slider-2, snugging the 8 screws in a diagonal pattern before fully tightening; refit fan and adapter board, then the female base (group 2), fan enclosure and duct (group 1).
Run homing calibration under Settings > Maintenance.

entries.title: U1 XY motor driver running hot (TMC2240): normal range and advice
entries.summary: The U1's XY motors use TMC2240 driver chips rated for -40 to 125 C; as power components they normally run hot. Long periods at high temperature do shorten their life, and fitting the top cover raises driver temperature under the same load, so Snapmaker recommends a 0-30 C room. In hot environments, consider adding driver cooling based on community solutions.
facts: XY driver chip: TMC2240, operating range -40 to 125 C.
Recommended ambient temperature: 0-30 C.
Printing with the top cover fitted increases driver temperature.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 XY motor cable
entries.summary: This cable links the main control board with both the left and right XY motors. Replacing it is difficult (4/5, about 60 minutes) because the side panels, rear cover and toolhead docking bracket assembly must come off. Tools: H2.0 hex key, tweezers, needle-nose pliers and zip ties.
steps: Unload all toolheads, wind back the filament and remove the 4 spools with their holders.
Power off; unscrew and unplug the 4 toolhead USB cables (8 screws), pull out the 6 mm tubes with their holders and take all toolheads off.
Release the 4 mm feeder tubes and remove both feeders, unplugging their cables.
Remove the top cover (4 screws under silicone plugs), both plastic side panels (8 screws each, unplug 2 RFID cables per side) and the rear cover (11 screws).
Remove the toolhead docking bracket assembly (4 screws) and its rear cover.
Unplug the cable at both ends, cut the zip tie, pull the old cable out, route the new one along the same path, reconnect motor and control board, and zip-tie the bundle.
Reassemble in reverse, set toolhead latches (Toolhead 1 to the left end stop, 2/3/4 to the right), dock the heads, reconnect tubes and USB cables, and reload filament.

sources.title: U1 XY motor cable replacement guide

entries.title: Replacing the U1 XY (CoreXY) motors
entries.summary: On the U1's CoreXY system both motors work together for every X and Y move, so the X and Y motors do not each drive one axis. Replacing them is very difficult (5/5, about 120 minutes): remove the panels (ideally the HUB board too, since flipping the machine helps), the docking bracket and the swapper, release the belt, then swap the left (X) or right (Y) motor. Re-run Device Calibration afterwards.
steps: Remove the top panel, side panels and rear cover per the Hub Board Replacement Guide.
Remove the toolhead docking bracket assembly.

Dismantle the toolhead swapper, separate X-axis Slider-1 from Slider-2 and keep the 4 anti-backlash springs; use an H2.0 key to press the belt anchor block out of Slider-1 from behind, freeing the belt.
Zip-tie the belt to the X axis so it cannot jump off the idlers (if it does, re-route it with the XY belt path guide).
Left/X motor: unplug it, turn the machine upside down, remove the 4 bottom screws through the frame access holes and swap the motor.
Right/Y motor: unplug it using tweezers, remove the 4 top screws and swap the motor.
Make sure the toothed side of the belt engages the motor pulley, tighten the screws and reconnect the cable.
Refit the belt anchor, swapper, docking bracket and panels, then re-run every item on the Device Calibration page.
facts: Parts and tools: 2 XY motors, H2.0 and H1.5 hex keys, tweezers, 2 zip ties.

entries.title: U1 X/Y movement exceeded travel limit 0003-0522-0000-0013 / 0003-0522-0001-0013
entries.summary: These errors mean a G-code move tried to go beyond the U1's X or Y travel. Snapmaker covers three cases: near full-size models (switch Z-hop type from Auto to Normal), a slicer warning that paths leave the bed (prime tower placement or more than four filaments), and errors only on the printer (inspect travel moves in preview and nudge first layer height or prime tower width). Update Snapmaker Orca first.
steps: Update Snapmaker Orca to the latest release.
Near full-size model: switch the extruder's Z-hop type to Normal (it defaults to Automatic), save, and slice again.
Slicer warns that G-code paths exceed the bed: move the prime tower fully onto the bed and re-slice.
More than four filaments configured: move the model and re-slice; or set the prime tower outer wall to a specific filament instead of the default; or merge or delete filaments down to four or fewer.
Error only while printing: turn on Travel display in the preview and look for moves beyond the motion limits.
Workarounds: change first layer height slightly (e.g. 0.25 to 0.24) or, preferably, prime tower width slightly (e.g. 30 to 29).
Re-slice, confirm nothing leaves the bed in preview, then print.

settings.advice: Change from Auto to Normal when printing near full-size models to avoid this error.
Keep the prime tower entirely inside the bed.
Keep the prime tower entirely inside the bed.
With more than four filaments, set the tower outer wall to a specific filament instead of the default.
Preferred workaround if a travel move exceeds the limit: change slightly, e.g. 30 to 29.
Alternative workaround: change slightly, e.g. 0.25 to 0.24.

facts: The Z equivalent, 0003-0522-0002-0013 (Z travel limit), has no dedicated article in the error table.

sources.title: U1 X/Y movement exceeded travel limit

entries.title: U1 Homing Sensor Not Triggered 0003-0528-0003-0004 (Z homing)
entries.summary: The U1 homes Z by raising the bed until it touches the nozzle, and this error fires when Z has travelled far enough without the sensor triggering. Either the bed's travel is blocked so it never reaches the nozzle, or the sensor is not working. Diagnose by where the bed stopped: at the bottom, partway up, or right below the nozzle.
causes: Heated bed shipping screws not removed
Z travel obstructed or a lead screw/linear rod out of place
Residue on the nozzle
Hotend gap outside 0.1-0.4 mm
Vibration from nearby machines or fans
Possible firmware bug when rare and random
steps: Bed at the bottom, won't rise, noisy: remove the heated bed shipping screws (H2.0). If already removed, look for interference; if a screw just spins, see Heated Bed Screw Spinning and Cannot Be Removed.

Bed partway up: with power off, pull the bottom belt counterclockwise to raise the bed and feel for heavy resistance; if present, check whether a linear rod or lead screw has come out of place and follow the misalignment recovery tutorial.
Bed partway up, no noise: if the error is rare and random, update firmware; if frequent, export logs right away and contact support.
Bed close to the nozzle: heat the active toolhead's nozzle to 200 C and scrub it with a wire brush.

Check the gap between hotend and extruder bottom is 0.1-0.4 mm: plain A4 paper (about 0.1 mm) should slip in, the same sheet folded twice (about 0.4 mm) should not. Tighten or loosen the hotend screws to correct it.

Rule out vibration: move the printer to a level floor with nothing underneath and home manually; also try homing with the part cooling fan at maximum, and with the nozzle at 140 C so the hotend fan runs, to see if extra vibration triggers the error.

entries.title: Replacing the U1 Z motor and re-tensioning the Z belt
entries.summary: The U1 Z motor sits behind the right side panel. Replacement is moderate (about 45 minutes, H2.0 key): unload Toolheads 3 and 4, lower the bed, remove the right feeder and right panel, release the Z belt at the tension arm, swap the motor, route the belt over all 4 pulleys and let the spring set the tension.
steps: Unload Toolheads 3 and 4, wind back spools 3 and 4 and remove them with their holders.
Pull the timing belt under the machine to the right to drop the bed to its lowest point.
Power off; remove the right feeder (release its two 4 mm tubes and cable), unplug the 4 USB cables, remove the top cover screws and the right plastic panel (8 screws, 2 RFID cables).
Lay the printer on its back and remove tension arm screws 1 and 2 with the washer; the two screws differ, so keep them apart.
Press the tension arm to slacken the Z belt and lift it off the motor pulley; remove the 4 motor screws, unplug, fit the new motor with its connector facing the same way, reconnect and tighten.
Route the belt over the 2 motor pulleys so it runs over 4 pulleys in total; turn the timing pulley fully clockwise and hold it there so it cannot turn counterclockwise while you route the belt.
Refit screws 1 and 2 loosely so the arm can slide, let the compression spring set the tension, then tighten them.
Refit the panel, top cover, feeder, spools and USB cables, then load Toolheads 3 and 4 again.

entries.title: U1 Z-axis thumping or banging noise during Z-hop: normal behaviour and how to reduce it
entries.summary: A thump or knock when the U1 reverses Z quickly or performs Z-hop comes from the Z motor's sudden reverse force travelling into the plastic base. Snapmaker considers it normal and it varies between units; if prints are fine it can be ignored. To reduce it: firmware 1.1.0+, check the Z belt tensioner screws, cut Z acceleration to 200 mm/s², set Z-hop type to Normal and lubricate the lead screws.
steps: Update firmware to version 1.1.0 or later.
Check and tighten the Z belt tensioner screws at the bottom of the machine, then re-tension the Z belt (U1 How To Tighten The Z-axis Timing Belt).
If screw 1 is stripped, it is only auxiliary; make sure screw 2 is tight. Optionally replace the ST3x8 at position 1 with an ST3x10 self-tapping screw.
Lower Z acceleration to 200 mm/s² in printer.cfg (see the Z acceleration entry).
In Snapmaker Orca change Z-hop type for Extruders 1-4 from Auto to Normal.
Lubricate the lead screws; Snapmaker recommends maintaining them quarterly.

settings.advice: Change from Auto to Normal on all four extruders to reduce Z thumping.

sources.title: U1 z-axis noise (thumping sound) explanation and temporary solutions

entries.title: U1 Z-axis step loss: missing layers, taller prints, Z motor current and resistance
entries.summary: When the U1's Z motor misses steps the bed does not reach its target height, leaving random or single missing layers, horizontal gaps and parts taller than designed, most often in multi-color prints. Check feet, debris and anything under the printer, cable snags, then firmware (V1.1.0+ sets Z current to 0.85 A) and Z acceleration, then lead screw lubrication and belt tension, and finally the motor.
symptoms: Irregular missing layers at random heights, or a single missing layer at one height
Overall print taller than designed
Horizontal missing bands, sometimes with slight layer shift
Happens more often in multi-color prints
causes: Mechanical resistance from debris, dried lubricant or snagged cables
Z motor current too low on older firmware (0.7 A)
Z speed or acceleration too high
Z belt too loose (slips) or too tight (extra load)
Worn or faulty Z motor
steps: Check that all machine feet are present and correctly fitted.
Clear debris from the three bed sliders, above their lead screws and the base areas shown in the guide; keep foam, film, cardboard, pads, tablecloths or carpet out from under the printer.

If layers always vanish at one height and the bed catches there when raised by the belt with power off, remove the right panel and check the AC board-to-mainboard power cable, the feeder cable and the heated bed cable (which should run over the screw boss) for interference.
Update firmware to V1.1.0 or later (Z current 0.85 A instead of 0.7 A); do not set Z current above 0.85 A.
If needed, lower Z acceleration (see the Z acceleration entry) and run a test print.

With power off, raise the bed to the top via the belt and push it down by hand; stutter, notchy resistance or noise means friction, so clean and grease the lead screws (U1 core components maintenance guide).
Loosen the 2 tension arm screws so the spring sets Z belt tension, then retighten.
If nothing helps, get a replacement Z motor from support (U1 Z motor replacement guide) and re-level the bed afterwards.
facts: Not Z step loss: uniformly thin layers (under-extrusion), weak layer bonding (temperature), defects only in bottom layers (adhesion), or variation from wet or uneven filament.
Above 0.85 A, long prints with the top cover on or high room temperature can degrade the motor's magnetic performance and cause step loss.

entries.title: U1 under-extrusion: thin lines, voids and weak walls
entries.summary: Too little filament gives thin lines, holes, weak or missing walls. Work through: filament diameter setting, nozzle clog, flow ratio, pressure advance, then print speed. Tools: calipers, the toolbox cleaning needle and heat-resistant gloves.
symptoms: Thin or broken extrusion lines
Holes and gaps in walls or top surfaces
Weak, delaminating or incomplete parts
causes: Real filament thinner than the profile diameter
Partially clogged nozzle
Uncalibrated flow ratio
Wrong pressure advance value
Speed too high for the hotend to melt enough filament
steps: Measure the filament with calipers at 6 spots, average them and enter the result in the filament profile diameter
Light clog: clear the hot nozzle with the toolbox cleaning needle (not for nozzles smaller than 0.4 mm)
Heavier clog: perform a cold pull (230 °C extrude, cool to 70 °C, pull)
Run Calibration > Flow rate > YOLO and set flow ratio to current value plus the best block's correction
Run the PA Line calibration and enter the best pressure advance value
Lower outer and inner wall speeds

settings.advice: Enter the measured average; a value larger than reality causes under-extrusion.
Add the YOLO calibration correction (e.g. 1 + -0.01 = 0.99).
Use the PA Line result; too low leaves thin lines where the head accelerates.
Lower if the hotend cannot melt filament fast enough.
Lower along with outer wall speed.

entries.title: U1 model warps, detaches or collapses
entries.summary: Shrinkage stress curls the base corners up and can knock the part over. Besides adhesion problems (wrong plate for the filament, dirty plate, unlevel bed, fast first layer, cool bed), strong part cooling and a cold environment make it worse. A brim is the extra fallback.
symptoms: Corners or edges curl upward
Model breaks free of the plate mid-print
Tall part topples or collapses
causes: Plate not suited to the filament
Contaminated plate
Unlevel bed
First layer too fast
Bed temperature too low
Part cooling too strong
Cold or drafty surroundings
steps: Match the plate to the filament (the guide gives Smooth PEI for PEBA and Textured PEI for ABS; check the filament data sheet's Bed Type)
Clean the plate with ethanol, level the bed, slow the first layer and raise first-layer bed temperature
Lower the maximum part cooling fan speed
Enclose the printer with the Top Cover; the guide states ABS wants at least 60 °C ambient
Still warping: add an outer brim of 5-10 mm with a 0 mm gap

settings.advice: Set to Outer brim only to anchor corners.
About 5-10 mm depending on part size.
Set 0 mm so the brim is fused to the part.
Reduce; fast cooling increases shrinkage stress.
Reduce for better first-layer bonding.
Raise first-layer bed temperature for the plate in use.
